title: Cowboys agree to terms with WR Ryan Flournoy on one-year extension
summary: The Cowboys have agreed to terms with wide receiver Ryan Flournoy on a one-year contract extension, according to Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report.
full_text: The Cowboys have agreed to terms with wide receiver Ryan Flournoy on a one-year contract extension, according to Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report. The deal is worth up to $6 million. Flournoy, 26, was entering the final year of his deal, which will pay him $1.075 million in 2026. He would have become a restricted free agent in 2027. After being waived out of training camp, Flournoy became the team's third wide receiver last season. He caught 40 passes for 475 yards and four touchdowns, earning a promotion to the active roster from the practice squad early in the season. The Cowboys drafted him in the sixth round in 2024, and he played 156 offensive snaps and 140 on special teams in 11 games as a rookie. The team's leading receiver from last season, George Pickens, is playing under the one-year franchise tag and is scheduled to become a free agent in March.
author: Charean Williams

title: Missing surveillance video hovers over the Shilo Sanders bankruptcy trial
summary: The Shilo Sanders bankruptcy trial ended last Friday.
full_text: ' The Shilo Sanders bankruptcy trial ended last Friday. The decision, to be issued not by a jury but by the presiding judge, is pending. One big issue in the case relates to the whereabouts of surveillance video of the altercation that led to the $11.89 million civil judgment that Shilo hopes to have discharged. Via Brent Schrotenboer of USA Today , Judge Michael E. Romero is well aware of the missing footage . “It just appears real obvious that there is some missing video that no one seems to have been able to find,” Judge Romero said during the trial. There are breadcrumbs potentially leading to Shilo's father, Deion Sanders. As noted by Schrotenboer, Deion testified about his ability to secure video of the incident during a prior deposition. “I have no idea, but whoever it was, they weren’t gonna give me the video,” Sanders said. “I forgot who, someone slipped and gave, not slipped, but they manipulated and gave us the video. That’s how we got our hands on the video. It’s not like the school provided the video for us.” Deion was asked whether this means someone got him the video on the "down low." "They did," Deion said. Judge Romero realizes the potential significance of the missing clip. “The reason I’m getting into that is because the rules require best evidence,” Judge Romero said during the trial. “You have to have video unless it’s missing or can’t be found. And it appears, from what I’m hearing already, that there is a third one out there that’s just gone.” Added Judge Romero: "I'll be dreaming of those videos until sometime in October." The missing video, showing a third angle of the key interaction, is potentially critical to the question of whether the injuries suffered by John Darjean, who was a security guard at Shilo's school in 2015, were "willful and malicious." If so, the debt will survive. If not, it will be avoided. Judge Romero will surely develop his own theory about where the video is, how it ended up missing, and what it potentially shows. And while his eventual ruling may articulate the issue one way, his mental impressions and true suspicions may never be said out loud or written into his ruling. His subjective beliefs surely will guide his broader analysis, at some level. There seems to be enough evidence to justify a finding in either direction. If Judge Romero senses that the video is missing not because it exonerates Shilo but because it confirms that he was the aggressor in the fight with Darjean, Judge Romero becomes more likely to piece the available evidence together in a way that leads to a finding that Shilo will not be able to shirk the $11.89 million debt to Darjean through the bankruptcy laws.
author: Mike Florio

title: "Strong possibility" Tua Tagovailoa will be cut, if/when benched
summary: On Sunday, Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa returns to the place where he made his last start with the Dolphins.
full_text: '' On Sunday, Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa returns to the place where he made his last start with the Dolphins. And he's the starter, for now, with his new team. He essentially won the job by default, prevailing in a competition for which the other primary contender has yet to be able to truly compete. It seems to be a given that, once Michael Penix Jr. believes he's able to play and, more importantly, to protect himself and his surgically-repaired knee while playing, Penix will take over. For now, Tua has a chance to fend off a benching. If he can't, he may not be able to fend off a termination. There is, we're told, a "strong possibility" Tua will be released if/when he's replaced. The chance of that happening will increase if he eventually yields not to Penix but to veteran Cooper Rush, who has 16 NFL starts under his belt. The Falcons signed Tagovailoa to a one-year, $1.21 million contract. It technically becomes fully guaranteed as CBA-mandated termination pay, if he's on the Week 1 roster. But with the Dolphins owing him $54 million minus whatever he earns elsewhere in 2026, he could choose to forgo the termination pay from Atlanta — especially since it's a one-time-only benefit. Even if the Falcons have to pay his salary, it's a minuscule investment. And it was worth rolling the dice; last year, Tua led the Dolphins to a convincing win over the Falcons in Atlanta. This year, something is off. It's been obvious when he played in the preseason. If/when Tagovailoa is released, he'll be a free agent (unless the release comes after the trade deadline). The next question would be whether another team would sign him. He'd have to be willing to embrace backup status, and a new team would have to be confident he could function in that role. The bigger question is whether he can function on the field, if/when he plays. It seems that the league at large has figured out how to stop him from doing the things that made him the NFL leader in passing yardage in 2023, unlocking what was in hindsight a massive mistake by Miami to give Tua a contract in the range of market value. The more immediate challenge for Tua is to return to Acrisure Stadium and to have a better performance than he did last December, in the game that got him benched and eventually released by the Dolphins. In many respects, his tenure in Atlanta (and possibly his career) is riding on it.
author: Mike Florio

title: Myles Garrett: "This was the worst version of myself that I've put out there"
summary: Garrett said he needs to get healthy after missing most of training camp with a knee injury.
full_text: ' Myles Garrett didn't have a single tackle, sack or pressure in his much-hyped debut for the Rams on Thursday night, and afterward he said the 27-7 loss to the 49ers was as bad a game as he's ever played. "This was the worst version of myself that I've put out there," Garrett said. "I've got to be better. I've got to find a way to recover and get back to the player I know I can be and I've shown that I've been before." Garrett, who didn't play in the preseason and barely practiced in training camp because of a knee injury, said his primary focus now is "getting healthy." "That's the main thing," Garrett said. "When I was out there I was a little more focused on myself and trying to stay healthy than what they were doing, and it showed. I wasn't what I needed to be for my team." Garrett said he didn't think the long trip to Australia or the Rams' decision to arrive the day before the game had anything to do with it. "I wasn't the player I wanted to be, I didn't feel like I was the player I've been before when I stepped onto that field. I've got to do what I can to get back to that," Garrett said. Garrett, the reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year whose trade to the Rams was the NFL's most talked-about offseason move, was a total non-factor against the 49ers. The Rams have to hope that was the worst version of him they'll see.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Fred Warner felt the Rams "withered away" as game went on
summary: The Rams took a 7-3 lead over the 49ers on the first play of the second quarter on Thursday night, but it was not a sign that things were going to go their way for the rest of their time in Melbourne, Australia.
full_text: The Rams took a 7-3 lead over the 49ers on the first play of the second quarter on Thursday night, but it was not a sign that things were going to go their way for the rest of their time in Melbourne, Australia. A Demarcus Robinson touchdown catch put the 49ers up 10-7 at halftime and the 49ers would score 17 more points in the second half while shutting out the Rams. The biggest defensive play of that effort came when the Niners stoned the Rams on four goal-to-go plays in the third quarter, including a Matthew Stafford sneak on fourth down that went nowhere. Linebacker Fred Warner was at the point of attack on that play and many others over the course of the 27-7 win. He finished his first game back from a serious ankle injury with 11 tackles and a forced fumble in the fourth quarter. After it was over, he pointed to the different approaches the two teams took in going to Australia — the 49ers were there for a week, the Rams got there the day before — in helping to fuel the way things played out. “I think it was definitely a matter of us feeling like we got stronger as the game went on ," Warner said in a postgame press conference. "The opposing team, it felt like they kinda withered away. . . . Our plan was great. Coming out here early, all the resources they gave us to be successful for today is what gave us a chance to win this game." The second half of the travel question is the impact it will have on the two teams once they are back home. Time will tell how that plays out, but having Warner back in the middle of the defense should only help their chances of keeping things rolling.
author: Josh Alper

title: Patrick Mahomes: Kenneth Walker can break a touchdown at any moment
summary: Throughout the offseason, Chiefs players and coaches have spoken with a lot of excitement about running back Kenneth Walker and what he can bring to the offense.
full_text: Throughout the offseason, Chiefs players and coaches have spoken with a lot of excitement about running back Kenneth Walker and what he can bring to the offense. That trend continued on Thursday with quarterback Patrick Mahomes, who noted the versatility Walker has displayed in practice through training camp. “You’ve got to use that guy,” Mahomes said of Walker in his Thursday press conference. “I mean, he's a talented football player. He runs tough. He has speed. He can break a touchdown at any moment. He can catch the ball. He does kind of it all. “And so, when you have those guys on your team, you find ways to get them the football. If that's either just handing the ball off to them or throwing it to them, you’ve got to and so we got him for a reason. He came in with the right mindset and mentality, and he's really attacked this offseason. And so, I think he's as excited as anybody to get out there in Arrowhead and have Chiefs Kingdom behind him, and so him as well as Emmett [Johnson] and Brashard [Smith], I mean, we’ve got a good running back room, and we'll utilize those guys within this offense.” The first chance we’ll all have to see Walker with the Chiefs will be on Monday night when the club takes on the Broncos.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Myles Garrett's comments, usage are concerning
summary: It's one thing for Rams defensive end Myles Garrett to make no impact in his first game with his second team.
full_text: It's one thing for Rams defensive end Myles Garrett to make no impact in his first game with his second team. It's quite another to hear Garrett explain the reasons for his struggles. “When I was out there I was a little more focused on myself and trying to stay healthy than what they were doing, and it showed," Garrett said. That's alarming. And unusual. Typically, players don't play if concerns about their health become a distraction to the task at hand. It's fair to wonder why Garrett played — and why the Rams didn't intervene and stop him from playing. It's also fair to wonder whether the Rams knew about Garrett's circumstances. If they had, the Rams may not have used him for six special-teams snaps, hopeful he'd show off his ability to block a kick, or two. The urgency to play was surely very, very strong for Garrett. It was the biggest move of the offseason. Garrett, who had wanted to be traded by the Browns for years, finally got his wish. The transaction made the Rams the presumptive Super Bowl favorites. It got Aaron Donald to come out of retirement. And then, in Week 1, Garrett had the same impact on the game that Donald did, even though Donald didn't even make the trip. A player should be at his healthiest in Week 1. For Garrett, he'll need to get to 100 percent with a fresh train on the tracks, each and every week. With the bye not coming until Week 11, Garrett has nine more games to go until he gets extra time to recover. Fans and media spend most of the offseason pondering the hypothetical regarding the season to come. Once the games begin, the practical takes over. Through one game, the practical impact of Garrett was far below what it could have and should have been. The clock is now ticking toward Week 2, vs. the Giants. And Week 3, at the Broncos. And Week 4, at the Eagles. And Week 5, vs. the Bills. Will Garrett, now 30, have a chance to get his body to where he wants to be? If not, how loud will the questions become about whether the Rams may have been better off if they'd kept Jared Verse? The volume will also depend on Verse's performances for the Browns, starting in two days at Jacksonville.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kyle Shanahan: Win or lose, everyone would make a big deal about our travel schedules
summary: The 49ers and Rams took opposite approaches to the longest road trip in NFL history: The 49ers arrived in Australia a full week early to give themselves time to acclimate.
full_text: ' The 49ers and Rams took opposite approaches to the longest road trip in NFL history: The 49ers arrived in Australia a full week early to give themselves time to acclimate. The Rams arrived in Australia the day before in an attempt not to acclimate, and simply to act as if they were still at home. So does the 49ers' 27-7 win vindicate their approach? 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan downplayed that when asked if the 49ers' travel plan worked. "I mean, the game worked," Shanahan said. "Win or lose, I knew everyone was going to make a big deal about that, for either team. You never know how much that factors into it, you just try to do the best to prepare for three and a half hours. I liked how we prepared, but more importantly I liked how we played." Shanahan said he hopes to visit Australia as a tourist some day but didn't focus on anything but football for this trip. "I'd like to come back when I'm not working, enjoy it a little more," Shanahan said. "It's tough to have fun when you're working all week." Asked if he'd like to return to Australia for another game, Shanahan said he'd always prefer to avoid long road trips. "To play? I'd like 17 home games in San Francisco," Shanahan said. "Nothing against Australia, I just don't like to travel."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Roger Goodell: NFL will make announcement on Jed York when investigation is completed
summary: An appearance by Commissioner Roger Goodell on the Netflix pregame show in advance of 49ers-Rams in Melbourne included a box-checking question about the no-contest plea by 49ers owner Jed York on a pair of misdemeanor charges arising from a prostitution-related arrest last month.
full_text: An appearance by Commissioner Roger Goodell on the Netflix pregame show in advance of 49ers-Rams in Melbourne included a box-checking question about the no-contest plea by 49ers owner Jed York on a pair of misdemeanor charges arising from a prostitution-related arrest last month. Goodell confirmed that the situation is being "looked at" under the Personal Conduct Policy. "When we get it completed, we'll obviously make an announcement at that point in time," Goodell told Netflix host Elle Duncan. Other areas of potential curiosity could have included, for instance, why it's taking so long, given that he resolved the case one day after the arrest? Likewise, it would have been fair to ask whether York will be held to a higher standard than would be applied to a player and, if so, how that may be reflected in the punishment. It's a delicate balance, to be sure. The league surely prefers not to shine a spotlight on a source of embarrassment. And Netflix undoubtedly doesn't want to damage a burgeoning partnership. Still, it happened. And the league doesn't hesitate to bang the drum on playing in the NFL being a privilege, not a right. When player behavior falls short of the league's standard, consequences are imposed — often swiftly and rarely equivocally. And if there was any doubt about the other side of the coin, Netflix analyst Michael Irvin was not given an opportunity to repeat his " everybody’s paying for it " defense of York.
author: Mike Florio

title: Brock Purdy, 49ers dominate Rams 27-7 in Australia
summary: The 49ers quarterback outplayed Matthew Stafford, completing 25 of 34 passes for 205 yards with three touchdowns and an interception.
full_text: Much will be made of the travel arrangements for the 49ers and Rams, but Los Angeles better hope its lackluster performance is jet lag and nothing more. The 49ers dominated the Rams from start to finish, winning 27-7 in Melbourne. San Francisco spent the past week in Australia, while Los Angeles showed up 28 hours before kickoff and stayed on Pacific Time in its brief stay. The 49ers not only looked like the fresher team but the better team. Mike Evans scored a touchdown in his 49ers' debut; Deebo Samuel scored a touchdown in his return; Nick Bosa, Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw showed what a difference they make to the team's defense; and Trent Williams confirmed he's the best left tackle in the game. Brock Purdy outplayed the reigning NFL MVP, completing 25 of 34 passes for 205 yards with three touchdowns and an interception. He also ran for 29 yards on five carries. Purdy's touchdowns covered 39 yards to Demarcus Robinson, 5 yards to Evans and 15 yards to Samuel. Evans caught six passes for 49 yards, with five of his catches converting third downs, and Samuel had six catches for 48 yards and a 45-yard kickoff return. 49ers kicker Eddy Piñeiro kicked field goals of 20 and 56 yards but hit the right upright and missed from 52 yards. The 49ers had more yards (379 to 290), more first downs (23 to 15), more plays (64 to 57), fewer turnovers (one to two), fewer penalties (two to four) and a better third-down percentage (7-of-12 to 2-of-9). Matthew Stafford threw an interception, had a 61.2 passer rating and failed on two fourth-down plays. In his previous 84 starts, Stafford had scored fewer than 10 points only once. He directed the Rams to only nine points in a 24-9 loss to the 49ers in 2022. He was stopped short of the goal line by Warner and rookie Gracen Halton on a quarterback sneak on fourth-and-goal from the 1 with 3:46 remaining in the third quarter. Then, with 7:54 left, he threw incomplete on fourth-and-9 to end all hope of a comeback. He finished 15-of-25 for 155 yards before turning it over to Stetson Bennett for mop-up duty with 3:29 left. Kyren Williams scored the Rams' only touchdown on a 5-yard run, giving them their only lead at 7-3. Puka Nacua caught five passes for 74 yards. Myles Garrett, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year, did nothing in his Rams debut. He had no stats, spending much of his night going one-on-one with Williams, and appeared gassed in the fourth quarter. Garrett did not practice much this summer due to knee swelling. Warner totaled 11 tackles, a pass defensed and a forced fumble; Greenlaw had six tackles; and Bosa recorded four tackles, two for loss, and a quarterback hit.
author: Charean Williams

title: Josh Jacobs pleads no contest to two misdemeanor charges
summary: Jacobs was placed on paid leave by the NFL last month.
full_text: Packers running back Josh Jacobs has resolved the criminal charges that led to him being placed on the NFL's Commissioner Exempt list last month. Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property in a Wisconsin courtroom on Thursday. That court appearance was moved forward from November to today last week at Jacobs's request. Both that request and Jacobs's plea suggest he wanted to resolve the case sooner rather than going through a protracted time in the legal system before learning his fate. The resolution of the case opens the door for the league to take disciplinary action via a suspension, which would cost Jacobs money while providing a timeline for his return to the team. Per multiple reports from the hearing, the court ordered Jacobs to to avoid contact with the victim, receive counseling, remain under supervision of criminal justice officials, and pay restitution to the victim as part of accepting his plea.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jonathan Greenard feels "close," but Eagles' plan for Sunday remains unknown
summary: Linebacker Jonathan Greenard has been practicing for the Eagles this week, but it remains unclear whether he'll be on the field against the Commanders on Sunday.
full_text: Linebacker Jonathan Greenard has been practicing for the Eagles this week, but it remains unclear whether he'll be on the field against the Commanders on Sunday. Greenard did not practice at all this summer due to a pectoral injury and has been listed as limited on the first two injury reports of the week. Friday will bring another practice and the issuing of injury designations that could shed more light on whether the offseason acquisition will be part of the Week 1 plan. “They haven’t told me anything ,” Greenard said Thursday, via Reuben Frank of NBCSportsPhiladelphia.com. “I just know I've been getting right, going through the motions of just trying to get back into the swing of things before I get fully thrown out there. But it's something every day. So I just listen to them. I trust their judgment. I'm literally just trying to work day by day. Like, I literally am out there every second trying to just show what I can do. And that's tough for them, but I feel pretty solid. . . . It’s not for me to decide. I feel good, though. I will say I feel I'm in a good spot. I know that I'm working every day to continue to try to get this thing stronger. We're close. I know that.” Greenard will likely play a reduced number of snaps if he is active against Washington, but the Eagles will take whatever they can get if Greenard is ready to start helping the team's pass rush.
author: Josh Alper

title: Packers DC Jonathan Gannon: Kyler Murray can wreck games if you're not coordinated
summary: The Jonathan Gannon-Kyler Murray partnership in Arizona ended with both men moving on after the 2025 season, but they'll be back together for the first game of their new starts.
full_text: '' The Jonathan Gannon-Kyler Murray partnership in Arizona ended with both men moving on after the 2025 season, but they'll be back together for the first game of their new starts. Gannon is now the Packers' defensive coordinator, which means he'll be charged with slowing Murray down in his debut as the Vikings' starting quarterback. In a press conference this week, Gannon said that his experience coaching Murray left him aware of exactly what the defense has to be on guard for on Sunday. "Really good player," Gannon said, via WLUK. "He's in a really good offense with some elite players. Obviously I've got nothing but love and respect for K-1. He's competitive, he's smart, he can make all the throws and he can beat you with his legs. So a bigtime challenge. As I know firsthand what this guy can do with his legs and he can train wreck the game real fast if you're not coordinated the right way. We gotta contain him. We gotta be ready to plaster at all times 'cause he has just kind of a way of getting out that pocket and extending plays. And then when he's out that pocket is when I think he's most dangerous." Murray was shut down after hurting his foot early in the 2025 season and that decision was tied to contractual matters as the Cardinals wanted to avoid being on the hook for any of his 2027 money. That didn't help Gannon keep his job and shutting down his former quarterback would be the best way to start his new gig on the right foot.
author: Josh Alper

title: Matthew Stafford rarely succeeds on quarterback sneaks, but Rams tried one anyway
summary: With the Rams facing fourth-and-goal at the 1-yard line on Thursday night, Matthew Stafford attempted a quarterback sneak.
full_text: With the Rams facing fourth-and-goal at the 1-yard line on Thursday night, Matthew Stafford attempted a quarterback sneak. It did not go well: Stafford took the snap and fell into the line, going nowhere and ending what had been an excellent drive just short of the goal line. That raised an obvious question: Why was a quarterback sneak the play call? Stafford isn't Jalen Hurts or Josh Allen. He's a 38-year-old who attempted two quarterback sneaks last year and failed on both of them, and who didn't gain as much as a single rushing first down in 17 regular-season games last year. Rams coach Sean McVay said after the game that he viewed failing to score at the end of that 12-play, 72-yard drive as the moment the wind went out of the Rams' sails. "We go right down the field and then we don't get in on the QB sneak, and things got out of hand from there," McVay said. Given that, McVay needs to look in the mirror at his own play-calling decision. Stafford confirmed that the sneak was a called play and not something he did on his own. "I've just got to find a way to get in," Stafford said. If McVay wanted to sneak it in from the 1-yard line, it would have made more sense for the Rams to snap the ball to a tight end or running back, which many teams with aging or immobile quarterbacks do. Or McVay simply could have called another short-yardage play. McVay's decision to go for it on fourth-and-goal was a good one, but the play call was a bad one.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Kyle Shanahan: I love calling plays for Mike Evans
summary: Mike Evans built his career with the Buccaneers on being the guy quarterbacks looked to on third down and in the red zone, and it didn't take long for him to take on the same role with the 49ers.
full_text: ' Mike Evans built his career with the Buccaneers on being the guy quarterbacks looked to on third down and in the red zone, and it didn't take long for him to take on the same role with the 49ers. Evans converted three third downs on the team's opening drive to set up a field goal and the wideout extended the 49ers' lead to 17-7 by catching a fade from Brock Purdy for a touchdown in the third quarter. Evans finished the 27-7 win with six catches for 49 yards and head coach Kyle Shanahan said at his postgame press conference that he's already realized that "I love calling plays for Mike." Shanahan also noted that Evans missed time this summer and that his connection with Purdy should only get stronger. "We've watched Mike do that for his whole career," Shanahan said. "I've just never been on the team with him. I mean, he did that to us a ton when I was in Atlanta. Mike is as good as any receiver who's played down there. Hadn't got to work on it as much as we would like during training camp. It was something that we told them early on that we wanted them doing when they were in Tennessee working together [this offseason]. They were working on the side a little bit this week, and I said I want to give them more opportunities to get better at it, but they didn't need it today. They looked pretty good at it." The 49ers saw another wideout go down with injury during the win and any absence for De'Zhaun Stribling will make Evans even more important to the offensive plans that Shanahan draws up in the weeks to come.
author: Josh Alper

title: Sean McVay: "This will define us only if we allow it to"
summary: Something happened on the road to a perfect season for the Rams.
full_text: Something happened on the road to a perfect season for the Rams. The road took them to Australia, where they got their butts kicked, 27-7, by the division rival they hand-picked to face there. After the loss to the 49ers, Rams coach Sean McVay accepted the outcome — but he won't regard it as the start of a trend. "This will define us only if we allow it to," McVay told reporters. "And today was one of those days." McVay took the blame for the loss. "I always look inside-out," he said. "I didn't do [a] good enough job getting us ready to go. There were some opportunities where maybe the game could have flipped, but they deserved the win. They were ready to go. And we'll look at it. We'll see where we can improve, and be better moving forward. "But this is a good humbling day. This is what can sometimes happen in sports. I love this locker room and, you know, the first thing that I'm gonna look at is myself, and I have to do a better job for a group collectively, with our coaches, with our players, and we'll look at this film, and we'll get back to work because, clearly, that's obviously what we've got to do, and sometimes sports can humble you, and today was one of those days." The travel decision will loom over the showing, and McVay mentioned it. "I make no excuses and, you know, whether you want to say it's about travel, whatever, we just weren't good enough in that window," McVay said. "I didn't coach good enough, and we'll look at it and we'll move forward, and that's where we're at right now. But it was a great atmosphere. Give credit to the 49ers. They deserve it, and we're 0-1, and we'll move forward." Sixteen games remain. The only thing we know at this point is that the 49ers can't be worse than 1-16, and the Rams can't be better than 16-1. Still, the Week 14 rematch will loom over L.A. Another loss to the 49ers means a sweep, which becomes a de facto three-game hole in the standings vs. San Francisco.
author: Mike Florio

title: 49ers tight end Jake Tonges suffers MCL injury, Kyle Shanahan says "it wasn't good"
summary: 49ers tight end Jake Tonges left Thursday night's win over the Rams with a knee injury, and coach Kyle Shanahan offered an ominous update after the game.
full_text: 49ers tight end Jake Tonges left Thursday night's win over the Rams with a knee injury, and coach Kyle Shanahan offered an ominous update after the game. "It wasn't good. It's not an ACL, it's the MCL, I believe, but there's some issues with it that we've got to see how it is. There's a little more information to it, but we don't know yet," Shanahan said. The 49ers likely won't know the full extent of Tonges' injury until they're back from Australia and can give him a full battery of tests, but Shanahan's tone suggested that the medical staff thinks Tonges will miss significant time. The 27-year-old Tonges has been with the 49ers since 2023. He spent his first year in San Francisco on the practice squad and played mostly special teams in 2024, but he saw a much bigger role on offense in 2025 because of injuries to George Kittle. Last year Tonges caught 34 passes for 293 yards and five touchdowns, and this offseason he signed a two-year, $8 million contract.
author: Michael David Smith

title: 49ers WR De'Zhaun Stribling's Achilles is intact, to undergo MRI on ankle
summary: The way 49ers wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling suddenly ended his route and started limping on one leg had everyone thinking the worst.
full_text: ' The way 49ers wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling suddenly ended his route and started limping on one leg had everyone thinking the worst. Stribling has an injured left ankle, coach Kyle Shanahan said after the 49ers' 27-7 win over the Rams, but the rookie's Achilles is intact. Stribling will undergo further medical testing to determine the severity of the injury. He injured his ankle early in the game and was questionable to return, but after running up and down the sideline, Stribling did return. With 7:16 remaining in the first half, though, Stribling pulled up while running a route. He could not put any weight on his left leg and needed help to get to the sideline medical tent. Eventually, Stribling was carted to the X-ray room. The 49ers quickly ruled him out. He had no catches.
author: Charean Williams

title: The 49ers-Rams travel question won't be fully resolved until Week 2, or beyond
summary: Based on Thursday night's smothering down under by the 49ers against the Rams, it appears that San Francisco's early-arrival approach worked better than the Rams' strategy of barnstorming.
full_text: ' Based on Thursday night's smothering down under by the 49ers against the Rams, it appears that San Francisco's early-arrival approach worked better than the Rams' strategy of barnstorming. But Week 1 is just part of the equation. The Rams were surely thinking about the recovery from the long trip, with the goal of being ready for the next game, against the Giants to cap Week 2. And it doesn't get easy after that. The Rams travel to Denver for a Sunday night game before playing in Philadelphia the next Sunday afternoon. After that, it's another Monday night game — against the Bills. The 49ers will have to fly home after fully acclimating to Australia and re-acclimating to America. The Dolphins come to town in Week 2, followed by visits from the Cardinals and Broncos. In Week 5, the 49ers make their annual visit to the Seahawks. In many respects, Thursday night's game is only the beginning. Where both teams go from here after going home will show plenty.
author: Mike Florio

title: "Excited" Kyler Murray is ready for his Vikings' debut
summary: The first pick in the 2019 draft is getting a fresh start on Sunday, with the team he grew up rooting for.
full_text: '' The first pick in the 2019 draft is getting a fresh start on Sunday, with the team he grew up rooting for. And Kyler Murray is ready for the moment. "I'm excited," Murray told reporters on Thursday. "Out of my, I don't know how many years I played football, this has got to be right up there for the most anticipated. I can't tell you how excited and ready I am to just be on the field again. Like I said, I haven't played since October, so it's been a long time for me." Will he be feeling any nerves in his debut as a Viking? "Nerves? Honestly, I've been playing football my whole life," Murray said. "If I didn't have, you know, those anxious butterflies, those nerves, I feel like, you know, maybe I shouldn't be doing it anymore, but I do believe, you know, I'm excited. I'm excited, and, you know, I can't wait." He'll also be a captain in his first season with the Vikings. "It means a lot," Murray said. "It means the world, actually. I mean, for me to be here, a new guy, and the guys, you know, put their faith and trust in me. It's emotional, but like I said, it means a lot. I'm appreciative, and I take great pride and honor to wear that 'C' on my chest." The Vikings get a big game right out of the gates, against the Packers at home. A win fueled by a strong performance from Murray will provide instant validation of the effort to sign him. A loss will lead to head scratching for a team that should be good enough, on paper, to get back to the postseason.
author: Mike Florio

title: Deebo Samuel's TD catch has 49ers up 24-7 in fourth quarter
summary: The 49ers have a big lead in the fourth quarter, having dominated the first three plus quarters.
full_text: '' The 49ers have a big lead in the fourth quarter, having dominated the first three plus quarters. The Rams will need a big comeback for a season-opening win. San Francisco leads 24-7 with 12:57 remaining. The 49ers took control by stopping Matthew Stafford on a quarterback sneak on fourth-and-goal from the 1 with 3:46 remaining in the third quarter. Fred Warner and rookie Gracen Halton stopped the Rams quarterback short of the gaol line. The play was upheld on replay. The 49ers then drove 99 yards in 11 plays, with Deebo Samuel catching a 15-yard touchdown. It was Brock Purdy's third touchdown pass, following a 39-yarder to Demarcus Robinson and a 5-yarder to Mike Evans. Purdy is 24-of-32 for 205 yards with an interception. The 49ers have outgained the Rams 358 to 222.
author: Charean Williams

title: Mike Evans scores first TD as a 49er, 109th of his career
summary: Mike Evans scored 108 touchdowns for the Buccaneers.
full_text: Mike Evans scored 108 touchdowns for the Buccaneers. He just scored his first for the 49ers. The wide receiver caught a 2-yard score from Brock Purdy on the 49ers' first drive of the second half. It pushed the 49ers' lead to 17-7 with 11:03 remaining in the third quarter. On third-and-goal, Evans snatched the ball away from cornerback Jaylen Watson. He has six catches for 49 yards and a touchdown, with five receptions coming on third down. The seven-play, 51-yard touchdown drive was set up by Deebo Samuel's 45-yard kickoff return. Purdy is now 20-of-28 for 157 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. The 49ers have ruled out tight end Jake Tonges, who injured his knee late in the first half. They had already ruled out rookie wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling, with a left ankle injury.
author: Charean Williams

title: 49ers lead Rams 10-7 at halftime in Australia
summary: The 49ers have outgained the Rams 208 to 137.
full_text: Matthew Stafford hasn't looked like the MVP he was last year. Yet. The Rams quarterback completed only 4 of 11 passes for 65 yards and an interception in the first half. Forty-one of those yards came on one throw to Puka Nacua that set up their only touchdown. Stafford's passer rating is 19.1. The 49ers lead 10-7 at halftime, having outgained the Rams 208 to 137. Brock Purdy went 17-of-25 for 141 yards with a touchdown and an interception. He threw a 39-yard strike to Demarcus Robinson for the 49ers' first touchdown of the season. The 49ers settled for a chip-shot, 20-yard Eddy Piñeiro field goal on their first drive of the season, choosing not to go for it on fourth-and-goal from the Rams 2. Mike Evans has five catches for 47 yards, and rookie Kaelon Black has run for 36 yards on seven carries. Christian McCaffrey has three carries for 17 yards and four catches for 20 yards. Kyren Williams has the Rams' only touchdown, scoring on a 5-yard run after Nacua's long gainer to the 8. Williams has seven carries for 31 yards and Blake Corum six for 42. 49ers cornerback Renardo Green and Rams safety Quentin Lake each have an interception. Myles Garrett, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year, had a quiet first half. He has no stats yet.
author: Charean Williams

title: De'Zhaun Stribling carted off, ruled out with ankle injury
summary: 49ers rookie wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling injured his left ankle early in the game.
full_text: 49ers rookie wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling injured his left ankle early in the game. The team listed him as questionable to return. With 7:16 remaining in the first half, Stribling pulled up while running a route. He could not put any weight on his left leg and needed help to get to the sideline medical tent. Eventually, Stribling was carted to the X-ray room. The 49ers quickly ruled out Stribling with an ankle injury. Tight end Jake Tonges need help off the field with 2 minutes left in the first half. He could not put any weight on his right leg.
author: Charean Williams

title: Brock Purdy long ball to Demarcus Robinson gives 49ers the lead back
summary: Demarcus Robinson was with the Rams in 2023-24.
full_text: Demarcus Robinson was with the Rams in 2023-24. The Rams apparently forgot how fast he is. Robinson burned his former team for a 39-yard touchdown on a perfectly thrown ball by Brock Purdy. It gave the 49ers a 10-7 lead with 4:28 left in the second quarter. Cornerback Renardo Green set up the 49ers with an interception of Matthew Stafford on the seventh play after Rams safety Quentin Lake picked Purdy. The 49ers went 86 yards in nine plays for their first touchdown. Purdy is 15-of-22 for 134 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Mike Evans has five catches for 47 yards. Stafford has completed 4 of 10 passes for 65 yards and a pick.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jeremiyah Love mum on his availability for Sunday
summary: Jeremiyah Love wants to play.
full_text: ' Jeremiyah Love wants to play. He isn't saying if he will play. "If they want to put me out there, I'm going to go out and play, whether my ankle feels 100 percent, 50 percent, 70 percent," Love said, via Darren Urban of the team website. " I just want to play football . I'll fight my hardest to be out there every game this season." The rookie running back injured his ankle in an Aug. 13 preseason game against the Raiders. It was diagnosed as a high-ankle sprain, and he only returned to practice this week. Love was limited again Thursday. "I have been itching to get back out there ever since I injured my ankle," Love said. Coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday "we feel good" about Love's availability for Sunday's season opener. Love, the No. 3 overall pick, had 14 touches for 72 yards in his only preseason action.
author: Charean Williams

title: Kyren Williams gives Rams a 7-3 lead
summary: The Rams had nine plays for 24 yards, one first down and two punts on their first two drives.
full_text: ' The Rams had nine plays for 24 yards, one first down and two punts on their first two drives. They went 57 yards on only four plays for a go-ahead touchdown on their third series. Matthew Stafford hit Puka Nacua for 41 yards to the San Francisco 8 on their second play of the drive. Kyren Williams had the rest of the yards, with three carries for 16 yards. Williams scored on a 5-yard run, following Nacua into the end zone. The 49ers went 65 yards in 15 plays with Mike Evans turning three third-down receptions into first downs, but they settled for a field goal on fourth-and-goal from the 2. Eddy Piñeiro's chip-shot 20-yard field goal was good. 49ers rookie wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling injured his ankle and was initially questionable to return, but he has come back into the game.
author: Charean Williams

title: Reports: A.J. Brown is expected to miss at least four weeks
summary: Patriots wide receiver A.J.
full_text: Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown's ankle injury is expected to keep him out for an extended period of time. According to multiple reports, an MRI on Thursday confirmed that Brown suffered a high-ankle sprain when he was injured during Wednesday night's 13-10 loss to the Seahawks. Those reports also say that Brown is expected to miss at least four weeks while he recovers from the injury. That time frame would make him a candidate for injured reserve, but there's no word on the team's plans at this point. The Patriots face a run of 2025 playoff teams during the first weeks of Brown's expected absence. They host the Steelers in Week 2 before traveling to Jacksonville and Buffalo for their next two games. Navigating that stretch without Brown will be tougher and it's not an ideal start to the wideout's tenure with the team. Drake Maye is coming off a three-interception fourth quarter in Seattle on Wednesday that also featured a crucial drop by Romeo Doubs. Doubs was the most prominent addition to the receiving corps for most of the offseason and the team will need him to thrive in a prominent role to get the offense on track without Brown.
author: Josh Alper

title: Puka Nacua addresses "darkest times" in his life, fueled by "drowning" in alcohol
summary: Nacua opens up about time spent at a holistic rehab facility.
full_text: Rams receiver Puka Nacua had a difficult and challenging offseason. In an interview with Elle Duncan of Netflix prior to L.A.'s season-opening game against the 49ers, Nacua called his experiences the "darkest times I've had in my life." Nacua spent time in a holistic rehabilitation center. He was asked what he learned about himself. "I think I learned that I'm very avoidant of conflict," Nacua said, "which is very interesting due to the football nature of — I would like to say, I play very physical, just avoidant of the things that I know were causing me stress." Where did the stress come from? "Just, I think, some of the change in lifestyle that came unto me, becoming a public figure, the stress of performing at a high level," Nacua said. "And then I recently became a father. My son is 10 months old, and navigating that co-parenting relationship with his mother, I would kind of isolate myself to feel, like, the weight of all the issues and things that I have was stuck on my shoulders and not being willing to ask for help. I was never one to share my fears, my worries. I was always finding different ways to escape, I guess, from that tension or that stress." How did he deal with the stress? "I think one, alcohol was definitely a thing for me. Just kind of drowning myself, so that the issues and the stress that I was feeling never had the opportunity to be addressed," Nacua said. "But right when I entered the rehabilitation center, I was able to have open and honest conversations." There's still a potential price to be paid. A civil lawsuit is pending. As PFT reported earlier in the day, Nacua has commenced the process of fulfilling a diversion program in lieu of prosecution, which could prompt the NFL to take action sooner than later under the Personal Conduct Policy. Perhaps most importantly, the off-field issues undoubtedly have delayed Nacua's reward for three seasons of high-level performance despite being a fifth-round pick. At a time when Seahawks receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba has a deal that averages more than $42 million per year in new money, Nacua enters the final year of his rookie deal, at only $5.767 million. And he does indeed play with a very physical style. Which enhances the risk of injury. Which puts an even greater premium on shifting the injury risk to the Rams.
author: Mike Florio

title: Commanders add DT Daron Payne to injury report
summary: The Commanders added defensive tackle Daron Payne to their injury report on Thursday.
full_text: The Commanders added defensive tackle Daron Payne to their injury report on Thursday. They list him as limited with a knee injury. That is not a good sign for the team ahead of Sunday's season opener against the Eagles. The Commanders also added defensive lineman Javon Kinlaw to Thursday's report, but he was a full participant with a back injury. Outside linebacker K’Lavon Chaisson (knee), running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) and outside linebacker Odafe Oweh (calf) remained limited a second consecutive day. Center Mick Allegretti (calf), linebacker Jordan Magee (chest), quarterback Marcus Mariota (knee), defensive end Charles Omenihu (wrist) and tight end Ben Sinnott (oblique) were full participants again.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bills vs. Texans: Houston seeks fifth consecutive home win over Josh Allen in 2026 season opener
summary: Buffalo has to buck a recent trend in order to start the season in the win column
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are no stranger to the Lone Star State. For the third consecutive year, the Bills hit the road to square off against the Houston Texans , but history is not on their side in this Week 1 clash between reigning postseason teams. Each of their last four trips to Houston ended in defeat.
Can the Texans keep their home dominance against the Bills rolling? There is plenty of reason to believe that DeMeco Ryans ' crew can open their 2026 campaign with yet another win over the perennial AFC title contenders. Their overwhelming defense has been a problem for Buffalo ever since Ryans took the job, and a few personnel changes on offense suggest the offense can keep pace with the unit on the other side of the ball.
The side that comes away victorious from this marquee opener will start the year with one of the NFL's most impressive early-season wins. To defeat a fellow Super Bowl hopeful right out of the gate is exactly how these teams can assert themselves as top-flight candidates to run the conference.
Not only did the Texans extend their reign of dominance over the Bills the last time these teams met in Houston, but they also did so with a backup quarterback at the helm. If Stroud can be at least as effective as Davis Mills was in the 23-19 victory last November, then the blueprint exists for this to turn into a season-opening win. Buffalo surrendered eight sacks and three turnovers in that contest, and nearly the exact same offense rolls into town in 2026. New wide receiver DJ Moore cannot right that many wrongs.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Seahawks can keep winning with Drew Lock, but history offers one big warning
summary: History shows good teams can survive a short-term QB injury — and Seattle has the roster to do it
full_text:
Sam Darnold was five snaps into the 2026 NFL season — and the Seahawks were five snaps into their Super Bowl title defense — before everything took an unexpected turn. A sack ended Seattle's opening possession. Darnold walked gingerly to the sidelines before later limping to the locker room with a hip injury, and suddenly Drew Lock found himself as QB1.
Seattle won anyway ( with some help ); Lock finished 16 of 22 for 187 yards and a touchdown, the defense picked off Drake Maye three times in the fourth quarter and the defending champs rallied from a 10-point deficit. The early news on Darnold has been encouraging – tests ruled out a fracture and the injury is believed to be muscular — but he is expected to miss at least the Week 2 matchup against Arizona.
Which brings us to a question that comes up almost every NFL season: What actually happens when a championship-caliber team loses its starting quarterback?
The easy answer: The team gets worse. The more interesting question is whether the rest of the roster can absorb that drop-off without letting one injury change the entire season. History says good teams can survive losing QB1 — especially when the absence is short and the backup fits the offense.
So, yes, no surprise here: Good teams get worse when they lose their starting quarterback. The surprise is how often they still survive it.
Looking at data from 2015-2025, 41 teams were above .500 at the time they had to turn to a backup quarterback. Those backups went just 55-82, a .401 winning percentage, which tells you exactly what you'd expect: Losing your starter usually makes even a good football team significantly worse.
Here's the caveat: 24 of those 41 teams — nearly 60% — still made the playoffs. Twelve won at least one postseason game, and four eventually won the Super Bowl.
And the better the team, the better its chances of surviving. Among more established contenders — teams that had played at least four games and were winning at a .600 clip or better —nearly two-thirds still made the playoffs despite their replacement quarterbacks going just 36-47.
That's the important part. The backup usually isn't making the team better. Everyone else on the roster makes it possible for the backup to keep the season from falling apart.
You can see it in the scoring numbers. Those contender-level teams averaged roughly 25 points per game before losing their starter while allowing a little more than 20. With the backup, scoring fell to about 19 points while the defense allowed about 22 — an eight-point swing from plus-5 to minus-3. For context, the median NFL game over the last two seasons was decided by seven points.
So the roster doesn't suddenly become bad because QB1 got hurt. But the offense loses roughly a touchdown's worth of margin for error, which means games that once might have been comfortable suddenly have to be survived.
That's essentially what happened Wednesday night. Seattle scored just 13 points with Lock under center, but its defense held New England to 10. Yes, thanks in no small part to the Drake Maye 4th Quarter Turnover Extravaganza – but that's the point. Lock didn't need to replace Darnold's productivity. He just needed to do his part, take care of the football, avoid the backbreaking mistakes and allow the rest of the roster to conduct business as usual.
If there is one number that matters most for the Seahawks, it's how many games they'll actually need Lock to start. Among teams that were above .500 when the backup quarterback took over, the difference between a short absence and a long one was stark.
That first row in the table above is where Seattle should find comfort. The backups were barely .500, yet nearly 68% of those teams still made the playoffs. And that's really the whole idea. The guys who started the season on the sidelines holding the clipboard and wearing the baseball cap didn't need to become stars. They needed to keep a good team from turning one bad Sunday into a month-long problem.
Once the absence stretched beyond three starts, though, the math changed … quickly. Fewer than 40% of the teams requiring four or more replacement starts made the postseason, and 17% of teams that needed a backup for seven or more starts got there.
So if Darnold misses the Arizona matchup in Week 2, and maybe even the Commanders a week later, history offers hope. If we're still talking about Lock starting a month from now, that's a very different story. In part because that's what history tells us; in part because here is Seattle's schedule starting in Week 4: Chargers , 49ers , at Broncos , Chiefs and Bears .
There's another distinction that matters when we talk about teams "surviving" a quarterback injury. Making the playoffs with a backup holding things together isn't the same thing as asking that backup to win playoff games.
In our previous data, of the 24 teams that were above .500, lost their starter and still reached the postseason, 14 had their QB1 back to start every playoff game. Nine had to continue with a backup quarterback throughout the postseason. (The 2020 Rams split the difference: John Wolford started their wild-card win before Jared Goff returned for the divisional round.)
Backup quarterbacks in those situations went 5-8 in playoff starts. Three of those five wins belonged to Nick Foles .
That tells you just about everything. History says a good roster can often survive the injury. History is much less encouraging when the backup has to become "That Guy" for the duration.
Foles remains the obvious exception. The 2017 Eagles were 11-2 when Carson Wentz tore his ACL. Foles went 2-1 to finish the regular season and then went 3-0 in the playoffs, including one of the greatest Super Bowl performances by a backup.
The 2016 Raiders , meanwhile, are the other extreme. Oakland was 12-3 when Derek Carr broke his leg; Matt McGloin lost the regular-season finale and then got hurt himself. That left rookie Connor Cook making his first career NFL start in the wild-card round where he went 18 of 45 with a touchdown and three picks. The Raiders lost to the Texans , 27-14.
Oakland still had a 12-win roster, but Carr went down in Week 16 — about the worst possible time to lose your starter. And if you don't have a legitimate backup plan, this is what can happen: The margin for error evaporates, no matter how good the rest of the team is.
0-1 regular season; Cook lost WC game
The best examples aren't always the backups who played like stars. They're the guys who understood the assignment and landed in a situation that didn't ask them to be something they weren't.
New Orleans was only 1-1 when Drew Brees injured his thumb in 2019, which is why a team's early-season record can be misleading. The Saints were obviously very good. Teddy Bridgewater stepped into a Sean Payton offense loaded with answers, completed nearly 70% of his passes in his five starts, threw nine touchdowns and just two interceptions. He went 5-0.
Payton wasn't asking him to be Brees, either. He talked at the time about highlighting what Bridgewater did particularly well and building a plan around it. That's pretty much the definition of making the backup fit the offense — and the offense fit the backup.
Brees returned. New Orleans finished 13-3. Mission accomplished.
Cooper Rush did something similar in Dallas three years later. Dak Prescott was injured in the opener, and Rush stepped into a Cowboys team that was much better than the 0-1 record suggested. He went 4-1 in Prescott's absence. Dallas eventually finished 12-5, and Dak was back when the games mattered most.
Then there's Mac Jones last season. Brock Purdy went down after San Francisco's 2025 season opener; Jones won both games during the first absence and eventually went 5-3 across Purdy's two injury stretches . The 49ers finished 12-5 and won a playoff game after Purdy returned.
The interesting part wasn't that Jones suddenly became a different quarterback. It was that San Francisco put him in an…
author: Ryan Wilson

title: NFL Week 1 picks, odds, best bets: Aaron Rodgers beats Falcons, Broncos upset Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs
summary: Reigning picks champ Jordan Dajani gives his picks for Week 1 of the 2025 NFL season
full_text:
Welcome to the 2026 season, and congratulations to you, because out of all the picks columns you could click on at CBS Sports, you chose the one featuring the analyst that was the company's top against-the-spread artist in 2025. I went 148-122-2 ATS in 2025 to capture the CBS Sports crown, and now I have a target on my back like the Seattle Seahawks .
Week 1 in the NFL is probably my favorite betting week of the year. It's your preconceived notions vs. the sportsbook, and sometimes, you can rake in the dough. There are other years where you can be humbled, but it's all part of the experience. This is one of three gambling pieces you'll see from me every week this year. I go head to head with my friend and coworker Jared Dubin on the biggest games of the week. That comes out every Thursday morning. Then, every weekend I post a column on anytime TD scorers.
Here's a look at what I'm thinking this week. As always, credit to the CBS Sports research team for making me sound smart.

Top five picks ATS record: 0-0 Overall ATS record: 0-0 Straight up record: 0-0
Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free)
The Atlanta Falcons rushing to sign Tua Tagovailoa was one of the weirdest moments of the offseason. I mean, they POUNCED on him. To the surprise of very few, the former Dolphin has not looked great through preseason and in practice. I think Michael Penix Jr . would be starting if he were healthy. The Falcons have a great cast of weapons with Bijan Robinson , Drake London and Kyle Pitts , but if you don't have a quarterback, does it even matter?
On Thursday, Tagovailoa suffered what was described as an oblique injury in practice, and Cooper Rush could be in line to start in his place. I'm not sure that helps the Falcons' case very much. The line shifted two more points in favor of the Steelers.
Atlanta is 0-7-1 all-time in Pittsburgh, while the Steelers are 6-2 against the spread as home favorites over the last two seasons. That's tied with the Jacksonville Jaguars for the best mark in the NFL. I don't believe the Steelers are going to repeat as AFC North champions, but they are a better team than the Falcons right now. Aaron Rodgers may be 100 years old, but he's been effective in season openers over his career. He's 12-6 in Week 1 with 32 touchdowns compared to 10 interceptions. That includes four touchdowns thrown in last year's season opener.
The pick: Steelers -5.5 Projected score: Steelers 20-13
Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ )
It seems people are higher on the Green Bay Packers than I am this year. I even said they had one of the worst offseasons in the NFL. Their star running back is on the commissioner's exempt list, their star pass rusher is on the PUP list, they lost their most reliable wide receiver in free agency and there are some concerns when it comes to Jordan Love's offensive line.
I go back and forth whether the Minnesota Vikings are a legitimate sleeper in the NFC. People forget they went 9-8 with J.J. McCarthy at quarterback and had a top three defense. Imagine if Kyler Murray can just play point guard and run Kevin O'Connell's system. He's got a great trio of wideouts to utilize, plus a nice one-two punch at running back. I'm high on Jordan Mason this year. I'm not saying Murray lights it up in his first action as a Viking, but I see a low-scoring affair where Minnesota just simply looks like the better team.
The pick: Vikings -1.5 Projected score: Vikings 22-16
Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free)
I'll bite on the Kirk Cousins Las Vegas Raiders . We don't have a lot of advanced stats to utilize for this pick since it features two very new teams with new quarterbacks and new head coaches, but I would argue that the Raiders are actually one of the most-improved teams on paper. Cousins will be an upgrade over Geno Smith , the offensive line will be better with Spencer Burford and Tyler Linderbaum , and the defense will be improved with all the new faces, such as Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker .
Speaking of "on paper," the Miami Dolphins look like the worst team in the league on paper. This wide receiving corps is headlined by Malik Washington , Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell , and the secondary looks even less promising with Jason Marshall Jr. , JuJu Brents and first-round pick Chris Johnson . Maybe Malik Willis is a legitimate star and the Dolphins surprise everyone this year, but to me, the Raiders are the better team.
The pick: Raiders -3 Projected score: Raiders 23-17
Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET (NBC, Stream: Fubo , try for free)
The New York Giants are 1-7 in Week 1 vs. the Dallas Cowboys over the last 20 years, and the Cowboys are 8-0 vs. the Giants in Week 1 primetime games. I would know, because I tried to back the Giants as Week 1 home dogs vs. the Cowboys in 2023. New York lost, 40-0.
I'm high on the Cowboys this year, so I'm putting my money where my mouth is Week 1. This offense is dangerous, as Dak Prescott commanded the No. 2 passing attack and No. 2 total offense in the NFL last year throwing the ball to CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens . The defense famously was atrocious, but it's going to be better with all the additions they made. Guys such as Caleb Downs , Malachi Lawrence , Rashan Gary , Dee Winters and Cobie Durant will help the Cowboys get back to the playoffs in 2026.
The pick: Cowboys -3 Projected score: Cowboys 28-23
Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET (ESPN/ABC, Stream: Fubo , try for free)
Patrick Mahomes will start under center just nine months after tearing his ACL. Credit to him, but I have a hard time believing he's going to be able to run around like we're used to. Plus, it appears undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson will start at one of the tackle spots for the Kansas City Chiefs , which is concerning. This Denver Broncos defense ranked top three in points per game (18.3), yards per game (278.2) and third down percentage (33.8%) last year, and was one of the most aggressive units in the NFL with a league-leading 68 sacks.
I'm curious to see how different this Broncos offensive attack will be with Davis Webb calling the plays. Sean Payton is an NFL legend, but some of his play-calls last year were confusing to me. Maybe the Broncos offense finds more rhythm immediately. I'm not ruling it out. Bo Nix is a legitimate starting quarterback, as he became the first to ever win 10 games and score 30 total touchdowns in each of his first two seasons. Now, he has Jaylen Waddle out wide, who I think will really open up the offense. I'm not saying "Monday Night Football" is going to be a shootout, but I'm calling for the upset in Arrowhead.
The pick: Broncos +2.5 Projected score: Broncos 17-14

author: Jordan Dajani

title: Week 1 2026 bold predictions: Can Tua Tagovailoa best Aaron Rodgers in Pittsburgh?
summary: Five bold predictions to start the NFL season, from Tua Tagovailoa outdoing Rodgers to Josh Allen finally overcoming his Houston woes
full_text:
The NFL is back, which means our weekly bold predictions column at CBS Sports is too! Just when we think we know what's going to happen around the league, surprises happen every week.
Just look at the Super Bowl preseason favorite Los Angeles Rams . They faceplanted in a 27-7 Week 1 defeat against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia, marking the largest Week 1 loss (20 points) by the preseason Super Bowl favorite in recorded history (odds have been available for the last 50 seasons), per CBS Sports Research. The defeat also marked the fewest points the Rams have scored in a game with 2025 NFL MVP Matthew Stafford as their quarterback. Even 2025 NFL Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett couldn't do anything to slow San Francisco down, registering his fourth career game without a tackle despite playing 39 snaps against the 49ers.
What other head-scratching events will go down in Week 1? Let's take a look at five bold predictions.
Pittsburgh was the site of Tua Tagovailoa's final start as a Miami Dolphins , a 28-15 loss in Week 15. Tagovailoa didn't play terribly, throwing for 253 yards, two touchdowns and an interception on 22-of-28 passing, while taking four sacks. However, Aaron Rodgers was more efficient with 224 yards passing and two passing touchdowns on 23 of 27 passing while taking three sacks.
Fortunately for the Falcons and their loaded cast of playmakers ( Bijan Robinson , Kyle Pitts and Drake London ), the Steelers defense had a 20.9% missed tackle rate in 2025, the sixth-highest rate in the NFL . New Pittsburgh defensive coordinator Patrick Graham produced a 27.9% missed tackle rate with the Las Vegas Raiders defense last season, the second-highest rate in the league. Yards-after-catch opportunities will be available for Tagovailoa and friends.
Tagovailoa will return to Pittsburgh on Sunday, and if he's able to play after suffering an oblique injury in practice on Thursday , he'll outplay Rodgers to shock the Steelers en route to a Falcons victory. This, of course, would be jaw-dropping after watching his 2026 preseason.
Tua Tagovailoa's Falcons debut: - fumble on his 2nd snap - zero passes over 5 air yards - 3/5 for 22 yards with all four targets being underneath routes to Kyle Pitts pic.twitter.com/2tmX2KjLTG
Josh Allen is one of the best quarterbacks playing today, but the Houston Texans have his number. In the 2024 season, Allen totaled a career-low 30% completion percentage (9-30), the worst by any quarterback with 30-plus pass attempts in a game since 1992, per CBS Sports Research. Last year, the Texans sacked Allen a career-worst eight times, with Will Anderson Jr . (2.5) and Danielle Hunter (2.0) becoming the first duo with multiple sacks each against Allen in the same game.
Anderson and Hunter's dynamic has kept Allen in the pocket and under pressure, allowing the Texans to avoid blitzing and keep a fully stocked second level in coverage. Allen will buck this trend of getting his face caved in by Houston by finding new WR1 DJ Moore early and often, as well as relying on the screen game at unforeseen levels to turn the pressure level down. This will free up Allen to play a less chaotic brand of football and settle into the game, thus allowing him to have an average to above-average game against the Texans for the first time in years.
Four-time Pro Bowl edge rusher Trey Hendrickson totaled just 4.0 sacks in 2025 because he was limited to seven games thanks to a hip injury. Two years ago in 2024, the last time he was fully healthy, he led the league with 17.5 sacks. Hendrickson is now 31 years old and fresh off season-ending surgery. However, he'll announce his return to action with a bang, with a couple of sacks of Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in Week 1.
Jones is returning from a torn Achilles, and Hendrickson is coming back from a hip/core muscle injury. Hendrickson finds his footing faster and sacks Jones twice.
Not only were the Jacksonville Jaguars the owners of the No. 1 run defense (85.6 rushing yards per game allowed) in 2025, but they were also just the fifth team since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger to not allow an individual player to rush for 75 yards against them in a game.
Cleveland Browns running back Quinshon Judkins ran for 827 yards as a rookie in 2025 despite the corpse of Joe Flacco , third-round rookie Dillon Gabriel and fifth-round rookie Shedeur Sanders all starting at quarterback last season. He's used to facing loaded boxes and opponents going all out to take away his production. Judkins will summit the mountain that is the Jaguars' run defense and break the 75-yard mark against them this week after no player did that against them in 2025.
No team is tanking in 2026 quite like the Miami Dolphins. They are paying more money for players not on their roster — a combined $183 million dead money cap hit — than they are for players on their roster, a combined $104 million cap hit for their active roster. That's right: 60.7% of the Dolphins' 2026 salary cap is dead money. If that sounds unprecedented, that's because it is. No other team on record, since Spotrac began tracking this statistic in 2011, is above 45%, per CBS Sports Research.
That's how quarterback Malik Willis ' No. 1 wide receiver (in terms of career receiving yards) ends up being longtime Dallas Cowboys depth piece Jalen Tolbert with 1,093. Miami thought ahead in this regard and made sure Pro Bowl running back De'Von Achane was paid (four years, $64 million with $27.378 million guaranteed) before it asks him to run the ball over and over again this season. Achane led the NFL in yards per carry (5.7) last season, and he averages the second-highest career yards per carry number (5.62) by a running back in league history (minimum 500 carries).
Achane is going to get ample opportunity to pursue the rushing title, and he'll start that pursuit against a Raiders defense that missed 27.9% of their tackle attempts, the second-worst rate in the league last season. Yes, Las Vegas remade its front seven with the free-agent signings of Kwity Paye , Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker . But their defensive coordinator, Rob Leonard, served as the team's defensive line coach and defensive run-game coordinator last season. Leonard had a heavy hand in coaching a defense that struggled to tackle consistently in 2025, and Achane will take advantage of that in a big way to kick off the 2026 season with at least 150 yards rushing.
