title: NFL Week 1 picks: Our experts face off on 49ers vs. Rams in Australia, Bills at Texans and more
summary: CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games
full_text:
Welcome to the 2026 NFL season, and our league overlords have put together quite the opening slate of games for us to enjoy. The Super Bowl rematch on Wednesday night saw the Seattle Seahawks hand the New England Patriots another loss, while we have football in Australia on Thursday night between the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams , and then a whopping 13 games on Sunday.
Josh Allen has to open up the season against a scary Houston defense, Lamar Jackson and Daniel Jones face off in Indy, we get an NFC North matchup right off the bat between the Green Bay Packers and Minnesota Vikings , and an AFC West showdown on "Monday Night Football" between Patrick Mahomes and Bo Nix . So, which teams should you pick in Week 1, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Sept. 7 over at DraftKings Sportsbook.
Dajani (Rams -3.5): This matchup is much more than just two rival contenders kicking off the season in the land down under. You need to know that this game features two international juggernauts. The 49ers are 3-1 in games outside the United States, having won their last three, while the Rams have also won three straight international games, boasting a +25.0 points-per-game differential in those wins!
Honestly, I'm not expecting fireworks in this star-studded matchup. But I'm leaning towards the favorites. George Kittle is attempting to play after tearing his Achilles tendon about eight months ago, Christian McCaffrey is in the midst of a ramp-up regimen, and Nick Bosa is coming off a torn ACL. I'm just hoping I don't get caught by the hook … Prediction: Rams 24, 49ers 20
Dubin (Rams -3.5): The Rams are, unsurprisingly, my pick to win the Super Bowl this season. So original, I know. The roster is just that loaded, though, and I think we are going to see that in terrifying fashion right from the first game of the season. The 49ers, as Jordan mentioned, are still working through some injury returns for some of their key players, and that's not exactly an ideal place to be against a team that comes in at full strength.  … Prediction: Rams 31, 49ers 21
Dajani ( Texans +1.5): I love the Buffalo Bills and believe they will win the AFC East this year. But I'm also high on Houston and expecting a bounce-back from C.J. Stroud . The Texans have the best defense in the NFL, but you don't have to tell Josh Allen that. He's 0-4 against the Texans in Houston in his career, including playoffs, and has two total touchdowns over those four starts. It's actually tied for the most losses by a visiting quarterback in Houston all-time. Give me the Texans in the season opener, who are 4-0 straight up in their last four games as an underdog  … Prediction: Texans 23, Bills 21
Dubin (Texans +1.5): I hate to keep parroting the same ideas as Jordan here, but the numbers for Josh Allen against this Houston defense are not pretty. With the Texans playing this game at home, I feel really good about their chances of holding Buffalo's offense in check, and if the Bills aren't going to light up the scoreboard, I don't feel that great about their chances of winning the game, given the question marks they still have on defense.  … Prediction: Texans 20, Bills 17
Dajani ( Ravens -3.5): A home dog at 3.5 points sings to me like the sirens to Odysseus, but I'm afraid something has tied me to the ship's mast. For one, the Ravens average 33.3 points per game in Week 1 with Lamar Jackson starting. The two-time NFL MVP has averaged the most yards per attempt (9.1) and registered the highest passer rating (120.1) in Week 1 starts since 1970. Furthermore, I have questions about the Indianapolis Colts . Daniel Jones is coming off a torn Achilles, and his new WR1, Alec Pierce, missed most of the offseason work due to ankle surgery. Jonathan Taylor will be ready to rock, but will this passing game sputter against a Jesse Minter-led defense?  … Prediction : Ravens 27, Colts 23
Dubin (Ravens -3.5): I'm extraordinarily high on the Ravens this year, and comparatively low on the Colts. With Lamar Jackson back at full health, I expect the Ravens to be one of the best teams in the AFC. They always are whenever he makes it through a full season. Their defense should be improved this year with Jesse Minter at the helm, as well. Meanwhile, Jordan mentioned the various injury issues that could hold the Colts back early in the year. It all adds up to a big Ravens win. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Colts 14
Dajani ( Buccaneers +3.5): My logic here is simple. The Buccaneers have won and covered in Week 1 games over four straight seasons, which is the longest active streak in the NFL. The Cincinnati Bengals, on the other hand, are 1-5 against the spread in Week 1 when Joe Burrow starts. It's weird, the Bengals barely beat the Cleveland Browns last year (17-16), lost to Jerod Mayo 's Patriots in 2024, and fell to the Browns in Cleveland, 24-3, in 2023. Meanwhile, the dark cloud that was Baker Mayfield 's future has lifted thanks to a three-year extension. Vibes are high for the Bucs this week.  … Prediction: Bengals 21, Buccaneers 20
Dubin (Bengals -3.5): I know the Bengals always start the season slow. And I know that picking them early in the season always leads to regret. But I like this matchup for them offensively, and I think their defense will be improved after they drop Dexter Lawrence into the middle of the defensive line. With the Bucs having Emeka Egbuka coming off a toe injury that kept him out for a bunch of camp, I don't think they keep pace with Cincinnati in the opener.  … Prediction: Bengals 27, Buccaneers 21
Dajani (Vikings -1.5): Full disclosure, I don't understand why people are relatively high on the Packers this year. Their most reliable wide receiver left in free agency, their star running back is on the commissioner's exempt list, their star pass rusher is on the PUP list, and the offensive line has some question marks. We'll see how Kyler Murray fares in his first start with the Vikings, but he has the backing of some great playmakers, plus what was a top-three defense last year. To be honest, this line just confuses me. Vikings win … Prediction: Vikings 22, Packers 16
Dubin (Packers +1.5): I'm pretty lukewarm on both of these teams this year, but I like Green Bay's chances to get off to a hot start offensively in this matchup. This is going to need to be Brian Flores' best coaching job in recent memory, because the defensive personnel on hand is not what it once was. I can see Jordan Love putting on a fireworks show here in the opener, winning a shootout against an also-improved Vikings offense with Kyler Murray replacing J.J. McCarthy .  … Prediction: Packers 30, Vikings 27
Dajani ( Cowboys -3): The Cowboys are 8-0 all-time in Week 1 primetime games against the New York Giants . The last one came in 2023, when I tried to back Daniel Jones and Saquon Barkley . They lost, 40-0. Yes, the Giants have reasons for optimism with John Harbaugh and Jaxson Dart , but I have much more optimism when it comes to the Cowboys. I even have them winning the division! We all know about Dak Prescott 's offense with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens , but I think the defense is going to be improved. Caleb Downs is going to win Defensive Rookie of the Year, then the other additions of Rashan Gary , Dee Winters , Cobie Durant and Malachi Lawrence will make their impacts as well. Maybe Malik Nabers is fully healed and Dart is actually a franchise quarterback, but I'm going to back the Cowboys here under the lights of the Meadowlands  … Prediction: Cowboys 28, Giants 23
Dubin (Cowboys -3): I never get sucked into the Cowboys. I always maintain that they're going to be an unserious team. title: Houston house of horrors: Why Josh Allen has struggled vs. Texans' turbo-charged defense
summary: Allen faces the defense best equipped to shut him down to kick off the Bills' 2026 season
full_text:
Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen must be on NFL commissioner Roger Goodell's bad side. The league gave the 2024 NFL MVP his bogeyman to kick off the 2026 season in Week 1: the Houston Texans .
Allen is 0-4 on the road in Houston, including the playoffs, with just two total touchdowns in four starts. Those four defeats are tied for the most losses by a visiting quarterback at the Texans all-time, along with former AFC South passers Kerry Collins and Blake Bortles .
Allen, whose 301 total touchdowns are the most in a player's first nine seasons in NFL history, enters this season trying to figure out how to survive against the Texans' All-Pro edge rusher duo of Will Anderson Jr . and Danielle Hunter . Anderson Jr. and Hunter have been the NFL's most prolific pass-rush duo since 2024, leading the league among all-teammate duos with 50.0 combined sacks. Four-and-a-half of those sacks between Anderson Jr. (2.5) and Hunter (2.0) have come against Allen.
Each of the last two times Allen has faced the Texans' star-studded defense with Anderson Jr., Hunter, All-Pro cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. , Pro Bowl cornerback Kamari Lassiter , Pro Bowl linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair and Pro Bowl safety Calen Bullock , he's been shredded. In 2024's contest, Allen posted a career-low 30% completion rate (9-for-30), the worst by any quarterback with 30-plus throws in a game since 1992, per CBS Sports Research. In 2025, the Texans sacked Allen a career-worst eight times, with Anderson Jr. (2.5) and Hunter (2.0) becoming the first duo with multiple sacks each on Allen in the same game.
So why has Houston vexed Allen so? Here's a closer look at why and what needs to happen for Allen to turn the tide against the Texans.
The common talking point for slowing down a dual-threat quarterback like Allen is to keep him in the pocket and make him one-dimensional by taking away his ability to scramble. That's easier said than done with Allen, but the Texans are able to do that thanks to having two All-Pro bookends on the line of scrimmage in Anderson Jr. and Hunter. This year, they beefed up the interior of their defensive line by drafting Ohio State defensive tackle Kayden McDonald , the 2026 NFL Draft's top DT prospect, in the second round of the draft in April.
Since Houston can keep Allen trapped in the pocket with its front four alone, it doesn't have to sacrifice resources in coverage. Thirteen of the 15 pressures and seven of the eight sacks the Texans racked up on Allen in 2025 came when sending four or fewer pass rushers, per NFL Pro. Houston didn't blitz a single play against Allen in their 23-19 victory in Week 12 last season. Not blitzing allowed the Texans to use man coverage on 42.2% of their dropbacks against Allen that night, their second-highest rate in a game last season, per NFL Pro.
Allen struggled against Stingley, Lassiter, Bullock and safety Jalen Pitre in man coverage, completing just 5 of 11 throws for 45 yards and one interception. He fared much better against the Texans' zone, completing 19 of 23 throws for 208 yards and an interception against zone coverage. It also aided Houston's cause that they weren't afraid to go to man coverage against any of Allen's wide receivers, with Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman being Buffalo's scariest options a year ago.
Buffalo hopes that the Bills' new No. 1 wide receiver DJ Moore can open things up for Allen against Houston's stifling man coverage. That option wasn't available to him in his previous two matchups. That's despite Moore being fresh off career lows in catches (50) and receiving yards (682) with the Chicago Bears in 2025 . However, when Moore last worked with new Bills head coach Joe Brady from 2020 to 2021 (with Brady as his Carolina Panthers offensive coordinator), he racked up 2,350 yards receiving, the seventh-most in the NFL. Brady's ability to unlock the full potential of Moore's game is pretty much Allen's and the Bills' only hope.
Everything else is pretty much the same for both Buffalo's offense and Houston's defense, with the exception of the Bills' trade for Moore and the Texans' free agency acquisitions of safety Reed Blankenship and edge rusher Jadeveon Clowney . Bills right tackle Spencer Brown will once again see plenty of Anderson, who recorded five of his eight pressures and one of his two-and-a-half sacks against him in this game last season.
If Moore can't give Allen much, much more to work with, Sunday afternoon in Houston will feel like Groundhog Day for the Bills' 2024 NFL MVP-winning quarterback.

title: Here are 3 keys for the Cardinals to defeat the Chargers
summary: The Arizona Cardinals are making all the preparations they need as they are getting ready for the 2026 NFL season. Right out of the gate, they are set to open their Week 1 contest on the road against the Los Angeles Chargers. Last year, the Chargers proved they were a very good team with a […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - JULY 26: Tyler Allgeier #22 of the Arizona Cardinals participates in a team practice ahead of the NFL season at State Farm Stadium on July 26, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals are making all the preparations they need as they are getting ready for the 2026 NFL season. Right out of the gate, they are set to open their Week 1 contest on the road against the Los Angeles Chargers. Last year, the Chargers proved they were a very good team with a playoff berth. A lot of time and effort have been deposited into this Cardinals’ roster ever since Mike LaFleur was hired as the new head coach. There are many exciting aspects from last year, and as with every team, there remain some concerns. Mostly with this year’s version, Arizona will start off their first game with three new starting offensive linemen. The offensive line must be a cohesive unit of five men instead of five individuals. RELATED: LOVE OFFICIALLY LISTED AS LIMITED And right out of the gate, the Cardinals must face the Chargers. Last year, they finished 11-6-0 since Jim Harbaugh took the reins. This year, Arizona’s coaching staff wants to run the ball effectively. Last year, LA was ranked #5 in overall defense and averaged just 285.2 combined yards per game on average. That breakdown is #5 against the pass and #8 against the run. Let’s look at three things the Cardinals must accomplish to defeat the Chargers. Establish a balanced rushing attack This new offense has several aspects that LaFleur wants to maintain. A short passing game is one. Usage of multiple tight ends is another. And a consistent rushing attack is paramount. That is why Arizona used the third overall draft pick on a stud running back instead of one of the elite pass rushers that were available. LaFleur wants to run the ball. Last year the Cardinals were #31 in rushing, averaging just 93.1 yards a game. They were #22 in red-zone scoring at 54.1%. All of that needs to change. How were the Los Angeles Rams in 2025, the team LaFleur left as their OC? #1 in total offense, #1 in passing, #7 in rushing, #1 in scoring offense, and #7 in Red Zone efficiency. This will not happen overnight, but LaFleur has multiple years of running this offense, and it will get there eventually. For now, the Cardinals need to have their running game produce and become a game manager against the Chargers. Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love returned to practice today in a limited capacity as he continues working back from a high ankle sprain. Love had been sidelined since suffering the injury during the preseason. A positive step for Arizona ahead of Sunday’s Week 1 matchup against the… pic.twitter.com/B05ADRlwsO — The Sports Place (@offsportsplace) September 10, 2026 Arizona’s offense needs a balanced rushing game. The bulk of carries will most likely come from Tyler Allgeier. If rookie Jeremiyah Love is 100% with his ankle issue, he will get his fair share of carries, but don’t expect a full load. A balanced attack will ease the need to pass the ball often and also help control the clock. Now, how will the offensive line react? Already, RG Isaish Adams is ruled out, and rookie RG Chase Bisontis is on IR. This is already a problem. Jon Gaines will take the reins and had a great camp and preseason. LG Isaac Seumalo is also a question mark. So, we’ll see. Keep out the Chargers’ pass rush The Chargers have a very good pass rush, and it comes from various spots and players. They generate a great pass rush with LB Tuli Tuipulotu, who actually lines up as an EDGE rusher, and Khalil Mack, who has returned to California. To counteract these fine athletes, the Cardinals depend greatly on the skills of RT Elijah Wilkinson and LT Paris Johnson on the corners. The Wilkinson vs. Tuipulotu will become a battle and just might determine quite a few things in this ballgame. What is that called? Baptism by fire? Mack is a beast and has been for years. He was the “NFL Defensive Player of the Year” back in 2016 but dislocated an elbow last year, which landed him on IR. Mack finished the 2025 season with 11 starts, 32 total tackles, 5.5 sacks, 11 QB hits, 11 hurries, and 23 pressures. Tuipulotu has a leaner build and was a second-round draft pick. He was exceptional in college at USC and totaled 21 sacks in a tough conference. He led the conference in tackles for loss (22) and sacks (13.5) in his final year. He was a unanimous All-American, a two-time All-Pac-12 recipient, and was named the “Polynesian College Football Player of the Year.” In the 2025 NFL season, Tuipulotu racked up 13.0 sacks and has 26 for his three-year career. His quickness off the edge and a fast first step are his calling cards. 39 tackles for loss, 52 QB hits, and 73 pressures are why he is such a menace. Tuipulotu was limited in practice on Thursday, but is expected to play. Can Johnson contain him? Stay tuned. Attack the Chargers’ receivers Arizona’s defense has to have constant pressure on Chargers QB Justin Herbert every time he drops back to pass. But he will have time to throw. And when he does, the back end of the Cardinals defense has to be ready. Herbert has a good arm and can’t be allowed to set up and go through his progressions and set up the short passing game. If Herbert is able to set his feet at will, it will become a very long day. He can throw into tight windows when he has time to survey the field, and can throw long. Whether the defensive line can rattle Herbert is one issue, but when he does throw, the Cardinals’ defensive backfield has to come through. It is not clear if Garrett Williams will play, or at the very least become limited in his snaps. A guy like Williams is as real as they come and is a critical piece to the pass defense. This would mean that Max Melton will become the default starter on the outside with Will Johnson. Denzel Burke will then be moved to the slot corner position. The coaching staff has complete trust in all four players. Keeping Herbert out of his comfort zone will be a huge plus to this game with containment. The Chargers have a very good receiver corps headed by Ladd McConkey. Also in this group are Quentin Johnston and Tre’ Harris. Rookie WR Brenan Thompson was drafted in Round 4 and is expected to have a decent number of offensive snaps.

title: Tua Tagovailoa exited practice with oblique injury, Cooper Rush next man up
summary: Cooper Rush is about as good of a third quarterback as you’ll find in today’s NFL, and is certainly one of the most experienced. That said, when you’re staring down the barrel of starting your QB3 in Week 1 of the NFL season, something has gone terribly awry. We’ll get more updates tomorrow, but that […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - AUGUST 22: Cooper Rush #13 of the Atlanta Falcons looks to pass during the first quarter of the preseason game against the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Chris Carter/Getty Images) | Getty Images Cooper Rush is about as good of a third quarterback as you’ll find in today’s NFL, and is certainly one of the most experienced. That said, when you’re staring down the barrel of starting your QB3 in Week 1 of the NFL season, something has gone terribly awry. We’ll get more updates tomorrow, but that seems like a real possibility after Tua Tagovailoa left practice today with what the injury report classified as an oblique injury. He was listed as a limited participant—because he did participate before he got injured!—but we have no idea how significant that injury is at this point. 11Alive’s Reggie Chatman Jr. got footage of the injury and aftermath. #WATCH : I happened to catch the moment #Falcons QB Tua Tagovailoa went down briefly during the open portion of #Falcons practice He stood off to the side for the rest of the period we were able to watch. https://t.co/VyzfRrzond pic.twitter.com/sIO2CtmOkF — Reggie Chatman Jr. (@ReggieChatman) September 10, 2026 If Tua’s fine, he’s starting against the Steelers in Week 1. If not, Cooper Rush will take the start with Jack Strand as his backup, and it would not be stunning to see the increasingly snakebitten Falcons adding another veteran quarterback to the practice squad. Things are getting real grim, real fast. If Rush is up, he’ll be making his 17th career start. He’s completed 364 of 596 passes for 3,766 yards, 20 touchdowns, and 14 interceptions with 62 rushing attempts for 20 yards. The Falcons will be a little more likely to attack downfield with Rush under center in theory, but in practice I imagine he’ll get an ultra-conservative gameplan that features a lot of Bijan Robinson. We’ll see what updates tonight and tomorrow bring us, but for the moment all we can do is hold our breath. Rush, meanwhile, just has to get ready in case he’s called upon.

title: Falcons vs. Steelers: What will Week 1’s win or loss mean for Atlanta?
summary: We’re at the starting line of yet another NFL season, as the Atlanta Falcons look to fight their way out of the wilderness. The team made headlines this offseason by cleaning house from top to bottom and replacing all of the primary decision makers in Flowery Branch, booting away Raheem Morris, Terry Fontenot and Rich […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re at the starting line of yet another NFL season, as the Atlanta Falcons look to fight their way out of the wilderness. The team made headlines this offseason by cleaning house from top to bottom and replacing all of the primary decision makers in Flowery Branch, booting away Raheem Morris, Terry Fontenot and Rich McKay after another period of failure. Now, with Matt Ryan, Ian Cunningham and Kevin Stefanski at the helm, Atlanta looks to transition into a period of prosperity, something they haven’t had since Ryan himself was operating under center as the team’s quarterback. We will go game by game with the Falcons throughout the season answering two simple questions before each game — what will happen from a scenario perspective if they win this coming week, as well as if they lose. The Falcons are currently in the midst of a nine year playoff draught, the second-longest active streak in the NFL. If they win and are in contention for a post season spot, this series will be looking at possible playoff and division based scenarios. Conversely, if they go the familiar route of losing too much, this will become a series looking at draft based scenarios. Let’s get right into it then for the 2026 season. Here is the scenario the Falcons face if they beat the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 1, as well as if they lose. If the Falcons win It will be a dream start for Kevin Stefanski, who will become the first non-interim Falcons head coach to start his tenure with a victory since Dan Quinn’s victory on Monday Night Football in 2015. He will do so by beating a team he faced as a division rival the last six seasons, in Cleveland, as well. The Falcons themselves will get off to their first 1-0 start since beating Carolina at home in 2023, and will avenge a 2024 home defeat against the Steelers in that season opener, which was also Raheem Morris’ first game in his new Falcons tenure. This would also be just the second time Atlanta won game one of the season since 2017, which is also the last time they made it to the playoffs. This would not be a victory against just any opponent — it would be just Atlanta’s third triumph over the Steelers in 20 tries, historically. Pittsburgh is the team that has beaten the Falcons more thoroughly than anybody else according to win percentage. This would be the Birds’ first win in this matchup in exactly two decades; it would also be their first victory in Pittsburgh ever. The Falcons have a home game against a Panthers team that’s had their number in recent memory coming up, and going into that game with a 1-0 record will not only increase their confidence but it would relieve any pressure of potentially digging themselves into an 0-2 hole from the jump. If the Falcons lose It will be more of the same historically — another head coach starting his Falcons career off with a defeat, another season starting 0-1, another loss to the Steelers specifically. Following a turbulent training camp and preseason period, the fanbase will likely be a bit more distraught than usual with another poor start. Stefanski’s own personal record against the Steel Curtain will fall to 6-8 (6-7 with Cleveland which, all things considered is pretty good given how bad the Browns have historically been in that matchup since becoming reestablished as a franchise). Atlanta’s schedule this season isn’t what I would consider light. Early on, their upcoming games in the immediate aftermath of this one will be against a Panthers team that swept them last season followed by a Thursday night trip to Lambeau Field to face a very good Packers team. This isn’t even getting to the difficult part of the schedule yet. Things could begin getting a bit dire quickly if they start out with a defeat right from the jump.

title: Zay Flowers upgraded on Ravens’ Week 1 injury report
summary: The Baltimore Ravens upgraded star wide receiver Zay Flowers to full participation on their second injury report of the 2026 NFL season. Flowers, 25, was listed as as a limited participant on Wednesday with a hamstring injury. He previously dealt with a minor groin injury during training camp but was quickly back on the field. […]
full_text: OWINGS MILLS, MD - AUGUST 26: Zay Flowers #4 of the Baltimore Ravens laughs during the Washington Commanders and Baltimore Ravens joint practice at Under Armour Performance Center Baltimore Ravens on August 26, 2026 in Owings Mills, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens upgraded star wide receiver Zay Flowers to full participation on their second injury report of the 2026 NFL season. Flowers, 25, was listed as as a limited participant on Wednesday with a hamstring injury. He previously dealt with a minor groin injury during training camp but was quickly back on the field. His upgrade should quell any concerns about his availability in Week 1. Baltimore’s injury report was otherwise the same as Wednesday’s. Linebacker Teddye Buchanan (knee), defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike (neck), and wide receiver Devontez Walker (groin) were all limited. The Colts had five status changes on their Thursday injury report. Rookie safety A.J. Haulcy (ankle), depth tight end Drew Ogletree (neck), and backup center Sedrick Van Pran-Granger (illness) were all upgraded from limited to full participation. Quarterback Anthony Richardson (illness) was listed as a full participant, while defensive tackle Grover Stewart (rest) did not practice. The only constant for Indianapolis was wide receiver Alec Pierce (heel), who remained limited as he works his way back to 100%. Head coach Shane Steichen said earlier in the week that he is expecting the 26-year-old to take the field on Sunday. However, if he is out of the picture, the Colts’ wide receiver corps will be led by Keenan Allen and Josh Downs with former Raven Laquon Treadwell elevated to the No. 3 role. Neither Allen nor Downs particularly impressed in 2025; both averaged just 6.4 yards per target. But the former is still a crafty route-runner who will find the soft spots in zone coverage, and the latter can be a dangerous threat with the ball in his hands. The Colts’ offense was one of the best in the league before Daniel Jones’ injuries last season, including a 38-point, 401-yard outburst against the Chargers’ Jesse Minter-led defense. Pierce had nine catches for 98 yards in that game, so his potential absence could make a difference on Sunday.

title: AFC North Preview, Week 1: Browns a lone underdog to begin the 2026 season
summary: The 2026 regular season is officially here, and all four AFC North teams are set to kick things off in the early afternoon window on Sunday. This year promises to be eventful again in the division with more new storylines and fresh faces than ever before in recent memory. While there are expectations for how […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: Jesse Minter head coach of the Baltimore Ravens looks on against the Minnesota Vikings during the fourth quarter of the preseason game at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 regular season is officially here, and all four AFC North teams are set to kick things off in the early afternoon window on Sunday. This year promises to be eventful again in the division with more new storylines and fresh faces than ever before in recent memory. While there are expectations for how the season will shake out for the Baltimore Ravens, Cincinnati Bengals, Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns, everyone is 0-0 currently and anything is possible. What does Week 1 look like for the AFC North squads? Let’s run through every game and preview what’s in store. Cincinnati Bengals Matchup: vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 1:00pm EST The Bengals commence a pivotal 2026 campaign against a familiar quarterback, Baker Mayfield, and the Buccaneers. Cincinnati is favored to win by just over a field goal and projections are anticipating a high-scoring affair between these two teams. The Bengals have found themselves engaged in a number of offensive shootouts in recent years, so another one of those here is certainly in the cards. The issue for them is that they’ve often come out on the losing end of these tilts, which is why they exhausted a lot of capital on defense this offseason. All eyes will be on the likes of high-profile newcomers like Dexter Lawrence and Bryan Cook to see how fit in on the Bengals’ defense and how much of an impact they can make right away. This will be a good test in Week 1, as the Buccaneers have a capable scoring offense with playmakers like Chris Godwin, Emeka Egbuka, Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell. On the other side of the ball, the Bengals are positioned to start fast with their core of offensive talent returning for another year. The biggest question mark is the health of their star wide receiver duo as both Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are nursing injuries heading into this game. The Bengals’ offensive line is another area where hopes are high for significant improvement, particularly in pass blocking. Under head coach Zac Taylor, the Bengals have notably been a slow-starting team to begin the season. While they did go 2-0 last year, both wins were very narrow, and they have a 3-11 overall record in the first two weeks of the season since 2019. Bucking that trend with a strong performance this Sunday would go a long way to setting the tone for the 2026 season. Baltimore Ravens Matchup: @ Indianapolis Colts, 1:00pm EST After an offseason of significant change in Baltimore, this is one of the more anticipated Week 1 contests for the Ravens in recent memory. Jesse Minter’s first regular season game as head coach will see the Ravens travel to Indianapolis to take on the Colts, where they are favored by several points on the road. In addition to Minter, the Ravens are rolling out new coordinators and position coaches all around, so how the team gels on both sides of the ball will be the overarching storyline. If the preseason was any indication, the Ravens should have a top-tier defense under Minter and DC Anthony Weaver. Their first big test will be slowing down All-Pro running back Jonathan Taylor, who scored 20 total touchdowns with almost 2,000 scrimmage yards in 2025. The Colts’ passing attack, with quarterback Daniel Jones returning from a torn achilles, is less imposing, but they still have multiple capable playmakers. Expect Minter to dial up pass rushes to test Jones’ mobility and force the Colts to beat them through the air. Lamar Jackson will be facing a defensive coordinator, Lou Anarumo, who is plenty familiar with him from his years with the Bengals. Expectations are high for Jackson and company after a hype-filled offseason since Declan Doyle became the team’s new offensive playcaller. It’s fair to expect some level of growing pains out of the gate, though, as they incorporate three new starters on the offensive line and a new mix of pass-catchers. Pittsburgh Steelers Matchup: vs. Atlanta Falcons, 1:00pm EST Like the Ravens, this offseason brought about a lot of change for the Steelers, with Mike McCarthy taking over for Mike Tomlin as the team’s new head coach along with three new coordinators. Aaron Rodgers is back for one last NFL season at 42 years old, surrounded by some notable playmakers and offensive lineman. With McCarthy at the helm, expectations for offensive improvement are legitimate, as the veteran coach has a history of leading top-tier offenses — notably for many years in Green Bay with Rodgers as his quarterback. The Steelers get a favorable matchup to kick off a new era, hosting the Falcons as roughly a three-point favorite. Atlanta hired longtime Cleveland Browns’ head coach Kevin Stefanski this offseason, who in theory should provide a coaching upgrade for them. With serious question marks at quarterback, though, the Falcons are not expected to compete as a postseason team this season. Tua Tagovailoa will open the season as the team’s starting signal-caller. Expect the Steelers, now coordinated on defense by Patrick Graham, to bring the heat against Tagovailoa and force him to complete throws under pressure on the move. Bijan Robinson and Drake London are the center of Atlanta’s offensive universe, and thus slowing them down will be top priority for the Steelers. On offense, they should attempt to establish a strong run game with Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle, to open up opportunities for explosive passing plays against a vulnerable Falcons’ defense. Cleveland Browns Matchup: @ Jacksonville Jaguars, 1:00pm EST The Browns begin the season on the road with a tough afternoon bout against the defending NFC South champions. It was another rollercoaster offseason for the Browns in Todd Monken’s first one as the team’s new head coach. Losing Myles Garrett was obviously a major blow to their defense, and a cloudy quarterback competition between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders did little to inspire confidence for their offense. The Browns are underdogs by more than a touchdown in this matchup. Watson ultimately won the starting role and will lead the offense in Week 1, but his leash is likely shorter than any other starter in the league. Jacksonville has good defensive talent and will pose a challenge for the Browns in this game. Placing too much pressure on Watson under center is likely a losing recipe and the Browns will need to run the ball effectively with Quinshon Judkins, a talented rising sophomore. The Browns are incorporating multiple new starters along the offensive line and two incoming rookie wide receivers, KC Conception and Denzel Boston, so growing pains are to be expected early on. While losing Garrett is undoubtedly a huge blow, the Browns still possess good players on defense in every position group. They will need to fluster Trevor Lawrence into turnovers and flip field position to have a chance for an upset. Their secondary will be tested by the Jaguars’ passing attack, which features several high-level playmakers at wide receiver. Are you confident the Ravens are headed in the right direction? | Baltimore Beatdown

And while he has spent the past few years working with Josh Allen and directing one of the league’s highest scoring offenses, Brady says his primary focus has always been on connecting with his players through his authentic, energetic approach to leadership. “I never thought my identity was, ‘I want to be a head coach,'” Brady told BuffaloBills.com . “I just wanted to call plays.” After spending time as Buffalo’s quarterbacks coach (2022-23), interim offensive coordinator (2023) and offensive coordinator (2024-25), Brady realized he was ready to take on the challenge of being a head coach. Today’s edition of Buffalo Rumblinks leads off by breaking down Brady’s leadership and coaching style, discussing what motivates Brady and finding out how Brady is bringing a new energy to the Bills. Check out the assessments below and then let us know your thoughts in the comments section. How Joe Brady is preparing for his head coaching debut Head coach Joe Brady is preparing for his first meaningful game leading the Buffalo Bills, but as he’s leading the preparations for Sunday’s season opener against the Houston Texans, Brady admits he’s not focusing at all on the fact that this will be his head coaching debut. “I’m run different. I don’t ever take those seconds and appreciate that,” said Brady ahead of Wednesday’s practice in Orchard Park. “I know we have a huge test for our guys this week, and I’ve got to be whatever they need me to be. That’s the most important thing.” “He’s the first one in, the last one out,” quarterback Josh Allen said. “When he says he loves to work, he truly loves to work,” Allen said. “He loves football, he loves this game.” We also explore how new offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael Jr. and new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard are embracing their first NFL coordinator roles; check in on the status of several injured Bills players; and find out how starting left tackle Dion Dawkins is preparing for the start of his 10th season in Buffalo. title: NFL Power Rankings, Week 1: Buffalo Bills favored to begin 2026 season
summary: Despite the fact the NFL has only played two games of the 2026 season thus far, nothing was going to stop analysts and prognosticators from revealing their first Power Rankings of the regular season. Some call it “Week 0” and use the endeavor as a means to discuss expectations and rank accordingly. Others? It’s it’s […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 20: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills scrambles and looks to pass during an NFL football game against the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on November 20, 2025 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Despite the fact the NFL has only played two games of the 2026 season thus far, nothing was going to stop analysts and prognosticators from revealing their first Power Rankings of the regular season. Some call it “Week 0” and use the endeavor as a means to discuss expectations and rank accordingly. Others? It’s it’s their own version of the wild west borne out of quota needs. That doesn’t mean we should focus only on those that are observably button-up, since sometimes the off-the-beaten-path offerings are far more entertaining. If you’ve followed along with me in prior seasons, you’ll know I try to remain consistent in sharing the same group of “rankers” each week. You may see some outfits join in or drop off, depending on vibes. That’s to be expected because we all know how important it is to give such an opinionated exercise the level of seriousness it deserves. One thing’s clear in looking over this batch: Everyone LOVES the Los Angeles Rams. We get it, they have the reigning NFL MVP in Matthew Stafford, made a massive trade for edge rusher Myles Garrett (injured, mind you), and someone convinced a well-retired Aaron Donald to come back and play defensive tackle. Plus they have some guys who are good at catching the football. Los Angeles is the easy pick. Well, it was until they took a flight just to mail in a game in Australia. Someone has to be crowned the premiere team ( The Athletic crowned them a “superteam”), and the Rams made the most sense. But their Week 1 effort should serve as a reminder that crowning a champion in September is foolish. In a similar way, any success a team finds early in the season should be dealt with in measured praise. Though quick to pass in our timeline, it’s a long season and very little reveals itself until after the Turkey (maybe Tofurkey or even lobsters) is (are) carved. We saw this play out last season when the Bills beat teams the experts didn’t view as a real threat. They wanted to see more out of Buffalo, only content to buy in once the playoffs began. Well, we know what happened on that front. Anyway… power rankings. It’s not that serious. Or is it? Seriously, power rankings are fun! We’re at almost 2,700 words with this one — featuring 20 outlets (plus one) — so this article should help dissolve away some of those Friday office blues in no time. This list may shrink in any given week, but this season’s first at-bat is swinging for the fences. No one aggregates Buffalo Bills power rankings data like Buffalo Rumblings! Let’s get to it, to see where the experts place the Buffalo Bills, shall we? SB Nation NFL 3 via: 2027 Super Bowl Chances by James Dator and Mark Schofield 4 via: Tim Lynch with Mile High Report 4 via: Brandon Lee Gowton with Bleeding Green Nation NFL.com : 4 “The vibes are generally high in Buffalo, although receiver Khalil Shakir’s health status is worth monitoring prior to the season opener in Houston. The potential for a honeymoon campaign with WR DJ Moore — oh, and the commencement of Joe Brady’s first season as a head coach — begins against an elite defense, which should inform us on where the Bills stand offensively.— Nick Shook The Athletic : 3 “ (Austin) Mock’s projected win total: 10.8” The defense is undergoing a significant change, entering a 3-4 scheme with six new starters, and that’s part of the reason for hope. The other is a fresh start with coach Joe Brady that could get this team over the hump and into the Super Bowl. Even if last season didn’t go as planned, it’s hard to keep a Josh Allen-led team out of the top five entering the season.” — Chad Graff/Josh Kendall ESPN : 3 “ Milestone to watch: Josh Allen surpassing Patrick Mahomes for the most combined passing and rushing yards by a quarterback in his first nine NFL seasons.” “This would take Allen close to the end of the season, but it is well within reach. Allen is 3,782 yards away from eclipsing Mahomes (38,604), and Allen has not missed a start since his rookie season. He averages 590.1 rushing yards and 3,762.8 passing yards per season, so he could pass Mahomes with multiple games to spare. Breaking records is a common occurrence for Allen, and with new No. 1 receiver in DJ Moore added to the mix, he’s primed to set many marks yet again.” — Alaina Getzenberg Sports Illustrated : 5 “Perpetually a team embodying the Atlas statue, the questions for the Bills are myriad. Can Josh Allen continue to play his style of football and get through a season relatively healthy? Will new head coach Joe Brady represent the right kind of vibe switch for Buffalo? Is Jim Leonhard’s defense finally going to provide Allen with some teeth on the other side of the ball and lessen the burden on his back? This is a team that we can almost assuredly believe will be there at the end of the year, though getting over the hump remains the eternal obstacle.” — Conor Orr FOX Sports : 7 Ralph Vacchiano is smart listing his rankings in descending order, that way you have to scroll all the way down to see who’s the top dog. No one scrolls an entire article to read who’s holding court in the basement, right? You do? Oh. Moving on… Vacchiano’s comments on Buffalo should serve as a warning, at least enough to give you pause about what president of football operations/general manager Brandon Beane built. However, most teams can’t endure the amount of injuries to one position that the Bills managed with their wide receivers this summer. “Summer injuries to WRs Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir were a dangerous reminder that receiver is still a problem for this team. Man, if they can properly address that position, look out.” — Ralph Vacchiano Bleacher Report : 5 We’re good with B/R these days, no? I am. They’ve come a long way, and to be clear they offer a very slick power rankings presentation. That’s the most important thing in all of this, yes? Well, it’s close to the most important thing. Remember, we’re having fun, folks! Gary Davenport makes a lot of key points about the Bills that fans of the team are woefully aware of, and which some are fearful may never change. He’s pretty spot on here, revealing that once again that most of this won’t matter if they lose in the postseason. “There isn’t a team east of Los Angeles more in Super Bowl-or-bust mode than the Buffalo Bills. The Bills dismissed their highly successful coach because he couldn’t get the team over the hump. They are led by Josh Allen, who has more playoff wins than any quarterback in NFL history without a Super Bowl appearance. The good news is the team should be in the thick of it in the AFC. title: Five bold predictions for the Buffalo Bills 2026 season
summary: Josh Allen just finished as the second-highest ranked player on the NFL’s Top 100 list for 2026, trailing only Myles Garrett and sitting ahead of every other offensive player in the league. That alone tells you where the conversation around this team should start. But this year’s Bills are also walking into Week 1 with […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 27: Head Coach Joe Brady of the Buffalo Bills on the sideline during a pre-season game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Highmark Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images Josh Allen just finished as the second-highest ranked player on the NFL’s Top 100 list for 2026, trailing only Myles Garrett and sitting ahead of every other offensive player in the league. That alone tells you where the conversation around this team should start. But this year’s Bills are also walking into Week 1 with a new head coach, a new defensive identity, and a roster that looks meaningfully different than the one that has been bounced from the playoffs six straight times. With training camp in the rearview and Houston up first, here are my five bold predictions for the 2026 Buffalo Bills. Josh Allen wins his second NFL MVP Not so bold, right? The league already told us where it stands on Allen entering this season. He’s the No. 2 overall player on the NFL Top 100, the highest-ranked offensive player in the sport, and Sports Illustrated’s most recent quarterback comparison had him at the top of the position as well, ahead of Patrick Mahomes. Dalton Kincaid even said out loud what a lot of people around the league seem to think — that Allen should have been No. 1. He’s also getting what might become the best supporting cast of his career. DJ Moore arrives via trade to reunite with new head coach Joe Brady, who was Moore’s offensive coordinator in Carolina back in 2020 and 2021 — the two best statistical seasons of Moore’s career. Allen himself has said the fit already feels seamless. Pair that with a difficult schedule that will force Buffalo to play its best football just to stay in the AFC East and wild-card race, and you have every ingredient for an MVP case: the talent, the weapons, the opportunity, and the motivation. Maxwell Hairston finishes with five or more interceptions Hairston’s rookie season was more about flashes than volume, and for a fair reason — a training camp knee injury cost him the first six weeks, and an ankle issue ended his year before the playoffs even started. He still finished with two interceptions and five pass breakups in just 11 games and three starts, good enough to tie for third among all rookie defenders in picks and to land him on both ESPN’s and The Athletic’s All-Rookie teams. The tape backs up the ceiling. In just his second career game, Hairston picked off Patrick Mahomes and led every Bills defender in PFF grade that day at 91.1, the highest mark on the field. His 4.28 40-yard dash gives him the recovery speed to play aggressive, ball-hawking coverage rather than just survive downfield. Now entering year two as an expected full-time starter across from Christian Benford, and hopefully healthy heading into the season, Hairston should get the reps and consistency his rookie year never allowed. I think he takes that leap into being one of the better young corners in football. My friend Raphael Sattamini, from the “SattaMiniCast” , has him leading the league in INTs! Terrel Bernard returns to All-Pro-caliber form Bernard and Hairston share the same theme: talent that hasn’t been able to stay on the field. Bernard’s ceiling isn’t in question — his 143 tackles in 2023 ranked 12th in the entire NFL, and he added 6.5 sacks and three interceptions that year. Even in a lesser 2024 campaign as a team captain, he still posted 104 tackles. But 2025 was a step back across the board, with just 65 tackles, zero sacks, and one interception in 12 games as injuries piled up. Here’s why I think that changes. Buffalo’s move to Jim Leonhard’s 3-4 scheme, with bigger bodies up front designed to occupy blockers, should keep Bernard cleaner than he’s ever been in the NFL. That’s not a new concept for him — he played inside linebacker in a 3-4 under Dave Aranda at Baylor, and Aranda and Leonhard worked together at Wisconsin, sharing a defensive philosophy built around disguised pressure. With the extra defensive linemen and Dorian Williams taking on more of the load absorbing bigger offensive linemen in the new base defense, Bernard gets to play in space again, doing what he does best: making plays sideline to sideline instead of constantly shedding blocks from guards and centers. I think he’s not just healthy this year — I think he’s back to being one of the most disruptive off-ball linebackers in the league, earning a Pro Bowl nod and being in the All-Pro conversation. The Bills finish top three in the NFL in sacks Jim Leonhard isn’t walking into Buffalo without a résumé. He spent the last two seasons on Vance Joseph’s staff in Denver, where the Broncos set a franchise sack record in 2024 and led the entire NFL in sacks again in 2025. Before that, at Wisconsin, Leonhard ran defenses that blitzed on over half of all dropbacks across six seasons, touching nearly 72% in 2020. Aggressive is the baseline, not the exception, for this coordinator. He’s also inheriting more juice than Buffalo’s pass rush has had in years. Bradley Chubb signed a three-year, $43.5 million deal after an 8.5-sack season in Miami and slots in as a starter. T.J. Parker, Buffalo’s second-round pick out of Clemson, adds another true edge threat. Inside, Deone Walker and Ed Oliver give Leonhard real interior push to pair with an outside rotation that also includes Greg Rousseau and Michael Hoecht. After finishing 27th in pass-rush win rate a year ago, this group has the pieces and the coordinator to flip that number completely. I expect it to show up immediately in Week 1 against Houston, and I expect it to hold up over 17 games — this defense finishes top three in the league in sacks. The Buffalo Bills win the Super Bowl Let’s be fair about what actually happened over the last six years. Sean McDermott built a genuinely winning culture in Buffalo, and that part of his legacy is real. But it’s also fair to point out that his defenses collapsed at the worst possible moments, over and over. Six straight playoff losses since 2020 for a combined 199 points allowed — the most in the NFL over that stretch. Four blown fourth-quarter leads in five of those eliminations. Zero sacks and one takeaway in the loss to Denver that got him fired. That’s not all bad luck or bad calls. That’s a pattern. Speaking of bad calls, though — they were real too. The fourth-and-1 spot in the 2025 AFC Championship Game, with Buffalo up 22-21 and 13 minutes left, went against Allen on a quarterback sneak that plenty of people, including cameras from multiple angles, thought he got. Kansas City scored a touchdown on the ensuing drive and won by three. That’s not the only time a Bills season has ended on a coin flip of a spot or a measurement. Sure, Josh Allen had plays he wanted back, which quarterback, EVER, doesn’t? However, his playoff résumé already speaks for itself: a 101.5 passer rating, 3,915 yards, 29 touchdowns, and only six interceptions across 15 career playoff games. He has nine rushing touchdowns in the postseason, second all-time behind only Jalen Hurts. He’s made the playoffs every year of his career except his rookie season, and he’s one win away from tying Tom Brady’s record of eight straight seasons with at least one playoff victory. Allen has done more than enough to get this team to a Super Bowl. What he hasn’t had is a defense that matches his level in December and January, or the racing luck to go with it. That’s what’s different now. Buffalo kept the locker room culture and the professionalism that McDermott built, while removing the parts that kept costing them in January. Joe Brady gives the offense continuity instead of a teardown. Leonhard gives the defense an identity that should hold up under pressure instead of folding. Add a fairer bounce or two along the way, and I think this team finally has everything around Allen that it’s been missing. Get the Bills to the Super Bowl, and I don’t…

title: Buffalo Bills Record Book: What could change vs. Texans in Week 1
summary: A new season means new chances to rewrite the record books. And Week 1 is as good a place as any to get started. So, sharpen your pencils, find your erasers, and let’s get ready to mark up the books.  Each week, we’ll open the Buffalo Record Book to four chapters: Sure Things, A Good Bet, Not Impossible, and Superhuman. Some weeks, we […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - DECEMBER 21: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates a touchdown over the Cleveland Browns in the the first quarter of the game at Huntington Bank Field on December 21, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images A new season means new chances to rewrite the record books. And Week 1 is as good a place as any to get started. So, sharpen your pencils, find your erasers, and let’s get ready to mark up the books. Each week, we’ll open the Buffalo Record Book to four chapters: Sure Things, A Good Bet, Not Impossible, and Superhuman. Some weeks, we will have an entry in every chapter. Other weeks, we may be more selective. Either way, we’ll know which numbers to watch as this version of the Buffalo Bills writes its story. _____________________________________________________________________________ WEEK 1 – September 13, 2026 _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 1: Sure Things We have just one entry here • Josh Allen’s consecutive-start streak: Allen has started 122 straight regular-season games. When he takes the field Sunday, he will have 123. I know, I impressed you with my math skills there. But here’s why that number matters. Allen already owns the league’s longest streak among active starting quarterbacks. Joe Flacco, who is now serving as Joe Burrow’s understudy, has 122 straight regular season starts (a streak that ended in 2015 due to a knee injury). Number 123 will move Allen into sole possession of eighth place among NFL quarterbacks. Ever. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 2: A Good Bet Nothing here this week. It’s too early in the season for me to call something a good bet, watch your parlay fall apart, and find myself at the center of a Bills Mafia witch hunt by Sunday night. We’ll fill this chapter when the numbers earn it. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 3: Not Impossible • Dawson Knox receptions: Knox needs just three catches to go from 229 to 232 (again, I’m good at math). That higher number would move him past wide receiver Cole Beasley on the Bills’ all-time receptions list and slide the tight end into 15th place Sunday. • Dawson Knox touchdown catches: Our next entry is Knox again. Should Allen find him in the end zone Sunday, the Buffalo tight end would tie fan-favorite former wide receiver Stevie Johnson with 28 touchdown catches. If he were to snag a second touchdown catch, his 29th, he would find himself tied with Jerry Butler at seventh all-time on the Bills’ list of touchdown catches. But that’s not so serious. • Khalil Shakir receptions: Next up is the human pinball wizard himself: Khalil Shakir. The Bills wide receiver has bounced, bopped, and weaved his way down the football field for four years, so, obviously, we should expect to find his name scattered throughout the record book. This entry could move him into 17th place in franchise history. Shakir enters the season with 197 catches. Eight more—that’s 205 for those of you keeping up with my math skills—and he would pass Robert Woods and Jay Riemersma. • Josh Allen’s dual-threat record: Allen’s entry comes with a wink because the record is already his. He’s just trying to put it out of reach for every other human. It’s his dual-threat record. The Buffalo quarterback has scored both a passing and a rushing touchdown in the same game 50 times, the most in NFL history. Week after week, he’ll have another chance to add to that number. Or so we hope. • Joe Brady’s Bills debut: We’re putting this one under Not Impossible because calling it anything stronger feels like a good way to upset the football gods. With a win in his regular-season debut, Joe Brady would become the fourth head coach in franchise history to win his first game with the Bills. He would join Marv Levy, Rex Ryan, and Sean McDermott. • Josh Allen keeps chasing running backs: Two rushing touchdowns would bring Allen’s career total to 81 and move him into a tie with Frank Gore and Ottis Anderson for 20th on the NFL’s all-time list. Which is, obviously, a completely normal place to find a quarterback. • Bradley Chubb’s road to 50: Chubb arrives in Buffalo with 48 career sacks. Two against Houston would get the new Bills captain to 50—and give him a pretty memorable way to introduce himself in his first regular-season game wearing red, white, and blue. • Josh Allen on opening day: Allen again. Get used to it. With 300 passing yards Sunday, he would record his third 300-yard season opener and tie Jim Kelly for the most in Bills history. He would also become the first Buffalo quarterback to throw for at least 300 yards in consecutive season-opening games. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 4: Superhuman • James Cook rushing yards: James Cook opens the season sixth on the Bills’ all-time rushing list with 4,259 yards. He would need 187 against Houston to pass Joe Cribbs’ 4,445 and break into the top five. That earns Cook a spot in our Superhuman chapter. Except he ran for 216 yards in a game last season, so, apparently, superhuman is something James Cook has already done. _____________________________________________________________________________ For now, all of these numbers stay in pencil. Sunday will tell us which ones earn ink in the Buffalo Record Book, which ones move to a different chapter, and which ones stay right where they are. Then, when we reopen the book next week, we’ll do the math. Again.

title: Buffalo Bills DC Jim Leonhard ready to attack Houston Texans in Week 1
summary: The Buffalo Bills are just a few days away from their Week 1 road game against the Houston Texans. It’s a daunting task for first-time head coach Joe Brady and first-time NFL defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. As a franchise, the Bills haven’t won a game at NRG Stadium since 2006 — a place that frequently […]
full_text: Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard watches as the defense takes the field during first half action of the Bills preseason game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Highmark Stadium on Aug. 27, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Buffalo Bills are just a few days away from their Week 1 road game against the Houston Texans. It’s a daunting task for first-time head coach Joe Brady and first-time NFL defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. As a franchise, the Bills haven’t won a game at NRG Stadium since 2006 — a place that frequently turns into a house of horrors for Buffalo’s fans. But with a new coaching staff comes new opportunity, and new approaches to dealing with trouble. Houston is expected to bring plenty of the latter to Buffalo on Sunday afternoon, but you can count on the team’s new coaching staff doing anything other than backing down. The first week of any NFL season is rife with irregularity, and we have little to go on regarding what the Bills look like on defense under Leonhard’s guidance. That could prove advantageous, but with that comes a learning curve. So what might we expect to find out of Leonhard’s system, his defensive mantra, if you will? Matt Bové wonder the same thing, and asked an enlightening question of Leonhard about his mindset. The one thing anyone who follows this game closely understands is that you always find Jim Leonhard and aggressive defense mentioned in the same first breath. To that end, Bové presented the following to Leonhard : “I’m not asking, I guess, from a schematic standpoint, but you know, we’ve heard so many people say so many times that you’re an aggressive defensive play caller. In your words, what does that mean?” To which Leonhard explained: “To me, that just means you’re not going to let the offense dictate the game. Right? We have to throw our punches, too. And… they’re strategic. Right? You’re doing them on purpose. I don’t like to be reckless as far as how I call a game, but I’m not just gonna sit back and say like ‘we’re just gonna out-execute you week in, week out, every situation that comes up throughout the game.‘ So, there are certain scenarios within a game that we wanna be really aggressive, and there’s others that we will consistently be a little bit more passive on. Right? And that’s the way I like to call games — and you know, we have to make an offense react to us at times. Right? Otherwise, the good offenses — if they get in a rhythm, right — sometimes it’s hard to regain the momentum. So, you have to keep offenses off rhythm, whether it’s speed him up or it’s slow him down, there’s multiple ways you can do that.” Whether wholly revealing or not, it felt like the first time we’d heard Leonhard speak to his defensive philosophy in such a candid manner. There’s a lot to be said for his approach, as well. Certainly, it can lead to negative plays if done recklessly, but Leonhard assured all that’s not his intent. His approach instead appears to be measured aggression where an offense and its coordinators are constantly trying to adjust to absorb the next blow. Leonhard went so far as to relate it to boxing, calling out the idea of “throwing our punches” in “strategic” fashion. Being aggressive for aggression’s sake is a losing formula, where carelessness often creeps in at the worst time. It seems pretty clear that despite his reputation for being aggressive, Leonhard isn’t going to just throw caution to the wind unless strategy calls for such a storm. Catch up with all the latest from Jim Leonhard via the embedded video, below:

title: Christian Benford headlines Buffalo Bills X-factors vs. Houston Texans in Week 1
summary: The Buffalo Bills and Houston Texans game in Week 1 is reasonably star-studded with Josh Allen, Will Anderson, Danielle Hunter, and DJ Moore, but this game just might hinge on some of the role-players for each club. These are my Bills X-factors for this showdown in Houston. 3. Joshua Palmer The Texans allowed a 20-plus […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - NOVEMBER 20: Christian Benford #47 of the Buffalo Bills defends in coverage during an NFL football game against the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on November 20, 2025 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills and Houston Texans game in Week 1 is reasonably star-studded with Josh Allen, Will Anderson, Danielle Hunter, and DJ Moore, but this game just might hinge on some of the role-players for each club. These are my Bills X-factors for this showdown in Houston. 3. Joshua Palmer The Texans allowed a 20-plus yard play on 8.4% of opposing quarterback drop backs in 2025, which isn’t exactly an indicator of a unit susceptible to big plays through the air. However, that was just the 12th-lowest in football, a relative far cry from Houston’s defense essentially ranking in the Top 5 in every other category last season. And Palmer was signed by the Bills to be a man-beating vertical threat, as he was in Los Angeles with the Chargers in his first four NFL seasons. In an injury-riddled first year in Buffalo, three of Palmer’s 22 receptions came on throws 20-plus yards downfield. During Palmer’s last season with the Chargers, eight of his 39 receptions were on deep targets. Palmer played against the Texans a season ago, but was clearly not himself after returning from the serious lower-body injury he suffered on a hip-drop tackle in Week 6 against the Falcons. It was his second game back after more than a month-long absence. He caught two passes for 21 yards, and frankly, never regained his vertical juice post-injury in 2025. A healthy Palmer could be low-key vital for the Bills in this game, even if he’s found downfield once or twice — maybe off play-action ? — from Josh Allen, because chunk plays are especially key against the Texans. 2. Terrel Bernard What Bernard are the Bills getting for this game? When healthy, he’s one of the better splash-play creating linebackers in football — particularly in coverage. Remember that second-half interception of C.J. Stroud in 2024? Vintage Bernard. Since the start of 2023, Bernard has six interceptions, 11 pass breakups, 7.5 sacks, and 22 tackles for loss in just 42 games. That’s filling the stat sheet. But the uncertainty with Bernard resides with his health. Is he 100%? Close to it? Bernard labored through another injury this summer, albeit minor, yet was not on Wednesday’s injury report. And now he’s playing in a scheme conducive to free-roaming linebackers due to the two-gapping in front of him from most — not all — of Buffalo’s defensive linemen. At his size, quite naturally, Bernard has struggled when enormous blockers can freely get to the second level. But with his speed, he can fly to the football. Bernard has proven to be consistently impactful on the Bills defense, when he’s healthy. And we’ll get a first glimpse of just how healthy he is and how well he fits in this new scheme on Sunday. 1. Christian Benford Bills fans are (rightfully) quick to mention Benford does not get enough national publicity… yet all offseason the cornerback No. 2 spot was all everyone wanted to talk about around Western New York. In this game, Buffalo’s No. 1 cornerback will see the towering, long-striding, deceptively physical Nico Collins on the outside. In last year’s clash with Collins, Benford allowed two catches for 43 yards against Collins. Fine work from Benford. While he didn’t shadow the veteran on every route, and it wasn’t a high-volume, game-altering receiving performance, Collins did only run 24 routes in the game, so it was a rather efficient showing. While see how much “keep it in front of us” coverage Jim Leonhard utilizes in this game — I have a feeling it will be less than the Sean McDermott defenses. Keeping Collins from going off, to force Stroud and Co. into longer, more methodical drives, which thereby increase the likelihood of Houston mistakes Buffalo’s defense can capitalize on, will be enormous in this game. Especially with everyone expecting it to be low scoring. Who are your X-factors for the Bills in this game?
author: Chris Trapasso

title: Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills quick passing game will shape Week 1 vs. Texans
summary: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen is known league-wide for creating explosive plays outside the structure of the play call. When mere mortals hold the ball at quarterback, it usually leads to disaster. Late throws over the middle, risky tosses into triple coverage, sacks — you name it — and it often happens with later, off-schedule […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 20: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills gestures against the Houston Texans during the fourth quarter at NRG Stadium on November 20, 2025 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) | Getty Images Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen is known league-wide for creating explosive plays outside the structure of the play call. When mere mortals hold the ball at quarterback, it usually leads to disaster. Late throws over the middle, risky tosses into triple coverage, sacks — you name it — and it often happens with later, off-schedule throws. With Allen, however, those instances are when the magic happens. It’s when he hits Ray Davis fifty yards downfield while Hall of Famer Peyton Manning is yelling to throw it away. It’s when Khalil Shakir finds space between three defenders on a fourth down to catch a touchdown in such a small window that it would make people who suffer from claustrophobia nervous. It’s when Allen is Allen, as he makes us cringe, hold our breath, cover our eyes, and yell excitedly all in the span of three to five seconds. Against the Houston Texans, though, holding the football often leads to disaster. With Allen holding the football, scrambling, and searching for big plays down the field, it hasn’t led to success against Houston in the same way it has against other teams. In fact, Allen’s 1-4 career mark against Houston, including a 22-19 overtime playoff loss in his second season, is the worst head-to-head record he has against any team he’s faced so often. His 74 quarterback rating is significantly lower than his career total (94.4), and he completes just 52% of his passes against Houston compared to nearly 64% overall for his career. Houston has been a house of horrors for Allen and the Bills of late, and one way the team can overcome those struggles is for their top dog to take what the defense gives him in the passing game. What makes Allen great is his ability to break a big play on any given snap, but sometimes, that desire to break the big one leads him to ignore the “easy money” underneath. That puts the Bills in adverse situations offensively, and it allows a defense like Houston’s to do what it does best: hunt quarterbacks. In Allen’s five matchups against the Texans, he’s averaged at least 2.8 seconds to throw in four of those games. Buffalo lost all four of them. The one time Allen and the Bills beat Houston was when his time to throw was the lowest, coming in at 2.62 seconds on average. Granted, that 40-0 victory likely had less to do with Allen’s throw time and more to do with the lack of talent on Houston’s team in what was ultimately a 4-13 debacle of a season, but it definitely sticks out when comparing his struggles in the other four contests. In Allen’s first two matchups with Houston, his desire to create big plays while holding the ball was easy to explain. In his rookie year, he averaged 3.15 seconds per pass in a game where he ultimately left with an elbow injury. In the following season, Allen played one of the most reckless playoff games I can remember, holding the ball for an average of 3.28 seconds per pass in the eventual Wild Card loss. Both of those games were more the product of a young quarterback trying to do too much against a great defense. That can be explained. In the years since Allen has become a star, though, the Texans and head coach DeMeco Ryans have had his number. In Buffalo’s last two losses at Houston, a 23-20 loss in 2024 where Allen completed just 9-of-30 passes and a 23-19 loss last season where he threw two interceptions against zero scores, Allen’s time to throw was on the higher end. In 2024, he had approximately 3.05 seconds to throw on average, and while he took just one sack, he was pressured often. Last season, Allen had an average of 2.79 seconds to throw. The game plan did seem geared towards shorter, higher-efficiency throws, but as the game wore on, Allen kept trying to make plays downfield—plays that just weren’t there. His time-to-throw number was also lowered artificially by the fact that Houston had an absurd 43% pass rush win rate, which led to a career-high eight sacks in the game. Allen’s last two games against Houston have seen him eschew the easy money for deep, lower-percentage throws. In that 2024 matchup, especially, it looked as if Allen wanted to prove to everyone, but particularly Stefon Diggs, he could do plenty of damage without his former teammate. In last year’s matchup, there’s an argument to be made that Buffalo’s lack of receiving talent combined with Houston’s front four forced Allen to make chicken salad out of chicken feces far more often than he should have. In both games, Buffalo continuously — and stubbornly — countered Houston’s seven-man drop coverage with a five-man protection scheme, and Houston’s front four still found space despite playing a man down. Buffalo’s receiving corps was unable to do the same. This week, for better results when trying to solve Buffalo’s Houston problem, the Bills need to rely on quick-game concepts early. Yes, this might mean our favorite bubble screen play call (which, admittedly, did not work at all last November). And while Joe Brady loves the “mesh” concept, running it against what likely will be a zone-heavy Houston defense is not a good idea. Buffalo would be wise to give Allen some easy half-field reads with a built-in checkdown early in the game. It’s been Allen and the Buffalo offense that has been impatient in the recent meetings between these teams; this week, Buffalo needs to keep taking the easy money until Houston’s defense becomes impatient. Using Buffalo’s advantage in the middle of the field should be a priority this week. Khalil Shakir, Dalton Kincaid, and Dawson Knox need to be the focal points of the passing game, and using newly-acquired DJ Moore as a decoy early and often will help to give those other players space. Does that mean Allen should ignore his newest weapon? Of course not. What it does mean, though, is that I’d rather see him take a five-yard chuck against linebacker Aziz Al’Shaiir before he hurls one into double-coverage with Darryl Stingley Jr. sticking to Moore. Those deep shots can happen, and they need to at some point, but they don’t have to happen in ways where Allen is left to fend off unblocked defenders. Buffalo should take those shots off of max-protect looks, especially in early downs with their “12 or “13” personnel groupings. Why not use play-action with James Cook to hit Joshua Palmer on a deep crosser on first down? Why not use Jackson Hawes as a sixth offensive lineman while Dalton Kincaid stretches the seam? There are options, but more than we’re used to seeing, I think those options are going to have to come within the structure of the offense rather than after long scrambles where Allen holds the ball. It might be hard to teach an old dog new tricks, but at 30 years old, Allen still has some time to shift his game depending on the situation in front of him. While the off-schedule big play might be the thing that makes Allen superhuman, in Sunday’s matchup against Houston, Buffalo just needs Allen to be his normal, efficient self. As good as Allen has been when holding the ball for long periods of time, he has become one of the league’s deadliest quarterbacks when the ball comes out quickly, as well. When the ball comes out in under 2.5 seconds, Allen completes nearly 73% of his passes with a 4:1 touchdown to interception ratio. Sure, that total includes screens, swings, slants, and check-downs, but it keeps the chains moving and keeps the ball in Buffalo’s possession. In the last two meetings between Buffalo and Houston, it was the Texans defense forcing Buffalo into losses and errors, negative plays which ultimately prevented the Bills from scoring enough to win. On Sunday, Buffalo can flip the script, and the best way for their offense to do that would be to stick to the one authored by head coach and playcaller Joe Brady.…
