title: Is Houston Texans rookie the Key(lan) to victory for Buffalo Bills?
summary: I’ve been doing opponent preview articles for years and you know which ones suck the most to write? Week 1 of any season. I can’t truly rely on stats from last year because there are so many variables that change between years. I could historical matchups, but… see above. Player previews are fun but we’re […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - JUNE 04: Keylan Rutledge #66 of the Houston Texans takes the field during OTA Offseason Workouts at Houston Methodist Training Center on June 04, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images I’ve been doing opponent preview articles for years and you know which ones suck the most to write? Week 1 of any season. I can’t truly rely on stats from last year because there are so many variables that change between years. I could historical matchups, but… see above. Player previews are fun but we’re left with one of two choices. Option 1: Players who were on the team before where there’s plenty of footage. It’s not likely I’m sharing anything new and there’s always a chance of change between seasons. Option 2: Rookies where I can give authentic first impressions but it’s based on a very low data set. The title likely gave away I went with option 2 and that’s in large part thanks to some fantastic coverage by the rest of the Buffalo Rumblings team, breaking down hit recent history between the two teams and the ferocity of the Houston defense. Houston’s draft results this year though took me in a different direction. Keylan Rutledge So why Rutledge and why might he actually be the key to victory for Buffalo? If you read this by Chris Trapasso, or this by Rachel Auberger; you likely already know how ferocious the Houston defense has been and how they were the key to the game last year in beating Buffalo. However, if you read closely you likely also noticed that Buffalo’s offensive line was banged up as well as the skill players that day which shouldn’t be the case this time around. If you dive into the box score, you might also have noticed that despite the Texans barrage of sacks, the Bills put up a mostly average number of points and the defense held the Texans to a VERY average scoring output. Enter Keylan Rutledge. The rookie guard is the only member of the Texans’ 2026 draft class currently expected to start Week 1 against the Buffalo Bills. If the health of Spencer Brown, Dion Dawkins, Keon Coleman, and Dalton Kincaid will help the offense out, they might be able to normalize the points scored. If the defense can exploit the rookie lineman, that might help knock a few points off the Houston side of the ledger too. So what are we looking at? pic.twitter.com/42qUcYsz29 — Kuebiko (@Kuebiko_Kami) September 9, 2026 Play notes: I like Rutledge’s fundamentals here. The right hand grabs the shoulder (grab does not equal hold) and moves his feet well to keep the block established. Good awareness of the clutter in front of him prevents Rutledge from tripping, but the defender he’s blocking is able to free themselves relatively easily once they can accelerate. Rutledge’s mechanics fail him here and he goes upright. I point out the feet not because they’re horrible. It’s normal to see them come together and make a short base while moving. That is however, a big reason it’s so dangerous to get stood up like this. If you find yourself upright when your feet are tighter together it’s easy to get rocked. OK fine, I don’t love the feet either. His steps are choppy and at one point he’s pretty close to clicking his heels together. Not his best snap here. I note two things in the clip and both are related. He’s a little too eager on the block and gets ahead of his defender, which risks allowing your opponent to cut in and into the lane you’re, you know, trying to blocking from. Realizing that, Rutledge holds on and twists, and this should have been a holding call. This is a really good rep and shows why he’s the likely starter. Rutledge always finds work and starts off helping his tackle out. He’s quick to respond to the linebacker and gets a good piece of him. The only flaw is that there’s no latch on and the defender can scoot away to get back into the thick of things. What can you say here except that he’s a rookie? This is a good contrast to play 3. Rutledge’s body mechanics are like night and day. Again, rooke. Remember how I said Rutledge always finds work? Yeah, sometimes he shouldn’t. This should have been called as a block in the back and it wasn’t the only one. In summary, Rutledge is a lot of what you’d expect. There are certainly very good traits the Texans should be excited to see develop. They’re interspersed with moments of learning/vulnerability for now. If the Bills can take advantage of his mistakes, it could go a long way in flipping the script from last season.

title: Brian Answers: Bears/Panthers, Bryce Young, Brad Idzik, Fall happenings and more!
summary: Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! We’re only days away from the first regular season game, so only one set of questions away from having some clarity, and likely changing the focus of this column going forward depending on how it all goes. Let’s dive […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 21: Jonathon Brooks #25 of the Carolina Panthers scores a touchdown on a run against the Jacksonville Jaguars during the first half at EverBank Field on August 21, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! We’re only days away from the first regular season game, so only one set of questions away from having some clarity, and likely changing the focus of this column going forward depending on how it all goes. Let’s dive right into all your questions! PurrDurham: Will we see panthers or kitties vs. Bears? Which team is likely to show up for us? I think the Panthers will show up for this game. But all I have to base that on is vibes. Chef: Hey, Brian. So, I haven’t really seen much concerning the potential Waller impact on the passing game outside of his expected red zone targets. Is it foolish to expect him to be more than that in our passing attack or do you think people are sleeping on him? I don’t think Darren Waller would have been available as late as he was in the off-season if any team could reasonably expect him to be more than a complimentary passing target. I do think his addition reveals that the Panthers want to use more 13 personnel (3 TEs) and I also think he’ll be a decent move the chains option for Bryce Young. But I would temper expectations, he may not even be the leading receiver of the Panthers offense when its all said and done. But the more red zone targets, the better in my opinion. ImOpen: I believe that barring injury, Bryce starts every game….which could lead to them drafting a QB I believe we are one more offseason away from being a very good team….able to drop a QB into a good situation I am going to throw in an upset win and say our win total is 8-10…ehhhh 7-9…ish….kinda. What do you think of those statements? The question of the future of the quarterback position and Bryce Young will likely have a clearer answer following this season. I do tend to agree they may be one more solid off-season away from truly being a team that could compete for a deep run in the playoffs, but stranger things have happened. I have them at 9-8 as their overall record still but a deviation two games in either direction wins wise wouldn’t surprise me at all. If they decide Bryce isn’t the answer in the off-season, they should at least have a pretty good situation for the next guy. But I do hope we don’t have to deal with another reset at the QB position. schrodingersblackcat: I think some variation of this may have come up in this feature before, but what are some of your favorite Fall traditions, football related or otherwise? Food/Drink? Outdoor activities? Movies/shows? Social gatherings? Halloween-related stuff? Other? Maybe I’m jumping the gun here, but now that football is finally back, Oktoberfest beers are on store shelves, and we’ve had a couple cooler days to tease us, I am 100% ready for Fall. I’m definitely a fan of a good Oktoberfest beer. Some good whiskey and a cigar on a nice cool Fall night is also great. And I very much look forward to Thanksgiving dinner (sometimes for me, Friendsgiving on a different weekend). Big bonfire guy. Sitting outside in cool PA weather is great. Halloween films absolutely. Anything horror I’m always down for but October is the greatest time for it. Getting people together for some Rock Band is a year round event, but more common during the Fall. Super Smash Bros also tends to run itself back during this time for social gatherings. Oh yeah, and I’m starting my second or third full Dungeons & Dragons campaign following Panthers games most weekends. Lots of Halloween get togethers. I used to be more into dressing up for Halloween so that may be in the cards this year. Might have to bust out my Tommy Wiseau costume once again. Bruce Guild: What do you see for Cokers future Brian? Do you ever see a Pro Bowl or a year he ends up the top receiver by catch count, receiving yards or TD’s? Do you see him being a 6 to 10 year player for the team, or a guy that had the potential but ended up being very mid or oft injured and is out in 3 years? I am very much on the Jalen Coker train, but I need to see a full season of work from him to make a determination. Its very telling that the Panthers already gave him a 3 year extension, and I think he compliments Tetairoa McMillan well. Not seeing Pro Bowl or top of the league receiving stats in his future just yet, but that could change this season. @WTMealey: If we win the toss defer or take the ball? 1st down of 1st drive run or pass? Obviously I’d like to know the thinking behind your answers as well I’d expect the Panthers to defer on the first possession, give the defense a chance to come out swinging early. I think they’ll run the ball on the first play, but that’s not a solid answer from me because I don’t know what to expect from Brad Idzik just yet. WanderingJanusz: I’m surprising my dad for Christmas and taking him to our week 18 home game against Atlanta. Will this end up being a great gift or depressing gift? Well, Bryce Young always tends to go off against Atlanta, so my instinct here is should be a great gift. The Falcons also may not have a quarterback left standing by then based on their luck with injury there throughout the off-season. Even if the Panthers are mathematically eliminated from the playoffs, the Falcons games are always chaotic and unexpected. positivebob: Idzik. What’s the biggest difference we’ll see between him and DC? Again, very hard to say what the difference will be between Brad Idzik and Dave Canales calling plays, as it will all fall in the same system. I think Idzik may open up the passing game more than Canales was willing to, but that’s all based on conjecture and just general instinct. The Panthers may also be in more games where they have to open the passing game based on their 1st place schedule. Mozzie11: Play action pass on 1st down is the best play to make statistically. So do we get bold and run a pass play on the 1st offensive play of the game – and I do not mean a screen for -2 yd or go semi bold with a run up the middle for a yard and a half. Decisions, decisions…. While I said above I think a rushing play starts it out, I wouldn’t be surprised if the opening drive game script is designed to get Bryce Young into more of a groove early rather than having him rip is first pass on a 3rd down situation. I am hopeful they go this direction rather than the usual run first attempt. Bull123: Is Pat Jones hurt yet again? What are we gonna get from Chuba and Brooks? Pat Jones is not expected to play this Sunday, though this seems to be more of a day-to-day injury rather than anything long term. It sucks to not have him the first week of the season, but Ejiro Evero seems to have a plan. He talked up Princely Umanmielen quite a bit this week. I actually expect them to run the same time share they did with Chuba Hubbard and Rico Dowdle this past season, but I think it will work out better this time. These two have more of a complimentary skill set rather than running similar styles. Jonathon Brooks adds a different element as a pass catcher. That’s all for this week, Panthers fans! Enjoy your first game of the season, and KEEP POUNDING!

title: 2026 Season Opener Countdown: 2 Days Remaining
summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to […]
full_text: Dec. 8, 2008; Charlotte, NC, USA; Carolina Panthers defensive end Julius Peppers (90) reacts in the Panthers 38-23 victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Bank of America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Bob Donnan-USA TODAY Sports | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #2. Julius Peppers It is the penultimate entry in our list of top 100 Panthers of all time. We’ve hit lots of fan favorites and players that were good to great. Now we’ve reached the best of the best. The best player to ever suit up on the defensive side of the ball for the Panthers comes in at number two on our list, defensive end Julius Peppers. Peppers is a Carolina kid through and through. He grew up in Bailey, North Carolina, about 30 miles east of Raleigh. He didn’t play football growing up, but his sheer size and athleticism caught the eye of the coaching staff of his high school, and he quickly turned into one of the most dominant players in the state on both sides of the ball. He received a scholarship to play football at UNC and also walked on to the basketball team. He was a reserve forward for the basketball team while we was assembling an elite resume as a defensive end for the Tar Heel football team. He was considered a generational talent entering the 2002 NFL Draft. The Panthers had the number two pick in that draft with the first overall pick going to the expansion Houston Texans. Fortunately, the Texans elected to take David Carr with the first overall pick to be their franchise quarterback. That meant Peppers was sitting right there for the Panthers at the second pick. Peppers delivered on the hype. He registered 12 sacks, five force fumbles, and an interception en route to Defensive Rookie of the Year honors in 2002. He added a modest seven sacks in his sophomore season before fully breaking out as an elite defensive end. He earned his first of six All Pro nominations in his third season with 11 sacks and two interceptions, including a 97 yard pick six. He would spend five more seasons in Carolina after that, accumulating double digit sacks in all but one season in which he was uncharacteristically ineffective. The Panthers elected to let Peppers test free agency after the 2009 season, and Peppers opted to leave to sign with the Chicago Bears. He spent four seasons there before hopping over to the division rival Packers. He spent three years before making a return to his home state. He tallied 11 sacks in his first season back in Carolina despite being 37 years old. He added five more sacks in his age 38 season before announcing his retirement at the end of it. Peppers finished his career with 159.5 sacks, fourth most in NFL history (0.5 sacks behind Kevin Greene for third). 97 of those came with the Panthers, 29.5 more than any other player to wear the black and blue. He scored six defensive touchdowns and blocked 13 kicks, showing just how much of a menace he was in every facet of the game. The two seasons that Peppers spent in Carolina to end his career did a lot to improve his standing with the fan base. During his first stint, there was a perception among parts of the fan base that he wasn’t always giving full effort despite his dominance, and his even keeled persona was often misconstrued as apathy. Those frustrations further boiled over when Peppers refused to re-sign with the team and ultimately left in free agency. Some time apart allowed for a storybook ending, with Peppers returning home to become a fan favorite to end his career and ultimately ending up in the team’s Hall of Honor. Peppers was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2024 and became the first player to spend the majority of his career in Carolina to earn that honor. The end of his career quashed any beef between he and the fan base, leaving him as the inarguable best defensive player to play for the Panthers. For that, he comes in at number two on the list of top 100 Panthers of all time.
author: Jonathan DeLong

title: Panthers vs Bears: Storylines to watch
summary: The Panthers FINALLY are coming back home for regular season football, as the Bears travel to Charlotte to open the season. Its a game many fans have looked forward to, as we’ll see the quarterbacks involved in the famous (infamous?) trade between the two teams that saw the Panthers take Bryce Young at #1 overall, […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 06: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers runs with the ball away from Chris Williams #91 of the Chicago Bears during the fourth quarter at Soldier Field on October 06, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Panthers FINALLY are coming back home for regular season football, as the Bears travel to Charlotte to open the season. Its a game many fans have looked forward to, as we’ll see the quarterbacks involved in the famous (infamous?) trade between the two teams that saw the Panthers take Bryce Young at #1 overall, and the Bears taking Caleb Williams at the same spot a season later. Both teams are looking to build on playoff berths and start the year off strong. In this new game week column, I’ll be breaking down the storylines to watch for during the game. Offense: Consistency is key During the off-season, both head coach Dave Canales and the wonderful fans of the team talked ad nauseum about needing to be more consistent each week. For week 1, that’s the biggest storyline for a Panthers squad that can’t seem to start a season fast. There’s typically a “breaking in the cleats” period and the offense specifically almost always is the biggest offenders with that. We all know the problem if you’ve been following a long, so the question here is; what does consistency look like on the offensive side of the ball? Well for starters, this team absolutely needs to establish the run, early against this Chicago defense. They ranked 26th in yards per game (per Teamrankings.com), so the coaching staff is well aware of this deficiency. They added LB Devin Bush in free agency and S Dillon Thieneman in the draft who should both factor into trying to improve this aspect of the game. Whether its Chuba Hubbard or Jonathon Brooks (who Dave Canales said he’s optimistic will play but is currently listed on the injury report) taking the lions’ share of the snaps does not matter, but the biggest key for getting this offense into a groove and helping Bryce Young play up to a better standard the first week than we’ve seen is to get the offense on a schedule. Running the ball effectively will also play into the strategy that helped the Panthers win as many games against good offenses as they did last year, which is to control time of possession and keep the game close. They are going up against a very high powered Bears offense so keeping the game within reach is a big deal, running the ball effectively can do that. Defense: Contain Colston Loveland Another routine storyline for the last few seasons is this defense has struggled MIGHTILY defending against tight ends in the passing game. Much of that had to do with a very weak interior linebacker position, which the Panthers addressed this off-season by bringing in Devin Lloyd and eventually Bobby Okereke. The pass rush getting off to a hot start should also help, as it gives less time for a tight end to find a mismatch for a quick completion. The former first rounder Colston Loveland is coming off a 713 yard, 6 TD campaign in his rookie season and returned to a loaded offense at receiving options. Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn will likely have their work cut out for them already between WRs Rome Odunze and Luther Burden, so they may not be tasked with trying to help out with Loveland. Jaycee Horn will in theory work more out of the slot this season based on reports, so he may see more of Loveland, but I do believe Loveland will be the biggest key for the Bears themselves to keep on schedule in the passing game. The Panthers cannot give Caleb Williams easy completions. Loveland will eat, but I am hoping to see less of the several big catch receiving games by tight ends this year. This matchup will be a key test. X Factor: Which QB finds “it” first While Bryce Young has struggled in the past to open the season, Caleb Williams has also seen some slow starts in his first two seasons in the NFL. In 2024, Williams started with only 3.2 yards per attempt and 4.7 yards per attempt in his first two starts, one being a win over a bad Titans team and a loss to the Texans where he threw two interceptions. He started off a bit better in 2025, though they were both losses to divisional opponents before he started to come along the following week. Believe me, this is not an apples to apples comparison by any means, but I think this game hinges on which offense gets on schedule first, and that largely will lay at the feet and arms of the two quarterbacks. Obviously, Bryce Young is not coming off a season matching the statistical production of Caleb Williams, but it is a new season, and this is where it all starts. What storylines are you paying attention to for week 1, Panthers fans? Sound off below in the comments!
author: Brian Beversluis

title: Panthers vs Bears: Matchups to watch
summary: The NFL season is off and running. We got our first ever Wednesday night opener and we’re going to get our first ever game in Australia of all places on Thursday. The league will get back to normal on Sunday, and the Carolina Panthers will play host to the Chicago Bears when that happens. These […]
full_text: Nov 30, 2025; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan (4) celebrates with Carolina Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker (18) after a play during the fourth quarter against the Los Angeles Rams at Bank of America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Scott Kinser-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The NFL season is off and running. We got our first ever Wednesday night opener and we’re going to get our first ever game in Australia of all places on Thursday. The league will get back to normal on Sunday, and the Carolina Panthers will play host to the Chicago Bears when that happens. These two teams share a link with one another that’s going to give meetings between them a little extra juice. The teams essentially swapped first overall picks in 2023 and 2024, resulting in Bryce Young landing in Carolina and Caleb Williams landing in Chicago. Both teams ascended to the playoffs last season but did so with lots of late winners and close game luck. Both are looking to prove that last season wasn’t a fluke and that they are going to be players when the postseason comes around in a few months. There are a fair few similarities in the roster constructions as well, and that makes for some interesting match-ups across both units. We’re going to look at one of those match-ups on each side of the ball. The Panthers defensive front vs the Bears offensive line The Bears had one of the best offensive lines in the NFL last season. According to ESPN’s pass block win rate statistic , the Bears were the best team in the league at protecting their quarterback, and they’re returning most of the key components from that unit. Darnell Wright, who the Bears picked with the first round pick they received in the Bryce Young draft, is one of the best right tackles in the league. Jonah Jackson and Joe Thuney are an elite guard duo, while Braxton Jones will retake his starting left tackle spot that he vacated due to injury last year. The one exception is at center. Last year, Drew Dalman earned a Pro Bowl spot for his elite play at that spot, but he surprisingly retired this past offseason at age 27. They’re replacing him with Garrett Bradbury, a Charlotte native who has just been a serviceable center to this point in his career. On the other side of the line is a Panthers front that has struggled to generate pressure for several seasons now. They ranked 24th in pass rush win rate last season, so they went out and spent big money on Jaelan Phillips to try to rectify that. He’ll have his hands full trying to make an impact against such a formidable tackle duo, so the real difference maker here might have to be Derrick Brown. He had a career high five sacks last season, and he’s the best interior presence the Panthers have. He’ll probably spend most of his time against the guards, but he should get some pass rush opportunities over Bradbury, who projects to be the weak point on this offensive line. He and rookie Lee Hunter on early downs will need to make some noise to mitigate the advantage the Bears offense has in the trenches. Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker vs the Bears secondary The Bears overcame a brutal defense to make the playoffs last season, so they devoted their offseason to revamping that group. The biggest overhaul came in the secondary, but their big signing, cornerback Coby Bryant, is already out for the season with a knee injury. That leaves the Bears relying on Tyrique Stevenson (of Commanders Hail Mary fame) as their number two corner, which is exactly what they were trying to avoid by signing Bryant. Starting nickel Kyler Gordon is also out, leaving the Bears to rely on Cam Lewis to start in that spot. Their new starting safety duo is rookie Dillon Thieneman and veteran Xavier Woods, who Panthers fans should be familiar with. Jaylon Johnson is very good, so he’ll give problems to whoever is lined up across from him. Any other receiver on the field should be expected to have success. The unit has a reputation for catastrophic breakdowns in coverage, which should open up big play opportunities for McMillan and Coker. They need to capitalize on those opportunities and find the space provided to them, and quarterback Bryce Young needs to find those breakdowns in coverage and make some throws down the field. Bryce Young vs Week 1 This will be Young’s fourth Week 1. In his first three, he completed 49.5% of his passes for 4.4 yards per attempt (153.7 yards per game) with two touchdowns and six interceptions. It’s been nothing but bad. He’s entering a make or break year as it pertains to his future in Carolina. He can’t afford to start off so poorly once again.

summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA--OCTOBER 27: Linebacker Sam Mills #51 of the Carolina Panthers follows the action against the Philadelphia Eagles in the game between the Carolina Panthers vs Philadelphia Eagles on October 27, 1996 at Veterans Stadium in Philadelphia Pennsylvania. (Photo by Al Pereira/Michael Ochs Archives) | Getty Images Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #3. Sam Mills “When I found out I had cancer, there were two things I could do: quit or Keep Pounding. I’m a fighter. I kept pounding. You’re fighters, too. Keep Pounding! On offense. On defense. On special teams. On every. Single. Play. Keep pounding!” On January 2, 2004, Sam Mills unknowingly created the mantra for the Carolina Panthers franchise. He was a cancer riddled linebackers coach, uncharacteristically speaking to the whole team the day before a home playoff game against the Dallas Cowboys. But let’s back up first and get some perspective. Sam Mills was “the little guy who plays big” long before Steve Smith donned the black and blue. After going undrafted out of Montclair State following the 1981 NFL Draft, Mills signed on with the USFL’s Philadelphia Stars. Standing all of 5’9” and 230 pounds, played three years in the USFL before getting the chance at the NFL with the New Orleans Saints in 1986. He won one of the starting inside linebacker jobs in his first year with the team and wouldn’t relinquish that role for the next nine seasons, becoming a mainstay in the infamous Dome Patrol defense. During his Saints tenure, he earned four Pro Bowls and two Second Team All-Pro selections. In 1995, the expansion Carolina Panthers jumped at the chance to sign the Field Mouse after he was released by New Orleans. In Charlotte, Mills really shined. His first year with the Panthers, he made 110 tackles, five interceptions (one returned for a touchdown), 4.5 sacks, five forced fumbles, and four fumbles recovered. Mills was so good, he finished tied for third in the Defensive Player of the Year voting that year. He continued his dominance in 1996, earning another Pro Bowl nod, his first First Team All-Pro selection, and again finishing in the top five for DPOY. 1997 became his final NFL season, retiring after a solid but unremarkable statistical year that saw a huge drop in splash plays. His ties to Carolina, however, would stay strong as he joined the coaching staff as a defensive assistant for the 1998 season. He continued coaching the defense, particularly the linebackers, for the Panthers until a few months before his death in April of 2005. During the 2003 season, Mills was diagnosed with intestinal cancer. Regardless, he kept coaching, kept showing up every day. He didn’t miss a single game, scheduling his chemotherapy and radiation treatments around team activities. To make sure he could still be present for the team, Mills moved from the sideline to the coaches box on game days, still managing to attend one or two practices each week. The Panthers finished the season 11-5, drawing inspiration from Mills. From player accounts, Mills would still run sprints before practice despite the grueling treatment. He was never one to complain and never one to make grand speeches. So when he spoke up on that January day, the less than 100 people present listened intently. The Panthers went on to pummel the Cowboys 29-10. Then they beat the Rams on the road 29-23 in double overtime in a game they weren’t supposed to be competitive in. Then they beat the Eagles on the road 14-3 in a dominant performance by the defense. No matter the expectations, no matter the odds, no matter the opponent, Mills and his Panthers kept pounding. Mills lost his battle with cancer in 2005, earning a posthumous enshrinement in the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2022. While his time with the Panthers was brief, he achieved elite highs both personally and with the team. He starred in the franchise’s first NFC Championship Game and coached in the team’s first Super Bowl appearance. The undersized linebacker out of some no-name college in New Jersey changed the game for so many. So while the rival Saints can also lay claim to the beloved man, his dedication to the game of football and the Carolina Panthers specifically more than earned him this spot in our countdown.

title: Can the 2026 Bears Measure Up to the Greatest Scoring Offense of All-Time?
summary: With the start of the 2026 NFL season upon us, it’s time to set the stage for a project spanning the entirety of the season. That’s right, folks – I’m back to Benchmark Da Bears once again! Each week, I’ll be taking a look at Chicago’s offensive playmakers, tracking their production, and comparing their statistical […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - DECEMBER 12: Peyton Manning #18 of the Denver Broncos prepares for their game against the San Diego Chargers at Sports Authority Field at Mile High on December 12, 2013 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the start of the 2026 NFL season upon us, it’s time to set the stage for a project spanning the entirety of the season. That’s right, folks – I’m back to Benchmark Da Bears once again! Each week, I’ll be taking a look at Chicago’s offensive playmakers, tracking their production, and comparing their statistical output against a comparable player from Ben Johnson’s past. New this year, however, is the introduction of some additional milestones that hold historical significance either to the Bears franchise or even to the league as a whole. Both Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams have expressed a desire to field the most productive offense of all-time, so we’ll naturally have to keep one eye on the 2013 Denver Broncos (led by Bears legends John Fox and Adam Gase), who hold that distinction, having scored an average of 37.9 points per game. But without further ado, it’s time to name our players and the comps that have set the standard we will hold them to throughout the 2026 NFL season: Quarterback Caleb Williams , 3rd NFL season Comp Player: 2022 Jared Goff (Detroit Lions) Goff’s 2022 Statline: Games Starts Completions Pass Attempts Completion % Pass Yards Pass TDs INTs Pass Y/A Pass Y/G Pass Rating Sacks Rush Attempts Rush Yards Rush TDs Rush Y/A Rush Y/G QBR Fumbles Awards 17 17 382 587 65.1% 4438 29 7 7.6 261.1 99.3 23 29 73 0 2.5 4.3 63.3 7 Pro Bowl We’re starting off with a repeat, but truthfully, Caleb Williams is simply a player who is difficult to compare. Couple that with limited candidates (really just Goff and Caleb himself) and we’re left to select Goff’s first year under Ben Johnson’s direction once again. That said, Caleb is a very different quarterback than Goff, and these statistical benchmarks will serve as more of a measuring stick than the more literal comparisons we will find among some of the following players. Milestones: 4,000 passing yards; 29 passing TDs (franchise record – Kramer); 5,477 passing yards (2013 Peyton Manning); 55 passing TDs (2013 Peyton Manning) Running Backs D’Andre Swift , 7th NFL season Comp Player: 2025 D’Andre Swift (Chicago Bears) Swift’s 2025 Statline: Games Starts Rush Attempts Rush Yards Rush TDs Rush Y/A Rush Y/G Targets Receptions Rec Yards Rec Y/R Rec TDs R/G Rec Y/G Fumbles Awards 16 16 223 1087 9 4.9 67.9 48 34 299 8.8 1 2.1 18.7 2 – Kyle Monangai , 2nd NFL season Comp Player: 2024 David Montgomery (Detroit Lions) Montgomery’s 2024 Statline: Games Starts Rush Attempts Rush Yards Rush TDs Rush Y/A Rush Y/G Targets Receptions Rec Yards Rec Y/R Rec TDs R/G Rec Y/G Fumbles Awards 14 14 185 775 12 4.2 55.4 38 36 341 9.5 0 2.6 24.4 2 – While it was tempting to go with a “Sonic & Knuckles” duo for comparison here, Swift is too unlike Gibbs for that particular comp. Instead, I’ve chosen to compare Swift to his own performance from last season, which was arguably the best of his career to this point. Monangai, in his second season, should be expected to elevate his game and with that in mind, the Montgomery comparison feels apt as the more powerful runner in Johnson’s two-headed backfield. Note: franchise records are likely out of reach at this position for obvious reasons Milestones: 1,597 combined rushing yards (2013 Broncos RBs); 15 combined rushing TDs (2013 Broncos RBs) Tight Ends Colston Loveland , 2nd NFL season Comp Player: 2023 Sam LaPorta (Detroit Lions) LaPorta’s 2023 Statline: Games Starts Targets Receptions Rec Yards Rec Y/R Rec TDs R/G Rec Y/G Fumbles Awards 17 14 120 86 889 10.3 10 5.1 52.3 – Pro Bowl Cole Kmet , 7th NFL season Comp Player: 2021 T.J. Hockenson (Detroit Lions) Hockenson’s 2021 Statline: Games Starts Targets Receptions Rec Yards Rec Y/R Rec TDs R/G Rec Y/G Fumbles Awards 12 12 84 61 583 9.6 4 5.1 48.6 0 – I know some will wonder about the absence of rookie Sam Roush, but ultimately, I think it will take some time for him to grow into his role. Even then, there is a ceiling on his production with all of the mouths to feed in this offense. As far as Loveland and Kmet go, the comps here are extremely familiar as they are the same as last year’s. Loveland’s ascension in the latter part of the 2025 season should align him more closely with LaPorta’s fabled rookie season in 2026. Kmet (like all of the 2025 Bears TEs) had extremely limited production to start the year, but Hockenson is still a closer comp than most Johnson-coached products, even if this was during Johnson’s stint as the Lions’ TEs Coach. Milestones: 1,076 receiving yards (franchise record for TE – Ditka); 12 receiving TDs (franchise record for TE – Ditka); 90 receptions (franchise record for TE – Bennett); 14 combined receiving TDs (2013 Broncos TEs) Wide Receivers Rome Odunze , 3rd NFL season Comp Player: 2024 Jameson Williams (Detroit Lions) Williams’ 2024 Statline: Games Starts Targets Receptions Rec Yards Rec Y/R Rec TDs R/G Rec Y/G Fumbles Awards 15 11 91 58 1001 17.3 7 3.9 66.7 0 – Luther Burden , 2nd NFL season Comp Player: 2022 Amon-Ra St. Brown (Detroit Lions) St. Brown’s 2022 Statline: Games Starts Targets Receptions Rec Yards Rec Y/R Rec TDs R/G Rec Y/G Fumbles Awards 16 16 146 106 1161 11.0 6 6.6 72.6 0 Pro Bowl Kalif Raymond , 10th NFL season Comp Player: 2022 Kalif Raymond (Detroit Lions) Raymond’s 2022 Statline: Games Starts Targets Receptions Rec Yards Rec Y/R Rec TDs R/G Rec Y/G Fumbles Awards 17 7 64 47 616 13.1 0 2.8 36.2 3 – Zavion Thomas , Rookie season Comp Player: 2025 Luther Burden (Chicago Bears) Burden’s 2025 Statline: Games Starts Targets Receptions Rec Yards Rec Y/R Rec TDs R/G Rec Y/G Fumbles Awards 15 5 60 47 652 13.9 2 3.1 43.5 0 – I feel that you can make a strong case that this position group is simultaneously the most exciting and puzzling of the four. We largely know what to expect from the players I’ve covered above (albeit with varying levels of untapped potential), but the receivers on the 2026 Chicago Bears seem to be a group that many have opinions ALL across the board on. As far as comp players go, I see Rome Odunze lining up similarly to Jameson Williams’ primary deep threat role, while Luther Burden is set to take on the YAC production responsibility of a young Amon-Ra St. Brown. Kalif Raymond is compared to a past version of himself, but one that held a greater role in the Lions’ offense than in his most recent seasons. Finally, Zavion Thomas is hard to pin down, but Luther Burden’s output from last season seems a fitting measuring stick for another incoming rookie who will need to play himself into offensive snaps. Milestones: 1,430 receiving yards (2013 Demaryius Thomas); 14 receiving TDs (2013 Demaryius Thomas); 1,508 receiving yards (franchise record – Marshall); 13 receiving TDs (franchise record – Gordon, Kavanaugh); 38 combined receiving TDs (2013 Broncos WRs) It’s clear that this team will need these players to have some outstanding seasons in order for the Bears to experience success similar to what they found in 2025. To achieve the legendary status that Johnson and Williams have their eyes set on? That may take more than a couple of leaps. Still, a wise man once said, “the ceiling… is the roof,” and I’m hoping to see this team exceed all of our expectations.

summary: Heading into week one, it’s a good time to look at the first power rankings of the season. The Chicago Bears have real expectations this season. full_text: NASHVILLE, TN - AUGUST 29: Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson watches a replay on the video board during a preseason game between the Tennessee Titans and Chicago Bears, August 29, 2026 at Nissan Stadium in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Matthew Maxey/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Heading into week one, it’s a good time to look at the first power rankings of the season. The Chicago Bears have real expectations this season. Building on year one of Ben Johnson and a strong year two from Caleb Williams, the Bears face pressure for the first time in years. Sustained success has eluded this franchise for a long time. And now there is actual hype. About Chicago’s offense. And quarterback. And coach. It’s a new era. How are the Bears ranked in the first “official” rankings of the 2026 season? Sure, there have been periodic offseason lists, but now is when it starts to matter. At least to people who believe in power rankings, which is never you. That’s right, I see you in the comments. Telling me you don’t read power rankings. The number in the parentheses is the team’s previous ranking, where available. NFL.com – Nick Shook 11. Chicago Bears (10) I have questions about the Bears’ young receiving corps, though I am much more concerned about their pieced-together secondary following some terrible injury luck early in camp. I can be convinced this isn’t a massive issue if Chicago limits Bryce Young and Kyler Murray in the first two weeks of the season. PFT – Mike Florio Bears (No. 6; 0-0): Forty-one years after the pinnacle of the 46 defense, can they do enough on that side of the ball? The Athletic – Chad Graff and Josh Kendall 10. Chicago Bears Last ranking: 12 Mock’s projected win total: 9.5 There are questions on defense about the pass rush and depth on the back end after Coby Bryant’s injury. But Caleb Williams is promising, and Ben Johnson seems like the real deal, so how far can the offense carry this team? If Dennis Allen can manufacture some pressure, this could be a really good team. CBS Sports – Pete Prisco 15. Chicago Bears (10) Their offense will score a lot of points. But the defensive questions might mandate that. They aren’t good enough on that side of the ball. USA Today – Nate Davis 5. Chicago Bears (5): “I want to have the highest-scoring offense ever, which happens to be the 2013 Denver Broncos,” HC Ben Johnson told The Athletic last month. That Peyton Manning-led Denver squad scored 37.9 points per game, roughly 50% more than the 2025 Bears, before it managed eight in a humiliating Super Bowl 48 loss. Eye on the ball coach, maybe not the record book? Yahoo Sports – Frank Schwab 11. Chicago Bears (LW: 11) Ben Johnson has stated he wants to field the highest scoring offense in NFL history. That mark was set by the 2013 Broncos, who averaged 37.9 points. That would be a massive leap from the 25.9 points per game the Bears scored last season. There’s nothing wrong with lofty goals, and if Caleb Williams makes the leap to being an MVP candidate, Chicago could at least make a run at the highest scoring offense in the NFL this season. PFF – Bradley Locker 15. Chicago Bears Odds to make playoffs: 46% Odds to win Super Bowl: 3% Ben Johnson’s first season in Chicago couldn’t have gone much better, with the Bears making the NFC divisional and securing their first NFC North title since 2018. Caleb Williams’ upward ascension — paired with Johnson’s play-calling, burgeoning stars in the skill-position group and a strong offensive line — should make the team’s offense dynamic yet again. However, Chicago’s defense is suspect given a lackluster defensive line and impactful injuries in the secondary. With a lot of variation in these rankings, what do you think? Are the Bears overrated or underrated heading into week one? Which writers are haters and which are glazers?

title: What Drake Maye’s rough Week 1 reminds us about Caleb Williams and the Bears
summary: Yikes. While I did accurately predict the Patriots would play the Seahawks way more competitively than they did in the Super Bowl, I didn’t have them outright blowing their chance at a tone-setting Week 1 win the way they did. Especially not the way they did it. Because you don’t necessarily expect Drake Maye, the […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 09: Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots throws a pass against the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter in the game at Lumen Field on September 09, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Yikes. While I did accurately predict the Patriots would play the Seahawks way more competitively than they did in the Super Bowl, I didn’t have them outright blowing their chance at a tone-setting Week 1 win the way they did. Especially not the way they did it. Because you don’t necessarily expect Drake Maye, the MVP runner-up from last season, to throw the game away with the Patriots knocking on the door of a game-tying field goal with under a minute to play. But that’s what happened. Maye’s unconscionable interception—his third and final of the contest—was the thing nightmares are made of for a young star quarterback, costing New England the first of its 17 games in the 2026 season. All in all, Wednesday night served arguably the worst season debut Maye could’ve had, especially after a Super Bowl performance that left fans wondering if he was little more than a bum-slayer. While Maye did make some plays against the vaunted Seahawks defense, every one of his three picks broke New England’s back, particularly because the Seahawks didn’t even have starting quarterback Sam Darnold past the second quarter of this game. Now, on the one hand, it’s easy to look at Maye’s season-opening dud, which is eerily reminiscent of last year’s poor performance against the Las Vegas Raiders, and say, “See? That clown has nothing on Caleb Williams.” And you know what? As a Chicago Bears fan, I have no problem making the case that Williams, the No. 1 pick of the 2024 NFL draft and Bears starting quarterback, was the right pick for the Bears last year regardless of anything Maye did last season. Plus, as anyone who watches him knows, Williams has nowhere near the penchant for turnovers that Maye has. Even coming out of college, Maye, while highly talented, possesses a Josh Allen-esque brain worm gene that Williams hasn’t shown symptoms of. But while it’s tempting to gloat about Maye’s Week 1 stinker, I would actually caution Bears fans to show some restraint. Because you never know when Williams might have his own game like that. Progress is not a linear equation. Screwing up like Maye did last night can also help a player get better (provided he doesn’t make the same mistakes again—something Williams is good about). Just because these guys are in Year 3 doesn’t mean they have everything figured out, especially in Week 1. (Though I’d like to point out the number of Bears fans who were highly correct in their Week 1 Year 3 assessments about Mitchell Trubisky and Justin Fields in their “prove-it” years.) Williams is not in “prove-it” mode in the same way. He’s won a playoff game and delivered more than enough times in moments that mattered to cement himself as “The Guy” for the Bears past this season. Unless he’s absolutely horrid in 2026, he’s going to get that $60 million-a-year contract extension next offseason. And we should expect him to have taken a step forward by the time his third season wraps. But there’s probably going to be a week where he struggles. Where he turns the ball over multiple times. Where he struggles to complete more than 50% of his throws. Because even for the best quarterbacks in the league and of all time, season-long perfection is not possible. When that happens, let’s not act like the world is ending. Criticize where it’s required (especially if Williams throws that stupid of a game-losing pick), and then look for improvement the next week. Games like yesterday remind us of why Williams, not Maye, went No. 1 overall in 2024 and why he’s likely to be better. But he’ll still stumble from time to time. Let’s just hope it’s not this Week 1—or when the game is on the line.

title: Week 1 Game Preview: Stats, Matchups for Chicago Bears-Carolina Panthers
summary: The season is finally here. All the months of waiting are over, and we finally get to see the Chicago Bears play football. They open the season by traveling down to face the Carolina Panthers in Charlotte. It’s the first of seven teams they face that made the playoffs last season. While Chicago goes in […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 21: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers throws a pass against the Jacksonville Jaguars during the first half at EverBank Field on August 21, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The season is finally here. All the months of waiting are over, and we finally get to see the Chicago Bears play football. They open the season by traveling down to face the Carolina Panthers in Charlotte. It’s the first of seven teams they face that made the playoffs last season. While Chicago goes in as the favorites, this is hardly a gimme. The Bears have real expectations in their second year under Ben Johnson. Caleb Williams faces enormous pressure to build on the spectacular plays he made last season. Chicago has spent decades going up-and-down, with short spurts of winning, followed by a lot of mediocrity and plenty more losing. The expectation with Johnson and Williams is sustained success. But Carolina is trying to build their way back to relevancy, too. Young had a much-improved third season, but questions remain about his status as a long-term solution at QB. Head coach Dave Canales led the Panthers to the postseason, but the team had a losing record in the worst division in the league. Let’s dive into this matchup. Carolina Panthers SB Nation site: Cat Scratch Reader Record: 0-0 (8-9 in 2025, first in NFC South) Game day, time, TV: Sunday, noon, FOX Spread: The Bears are favored by 3 points Bears all-time record against: 9-4, including 0-1 postseason Historical meetings: This is the earliest the teams have met in a season since week two of 2008. The Bears traveled to Charlotte to meet the 1-0 Panthers. Chicago struck first, taking a 10-3 halftime lead by way of Brandon Lloyd recovering a blocked punt and a Roobie Gould field goal. In the third quarter, Jason McKie added a 1-yard TD. But in the fourth, the Panthers got going, and Jonathan Stewart scored twice. The first came after Greg Olsen fumbled. The second was set up by a 23-yard catch by current Bears assistant general manager Jeff King. The Panthers won 20-17. Last meeting: Week 5 during the 2024 season. The 2-2 Bears and 1-3 Panthers met at Soldier Field. Rookie Caleb Williams showed out against Carolina, leading touchdown drives on four of their six first-half possessions. He threw two TDs to DJ Moore. DeAndre Swift and Roschon Johnson both scored, too. The Panthers, meanwhile, turned the ball over on a fumble, downs and missed a field goal in the first half. In the third Andy Dalton was picked off by Kevin Byard. And while they managed to get a field goal later in the third quarter, the damage was done. Following Johnson’s second 1-yard touchdown of the game, making the score 36-10, the Panthers turned the offense back over to Bryce Young. Injury report: The Panthers had three players on their Wednesday report. Limited participation RB Jonathon Brooks (groin) DT Bobby Brown III (back) Did not participate OLB Patrick Jones II (back) Offense: The Panthers finished last season ranked 27th on offense in points and yards. Their passing offense finished 26th, and their rushing offense finished 19th. Bryce Young (63.6 pct. cmp./3,011 yds./23 TD/11 INT ) finished last season with respectable numbers and finally showed flashes of the talent that made him a first-overall pick. But he’s far from dominating or answering questions about his long-term status as a franchise quarterback. Last year’s Offensive Rookie of the Year, Tetairoa McMillan (70 rec./1,014 yds./7 TD) is the number one weapon for the Panthers’ offense. Xavier Leggette (35/363/3), Jalen Coker (33/394/3) and Jimmy Horn Jr. (11/108/0) round out the receiving corps. They’ve added Young’s college teammate John Metchie III (73/686/3 in his career) this offseason. TEs Tommy Tremble (27/249/2), Ja’Tavion Sanders (29/190/1) and Mitchell Evans (19/171/2) also get involved. Chubba Hubbard (134/511/1) is relied on to be a big part of the offense. Hubbard (30/223/3) was fifth on the team in receptions. The Panthers are expected to have former second-round pick Jonathon Brooks back from a torn ACL. They also signed AJ Dillon. Defense: The Panthers defense finished 2025 ranked 15th in points allowed and 16th in yards allowed. The passing defense ranked 26th, and the rushing defense ranked 20th. Cornerbacks Mike Jackson (68 tkls/19 PD/4 INT/1 FF/4 TFL) and Jaycee Horn (37 tkls/8 PD/5 INT) are problems for opposing receivers. Jackson led the league in pass breakups. Safeties Nick Scott (111 tkls/3 PD/1 INT) and Tre’von Moehrig (103 tkls/14 TFL/3 sk/2 PD/1 INT) also make a lot of plays. Up front, DT Derrick Brown (5 sk/5 TFL/7 PD/1 FF) led the way in pass rush. The Panthers added Texas Tech DT Lee Hunter in the draft to add another weapon. But Carolina lost their second-most sacks from 2025 with Nic Scrouton going out with an ACL in camp. And A’Shawn Robinson, D.J. Wonnum and Christian Rozeboom all moved on in free agency. However, they also added LBs Jaelan Phillips (28 career sacks; 73 QB pressures in 2025) and Devin Lloyd (5 INT/81 TKL and a Pro-Bowl nod in 2025). Key matchups: The Bears should have some advantages on the Panthers, but week one is always tricky. The Panthers have a strong ground game, but have been battling offensive line injuries throughout the summer. It’s tough to say Chicago can win a battle on the defensive line side, but I think that’s the case. And the Panthers added to the LBs in the offseason, but don’t have a ton of depth. Derrick Brown, Jalen Phillips and Devin Lloyd are the stars, but after them there is solid production but nothing eye-popping. If Chicago can win in the trenches on both sides, it will go a long way in this game. On the boundaries, Bears receivers will be facing one of the better corner duos in the league with Horn and Jackson. Key stats Bryce Young and Caleb Williams each had six game-winning drives in 2025 Williams was credited with six comebacks in 2025, while Young wasn’t far behind, with four. The Panthers were in 10 one-score games last season and went 7-3 in those games. Young is 14-11 against the spread at home. Last season, he was 6-2 as a home underdog ATS.

summary: Ja’Marr Chase, the Cincinnati Bengals’ superstar wide receiver, has a new podcast called “Chasing No. 1,” starring himself and viral NFL social media influencer Annie Agar. For their debut show, they had none other than Joe Burrow, Bengals quarterback and Chase’s best friend. Burrow didn’t hold back while on the show about how he felt […]
full_text: Feb 25, 2024; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Cincinnati Bengals players Ja'Marr Chase (left) and Joe Burrow sit court side of the Phoenix Suns game against the Los Angeles Lakers at Footprint Center. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con Ja’Marr Chase, the Cincinnati Bengals’ superstar wide receiver, has a new podcast called “Chasing No. 1,” starring himself and viral NFL social media influencer Annie Agar. For their debut show, they had none other than Joe Burrow, Bengals quarterback and Chase’s best friend. Burrow didn’t hold back while on the show about how he felt about the Bengals’ 2026 season. “I just want to win this year,” he said. “I just want to win. The rest will take care of itself. I think we’ll break a bunch of records eventually, but I think we’re going to have a really good team that has a chance to win every game that we step foot on the field for. I don’t know about you, but I could really feel it in my bones, in my soul, in OTA’s this year — different from years past.” While the offense managed to keep everyone together, the defense added Dexter Lawrence II, Jonathan Allen, Boye Mafe and Bryan Cook. The deep and talented defensive line has shifted from a weakness to a potential strength, which could have a trickle-down effect that benefits even the safeties. Burrow knows the additions of the veteran defenders have increased the odds the Bengals have of going deep in the playoffs for the first time since 2023. “We brought in a lot of the right guys, a lot of the right people with the right mindsets to go and chase this goal of winning a Super Bowl and winning as many games as we can and being the best possible team that we can,” he continued. “I felt it from our D-line. I felt it from our defense. Our offense has the same guys in years past… but these veteran guys that we brought in on defense to be able to help our younger guys.” Hopefully he’s right. If the Bengals’ offense can stay healthy and play like they’re capable, and if the defense is just good—not great, but good—there aren’t many teams that could stand between them and the Lombardi Trophy.

title: Cost and complexity of how to watch the Bengals in the 2026 NFL season
summary: The ease of being able to watch your favorite NFL team each week has gotten to a breaking point for most fans. As the NFL has been able to sell off streaming rights for packages of games rather than as a whole to one company, you likely will need several subscriptions if you have cut […]
full_text: Bengals fans cheer on a home win after the fourth quarter of the NFL Week 12 game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Pittsburgh Steelers at Paul Brown Stadium in downtown Cincinnati on Sunday, Nov. 28, 2021. The Bengals beat the Steelers 41-10. Pittsburgh Steelers At Cincinnati Bengals | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The ease of being able to watch your favorite NFL team each week has gotten to a breaking point for most fans. As the NFL has been able to sell off streaming rights for packages of games rather than as a whole to one company, you likely will need several subscriptions if you have cut the cord. We are about to look at the real cost of being able to watch all 17 regular season games, and the reality of what watching the NFL in 2026 has become. Luckily, the Bengals aren’t as bad off as some teams that have to have Netflix. Below is The Athletic’s schedule along with what network will be airing the game. Cable or Satellite We are getting to the point that cord-cutting is getting as — if not more — expensive than the alternative of traditional cable or satellite TV. You could also potentially find an indoor antenna to potentially get games that way, but it also requires you to be in-market. NFL Sunday Ticket and NFL RedZone For out-of-market fans looking for a legitimate way to watch games, NFL Sunday Ticket on YouTube TV, or bought through your YouTube profile, will cover games outside prime-time slots. NFL RedZone tries to follow the most exciting action. Typically following games that are close to scoring or have a drastic turn. You do not have control over what you watch, so it isn’t ideal for watching specifically Cincinnati. This can also be found on NFL+ Premium (that can be bundled with ESPN Unlimited). Online Stream options for the TV games We are talking CBS (Paramount+), Fox (Fox One), ABC/ESPN (ESPN Unlimited), and NBC (Peacock). It may also be worth adding NFL Network here since they fall under the Disney umbrella now. With ESPN, you can get the Madrid game in Week 9 on ESPN Unlimited, NFL+ Premium, or regular NFL+ (both are mobile only). Depending on your cable package, all of these games should be available with the exception of maybe NFL Network. It is very important to note that all of these apps that stream afternoon games are in-market games ONLY. Prime Video Surprisingly, one of the easiest and most accessible streaming options. You just need Amazon Prime, which will give you access to Prime Video. You could also watch free on Twitch with a registered account. Unfortunately, this only covers the New Year’s Eve game against the Ravens in Week 17. Grand Total In-market fans: Basic Cable ~$30 (CBS, FOX, and NBC), Prime Video ~$15, NFL+ (mobile only) ~$7, and ESPN Unlimited (because the Bengals Week 11 Monday Night Football game is exclusive to ESPN and not simulcast on ABC) ~$30 Total a month: ~$82 or ~$67 (if you are willing to watch the Prime Video game on Twitch). You could also cut out cable costs entirely for an antenna, but you are risking quality and video dropping. You aren’t saving by streaming with Paramount+ ~$9, Peacock ~$13 (their base plan does not include live sports) and FOX One ~$20 totaling to ~$42 a month. Peacock and Paramount+ at least also let you have shows and movies for the ~$12 more Out-of-market fans: For new users, NFL Sunday Ticket is $30 a month ($60 a month for existing), Prime Video is ~$15 a month, NFL+ (mobile only) ~$7 a month, and ESPN Unlimited ~$30 a month Total a month: $82 for new Sunday Ticket users or $112 for existing (because you get punished for loyalty) As a reminder, you wouldn’t even have the choice of streaming the big three channels as out-of-market fans. That ~$42 a month would easily clear and be a much better deal than the ~$60 for returning customers. This is trying to map out the cheapest way for fans to enjoy all the Bengals’ games from at least the comfort of their own home. You can also account for maybe only getting subscriptions like NFL+ or ESPN Unlimited for just the month Cincinnati plays their game, but you have to remember to cancel those subscriptions. That also means you won’t be watching most Monday Night Football or international games, though. We are all just going to have to start finding people nearby to watch Bengals games with just to split the cost of watching the games. I at least hope this helps some of you plan out how you will be watching some of these games.

title: Browns’ ceiling for the 2026 season
summary: While there are reasons to be optimistic about the Cleveland Browns heading into the 2026 season, they still have a realistic ceiling on what they can accomplish. The Browns went 5-12 last season largely due to struggles on offense. The team enters this season with plenty of changes, from a new coaching staff and revamped […]
full_text: While there are reasons to be optimistic about the Cleveland Browns heading into the 2026 season, they still have a realistic ceiling on what they can accomplish. The Browns went 5-12 last season largely due to struggles on offense. The team enters this season with plenty of changes, from a new coaching staff and revamped offensive line to the departure of Myles Garrett and the return of Deshaun Watson . Given all of this, what is a realistic ceiling for the team this season? Most projections and betting lines have Cleveland finishing with 4-5 wins, but if things go right, they can certainly outpace that. The Browns have the easiest strength of schedule in 2026 by many metrics. So while there are many questions about the Browns’ offense, many of their opponents have issues on either side of the ball as well. Opponents like the Las Vegas Raiders, New York Jets, New York Giants, and Indianapolis Colts all have similar questions about their quarterbacks, which allows Cleveland to sneak in some wins. The AFC North is always a competitive division, but even in some of the Browns’ toughest seasons, they have managed to squeak out a few division wins. Given all of these possibilities, it is not out of the question for Cleveland to reach nine wins this season. This best-case scenario could have them in the playoff conversation late into the season, which would be a welcome result for Browns fans. title: Browns HC Todd Monken doing the unpopular won’t matter if results are better
summary: When Cleveland Browns HC Todd Monken announced who would be their Week 1 starter when the team opens up on the road against the Jacksonville Jaguars, fans were unhappy. It’s not quarterback Shedeur Sanders; it was Deshaun Watson. The reaction was mainly negative, but head coach Monken went with the decision that most would deem […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 27: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns warms up prior to a preseason game against the New England Patriots at Huntington Bank Field on August 27, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images When Cleveland Browns HC Todd Monken announced who would be their Week 1 starter when the team opens up on the road against the Jacksonville Jaguars, fans were unhappy . It’s not quarterback Shedeur Sanders; it was Deshaun Watson. The reaction was mainly negative, but head coach Monken went with the decision that most would deem unpopular. It’s clear that the Cleveland Browns are not expecting to contend for the playoffs this season . If they do, all the better. The roster has young talent but is mainly inexperienced, and a head coach who has no NFL head coaching experience prior to being hired in Cleveland. Fans will want Monken fired and type mean things on the internet, but at the same time Monken, who is viewing this opportunity as a last chance to be a head coach, is going with the veteran instead of the second-year player. Watson, who hasn’t played well since being traded to Cleveland, blasted the fans on Saturday but later apologized for what he said. Monken talked about what went into the decision. Browns coach Todd Monken explains his decision to name Deshaun Watson the starting quarterback: Monken said he took in the “full body of work … ultimately felt like … Deshaun gave us the best chance to move the ball, score points.” pic.twitter.com/VWmwjhxOuw — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) August 24, 2026 Instead of making the decision based on one preseason game and the post-game press conference, Monken stuck to the full body of work. The reports throughout OTA’s and throughout training camp would be either Sanders or Watson was the better quarterback. Monken tipped his hand about who was the starter when the team had their joint practice with the Buffalo Bills. Regardless of how the preseason game went, the starter was already determined beforehand. Monken wasn’t willing to start Sanders because Sanders didn’t give him a legitimate reason to start him. It’s easier for Monken to start Sanders because of these specific things: Sanders is younger and has more upside Fans prefer Sanders over Watson (or anyone over Watson) Some fans believe that Sanders is the future (while others don’t) It’s rare for an organization to listen to its fanbase because if they did, those people in the organization would be out of a job. It wasn’t a decision made by owner Jimmy Haslam to start Watson; it was a decision made by the person who is on the practice field and in the offensive meetings every day. The last thing Monken needed to do was make an emotional decision and lose the locker room before the opening game. It was the unpopular decision, but it was the tough decision Monken had to make. Now, the results on the field will decide whether he made a proper decision. What has to happen for you to think Monken’s decision to start Watson was a good idea? Join the conversation! title: 3 keys for the Browns to defeat the Jaguars in Week 1
summary: The Cleveland Browns are set to open their Week 1 contest on the road against the Jacksonville Jaguars. A lot of time and effort has been put into this roster ever since Todd Monken was hired as the new head coach. There are many exciting aspects from last year, and as with every team, there […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - DECEMBER 28: Denzel Ward #21 and Mason Graham #94 of the Cleveland Browns react after their win against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Huntington Bank Field on December 28, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio. The Cleveland Browns defeated the Pittsburgh Steelers 13-6. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns are set to open their Week 1 contest on the road against the Jacksonville Jaguars. A lot of time and effort has been put into this roster ever since Todd Monken was hired as the new head coach . There are many exciting aspects from last year, and as with every team, there remain some concerns. Mostly with this year’s version, Cleveland will start off their first game with five new offensive linemen. In the history of the NFL, has that ever happened before? The offensive line must be a cohesive unit of five men instead of five individuals. RELATED: WEEK 1 TV MAP And right out of the gate, the Browns must face the Jaguars. This year, Cleveland wants to run the ball effectively. Last year, Jacksonville was ranked #1 against the run. Let’s look at three things the Browns must accomplish to defeat the Jaguars. Will this year’s defense continue to dominate? Cleveland had one of the best defenses in the league last season, but that was under defensive guru Jim Schwartz, who is no longer with the franchise. Monken stated early on that the team would follow Schwartz’s scheme. Monken stated seven months ago: “First off, my anticipation is we’re not going to change the system. Very difficult to go against. They can be rest assured that we’re going to keep the same system.” Which the Browns will need. Jacksonville has a very good offense and has added some pieces to this group since last year, including rookie draft pick Emmanuel Pregnon, who will start at left guard. The franchise also drafted two tight ends and two receivers. Their offense ranked #11 in 2025, averaging 337.4 yards a game on that side of the ball and scoring 55 touchdowns. The key for the defense is to stop the passing attack. Last year, this group averaged 222.3 yards a game passing and threw on any down regardless of down-and-distance. Throwing on first down was a regular occurrence for this offense, which shows confidence. If the Browns defense can throttle their aerial game, it will force them to run more. This was the Jags’ Achilles heel last year as they ranked in the bottom third in rushing and averaged 115.1 yards a game on the ground. Add the fact that their bell-cow running back, Travis Etienne, is no longer on the roster, and their starter this year was a fourth-round draft pick in 2025 who has zero NFL starts. This defense needs to be stout in the defensive backfield because Jacksonville and QB Trevor Lawrence are going to air it out. The Browns will lean on their cornerbacks, Denzel Ward, Tyson Campbell, and Myles Harden, to give but not break and force the Jaguars to run the ball instead. Quick note: The Browns’ defensive backfield has gone 45 consecutive games without giving up 300+ passing yards to an opposing quarterback. The team could reach the all-time record by Week 8 of this season. Keep out Jacksonville’s pass rush Like Cleveland, the Jaguars have a very good pass rush. And it comes from the corners. They generate a decent pass rush with LDE Travon Walker and RDE Josh Hines-Allen coming off the edge. The Browns will depend greatly on the skills of RT Tytus Howard and LT Spencer Fano, a rookie. The Fano vs. Hines-Allen just might determine quite a few things in this ballgame. What is that called? Baptism by fire? Walker is a beast but had an off-year last season with a wrist injury; he just signed a four-year, $110 million extension to keep him in-house. In 2023 and 2024, he had 10.5 sacks in both seasons, with 113 total tackles and 34 QB hits. He knows how to bring the heat and is showing why he was the first overall selection in the 2022 NFL Draft. Hines-Allen has a leaner build and was another first-round draft pick. He was exceptional in college and totaled 61 sacks while at Kentucky in a tough conference. As a senior, he was named the “SEC Defensive Player of the Year” and won four awards: the Lott Trophy, Bednarik Award, Nagurski Trophy, and the Jack Lambert Trophy. In the 2023 NFL season, Hines-Allen racked up 17.5 sacks and has 61 for his career. His quickness off the edge and a fast first step are his calling cards. 75 tackles for loss, 150 QB hits, and 239 pressures are why he is such a menace. Can Fano contain Hines-Allen? Stay tuned. Attack the “A” and “B” gaps on Jacksonville’s offense Cleveland must have success up the middle in these four running lanes. Lawrence has a good arm and can’t be allowed to set up and go through his progressions and set up the short passing game. This Browns defense has to have constant pressure on Lawrence every time he drops back to pass. If he is able to set his feet at will, it will become a very long day. He can throw into tight windows when he has time to survey the field, and can throw long. If Lawrence has to move around and consider fleeing the pocket, his attention is diverted from where his receivers and tight end are going. This responsibility will fall squarely on the starting defensive tackles Maliek Collins and Mason Graham, plus their rotational backups Mike Hall and Adin Huntington. Jacksonville’s interior of their offensive line is their weakest point. As mentioned, they are starting rookie Pregnon at left guard, who should be tested over his outside shoulder in order to see if he has the right combination of agility and can maintain anchor. Starting right guard Patrick Mekari missed most of training camp with back issues and finally had back surgery on August 17. The Jaguars placed him on IR with a designation to return. In his place is Ezra Cleveland, who has dealt with an ankle injury during camp. The only healthy interior lineman is center Robert Hainsey, who is entering his sixth NFL season. By placing pressure on the guards who have limited experience, this forces their mental processing to become slower and tend to struggle when they are required to pass off defenders who are on the move rather than blocking a stationary man. Mason Graham = good at football pic.twitter.com/o2B3UlyrO6 https://t.co/zl14HuM8J9 — TWSN (@TWSN___) September 21, 2025 Keeping Lawrence out of his comfort zone will be a huge key to this game with containment. Stunts and twists should be in order. To accomplish this, the DT will take his penetration and crash down on the guard towards the tackle. This will allow an opening for the defensive end to loop around and have a shot at Lawrence for the sack, or at the very least, make his attempt to escape the pocket, which interrupts any passing attempt. And even though Lawrence is a gifted runner, if he comes out of a damaged pocket and then attempts to scramble for yardage, that duty is now handed off to linebackers Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams. Both are dependable tacklers. What do you think the keys to the game are for the Browns versus the Jaguars in Week 1? Join the conversation!
