title: Setting 2026 Browns offensive, defensive expectations
summary: Sunday, September 13th, the 2026 Cleveland Browns will be back on every television screen in Northeast Ohio. The team is entering Year 2 of their rebuild as they will look different on both the offensive and defensive sides of the ball. Head coach Todd Monken is replacing Kevin Stefanski, while the defense will look to […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 22: Head coach Todd Monken of the Cleveland Browns coaches on the sidelines during the first quarter of the preseason game against the Buffalo Bills at Huntington Bank Field on August 22, 2026, in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sunday, September 13th, the 2026 Cleveland Browns will be back on every television screen in Northeast Ohio . The team is entering Year 2 of their rebuild as they will look different on both the offensive and defensive sides of the ball. Head coach Todd Monken is replacing Kevin Stefanski, while the defense will look to find a new alpha after trading away star defensive end Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams, as well as having a new defensive coordinator. A new season brings expectations, but it’s fair to keep those expectations as realistic as possible Offensive Expectations On paper, this unit should be improved from last season. The offensive line was overhauled completely with emphasis on versatility based on the players that the team acquired this offseason. Rookie Spencer Fano, should be the team’s long-awaited answer at left tackle and rookies Parker Brailsford and Austin Barber could contribute earlier than expected. The veteran additions should help right away. The wide receiver room was retooled as rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston add to a room that lacked quality and upside. Scheme-wise, Monken will offer a form of diversity that the team didn’t have last season under Stefanski. Despite all of the improvements, the team still lacks a clear answer at quarterback. The team deciding to start quarterback Deshaun Watson might have been an unpopular decision, considering that Watson hasn’t been available, and when he has, the play hasn’t been close to his days when he was playing for the Houston Texans. Shedeur Sanders might have upside, but it’s fair to question if he has a future with the team. Dillon Gabriel is closer to a backup than a long-term starter. Taylen Green has the athletic traits but is raw as a passer. The quarterback running game will be more of an emphasis due to the uncertainty in the passing game. Make no mistake, the offensive unit has blue chip talent. However, the uncertainty at the quarterback position hampers any realistic expectations for this group. The lack of an adequate passing game will allow teams to load the box while the Browns feel forced to run the ball more until teams respect the passing game. This unit won’t be the best in the league, but they won’t be the worst due to the upside of talent. Defensive Expectations Let’s start with the obvious. Losing a player like Myles Garrett will affect any defense. One of the many reasons why the Browns defense was so dominant was because of Garrett and the gravity he carried. Contrary to some fan belief, Garrett made the players around him better (mainly on the defensive line). On paper, this defense still has the potential to be a top 10 unit. It’s fair to say that the unit won’t be as dominant as last year but still good enough to keep the team in games. Defensive end Jared Verse, who the team acquired in the Garrett trade will not replicate what Garrett did but Verse is a top 15 edge rusher in this league. Defensive tackle Mason Graham showed a ton of promise in the 2nd half of last season and linebacker Carson Schwesinger is primed to build off last season. The secondary has cornerpieces in Denzel Ward and Grant Delpit, while rookie Emmanuel McNeil Warren will add versatility to the room. Losing defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz and replacing him with Mike Rutenberg will be an upgrade in terms of the scheme and versatility, but will come with more uncertainty. Schwartz was good during his time in Cleveland but his scheme lacked creativity and it often times showed whenever he went up against a great offensive mastermind. Overall, the defensive unit will have a drop off of some sort but it won’t be the dropoff that many fans believe will happen. This group has talent with a different scheme in place. The defense won’t be as elite as last year but good enough to be respectable. Overall Expectations Is it wrong to have lower expectations for the 2026 Cleveland Browns than last year? In this case, yes. The roster is better, but because of the uncertainty at the quarterback position and the team rebuilding the expectations are low. It might seem unfair but it’s the reality of the situation. Some fans already have an apathetic view towards the team, but when you are constantly losing, it’s hard to blame them. It’s unfortunate because the team has talent. Starting Watson was an unpopular decision with the fanbase, but it was the right decision to make at the time. The team has something to build on despite outside opinion. At best, this team could win six to eight games. Five is a fair enough projection, but overall this is a team that is likely to be picking in the top five in next year’s NFL Draft and will likely come away with their franchise quarterback. What are your expectations for the offense and defense this year? Join the conversation! title: Malik Nabers will be good test for Cowboys secondary
summary: For the first time since last September when he sustained a season-ending ACL injury, New York Giants wide receiver was a full participant in a game week practice on Wednesday afternoon, and is expected to be good to go for the 2026 season opener against the Dallas Cowboys. Facing a young, talented WR of Nabers […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - NOVEMBER 28: Malik Nabers #1 of the New York Giants makes a reception against the Dallas Cowboys during an NFL football game at AT&T Stadium on November 28, 2024 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the first time since last September when he sustained a season-ending ACL injury, New York Giants wide receiver was a full participant in a game week practice on Wednesday afternoon, and is expected to be good to go for the 2026 season opener against the Dallas Cowboys. Good news: #Giants WR Malik Nabers, returning from a torn ACL, was a full participant in practice today — the team’s first official practice of the 2026 regular season, per HC John Harbaugh. The Giants host the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night. pic.twitter.com/mahl4sZvdT — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) September 9, 2026 Facing a young, talented WR of Nabers caliber will be a good test for Dallas’ revamped secondary; he is someone who’s had quite a bit of success against them in the past. In the three games Nabers has played against the Cowboys in his young career, he is averaging nearly 100 receiving yards per game. As a rookie he caught 12 passes for 115 yards in their first meeting and eight catches for 69 yards in the second. Then in 2025 he caught nine passes for 167 yards and two touchdowns against the Cowboys in Week 2 before his season was cut short to just four games. Now back to playing status, Nabers will be looking to restart his dominance against the Cowboys in Week 1. The question is, will he be able to do so against a secondary that has been revamped in new defensive coordinator Christian Parker’s image? Highly regarded for his ability to develop defensive backs in his young coaching career, the 34-year-old Parker wasted no time rebuilding the Cowboys secondary after replacing Matt Eberflus. He added free agents Jalen Thompson and P.J. Locke to pair with Malik Hooker on the backend, drafted Caleb Downs to play the ever-important nickel/safety position, and signed Cobie Durant to solidify things at CB with DaRon Bland and Shavon Revel. Will it pay off though? From the defensive front to the back end of the secondary, we’ve seen signs of improvement throughout the offseason in organized team activities, training camp practices, and during preseason games from the defense. But, as of yet, we haven’t seen them do it in a meaningful game. That’s going to change when the Cowboys square off against the Giants in Week 1. Things are expected to improve in New York under John Harbaugh’s tutelage as the new head coach, but it’s unlikely they will be a high-powered offensive unit this season. Still, they are talented enough on the offensive side of the ball to give the Cowboys some problems. Especially with Nabers back in the mix. That is where the test comes in for Parker’s new defense and their new scheme.

title: 5 points: The important Cowboys-Giants storylines
summary: Football is back, and so is the five points column. Last year, this article came after the Dallas Cowboys played to break down what went right or wrong, and boy, a lot went wrong last year. I’m sorry if a lot of it came off as complaining. This year will hopefully be different. Instead, this […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - JANUARY 04: Jaxson Dart #6 of the New York Giants is tackled by Donovan Wilson #6 of the Dallas Cowboys during their game at MetLife Stadium on January 04, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images Football is back, and so is the five points column. Last year, this article came after the Dallas Cowboys played to break down what went right or wrong, and boy, a lot went wrong last year. I’m sorry if a lot of it came off as complaining. This year will hopefully be different. Instead, this year it will come before each matchup to help set the table on both sides and highlight the key factors to watch for each week. Some points will be a little more on the nose, while others may be a little more obscure. This will be the 13th season the Cowboys will begin the year with a game against the New York Giants . The Cowboys are 11-1 in the previous 12 games. History would dictate Dallas walking out of MetLife Stadium with a win, but the Giants have overhauled their team the same way the Cowboys have. It should be a game that’s more competitive than people think. Here are five points to watch for on Sunday. First Point: Did Dallas build their wall with sticks or bricks? If you don’t believe in an over-the-hill Odell Beckham Jr., or Jaxson Dart to take the next step as a quarterback, be fearful of what the Giants defensive line can do to the Cowboys offense. Headlined by Brian Burns, Kayvon Thibodeaux, Abdul Carter, and rookie first-round pick Arvell Reese, New York has reimagined a slew of pass rushers that mirror how they won their Super Bowl matchups against the New England Patriots. Dallas’ offensive line is young but growing quickly through continuity. However, Tyler Guyton needs to carry over his offseason bump to the regular season, Terence Steele needs to hold off Broderick Jones, and T.J. Bass has to fill in for All-Pro Tyler Smith for the next month or more. A second-year leap from Carter could be the key to the Giants’ pass rush Sunday night, especially if they move him all over the defense similar to how Micah Parsons played in Dallas. When Carter was on the field, the Giants generated quick pressure on 18.6% of opponent dropbacks , which would have been the second-highest mark of any defense on the season, per NFL Pro. How Dallas neutralizes the Giants’ pass rush will unlock whatever they want to do on offense. They can do that early by establishing the run and limiting the damage on the outside. Second Point: Jaxson Dart prefers his eggs scrambled If you have watched enough Cowboys football over the last decade, you understand the problem that’s plagued the Dallas defense has been the mobile quarterback. Rob Marinelli’s old saying of “keep the quarterback in the well” echoes every time an opposing QB scrambles for seven yards a carry. New York’s second-year signal caller was one of the best at getting out of the pocket last year. Dart had 18 explosive runs last year, tied with Patrick Mahomes for most in the league, and a 61.6% rushing success rate, per NFL Pro. That was the highest among QBs with at least 35 carries last season, and the fourth-highest career mark among QBs with at least 75 carries in the Next Gen Stats era (since 2016). The Cowboys’ defense gave up the third-most rush yards per game (23.4) and the most touchdowns (8) in the league to quarterbacks running. Having the league’s worst defense will do that. If Christian Parker wants to put his stamp on this defense, it’ll be keeping them disciplined and not allowing Dart to run all over the field for first downs. Maybe someone like Caleb Downs can be used as a spy on Dart to make sure that if he leaves the pocket, he’s there to clean it up before it reaches seven to ten yards downfield. Dallas no longer has a Micah Parsons on the outside to put Dart in pressure situations. Collapsing the pocket from the inside will bode well for Dallas’ defense. They need a big night from Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark. Third Point: Calling your Schott Brian Schottenheimer defied expectations placed on him last season as a play-caller. The Cowboys had a top-ten offense in almost every major category, along with career seasons from Dak Prescott, Javonte Williams, and George Pickens. The one black mark against the unit was how they fared in the red zone. Dallas finished 18th in red zone efficiency at 56.9 percent . Still middle of the league, but not good enough for an offense with this much talent. How Schottenheimer responds with his play-calling in year two, especially in the red zone, could be what puts Dallas over the top as a true NFC contender. The Giants’ pass rushers can be mitigated Sunday night by how Schottenheimer calls the game, so the sequence of play calls and how in tune he is with Prescott will matter in Dallas winning Week 1. Fourth Point: Passing the buck(eye) Before the NFL draft, Cowboys fans had sugar plums dancing in their heads of what life could be like with Caleb Downs falling to them and pairing him with Christian Parker. All along, it felt like a pipe dream. There’s no way Downs would not fall past the New York Giants, who picked twice in the top ten. John Harbaugh called Downs a generational talent at safety, almost tipping the internal feelings around the national champion. Then the unexpected happened. The Giants didn’t pass on Downs just once, but twice. The Cowboys traded up with the Miami Dolphins to pick 11, and the rest is history. Schottenheimer talked about how they felt heading into draft weekend; there was no chance they would be lucky enough to land their No. 1 player, but that’s what makes it so fun—the unknown. #Cowboys Brian Schottenheimer said Dallas had a deal in place with the Kansas City Chiefs to trade up and get Caleb Downs. Of course that all changed when the Chiefs moved up to get Mansoor Delane. “…we had four guys targeted that we really felt strongly about that would fit… pic.twitter.com/uu3qjtBUX9 — Brandon Loree (@Brandoniswrite) July 5, 2026 Downs will be making his professional debut as a member of the Cowboys on Sunday Night Football with all the eyes of the world on him—and yet he seems unfazed by it all. You wonder if there will be any extra motivation for someone who already plays with a chip on his shoulder, facing the team that passed on him twice. Players have talked in the past about how things like this can give them extra motivation in a game. Hopefully, for the Cowboys’ sake, it could bring out the very best in Downs in primetime. Fifth Point: Under-the-radar players There are a few guys who have not been talked about as much this offseason that could be key to a Cowboys victory: Cooper Beebe – The Cowboys center has had a quiet offseason. For the center position, that’s a great thing. Dexter Lawrence is no longer in the picture for the Giants, leaving veterans DJ Reader and Shelby Harris to fill the void. Both players are nowhere near the same level as Lawrence, so Beebe should have some favorable matchups. How he fares against some of the edge rushers who line up on the inside will be the biggest challenge. full_text: We are just days away from the Dallas Cowboys kicking off their 2026 season on the road, taking on a division rival, the New York Giants. Before the Cowboys go wheels up to New York, they took care of some business, inking tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford to a three-year contract extension to remain in Dallas. Spann-Ford has been one of the biggest risers for the Cowboys over the offseason, and his development was rewarded with a brand new three-year extension. They also took care of wide receiver Ryan Flournoy with a 1-year extension. Brevyn Spann-Ford agrees to terms on extension with Cowboys – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Brevyn Spann-Ford is expected to make a big leap in 2026. Before doing so, the Cowboys lock him in for three more years ahead of week one. FRISCO, Texas — The Cowboys and tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford have agreed to terms on an extension. Spann-Ford, who was set to be a restricted free agent after the 2026 season, will now stay in Dallas through 2029. During training camp, Spann-Ford grew into Dallas’ TE2 role behind Jake Ferguson, contributing as one of the offense’s best in-line blockers at the position and a key player on special teams. With three days to go until the Cowboys kick off the NFL season, Spann-Ford now gets added comfort long-term with Dallas being confident in what he can bring to the offense. Cowboys, WR Ryan Flournoy agree on 1-year extension worth up to $6M – RJ Ochoa, BloggingTheBoys.com Another deal indeed. Just before the league’s second game of the season kicked off in Australia, it was reported that Dallas agreed to a 3-year extension with tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford . That was great to see. About 5 minutes after the San Francisco 49ers polished off the Los Angeles Rams… news of the same variety broke. This time it is Ryan Flournoy. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . For Cowboys rookie Caleb Downs, opener vs. Giants offers opportunity for extra motivation – Joseph Hoyt, The Dallas Morning News The Dallas Cowboys first-round pick Caleb Downs is ready to make his NFL debut. From the sounds of it, it seems like he has a little extra motivation heading into New York. Now, instead of playing for the Giants, Downs will play against them in his NFL debut when the Cowboys open the season against New York on Sunday Night Football . There’s already a lot of excitement for Downs about getting the chance to live his NFL dream. Considering the Giants’ interest and their decision to pass on him not once, but twice, is there also some added motivation? Downs downplayed the notion when asked Thursday. “I’m just trying to win on Sunday,” Downs said. “That’s about it.” The Dallas Cowboys are getting mixed signals from the Giants as star player’s availability is getting seriously confusing – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports One of the biggest questions coming into Sunday Night Football is will Malik Nabers play? The Giants are doing a great job of keeping that information all in house ahead of their home opener. The Dallas Cowboys got hit by major injury news when they were forced to place All-Pro guard Tyler Smith on Injured Reserve . But other than that, their starting lineup looks ready to go. The biggest injury mystery ahead of Sunday Night Football is on the New York Giants’ side of things. That’s because Giants top wide receiver Malik Nabers is raising questions about his Week 1 availability despite being a full participant in practice in back-to-back days. Despite Nabers’ participation in practice, the Giants have been non-committal on his status for Sunday. That’s mostly because of Nabers, who claims the organization is letting him make the call. “I’m just focusing on today, had a really good day at practice,” Nabers told reporters. “I’ll let God tell me [when it’s time to return].” How the Cowboys offensive line matches up with the Giants front The Cowboys offensive line was going to have it’s hands full with the Giants pass rush before the Tyler Smith injury. With T.J. Bass in and Tyler Smith out, those problems could get louder on Sunday Night Football. The biggest concern for the Cowboys offensive line this week is not difficult to find. New York can send Brian Burns, Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux after Dak Prescott, and Dallas enters the season with questions at offensive tackle. That matters most on the right side. Terence Steele allowed 52 pressures last season, the most among qualifying offensive tackles according to PFF, while his 54.9 pass-blocking grade ranked 76th out of 89 tackles. Dallas trading for Broderick Jones just before the season and immediately putting him into competition with Steele tells its own story about how the Cowboys view the position. title: Dallas Cowboys 2026 Opponent Preview: Jacksonville Jaguars
summary: Right around this time in the NFL calendar, with the first full Sunday of games looming, there is one specific thing many fans are eager to do, and that’s be among the first to identify teams that did well last year that will regress in 2026. One such team that’s had this unfortunate label slapped […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - DECEMBER 7: Jourdan Lewis #2 celebrates with Josh Hines-Allen #41 of the Jacksonville Jaguars during the fourth quarter of an NFL 2025 game against the Indianapolis Colts at Everbank Stadium on December 7, 2025 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images Right around this time in the NFL calendar, with the first full Sunday of games looming, there is one specific thing many fans are eager to do, and that’s be among the first to identify teams that did well last year that will regress in 2026. One such team that’s had this unfortunate label slapped on them is the Jacksonville Jaguars, who will play at the Cowboys in Week 16 for a primetime game. Short of making the Super Bowl, the Jaguars will be the last AFC opponent the Cowboys see this season. This game comes directly after the “murderer’s row” stretch that’s drawn a ton of attention, at the Seahawks in Week 13, the bye in Week 14, then at the Rams in Week 15, making it really easy to scroll right past this first Cowboys-Jaguars meeting since 2022. Likely the biggest similarity of note between these teams going into 2026 is they both have head coaches going into year two after being first-time head coaches in 2025, while also calling plays on offense. Liam Coen won the second most games in the AFC in year one on the job, finishing 13-4 atop the division. Weirdly enough, this was the Jaguars’ first AFC South title since 2022, which was also year one for a new head coach at that time, Doug Pederson. Let’s take a look at what the Jaguars have done this offseason to try and build off their best win total since 1999. Jaguars Key Free Agent Signings/Departures * SIGNED IN FREE AGENCY RB Chris Rodriguez Jr. RB Ameer Abdullah CB Dane Jackson * DEPARTED IN FREE AGENCY LB Devin Lloyd RB Travis Etienne CB Greg Newsome SAF Andrew Wingard WR Tim Patrick WR Dynami Brown TE Johnny Mundt DE Emmanuel Ogbah This free agency coming and going list doesn’t exactly read like that of a team dead set on staying the team to beat in their division, with more big names leaving rather than coming to Jacksonville. With Trevor Lawrence setting a career high in touchdowns in Coen’s system last year, the pressure is firmly on his shoulders to continue being the catalyst for this Jaguars team to remain in contention. This free agency cycle marked 2025 as the last season Lawrence would have his former college teammate Travis Etienne at running back, as he signed with the New Orleans Saints. The Jaguars have strong continuity all over the depth chart offensively, but have remade the backfield with Bhayshul Tuten stepping up into the starting role and Chris Rodriguez plus Ameer Abdullah brought in. The Jaguars should have more physicality with this running back group, and added ability to control games and win in short-yardage situations without having to drop back to pass. This bodes well for a defense with it’s best players up front in the pass rush group, but also year two of Travis Hunter in the secondary and former Cowboy Jourdan Lewis still at cornerback. Jacksonville was among other successful teams like the Bears and rival Texans in turnover differential a year ago, and while this stat can be extremely volatile and point to where regression may happen, the Jaguars have the right pieces in place to be a good team in this metric yet again. Jaguars 2026 Draft Class Round 2, Pick 24 (56 Overall): TE Nate Boerkircher Round 3, Pick 17 (81 Overall): DT Albert Regis Round 3, Pick 24 (88 Overall): G Emmanuel Pregnon Round 3, Pick 36 (100 Overall): SAF Jalen Huskey Round 4, Pick 19 (119 Overall): EDGE Wesley Williams Round 5, Pick 24 (164 Overall): TE Tanner Koziol Round 6, Pick 10 (191 Overall): WR Josh Cameron Round 6, Pick 22 (203 Overall): WR C.J. Williams Round 7, Pick 17 (233 Overall): EDGE Zach Durfee Round 7, Pick 24 (240 Overall): LB Parker Hughes The wait for the Jaguars to come on the clock in April’s draft was a long one without a first-round pick, and a run of wide receivers plus Vanderbilt TE Eli Stowers going two picks ahead of them put them in a bit of a corner. The Jaguars still landed a tight end in Nate Boerkircher that can do a lot for them, mostly being versatile enough to help them in heavy personnel as a pass catcher and blocker but also playable in spread looks as a detached tight end. The Jags double-dipped at tight end later in the fifth round, and also added an enforcer to the offensive line in the third round with Emmanuel Pregnon. This team’s draft reinforced they are all in on Coen, who will be under the microscope in the way he adapts to new personnel and evolves the offense a step further from last year. Jacksonville found the right parts to do this in the draft after perhaps a quieter than expected free agency period. Jaguars 2026 Coaching Staff * New to staff this season: Run Game Coordinator Brian Picucci Defensive Pass Game Coordinator Mathieu Araujo Another very interesting note about Liam Coen going into year two as the Jaguars head coach is that 2026 will be the first time he’s spending at least a second consecutive year with the same team in any coaching capacity since 2019-20 with the LA Rams. With that, the overwhelming majority of his initial staff from last year has stayed on as well, with just these two new faces in Duval. Brian Picucci was the Buccaneers offensive line coach in 2024 and 2025, and in that first season Coen was offensive coordinator. We’ve highlighted running back as the position that’s undergone the most change for the Jaguars this offseason, so Coen landing a coach he has direct experience with to coordinate the run game is very well done. Mathieu Araujo was most recently with the Dolphins, staying in the state of Florida to now be passing game coordinator for the Jaguars. The Cowboys own coaching staff will have already been through a gauntlet of opposing coaching staffs to really know how they stack up by this December primetime game, but not sleeping on what the Jaguars can bring as the sandwich game in between those two hard road tests, and then the Giants and Commanders to finish will be critical. This will be the first ever primetime meeting between these two franchises. Thank you for following along with this preview series taking us right up to Cowboys kickoff on a new 2026 season! Stay tuned for scouting notes following every Dallas game, and see all of the opponent previews below. Previous 2026 Opponent Previews: Philadelphia Eagles New York Giants Seattle Seahawks Arizona Cardinals Baltimore Ravens Washington Commanders Green Bay Packers Houston Texans Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Tampa Bay Buccaneers Tennessee Titans Indianapolis Colts

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 3
summary: It is Day 3 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - JANUARY 30: Emmitt Smith #22 of the Dallas Cowboys running with the ball gets hit by Keith Goganious #50 of the Buffalo Bills during Super Bowl XXVIII on January 30, 1994 at the Georgia Dome in Atlanta, Georgia. The Cowboys won the Super Bowl 30 -13. (Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Day 3 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. We’re down to the final three of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, this time we revisit the night the Cowboys proved their return to the top of the NFL was no one-year achievement. Dallas trailed Buffalo at halftime, but James Washington changed the game with a defensive touchdown before Emmitt Smith took over completely at Super Bowl XXVIII. Sunday, January 30, 1994 Georgia Dome, Atlanta, Georgia Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 30, Buffalo Bills 13 This was a rematch of Super Bowl XXVII, and the Bills were appearing in an incredible fourth consecutive Super Bowl and were determined to avoid another defeat. Dallas had taken a much harder road back after beginning the season 0-2 during Smith’s contract holdout, but Jimmy Johnson’s team recovered to reach the championship game again. The opening half belonged largely to the kickers. Eddie Murray put Dallas ahead with a 41-yard field goal before Steve Christie answered from 54 yards for Buffalo. Murray connected again from 24 yards, giving the Cowboys a 6-3 advantage after the first quarter. Buffalo took control during the second quarter. Thurman Thomas scored on a four-yard run to give the Bills their first lead, and Christie added a 28-yard field goal as time expired. Dallas went into halftime trailing 13-6 having failed to score an offensive touchdown through the first two quarters. Whatever was said during halftime produced an immediate response. Just 55 seconds into the third quarter, Leon Lett stripped Thomas of the football. James Washington scooped it up and raced 46 yards for a touchdown, instantly tying the score at 13-13 and completely changing the atmosphere inside the Georgia Dome. Then came the drive that defined Smith’s performance. Dallas began at its own 36-yard line, and the league MVP essentially told offensive coordinator Norv Turner to put the game in his hands. Smith carried seven times for 61 yards during an eight-play drive, including six consecutive runs, before breaking through for a 15-yard touchdown. Dallas had suddenly transformed a seven-point halftime deficit into a 20-13 lead and from there Buffalo never recovered. Early in the fourth quarter, Washington struck again by reading Jim Kelly’s pass over the middle and making an interception. His second major takeaway gave Dallas possession in Bills territory and provided Smith another opportunity to finish the job. The Cowboys drove to the Buffalo goal line, but Smith was stopped on three consecutive attempts. Dallas faced fourth-and-goal from the one, and rather than getting clever, Johnson trusted his best player again. Smith powered across for his second touchdown, extending the lead to 27-13 with 9:50 remaining. Murray added a 20-yard field goal with 2:50 left, completing the scoring. Buffalo had managed 13 points before halftime but was shut out throughout the entire second half. Dallas had gone from trailing 13-6 to winning 30-13 with a combination of defensive takeaways and physical running, taking complete control after the break. Smith finished with 30 carries for 132 yards and two touchdowns, including 92 rushing yards after halftime, and was named Super Bowl MVP. His third-quarter performance was the perfect example of what made the Cowboys so difficult to stop during this era when everyone knew the ball was going to number 22, Dallas still imposed its will. This game belongs this high on the countdown because it showed the Cowboys dynasty operating at full strength. The previous championship had announced their arrival. This one proved they could handle being the team everyone was chasing, overcome adversity and win another title anyway. Dallas became only the fifth team at the time to win consecutive Super Bowls. #Cowboys vs #Bills 1994 Super Bowl XXVIII Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 30, Buffalo Bills 13 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/FfdHpkdpLf — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) September 10, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Smith completed an extraordinary individual season by becoming the NFL regular-season MVP and Super Bowl MVP in the same year. title: Behind the Numbers: Cowboys at Giants Week 1
summary: Each week, we’ll examine the numbers surrounding the Cowboys and their next opponent on the schedule. This data includes historical points as well as more recent numbers that may indicate which team has the edge in the upcoming matchup. The History The Cowboys lead the head-to-head matchup with the Giants all-time 78-48-2. The Dak Prescott-led […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - JANUARY 04: Dak Prescott #4 of the Dallas Cowboys and Jaxson Dart #6 of the New York Giants meet after the Giants beat the Cowboys 34-17 at MetLife Stadium on January 04, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images Each week, we’ll examine the numbers surrounding the Cowboys and their next opponent on the schedule. This data includes historical points as well as more recent numbers that may indicate which team has the edge in the upcoming matchup. The History The Cowboys lead the head-to-head matchup with the Giants all-time 78-48-2. The Dak Prescott-led Cowboys are 14-3 against the Giants. Two of those losses came in Dak’s rookie campaign while the other came in 2025. In that matchup, the Cowboys had already been eliminated from the postseason and Dak was pulled at halftime. In 17 games, Dak Prescott has thrown for 4,346 yards, 31 touchdowns, 9 interceptions, and has a passer rating of 101.5 . These are some of the best numbers that the Cowboys quarterback has against any team in the NFL. The new Giants head coach John Harbaugh is 4-1 against the Cowboys. The single loss came in 2016 during Dak Prescott’s rookie season. Week 2 of 2025 featured a ferocious display of offensive fireworks with an NFL record tying six lead changes. Dallas would go on to win this game in overtime off the leg of Brandon Aubrey. Home Field Disadvantage? New York has won zero of their Week 1 home openers since their last victory in 2010. This losing streak includes a 40-0 loss against the Cowboys in 2023. The Giants have won just three home games against the Cowboys since 2016. Dak Prescott played a total of six quarters in those three losses. Last season, the Giants had a record of 3-5 at MetLife Stadium. They were 3-3 at home with Jaxson Dart at the helm. Key Cowboys Stats Dak Prescott finished the 2025 season with 32 total touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Led by CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, Dallas finished with the number two ranked passing offense in the NFL. Javonte Williams led the rushing attack with 1,201 yards on the ground. This was good enough to finish ninth in yards among all running backs. Continuity is key for the Cowboys offense in 2026. This front office lost zero offensive starters from last year’s roster. The one meaningful change is that Tyler Smith will now be out for 4-6 weeks with the thumb injury. Key Giants Stats In 12 starts, Jaxson Dart finished his rookie campaign with 24 total touchdowns. Nine of those touchdowns were scored on the ground. He threw only five interceptions. Dart was sacked nearly three times per game last season. The Giants run game averaged an impressive 129.1 yards per game ( fifth in the NFL). New York ranked 17 th in scoring offense and 26 th in scoring defense. What Do the Numbers Mean? The Cowboys are the clear favorites on paper. Even without Tyler Smith, the Cowboys possess too much firepower for the Giants to match. Dak has been dominant against the Giants throughout his 10-year career. Some of his best performances have come against this NFC East rival. There is little reason to expect a different result considering the weapons Dallas possesses. Defensively, this will be Christian Parker’s first game calling plays. The question this season will be how quickly this defense can reach its full potential. The Giants offense may have some ability to create big-time plays throughout the game depending on the health of Malik Nabers, but Dallas will most likely see a heavy run-first committee approach from John Harbaugh and Matt Nagy. That backfield features both power and speed with the mix of Cam Skattebo, Najee Harris, and Tyrone Tracy Jr. Jaxson Dart can also catch fire if you allow him to utilize his legs. The good news for the Cowboys is the new defense was built to stop the run first and foremost. If they’re able to do that with consistent light boxes, Dallas should expect to keep the Giants run-heavy offense quite limited. This is week one of the new NFL season, so last year’s stats will only contribute so much to the story that is about to unfold in front of our eyes. However, the tale of Dak Prescott and the Cowboys over the last decade paints a clear and consistent picture versus the Giants. That picture tells us that Dallas should win this game convincingly.

title: How the Cowboys offensive line matches up with the Giants front
summary: We’re digging into the trenches, because that’s where the real action happens in an NFL game. We’re looking at the Dallas Cowboys offensive line to see where it might have an advantage, and where they could struggle against the New York Giants. Trench Dashboard As the season develops this will be updated with the offensive […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 21: Dallas Cowboys offensive line gets set during an NFL football game against the Chicago Bears at Solider Field on September 21, 2025 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re digging into the trenches, because that’s where the real action happens in an NFL game. We’re looking at the Dallas Cowboys offensive line to see where it might have an advantage, and where they could struggle against the New York Giants. Trench Dashboard As the season develops this will be updated with the offensive line metrics for the 2026 season. For Week 1, this is how the offensive line finished the 2025 season and how they ranked. Pass Block Win Rate – 63% 19th Run Block Win Rate- 72% 11th Pressure rate allowed – 35% 20th Sacks allowed – 8th OL Penalties – 32nd Last three week trend: N/A The Pressure Point Every opponent will look at the Cowboys offensive line and ask, where can we break it? Here’s what to watch for. PRESSURE POINT: New York’s edge rush The biggest concern for the Cowboys offensive line this week is not difficult to find. New York can send Brian Burns, Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux after Dak Prescott, and Dallas enters the season with questions at offensive tackle. That matters most on the right side. Terence Steele allowed 52 pressures last season, the most among qualifying offensive tackles according to PFF, while his 54.9 pass-blocking grade ranked 76th out of 89 tackles. Dallas trading for Broderick Jones just before the season and immediately putting him into competition with Steele tells its own story about how the Cowboys view the position. PRESSURE POINT: Tyler Guyton has to prove the improvement is real Guyton has received plenty of praise this summer, and the Cowboys appear much more confident in him than they did earlier in the offseason. Week 1 will provide an immediate test of whether this progress translates into real-game performance. If the right side is having trouble, and Guyton ends up destroying all optimism everyone had in him this preseason, then pressure flows for the Giants at both ends. Where to attack Every defensive line has a weakness, here are the Giants soft spots and where the Cowboys offensive line should attack. GREEN LIGHT: Run it up the middle If New York’s biggest advantage is on the outside, Dallas should make the Giants prove they have fixed the middle. The Giants finished last season allowing 5.3 yards per rush, the worst mark in the NFL. They have since completely rebuilt their defensive line and, most importantly, traded Dexter Lawrence to Cincinnati. D.J. Reader was brought in to help replace him, while Shelby Harris and second-year defensive lineman Darius Alexander are expected to have significant roles. That puts the strongest part of Dallas’ offensive line against one of New York’s biggest question marks. Attack here hard and fast and that takes the pressure off the tackles if things are looking tough on the outside. GREEN LIGHT: Make the Giants’ pass rushers defend the run There is another way to deal with Carter and Burns, do not allow them to spend the entire night charging after Prescott. Carter was excellent rushing the passer last season, but his 54.4 PFF run-defense grade ranked 95th among qualifying edge defenders. Burns was also far less effective against the run than as a pass rusher, finishing with a 59.8 run-defense grade. Running toward an aggressive pass rusher forces him to stop attacking the quarterback and instead hold his position against a blocker. Dallas can also use tight ends alongside the offensive tackles, pull Smith or Booker across the formation and use misdirection to punish Carter and Burns if they get too eager to attack upfield. The Chaos Report Here’s the Giants defensive trends from 2025 at the defensive line. For Week 1 we give you their trend from last year, but beyond this week we will give you the trends for each team as the season develops. Sack Total – 20th Pass Rush Win Rate- 41% 9th Run Stop Win Rate- 32% 13th Stunt Rate- 19% 26th Last three week trend: N/A Matchup of the week Tyler Guyton vs. Abdul Carter Whenever the Giants put Abdul Carter across from Tyler Guyton, watch that battle. Carter already established himself as one of the NFL’s more disruptive young pass rushers during his rookie season. His 66 pressures led all rookies, his 84.5 PFF pass-rush grade ranked 11th among qualifying edge defenders, and he became increasingly difficult to block as the season progressed. He has the speed to race around the outside of a tackle, but he can also change direction and attack inside when the blocker moves too quickly to protect the edge. That is exactly the type of defender who can tell us how far Guyton has progressed. Guyton has the size and athletic ability to deal with speed, and the Cowboys have praised the improvement in his footwork and his ability to react when a pass rusher changes direction. But the regular season is where that improvement has to show itself. Injury Updates: The big news dropped Monday that Tyler Smith will miss 4-6 weeks to have thumb surgery. Cowboys LG Tyler Smith will be having thumb surgery tomorrow and will miss 4-6 weeks, per HC Brian Schottenheimer. — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) September 7, 2026 As for the Giants, the only update so far heading into Week 1 is that defensive lineman Roy Robertson-Harris was sent to injured reserve with an Achilles tear back in mid-August.

title: Broncos at Chiefs 5 questions: What are the expectations in KC?
summary: For the first time in nine seasons, the Kansas City Chiefs failed to win the AFC West. If that wasn’t enough, the Chiefs didn’t even make the AFC Playoffs. To pour a little salt in the wounds, Patrick Mahomes tore his ACL. After nearly a decade of success, the 2025 season was a nightmare for […]
full_text: For the first time in nine seasons, the Kansas City Chiefs failed to win the AFC West. If that wasn’t enough, the Chiefs didn’t even make the AFC Playoffs. To pour a little salt in the wounds, Patrick Mahomes tore his ACL. After nearly a decade of success, the 2025 season was a nightmare for Kansas City. Now comes the opener on Monday Night Football against the Denver Broncos at Arrowhead Stadium. To get a feel for the expectations Chiefs Kingdom has (and what the reality is), plus why this season will be different, we go “behind enemy lines” with Maurice Elston from Arrowhead Pride . MHR: How is Chiefs Kingdom feeling heading into the season? What are the expectations for the team, and what is the reality? Maurice : I think Chiefs Kingdom will always lean toward the overly optimistic side of things as long as Andy Reid is the head coach and, more importantly, Patrick Mahomes is the quarterback. With those two here, it will always be Super Bowl or bust, unfortunately. I don’t think that expectation is far from reality, though. If the Chiefs can find a way to be more efficient in one-score games this season, I believe they will be a playoff team. And if Mahomes gets into the playoffs, he immediately becomes the quarterback no other team wants to face. MHR: Why will this season be different for KC? Tied into that is Patrick Mahomes going to be Patrick Mahomes? Maurice : I don’t believe Mahomes would be on the field if the Chiefs’ leadership and training staff didn’t believe he could play like his normal self. The Chiefs understand what he means to the franchise, so they aren’t going to jeopardize his long-term health just to get him on the field for opening night. What should make this season different is the supporting cast around him. The Chiefs added reigning Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III, giving the offense an explosive running back who can take some of the pressure off Mahomes. He should also finally have his full wide receiver room healthy and on the field together—something that never happened last season. If Mahomes is healthy and Kansas City can pair its complete receiving corps with a legitimate running game, this offense should look much different. MHR: What do the Chiefs need to do offensively and defensively against Denver on Monday night? Maurice : Offensively, the Chiefs need to run the ball effectively enough to keep Denver’s defensive front honest. Kansas City may also need to provide additional help on the left side of the offensive line to give Mahomes time against a Broncos defense that led the NFL in sacks last season. I expect Andy Reid to be prepared for that and use the running game, quick passes, and different protections to slow down Denver’s pressure. Defensively, Kansas City’s first priority should be stopping the run and forcing Denver into a pass-heavy game. If the Chiefs can put Bo Nix in obvious passing situations, I like Steve Spagnuolo’s chances of creating pressure and disguising coverages against him. MHR: What do you make of the current spread at FanDuel Sportsbook? And what is your best bet? Maurice : As of now, the Chiefs are 2.5-point favorites at FanDuel Sportsbook, and I think that spread is right where it should be. These teams are evenly matched, but Kansas City is playing at Arrowhead with Mahomes back under center. My best bet is Chiefs -2.5 because I expect Kansas City to squeeze out a victory with a late field goal, winning by three points. MHR: How does the opener play out, and what are your expectations? Maurice : I expect this game to remain tight throughout. Neither team’s starters played many preseason snaps together, so I anticipate some early rust—particularly from both offenses. The defenses could control the first half before the quarterbacks and play-callers begin settling into the game. Ultimately, I believe the opener will be decided late in the fourth quarter. Mahomes leads one final drive, Kansas City kicks the winning field goal, and the Chiefs open the season with a three-point victory.

title: Scouting the Enemy: Kansas City Chiefs
summary: The Denver Broncos kickoff their 2026 gridiron campaign defending their AFC West title against their longtime rival Kansas City Chiefs. For the first installment of Scouting the Enemy this year, we will take a look at how the Chiefs performed in 2025, their key offseason additions and departures, as well as their X-Factor players on […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 28: Tight end Travis Kelce #87 of the Kansas City Chiefs signals to stay in the game during the first quarter of an NFL preseason game against the Seattle Seahawks at Arrowhead Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos kickoff their 2026 gridiron campaign defending their AFC West title against their longtime rival Kansas City Chiefs. For the first installment of Scouting the Enemy this year, we will take a look at how the Chiefs performed in 2025, their key offseason additions and departures, as well as their X-Factor players on offense and defense for Monday Night Football . 2025 Kansas City Chiefs Season Review The Chiefs finished last season with a 6-11 record . It was the first time they had missed the playoffs since 2014 and their first losing season since 2012 when Romeo Crennel was head coach. 2026 Kansas City Chiefs Offseason Additions and Departures The big addition for the Chiefs over the offseason was signing running back Kenneth Walker III in free agency. They also brought back cornerback L’Jarius Sneed, who had spent the past two years with the Tennessee Titans. Kansas City also traded a late 2027 draft selection to bring in former first-round quarterback Justin Fields to be the backup to Patrick Mahomes. The biggest departure came via trade, with the GM Brett Veach trading two-time All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie to the Los Angeles Rams. Additionally, cornerback Jaylen Watson and defensive lineman Charles Omenihu both signed with the Washington Commanders in free agency. With extra selections after the McDuffie trade, the Chiefs focused on shoring up their defense. Kansas City moved up to get Mansoor Delane at the six slot in 2006 NFL Draft. The former LSU standout was touted as the best cover corner last April. Additionally, they added versatile Clemson defensive lineman Peter Woods late in the first round. To bolster their pass rush productivity, the Chiefs picked R Mason Thomas out of Oklahoma in the second round. I also liked their fourth-round selection, Oregon slot cornerback Jadon Canady. Their fifth-round picks, running back Emmett Johnson and wide receiver Cyrus Allen could be situational players for them as rookies. Offensive X-Factor: Running Back Kenneth Walker III All eyes are on the health of Patrick Mahomes and how he will return from an ACL injury last season. If he can revert to prior form, the Chiefs are likely title contenders. However, my X-Factor for them in Week 1 is free agent addition Kenneth Walker III. Last year’s Super Bowl MVP, Walker inked a 3-year, $34 million dollar deal this offseason to bolster their rushing attack. Walker had a productive 2025 season with 221 rushes for 1,027 yards, and 5 touchdowns. He added 31 receptions for 282 yards as a receiver out of the backfield. The creative playcalling of Andy Reid coupled with Walker’s skillset will be a big challenge for the Broncos. Limiting his impact will be critical to not only win the time of possession battle but also come out of Arrowhead with a victory. The Broncos can’t afford to let Walker run wild. Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph and his defensive front seven certainly have a tough challenge in the opening game. Defensive X-Factor: Cornerback Mansoor Delane The Chiefs opted to do a little bit of reshuffling in their defensive backfield this offseason. Their general manager has a history of trading away cornerbacks right before they are set to earn mega-extensions. Sending off McDuffie to the Rams was emblematic of that. That means rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane will have to play a huge role for them this season. On Monday night against the Broncos, he will certainly have his hands full. With Denver adding Jaylen Waddle into the mix, Delane will be tasked with not just covering him, but also having to battle longtime veteran Courtland Sutton as well. Both wide receivers have unique skill sets which will certainly test his abilities. Delane’s talented merited such an early selection, but I don’t see Bo Nix and the Broncos being shy about throwing in his direction. I expect them to test Delane early and often. How the Broncos can secure a victory over the Chiefs The Chiefs are a tough draw for the Broncos in Week 1, but I’m confident the Broncos can find a way to victory. As noted above, slowing down Walker will be a huge part of that. With it being a road game, slowing him down and finding a way to win the time of possession battle will be crucial. Not only that, but finding a way to force some turnovers on defense will be huge if Denver wants to earn a victory. That’s been a focal point of theirs over the course of the summer. Now it’s time to put their plan in action on Monday Night Football . On offense, the Broncos will need to limit their miscues and be efficient on the ground and through the air. The team’s rushing attack needs to hit the ground running, and Bo Nix needs to dial up a good game and find a way to get some explosive plays against their defense. Hart’s Prediction: Broncos 24, Chiefs 17.
author: Christopher Hart

title: Broncos coaches face major test against the Chiefs
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! When you face the Kansas City Chiefs, there are always built-in challenges. Andy Reid. Patrick Mahomes. Steve Spagnuolo. And that’s just to name a few. The last one may not get as much attention as the other two, but it doesn’t lessen the task in front of Bo Nix, Davis Webb, […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL, CO - August 18 : Denver Broncos Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph answers questions from reporters at Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Tuesday, August 18, 2026. (Photo by Hyoung Chang/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! When you face the Kansas City Chiefs, there are always built-in challenges. Andy Reid. Patrick Mahomes. Steve Spagnuolo. And that’s just to name a few. The last one may not get as much attention as the other two, but it doesn’t lessen the task in front of Bo Nix, Davis Webb, Sean Payton, and the Denver Broncos offense. Summit White helmets 🔛 pic.twitter.com/AWpem3F3Ft — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) September 10, 2026 Spagnuolo is one of the best defensive coordinators ever, and his defenses are always difficult to go against, especially at home. Welcome to your first game of calling plays, Mr. Webb. “My mind has gone back a few times,” Webb said to the media on Thursday after practice. “In Buffalo, we played him often. We were usually on the losing end of that. Then he was our interim head coach for the last four or five weeks of the season, I believe, back in the day (with the New York Giants in 2017). I was like a scout-team quarterback, so back in the day, only the defensive players and myself got banana pudding from his wife. I miss ‘Spags.’ He’s a great dude and one of the best defensive coordinators in this game’s history. He’ll be a tough challenge for us out of the gate.” It’s similar to what Vance Joseph will face in going against Reid, Mahomes, and Eric Bieniemy. What adds to all of this is Mahomes’s return from a knee injury and a season in which the Chiefs failed to make the playoffs. “I think Patrick is going to be Patrick,” Joseph said to the media on Thursday. “In my opinion, he wouldn’t play if he couldn’t be himself. He’s had a good summer and spring to kind of rehab, and from what I hear and from what I read, he’s feeling great. So we expect Patrick to be Patrick, and he is obviously the guy in the league who wins an awful lot. He’s obviously motivated, and it’s a big game for them; it’s a big game for us, obviously. It’s Week 1, so everyone’s healthy and excited to play, so we’ll get his best shot.” What helps with all of this is having a head coach like Sean Payton. Joseph and Webb know they have someone who has tons of experience and knowledge. “I think gameday will be similar to what it has been in the preseason,” Webb said. “He’s been awesome throughout the game. He has his few pointers here and there, and they are all productive pointers. He’s 62 years old, and I’m 31. It is what it is. He has a lot more experience than me. Even the last few nights, he’s given us five to 10 nuggets that have really benefitted us going through the game plan meetings. It’s still a Sean Payton offense, and that is how we want to operate it.” Added Joseph: “He is fabulous in front of the team. He can paint a picture each week for each opponent that we’re playing. That Wednesday meeting is interesting because he can paint a picture, and most of the time, that’s the picture that happens. That’s his strength. He can explain opponents, he can explain the keys to victory, things we have to do to win games, and he’s usually right. So I think for him, he can spend more time doing that. Obviously, he’s still involved with the offense, and the defense and special teams because he’s responsible for all of it, but he has more time now to do his thing. “That’s his best trait, in my opinion, is team building, keeping guys on edge, and keeping everybody humble and moving forward. When it’s really good, he’s hard. He keeps you going. That’s old school (Pro Football Hall of Fame) Coach (Bill) Parcells. When it’s bad, he shows grace, and that’s also old school in Coach Parcells. So he’s in his element, he’s happy, he’s getting rest. So it’s been fun to watch him work.”

title: Davis Webb on calling plays in his first game: ‘We’ll let it rip when it’s go time’
summary: The Denver Broncos are busy game planning their opening weekend road game against the Kansas City Chiefs. It’s prime time and the atmosphere will be as close to playoffs as a Week 1 game can get. Denver’s no offensive coordinator, Davis Webb, was asked about the emotions of calling plays getting to him ahead of […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 28: Offensive coordinator Davis Webb of the Denver Broncos walks on the sidelines during the fourth quarter against the Minnesota Vikings in a preseason game at Empower Field at Mile High on August 28, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. Denver’s no offensive coordinator, Davis Webb, was asked about the emotions of calling plays getting to him ahead of his first game and he seems pretty cool, calm, and collected heading into his debut as OC. “It’s going to happen, and I think that’s a good thing,” Webb said. “I think our staff is prepared, and I think that our players are prepared. We’ll let it rip when it’s go time, but right now there are butterflies for everybody. I think like as a player getting hit for the first time or the first completion, getting that first play call in and we’ll get rolling after that.” The challenge for him will be to maintain control of the game. I would imagine it could be easy for a young coach to chase something that just isn’t helpful for the situation. Something tells me that isn’t how Webb will be. I can’t wait to see how he performs on Monday night. Broncos daily recap Sean Payton offers thoughts on what makes the Chiefs defense tough “They mix a lot of looks up. The second game, we got a little bit more coverage than we had seen in maybe the game prior or the years prior. It all depends on what they’re trying to take away, but they’re well coached, they tackle well. They can create negative plays in both the run and passing game because of the pressure looks that you get,” stated Payton. Broncos vs. Chiefs: 3 Things to Watch in Week 1 It’s just the first game of the season, but this rivalry game will certainly be one of the best and most important to start the season. Here are three aspects of the game Broncos Country should keep a close eye on in the regular season opener. He is fabulous in front of the team. He can paint a picture each week for each opponent that we’re playing. That Wednesday meeting is interesting because he can paint a picture, and most of the time that’s the picture that happens. That’s his strength. He can explain opponents, he can explain the keys to victory, things we have to do to win games and he’s usually right. So I think for him, he can spend more time doing that. Obviously he’s still involved with the offense, and the defense and special teams because he’s responsible for all of it, but he has more time now to do his thing. That’s his best trait in my opinion, is team building, keeping guys on edge and keeping everybody humble and moving forward. When it’s really good, he’s hard. He keeps you going. That’s old school [Pro Football Hall of Fame] Coach [Bill] Parcells. When it’s bad, he shows grace and that’s also old school in Coach Parcells. So he’s in his element, he’s happy, he’s getting rest. So it’s been fun to watch him work.” On if there is a premium on in-game adjustments during Week 1 “Week 1’s always tough. Even though playing these guys every year, twice a year and we’ve been playing them for a long time, Week 1 is always tough because there are going to be some un-scouted looks and both sides will have those. If you can nail those early and get past those without having tragic results, that’s the key. So I think for us going on the road, it’s going to be a hostile environment, just playing clean early and obviously getting past the un-scouted looks because everyone goes through the offseason. Within your system you have to adjust. We do it every single year, and I’m sure [Chiefs Head Coach] Andy [Reid] and ‘EB’ (Chiefs Offensive Coordinator Eric Bieniemy] are doing the same. Who knows how the games play out with turnovers and whatnot. So we’ll kind of play that by ear as the weeks and the season go on, but my honest answer is we do a lot of discussing on the 48 guys that are going to be active and everybody’s role. That goes back to [Head Coach] Sean [Payton] having a really good grip on the roster.” On K Wil Lutz being named a captain “I’ve known [K] Wil [Lutz] a long time. The one thing I can say about Wil is to watch him grow both as a player, a teammate and a leader has been a really fun thing to watch his development. He deserves it. title: Broncos vs. Chiefs: 3 Things to Watch in Week 1
summary: The Denver Broncos square off against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 1 on Monday Night Football. It’s just the first game of the season, but this rivalry game will certainly be one of the best and most important to start the season. Here are three aspects of the game Broncos Country should keep a […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - DECEMBER 25: RJ Harvey #12 of the Denver Broncos reacts after catching a pass for a touchdown against the Kansas City Chiefs during the fourth quarter at Arrowhead Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos square off against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 1 on Monday Night Football . It’s just the first game of the season, but this rivalry game will certainly be one of the best and most important to start the season. Here are three aspects of the game Broncos Country should keep a close eye on in the regular season opener. Will Denver’s ground game start strong on the road at Arrowhead? Earlier today, I wrote about how it will be important for the Broncos’ offense to start off fast against the Kansas City Chiefs. A lot of that sentiment revolved around Bo Nix and the aerial attack making some slash plays down the field but having a formidable and consistent running game will be just as important. After J.K. Dobbins went down with an injury in the second half of their ‘25 season, the Broncos’ running game sputtered. They averaged barely over three yards per carry when he was sidelined. That’s simply unacceptable and something that had to be addressed. This offseason, they’ve worked diligently on their running game—from the blocking schemes up front, to even adding players to their backfield. While I expect Dobbins to get most of the carries against the Chiefs, the Broncos will need second year running back RJ Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman to also perform at a high level. I figure Harvey’s biggest utilization will come as a receiver out of the backfield, but if he can spring a big run or two with his game-breaking speed—that’d be huge for Denver. To spell Dobbins, I expect Coleman to get a handful of carries, perhaps in short-yardage or goal line situations where he excelled at during college. The Chiefs had a Top 10 run defense last season, so this will be a huge test for Denver on the road in Week 1. Hopefully, the Broncos’ offensive line can find a way to pave some paths for their talented trio of running backs that help lead them to victory. How will Denver’s defensive line and edge rusher rotation shake out? The Broncos have a roster loaded with continuity, but two major changes on defense will be in store for them as their regular season kicks off. The first will be finding out who will be tasked with replacing John Franklin-Myers. Zach Allen, D.J. Jones, and Malcolm Roach figure to be Denver’s starting three. However, who is in line for the next number of snaps remains to be determined. My bet would be on Eyioma Uwazurike, the fourth-year player from Iowa State who has had a standout camp. Head Coach Sean Payton recently highlighted Uwazurike as a potential breakout candidate for the defense this season. They will need him to step up in a big way to chase down quarterback Patrick Mahomes and stop Kenneth Walker III from having a big debut game with the Chiefs. Additionally, Denver will have to figure out the right formula at edge rusher. With Jonathon Cooper sidelined due to being on the NFL Commissioner’s Exempt List, the defense is down a quality player who has started all seventeen regular season games for them the last three seasons. Behind him, they have Jonah Elliss, Que Robinson, and Dondrea Tillman. Each have flashed and showed promise in their snap share, but all three will be tasked with greater responsibility to start the season. They’ll have to do their part alongside Nik Bonitto to dial up the pressure on Mahomes to try and destabilize the Chiefs’ passing attack. What changes are in store for the Broncos’ offense with Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb dialing up the plays? Earlier in the offseason, Broncos Country experience quite the shake up when Head Coach Sean Payton announced at the NFL Combine, he would be giving up playcalling duties and let Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb take the reigns of the offense. While the Broncos have certainly embarked on a tremendous turnaround the past three seasons with Payton leading the team, some of his decisions on offense have left many fans hoping for more. Only time will tell if this change will tur out to be the right call, but Broncos Country should be excited in the potential new wrinkles that are on the horizon for the upcoming season. Denver boasts a five-deep rotation at wide receiver with Courtland Sutton, Jaylen Waddle, Pat Bryant, Troy Franklin, and Marvin Mims Jr. When you factor in RJ Harvey’s receiving upside and the likelihood of tight end Evan Engram being more productive, the prospect of a top-flight aerial attack seems extremely realistic with third-year signal caller Bo Nix ready to roar on Monday Night Football . I’ll be paying close attention to the tempo of the Broncos’ offense, as well as what type of personnel groupings they deploy. They have a lot of playmakers on offense, so finding a way to get them all involved will be a challenge. But in my opinion—that’s a good one to have. How Webb goes about drafting up a gameplan to battle Steve Spagnoulo’s defense will be fascinating to watch unfold. What about you, Broncos Country? What storylines or developments have your attention for the regular season opener? Let me know in the comments section.
author: Christopher Hart

title: How the Broncos can defeat the Chiefs on Monday Night Football
summary: After an impressive 14-win season in 2025, the Denver Broncos are the reigning AFC West champions. They dethroned the Kansas City Chiefs from that spot, who endured their worst season in a decade last year. The Broncos’ quest at a second straight AFC West title and subsequent Super Bowl chase begins on Monday Night Football […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - DECEMBER 25: Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) flexes and yells to celebrate a 9-yard touchdown run in the third quarter of a Christmas Day NFL game between the Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs on December 25, 2025 at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After an impressive 14-win season in 2025, the Denver Broncos are the reigning AFC West champions. They dethroned the Kansas City Chiefs from that spot, who endured their worst season in a decade last year. The Broncos’ quest at a second straight AFC West title and subsequent Super Bowl chase begins on Monday Night Football at Arrowhead Stadium. The Broncos’ offense has to start off fast There are a lot of reasons to be optimistic about the Broncos in 2026. Nevertheless, one order of business must be achieved. That’s going from a middle-of-the-pack offense to a Top 10-unit in the National Football League. This season will be Bo Nix’s third year leading the offense and Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb’s first season calling plays for Denver. I’m bullish on what the two can accomplish and believe Nix is poised for his best year of his career. However, the Broncos must start off fast and forego their early seasons woes that have plagued the group’s efficiency and productivity in the first part of the past two seasons. On the road against the Chiefs, they face a formidable defense coached by Steve Spagnuolo. He does a great job dialing up pressure and confusing opposing quarterbacks. Kansas City used a lot of draft selections to bolster that side of the ball and ended up revamping a good portion of their secondary. With the addition of Jaylen Waddle, the Broncos have a premier playmaker in the mix that was absent from last year’s gridiron campaign. Getting Waddle, the ball and creating some explosive plays through the air will be mission critical to achieve victory. I’m hopeful Denver will be able to get him involved to boost their aerial attack and dial up some big plays against a revamped Chiefs secondary. The Broncos’ defense has to find a way to rattle Patrick Mahomes; slow down Kenneth Walker III Even with Patrick Mahomes coming off a down year that ended prematurely due to an ACL tear, the Broncos defense can’t underestimate his top-notch playmaking ability. In order to defeat the Chiefs, Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph is going to have to dial up the heat on Mahomes and force him into some bad decisions. Left tackle Josh Simmons may be sidelined from the game due to injury. If that happens, at least one of the Chiefs’ starting tackle spots will be manned by an undrafted rookie free agent. That may be just enough of an opportunity for Nik Bonitto and the rest of Denver’s front seven to feast and cause some havoc. Additionally, the Broncos have to find a way to slow down running back Kenneth Walker III. He is coming off a great season and was the Seattle Seahawks’ Super Bowl MVP last year. Setting the tempo and pace of the game is important, and finding a way to shut down Andy Reid’s ground game plans will be essential to earn a Week 1 win. Play disciplined football and win the turnover battle There were two major issues that were prevalent last year with the Broncos. They were the fourth most penalized team in football and ranked toward the bottom of the league in forcing turnovers. Knowing that, it’s quite impressive they managed to reel off 14 wins and advance to the AFC Championship Game. This season, things have to be different on both fronts. Last year, too many drives on offense stalled or were extended for the opposition with penalties and miscues. If they can cut down on those, the Broncos should be even tougher to defeat in ‘26. The Chiefs are already a tough opponent as is, they can’t make things harder for themselves by shooting themselves in the foot. In ‘25, the Broncos sported a -4 turnover differential. They were one of only a handful of teams to make the playoffs being in the negative. All offseason long, the coaching staff and players emphasized how essential it will be to turn the tides in that regard. Late last season and in the AFC Divisional Playoff victory over the Bills, we saw significant improvement with that. Hopefully, they can find a way to no What do you think, Broncos Country? What things do you believe Denver has to do to come out of Kansas City with a Week 1 victory? Sound off in the comments section and let me know your thoughts.
