title: Battle Red Blog Regular Season Power Rankings: 2026 Season
summary: Football is back! Every year here at Battle Red Blog, I spend some time every week gathering all of the Power Rankings pundits’ thoughts on the Houston Texans and relaying them here (of course, with some of my own thoughts sprinkled in). But, at the beginning of every season, I try to put together my […]
full_text: Football is back! Every year here at Battle Red Blog, I spend some time every week gathering all of the Power Rankings pundits’ thoughts on the Houston Texans and relaying them here (of course, with some of my own thoughts sprinkled in). But, at the beginning of every season, I try to put together my own personal power rankings, where I rank all 32 NFL teams, give a quick review of what I expect out of them this season, and predict their final regular season record. It’s may not come with as much cutting-edge analysis or data, but my rankings will be fun to look back on when they’re all wrong in a few months! Without further ado, here’s my 2026 NFL Power Rankings to start the NFL Season: 32. Cleveland Browns 2025 Record: 5-12 Notable Arrivals: T/G Tytus Howard T Spencer Fano (Rookie) LB Quincy Williams Notable Departures: DE Myles Garrett OG Wyatt Teller LB Devin Bush Once upon a time, Cleveland Browns 2026 Week 1 starting quarterback Deshaun Watson was the franchise savior for the Houston Texans. Now synonymous with the term “bust” in the NFL, Watson had an exceptional run as Houston’s starting signal-caller from 2017-2020, often recalled as some of successful yet fractious eras in Houston’s history. Former head coach/general manager Bill O’Brien was the ringleader of the Texans circus that Watson quarterbacked, but following O’Brien’s firing during a disastrous 2020 season, a lawsuit alleging extensive and shocking acts of sexual assault against Watson in early 2021 – that he originally swore to fight (to “clear his name”) only to settle in 2023 – as well his trade request following contract disputes with Houston, his fame in the city and in the world of sports took an unprecedented nose dive. Now in his fifth and final year of a gigantic, $250-million contract with the Cleveland Browns, Watson’s star has only continued to fade under Ohio skies and has often become the face of this woebegone era of the franchise. He reportedly barely won the starting job over second-year QB Shedeur Sanders despite being a highly paid veteran, and his open detest of the team’s supporters has practically earned him the honor of being a pariah in his own stadium. Watson just seemed to continuously sink further below the bar of what is deemed acceptable of a NFL quarterback throughout his half-decade in Cleveland, matching his zenith on the gridiron in Houston with piercing infamy in his new home. This year will be his last chance to turn it all around and prove to everyone that he can still be a competent NFL professional, but I sincerely doubt it. In front of him, Cleveland hopes to have a more consistent o-line – highlighted by the offseason signing former Texan RT/LG Tytus Howard and 2026 9th overall pick T Spencer Fano – as well as a better rushing attack with RB Quinshon Judkins back from injury. WRs Jerry Jeudy and rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston could make an intriguing combination to pair with TE Harold Fannin Jr., but they’ll need the QB to be consistent, which is wishing upon a star. Defense, as it often the case with Cleveland in this new era, their lone saving grace from being by far the worst team in football. But, even here, a decline will likely occur considering superstar DE Myles Garrett has been traded to the Los Angeles Rams. The Browns got DE Jared Verse in return, but he can only hope to fill half of the hole Garrett leaves. If DT Mason Graham can start realizing his draft hype, they might have a new young-duo up front, but they can only do so much. Cleveland does have some talent behind the line with reigning defensive rookie of the year LB Carson Scheswinger, LB Quincy Williams, CB Denzel Ward, and S Grant Delpit, who all will combine to create a strong backfield both against the run and against the pass. But, the big question mark at QB makes this season feel like a primer to the Arch Manning sweepstakes at the 2027 NFL Draft. Projected 2026 Record: 3-14 31. Miami Dolphins 2025 Record: 7-10 Notable Arrivals: QB Malik Willis CB Darrell Baker Jr. T Kadyn Proctor (Rookie) Notable Departures: QB Tua Tagovailoa WR Jaylen Waddle LB Bradley Chubb Like many other regimes in Miami, the Mike McDaniel era ended after just over three seasons at the helm. WR Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle are gone, QB Tua Tagovailoa is now the week one starter for Atlanta, and in his place is former Green Bay Packers’ backup QB Malik Willis. With new general manager Jon Eric-Sullivan and head coach Jeff Hafley committed to bringing some of that special Packers’ spice down south, the Dolphins will be trying to emulate a sort of smashmouth-esque offense complemented by an aggresive, ball-hawking defense. Miami’s offense will run through De’Von Achane, but in order for that to work, they’ll need a much better effort from 2025 second-rounder G Jonah Savaiinaea in his sophomore campaign as well as the entire tight end’s room to perform above expectations. Additionally, if their defense hopes to improve beyond their 24th-overall ranking last year, they’re going to need exceptional seasons from CB Jason Marshall Jr., and rookies Chris Johnson and S Michael Taaffe. Simply put, many positions on the Dolphins’ starting lineup are occupied by young and/or inexperienced players. They’ll be betting heavily on unknown prospects at multiple positions on both offense and defense, so…they’re tanking. The Miami Dolphins, despite having some intriguing players on the roster, did little this offseason to make them a better team than they were last year. If all of their young starters and rookies hit their ceiling in 2026, they have a chance to be interesting in December, but if not, they’ll be in the quarterback sweepstakes in April. Projected Record: 5-12 30. New York Jets 2025 Record: 3-14 Notable Arrivals: QB Geno Smith LB Demario Davis DE Joseph Ossai Notable Departures: S Tony Adams LB Jermaine Johnson G John Simpson How do you stay this bad for this long? I’ve ranked the Dolphins and Browns below the New York Jets for these power rankings, but at least both of those teams have appeared in the playoffs more than once in the last six years. Even the lowly Browns can lay claim to more playoff success than the Jets, who haven’t even sniffed the playoffs since 2011. It’s truly remarkable how this football team has practiced mediocrity with so many different coaches, general managers, quarterbacks, and more. This year’s rendition is led by second-year head coach Aaron Glenn, a former CB for the Jets who can now lay claim to NFL infamy for leading the very first defense in recorded history to finish the season with 0 interceptions. Isn’t it just poetic? It can’t get any worse than this, though. The only way to go is up for the defense, and they’ll do just that with new CB Nashon Wright and Ss Minkah Fitzpatrick and Dane Belton to complement Brandon Stephens. They’ll also be boosted by a completely remade defensive front, now manned by rookie second-overall pick David Bailey, trade acquisitions DTs Harrison Phillips and T’Vondre Sweat, and returning DE Will Macdonald IV. Big moves from a Jets front office that is appearing just as trade-happy as the previous, Joe Douglas-led regime, but don’t tell that to a Jets fan. It’s unlikely they’ll dig far out of the abyss they fell in last year, but the Jets should at least look competent on defense this year. On offense, QB Geno Smith’s long, winding journey back to the Jets starting job since losing it in 2015 makes for a good story to start the season with, but I’m trepidatious to say that it’ll be a success. WRs Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, rookie Omar Cooper Jr., and RB Breece Hall should give Geno enough weapons to be productive, but the o-line still has a lot to prove. Either way, Geno should be a better passer than Justin Fields was last year, but I wouldn’t bet on all of these spare parts gelling well right away. There might be some good Jets-related action by November or December, but their season will already be over by then.…

title: Five Good Texans questions with Buffalo Ramblings
summary: The NFL scheduling has its quirks and in one of those quirks, the Texans and the Bills match up for the third season in a row. The Texans owned Josh Allen in the first two matchups, but we will have to see if that happens yet again. A new season also marks a new opportunity […]
full_text: The NFL scheduling has its quirks and in one of those quirks, the Texans and the Bills match up for the third season in a row. The Texans owned Josh Allen in the first two matchups, but we will have to see if that happens yet again. A new season also marks a new opportunity to catch up with our comrades at the other sites. Matthew Bynum has always been a joy to work with. We caught up with him to check in on the Bills before Sunday. Battle Red Blog: The Bills achieved a lot of success under Sean McDermott but it ultimately wasn’t enough. Why do you think he came up short? Matthew Bynum: Sean McDermott accomplished so much as head coach of the Bills that it feels a bit unfair to say he came up short. But he did, simply because his teams never did win an AFC Championship Game, nor play in or (better) win a Super Bowl. It’s a small but significant list of items McDermott didn’t check off after nine seasons. McDermott and general manager Brandon Beane built teams to take down the Kansas City Chiefs. Yet every time they faced KC in the playoffs, they lost despite Josh Allen playing out of his mind most of the time. McDermott came up short because he was never the best coach in playoff games against the Chiefs. That’s enough, and a lot, but that’s not all there is to it. A very demanding coach, McDermott’s defensive scheme relied on intelligence, both individually and as a unit. Players had to be system sound in their assignments at all times, or else disaster would strike. Yet there was also a focus on a player’s RAS score. That meant trying to make it all work with two often diametrically unique types of player skill sets — the heady leader, and the instinctual athletic freak. Sure, anyone coaching an NFL team would welcome superlatives from both arenas, but McDermott relied on players being able to excel from both buckets whether or not they were capable. Too often, McDermott’s defense proved to be the team’s playoff Achilles heel. Not always, and in no way is the offense’s failures in more than one playoff game’s final drive overlooked. But the head coach was a defensive mind and his units faltered in the biggest moments. Time also worked against McDermott. Nearly a decade at the helm is a long time in the NFL. The reason people remember long NFL tenures is because it’s so rare. But McDermott-coached teams hold the best regular-season record in that span. You don’t just move on from a guy because he didn’t get lucky enough to play and win a Super Bowl. Well, at least not until missing out becomes a trauma-filled trend. The Bills have a large number of catch phrases attached to their worst moments, and McDermott owns many of them. When someone mentions “13 seconds” anyone who follows the sport immediately drifts to Buffalo’s gut-wrenching overtime loss against the Kansas City Chiefs. Many thought a change should have been made after that loss. But a lot of leeway was given simply because it was Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes. It wasn’t yet time. The trouble is that things didn’t meaningfully improve with time. With Allen, McDermott’s teams were a perennial playoff participant, and a Super Bowl favorite. The postseason was expected, all but guaranteed. Yet McDermott never could find a way toward earning the one seed. His teams were always forced to play on Wild Card Weekend, to the detriment of a severely injured defensive roster. You’d think that if the playoffs appeared automatic, then a lot of effort would be spent on the team’s second season. But too often if felt like the only one who showed up to play was Allen. That’s unacceptable, no matter how good Allen is. They were dog-walked at home against the Cincinnati Bengals the year after 13 seconds — the same season Damar Hamlin almost died playing against those same Bengals. McDermott managed Hamlin’s trauma well, but that clearly didn’t extend into the postseason. By and large, he should be given a pass for that, but it’s the same game where the Diggs-Allen drama gained legs. Then there was the home loss to the Chiefs the next season, which saw McDermott settle for a field goal try that wouldn’t have given them a win anyway. Instead, Buffalo missed another kick wide right (yup), and an over-matched defense folded while allowing Mahomes and company to win its first road playoff game. Whatever a person believes or doesn’t about last season’s loss to the Broncos, the fact is that the Bills were short-handed on defense thanks to McDermott’s decision to play then-rookie cornerback Maxwell Hairston Week 18. That resulted in an injury for Hairston during the closing minutes, which kept him out of postseason play. Sean Payton diagnosed an obvious weakness following an injury to Tre’Davious White that had Dane Jackson playing for Hairston, and it resulted in a touchdown. It’s not McDermott’s fault that the referees saw things a certain way to call the game as they did. It’s McDermott’s fault that his defense was ill-equipped to overcome injury. If I had to guess what really happened on an acute level, it’s that McDermott probably lost the locker room. That was perhaps true years earlier (specifically Diggs), but it’s difficult to move on easily from a coach who’s automatic in the regular season. Then there’s what co-owner Terry Pegula mentioned, seeing Allen beside himself. It may be that he’d seen enough and decided the franchise’s most prolific player was beginning to run out of time due to wasted opportunities. BRB: It’s a new era of Bills football with a new coach and new stadium. What changes are you expecting under Joe Brady? MB: Well, we’ve been told that the vibe is more relaxed, looser at One Bills Drive. Brady is the youngest head coach in the NFL, and by all accounts he’s a player’s coach who brings a more youthful and energetic swagger. He also comes from Sean Payton’s school of hard knocks (yes, that’s a sleight Payton’s way). No Brady is not a direct clone of Payton, but it would be silly to think he won’t lean on Payton’s leadership example while trying to find his groove. He also has John Fox to help guide him, but Brady’s familiarity with the offense should benefit his transition. I don’t necessarily expect a huge dynamic shift on offense, and it’s likely we’ll have to wait and see what the offense abandons and adds to know where he and McDermott differed. How much do you change for an offense that just finished top-three in the NFL last season? I do expect to see running back James Cook III more involved in the passing game. He came out of college dubbed a bona fide dual-threat player, but for the most part his usage there has been as a distant second fiddle. Time will tell if Brady allows Allen to do as he pleases as a run, and if he leans more heavily into the types of west coast scheme Payton teaches. BRB: Obviously championship windows are about the quarterback. Can you make your best case for Josh Allen to return to MVP Allen? MB: I guess my move is to offer up that I see zero need for Allen to reascend to an MVP level simply because I still see him playing at that level. Without Allen, the Bills are fighting with the Jets for a spot in the AFC’s basement each season. Allen raises everyone’s play around him, which included a less-than-stellar wide receivers room last season. All that Buffalo needs is competent play around Allen come playoff time. Otherwise, any MVP-worthy season by Allen will once again be little more than a regular-season award. But to honor your ask here, I suppose I see Allen winning the MVP if he puts together a season similar to or better than his 2024 campaign, while guiding the team to greater success under a rookie head coach. BRB: The Bills and Texans have butted heads the last two years. Who are some new Bills that will make a dramatic impact on Sunday? MB: Hopefully everyone focused on the field at NRG becomes well-versed in wide receiver DJ Moore. He came to Buffalo by way of a trade with the Chicago Bears. To this point, the reviews have been tremendous,…

title: 10 NFL Insiders pick Texans to make Super Bowl
summary: Ignored. Slighted. Dogged. Dissed. Part of life as a Houston Texans fan is expecting a significant percentage of the national media to dismiss or poorly characterize the franchise. Superficial “research”, echo chamber’d fake news, old narratives and mountains made from molehills have been the way for a long time. But… 2026 feels… different. Texans head […]
full_text: CORPUS CHRISTI, TX - SEPTEMBER 06: The Houston Texans Mascot Toro waves a flag prior to the game between the Springfield Cardinals and the Corpus Christi Hooks at Whataburger Field on Sunday, September 6, 2026 in Corpus Christi, Texas. (Photo by Vanessa Buentello/Minor League Baseball via Getty Images) Ignored. Slighted. Dogged. Dissed. Part of life as a Houston Texans fan is expecting a significant percentage of the national media to dismiss or poorly characterize the franchise. Superficial “research”, echo chamber’d fake news, old narratives and mountains made from molehills have been the way for a long time. But… 2026 feels… different. Texans head coach Demeco Ryans and general manager Nick Caserio have quietly built 1 of, if not the , best cultures in the NFL. And, they’ve filled that culture with incredibly talented players. World class athletes who are fully bought in on the Texans Way. This is no longer “Patriots South”. It’s H-Town Baby! While those of us “in the know” have known the truth for some time, the rest of the world is finally waking up to the reality that this Texans team is as for real as it gets. Case in point: Every year, ESPN’s Bill Barnwell puts together a comprehensive set of predictions for the season outcome. ESPN.com (Bill Barnwell) My pick for 2026: In the playoffs (AFC South champions) The 2025 Texans became just the second team since 2002 to start 0-3 and still advance to the postseason, following in the footsteps of the 2018 Texans. And after that 0-3 start, they were as good as any team in football. Despite losing C.J. Stroud for a month, the Texans went 12-2, outscored their opponents by nearly nine points per game and led all defenses in points allowed per drive (1.5). Stroud melted down in the postseason, which is obviously a concern if it carries over into 2026, but he was better in the regular season than those playoff memories would suggest. He has been a solid-or-better starter without any semblance of a running game, and if the move to add David Montgomery behind a reconfigured offensive line finally unlocks the Texans on the ground, we could see something closer to the rookie-year version of Stroud this season. The combination of Stroud, a truly dominant defense and a relatively weak division gives Houston a high floor. While he flirts with the “C.J. Stroud sucks” narrative crowed by those not-in-the-know, the notion that this offense will look entirely different with a competent run game isn’t wrong. Where things really got well for H-Town fans is the post tacked to the end of Barnwell’s piece , credited to “ESPN Staff”. 64 NFL insiders surveyed about their picks for 2026-27 Super Bowl glory. 10 of which chose the Houston Texans to make the show. ESPN staff AFC winner “Stanford Steve” Coughlin, commentator and betting analyst: Texans Turron Davenport, Titans reporter: Texans Jeremy Fowler, national NFL reporter: Texans Dan Graziano, national NFL reporter: Texans Mike Kaye, Panthers reporter: Texans Jason McCourty, NFL analyst: Texans Jordan Raanan, Giants reporter: Texans Nate Taylor, Chiefs reporter: Texans Stan Verrett, anchor: Texans Nick Wagoner, 49ers reporter: Texans Notice a betting analyst, BESF reporter, Carolina Panthers (who joint-practiced with Houston this year) reporter, and a Kansas City Chiefs reporter picked H-Town to claim the AFC Championship crown. Next up, 3 picked the Texans to bring a Lombardi trophy to NRG: Coughlin: Texans Fowler: Texans Raanan: Texans Also intriguing, Coughlin, the betting analyst, chose Will Anderson Jr. as the regular season NFL MVP. Definitely long odds for any defender to win the MVP, but notable that a betting analyst, who knows all about odds, would choose that – and chose Anderson Jr. as the player to grab that brass ring. With only a few days to go before Kickoff 2026 and the 1st Houston Texans game of the year, what do you think about these predictions?

summary: Every fanbase wants their rookies to make an immediate impact, but that’s not always the case. full_text: HOUSTON, TX - AUGUST 20: Center Keylan Rutledge #66 of the Houston Texans readies for play during the NFL preseason game between the Houston Texans and the Las Vegas Raiders on August 20, 2026, at Reliant Stadium in Houston, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Every fanbase wants their rookies to make an immediate impact, but that’s not always the case. Sunday’s matchup against the Buffalo Bills will shine a light on the potential of this impressive rookie class. Seven of the eight rookies made the roster, a novelty in the Nick Caserio era. While only First-rounder Keylan Rutledge is projected to start, expect the rest of the class to make their mark on the big game in their own way. The Monday after the game I will follow up this article with a post recapping each rookie’s performance against the key stat they’ll be evaluated against below. Keylan Rutledge, OG – Round 1 Role : Starter Expectations : To handle the tall task…Welcome to the NFL. Your first assignment is blocking Ed Oliver and Deone Walker. Houston will know exactly what they have in their first-round pick Rutledge after week one. The rookie will be asked to gel with Evan Brown and Aireontae Ersery fast to protect Stroud in an early and incredibly important game. Key stat: Pressures allowed Kayden McDonald, DT – Round 2 Role : Stop the run on early downs, third-and-short, and in the redzone. Expectation: Little has been made of McDonald’s preseason play despite the high draft capital expended on the defensive tackle. Much should be made of McDonald being listed as the fifth DT on the initial depth chart. McDonad’s role will be more profound in the back half of the season as he develops into a new role and system. For the game against Buffalo, he’ll need to help temper RB James Cook and force the Bills offense into third and long situations. Key stat : Run stuffs Marlin Klein, TE – Round 2 Role : Blocking TE and explosive play option Expectation : Starting Sunday, either Klein’s doubters or staunch supporters will be validated. Don’t expect Klein to make a major impact in the pass game Week One. One to two catches maximum should be expected from the rookie TE. His impact o nthe play action game and run will hopefully unlock this offense and free up the playbook for OC Nick Caley. Key stat : Run blocking grade, explosive plays Febechi Nwaiwu, OG – Round 4 Role : Special teams blocker Expectation: Nwaiwu is not expected to start. He may not even make the game day roster given the number of lineman Houston kept on the 53-man roster. It would be great to get his feet wet in special teams for him to get NFL snaps. He’s nowhere near a ready prospect, but slow-rolling the lineman could give him the confidence to one day take over the guard role in Houston. Key stat: Special teams snaps Wade Woodaz, LB – Round 4 Role : Third linebacker Expectation: With the injuries to linebacker, Woodaz has been elevated to a more prominent role on the defense. Jake Hansen is back and practicing, but it’s Woodaz who is slated to be the extra LB in 4-3 defensive sets. Woodaz is the younger, more athletic prospect and is better suited to complement starters Henry T0’oTo’o and Azeez Al-Shaair. Woodaz could arguably play the second most snaps as a rookie against Buffalo. Key stat: Tackles Kamari Ramsey, S – Round 5 Role : Special teamer Expectation : Ideally, Kamari doesn’t see the field on defense as the designated backup safety. He should contribute on special teams kickoff, return, and punt. his speed and tackling make for a plus-special teamer, but there’s a chance he’s inactive on game day for more experienced options. Key stat: Special teams tackles Lewis Bond, WR – Round 6 N/A – Practice Squad Aiden Fisher, LB – Round 7 Role : Earn the 53-man roster spot Expectation : Most likely, he’s among the inactive players on game day. If he’s available, he’ll be exclusively a special teams asset. The Texans kept six linebackers and Fisher is the sixth of those players. Getting him on the field will be a test of his growth early. For now, his opportunity against the Bills will come on special teams. Key stat: Active on game day

title: Houston Texans stats: Welcome to Week 1 vs. the Bills
summary: Welcome back to another year of football. We at value of things have a tradition that we do every week. You will see two features on a weekly the basis. The first will usually be a post-mortem on the previous’s weeks games. That will come on Monday or Tuesday depending on when the game was […]
full_text: Welcome back to another year of football. We at value of things have a tradition that we do every week. You will see two features on a weekly the basis. The first will usually be a post-mortem on the previous’s weeks games. That will come on Monday or Tuesday depending on when the game was played. We will include the relevant numbers from the game and either a great, good, and bad in victory or good, bad, and ugly in defeat. Then, later in the week you will see “By the numbers.” It is a simple look at the rankings on offense and defense to give us some idea of what each team will try to attack in the upcoming game. Early season games are difficult at best. Small sample sizes are the enemy of good analysis and a look at the previous season’s numbers is often even less significant. However, it is all we got in the early going. Obviously, we could do a huge deep dive into numbers and as much as I love deep dives, we want to keep this relatively simple so that everyone can digest it well. Below is a table of how each team ranked in passing yards, rushing yards, and passing yards defended, and rushing yards defended. It isn’t perfect and I know regular commenters will beg for more. We might get there in subsequent looks, but really this is what we have going in. Texans Bills Rushing Yards 22nd 1st Passing Yards 14th 15th Def Rushing Yards 4th 28th Def Passing Yards 6th 1st Keep in mind that all numbers have a context and they often play against each other in what Bill O’Brien used to lovingly call “complimentary football.” Being in the top of the league or bottom of the league in total yards in rushing or passing is not necessarily an indicator of anything by itself. For instance, the Bills struggled against the run, so teams just didn’t pass as much against them. They didn’t need to. On the flip side, when you are in the top ten in both categories (as the Texans are) then that means you have a really good overall defense. I know I’m not breaking any new ground here. What will the Bills offense try to do? It seems counterintuitive sometimes when you have a former league MVP at quarterback, but the key to the Bills offense is their rushing attack. Obviously, Josh Allen is a huge part of that. Still, if the Bills can run the football without Allen then they will be stay ahead of the sticks and keep the Texans’ pass rush at bay. Obviously, the Texans have been effective at stopping the run and some new defensive additions aim to get even better in that department. Allen has been harassed in two games against the defense and if they have to rely on his right arm to move the football it could be a long day for him again. What will the Bills defense try to do? It’s probably simple enough to say that whichever team runs the football most effectively will win the game. This is the weakness of the Bills’ defense, but it is something they hope they have addressed effectively in the offseason. Historically, the Texans have not been effective running the football, so this is a historical contest between two weak links to see which one has the upper hand. What will the Texans offense try to do? This is simple. They have to run the football effectively. That means converting on third and short and fourth and short to keep the sticks moving. If they are able to do that they will win the time of possession battle and keep their defense fresh. A fresh defense means more harassment and it means a more desperate Bills attack that will take chances. The numbers above don’t really capture the whole truth on the Texans history of running the football. They have been inconsistent from game to game in the past and the preseason didn’t show much as we did not see a lot of the starters. It is the biggest unknown of the entire offseason. What will the Texans defense try to do? This one is also simple. If the Texans can make the Bills one-dimensional then they will have a feast day again. The key is keeping them behind the sticks and keeping Allen bottled up in the pocket. History has shown that he will take chances and sometimes gets burned by those chances. Getting key turnovers in the game obviously feeds right into that offensive philosophy above. In particular, look for J.D. Clowney to play a key role in setting the edge on rushing plays when he is in the game. He gives the Texans a dimension they did not have in the last couple of seasons.

title: Here’s how the Colts can start 1-0
summary: 1-0 is a great sight for NFL fans. It is the validation that your hopes and dreams might be well placed. It also starts a team on the right track statistically to make the postseason and avoids the dreaded 0-2 hole to start the season. It isn’t a panacea, as things can go sideways, but […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - OCTOBER 11: Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts celebrates a touchdown during the first quarter in a game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on October 11, 2021 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Rob Carr/Getty Images) | Getty Images 1-0 is a great sight for NFL fans. It is the validation that your hopes and dreams might be well placed. It also starts a team on the right track statistically to make the postseason and avoids the dreaded 0-2 hole to start the season. It isn’t a panacea, as things can go sideways, but it feels pretty good. Here is how the Indianapolis Colts can get it done. The Ravens are a good team, so it won’t be an easy task. The Colts have some advantages, however. The home crowd will be back and ready. It hasn’t always translated into Week One wins, but the confines of Lucas Oil are much more advantageous than a road opener. The Colts are also trending towards good health. Daniel Jones is back, and Alec Pierce should be ready as well. The bumps and bruises of camp are also healing for Tyler Warren and Josh Downs. Jonathan Taylor is the bell cow, and the Ravens will have their hands full trying to contain him. If the Colts can establish the run game early, Taylor may prove to be too much for the Ravens late. A lot of Sunday’s success will come down to how well the defense contains Lamar Jackson. Jackson is electric. If they can keep him in the pocket, though, that electricity falls a few wattages. Speaking of a bell cow, Derrick Henry is in the backfield for the Ravens. Stopping the dual threat of he and Jackson will be tough, but it’s also the key to victory. The defense has some question marks. Veterans have returned to form, but the effectiveness of the line remains in the air. Young linebackers will be tested as well. If those units rise to the occasion, they can keep the Colts’ offense in position to win. Looking back at Week Ones for the Colts is troubling, so let’s not look back too far. How about one year? The Colts got off to a hot start by using the momentum of a win to start the season. The offense needs to find the footing that was lost in the back half of 2025, and the Colts need to control the line of scrimmage on defense. Do those things and the Colts will start 2026 with that coveted 1-0.

title: Ex-Colts CB Jaylon Jones reportedly signs with AFC South rival
summary: According to NFL Insider Jordan Schultz, the Tennessee Titans have signed former Indianapolis Colts cornerback Jaylon Jones, who reunites with his ex-defensive coordinator Gus Bradley in the Music City: Although he went unclaimed off league waivers, it only seemed like a matter of time before another NFL club would take a chance on the 24-year […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 08: Jaylon Jones #40 of the Indianapolis Colts reacts in the game against the Tennessee Titans at Lucas Oil Stadium on October 08, 2023 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to NFL Insider Jordan Schultz, the Tennessee Titans have signed former Indianapolis Colts cornerback Jaylon Jones, who reunites with his ex-defensive coordinator Gus Bradley in the Music City: The #Titans have signed former Colts CB Jaylon Jones, who started 29 games over his first three NFL seasons. The move reunites Jones with former Colts DC Gus Bradley. pic.twitter.com/rkAewtSSP3 — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) September 10, 2026 Although he went unclaimed off league waivers, it only seemed like a matter of time before another NFL club would take a chance on the 24-year old Jones, who was a former two-year starting cornerback for the Colts. Originally a 2023 7th round pick of Indianapolis, the 6,’2”, 203 pound cornerback’s early Colts career got off to a fast start, as he started in 27 games over his first two seasons—and had 2 interceptions during that same span. However, with veteran defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo’s arrival last year, Jones was miscast and less of a natural fit in his coverage scheme. He appeared in 10 games last season for the Colts, making 2 starts. While he played decently well this past preseason, he was playing late in the second half of games, meaning that he was squarely on the roster bubble. Even though he survived initial final 53-man roster cuts, he didn’t last on the Colts roster much longer, as Indy recently elected to carry backup offensive tackle Luke Tenuta instead. Jones had some initial success under Bradley, and it’s only logical that he reunites with the ex-Colts defensive coordinator, albeit with one of Indianapolis’ longtime AFC South rivals.

Safety AJ Haulcy (ankle) was limited at practice. Haulcy was was named a starter on the Colts latest unofficial depth chart, returned to practice after missing multiple during the final few weeks of pre-season training. Haulcy may be one who doesn’t manage to be full fit for the season opener but a limited practice on a Wednesday is still promising for his availability. Wide receiver Alec Pierce (heel) was also a limited participant at practice. Pierce missed pretty much the entire pre-season due to a lingering heel injury that required surgery pre-training camp. However he has managed to take part in practices the last week or so prior to the game week 1. Pierce is looking positive in terms of his availability for Sundays game. Tight end Drew Ogletree (neck) and Center Sedrick Van Pran-Granger (illness) were also limited participants at training. Van Pran-Granger was a last pre-season addition via trade with the Buffalo Bills to sure up the depth at center after the Colts lost free agent Danny Pinter to the Baltimore Ravens during free agency.

title: It took one series for Anthony Richardson to see his future with the Colts
summary: The first game of the NFL season is special. The NFL diluted it by moving the 22-year standard Thursday opener to Wednesday to fit a Netflix only special in on Thursday to squeeze more money out of its fans, but that’s a story for another time. Regardless, the home opener for the defending Super Bowl champs is […]
full_text: The first game of the NFL season is special. The NFL diluted it by moving the 22-year standard Thursday opener to Wednesday to fit a Netflix only special in on Thursday to squeeze more money out of its fans, but that’s a story for another time. Regardless, the home opener for the defending Super Bowl champs is always electric. With all that energy bouncing around, it didn’t take long for a quiet hush to fall over the festivities. With it, Anthony Richardson saw his future with the Colts. Sam Darnold was the bottom of the barrel until he became the top of the heap. He was a quarterback that the Jets couldn’t wait to unload after a disastrous tenure as the franchise quarterback. Yes, it took him leaving to find his footing, but a resurgence in Minnesota, followed by the greatest achievement in the game with Seattle, found him as the toast of the town and the entire league. On the first drive of the game, Darnold injured his hip and didn’t return to the field. Drew Lock stepped in and led the Seahawks to victory. That is the perfect example of how things can change in the NFL. The MRI for Darnold looks good, but it could have been bad, really bad. While Richardson isn’t rooting for Daniel Jones to get injured, it isn’t out of the realm of possibility that Jones misses time this season. It simply seems to be his M.O. If that happens, Richardson will be thrust into the spotlight with a chance to turn his career around. Darnold lasted one series, so that chance could present itself at any time. That should be enough of a glimpse into his Colts’ future to provide the motivation to be ready at a moment’s notice. Ideally, for the Colts, Anthony Richardson won’t see much time this season. That means Daniel Jones stays healthy and upright. That isn’t guaranteed, however. Sam Darnold lasted five plays. No one saw that coming. Whether one sees it coming or not, Richardson should be ready for that very scenario. Wednesday was the best glimpse he could have into his future with the Colts.
author: Jon Spradley

title: 5 Questions with Dawgs By Nature: Containing KC Concepcion is Priority No. 1
summary: As the Jacksonville Jaguars prepare to face the Cleveland Browns in Week 1, we exchanged questions with Chris Pokorny of Dawgs by Nature to learn more about the opposing side. Question 1: The Browns have a brutal QB situation and traded away a legendary defender. Do you expect Cleveland to still be competitive this season, […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - MAY 27: KC Concepcion #1 of the Cleveland Browns looks on during the Cleveland Browns OTA Offseason Workouts at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on May 27, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images As the Jacksonville Jaguars prepare to face the Cleveland Browns in Week 1, we exchanged questions with Chris Pokorny of Dawgs by Nature to learn more about the opposing side. Question 1: The Browns have a brutal QB situation and traded away a legendary defender. Do you expect Cleveland to still be competitive this season, or has the race for Arch Manning already begun? If the Browns had just received draft picks only, then it would have been a clear signal that the race for Arch Manning (or whatever quarterback) has already begun. But, the fact that Jared Verse was part of the deal was huge, and reportedly the only reason Cleveland agreed to it. Granted, Myles Garrett is in a league of his own as a two-time defensive MVP, but the fact of the matter is that Cleveland consistently had losing seasons even with his talent. Verse allows the team to still maintain a solid presence at his vacancy, and the defense in general still has the rest of the pieces that has made it successful over the years, including not allowing a 300+ yard passer in…I think it’s been 45 games? Cleveland’s defense will allow them to be competitive on any given Sunday, but the big question mark is how the offense will perform, which I’ll try to touch on more in your other questions below. Question 2: If we disregard final standings/draft order, what would a successful 2026 season look like for the Browns? A successful season for Cleveland would be if the offensive line builds some chemistry together, the young wide receivers look worthy of the draft spots they were taken, and the team has crystal-clear clarity as to how their quarterback situation will be handled next offseason. That could involve Shedeur Sanders (at some point) getting a chance to start and blowing people away, or it could involve Deshaun Watson continuing to be a liability and everyone confirming that “Cleveland is right there in terms of contention, but now we can use as many draft assets as we need to for drafting a quarterback in 2027.” Question 3: What are your expectations for first-time head coach Todd Monken? Have there been any positive or negative signs this offseason? Todd Monken seems to be in a unique position where this is going to be his only shot at being a head coach in the NFL. Even if he doesn’t say it, he knows that Cleveland could be transformed with a new quarterback next year, so if he wants to be part of that, the team needs to play relatively well. The quarterback play holding the team back will not be a red mark on him. If he makes dumb coaching decisions and the team loses motivation quickly, then he’ll be kicked to the curb and there will be no qualms about starting over next offseason. In general, he’s been fine this offseason. We’ve seen elements of the Ravens’ offense incorporated, and he’s inheriting a solid defense. He often talks candidly and has fun stories to listen to. The only thing that somewhat irked me earlier this offseason was during the quarterback competition, Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders would alternate first-team reps every other practice. Prior to one practice, Monken clearly said Sanders was going to get the first-team reps that day, but then when practice started, Watson got all of the reps instead, which made the media go into a frenzy about what it meant. The next day, when Monken was asked about it, he essentially said he changed his mind to balance things out and didn’t need to update the media. Which, on one hand I understand, but it just seems weird to switch it up so close to practice starting — like, shouldn’t that have been well-decided already? Question 4: What problems could the Browns pose for the Jaguars this week? The Swiss Army knife utilization of KC Concepcion can be a problem. Taken in the first round, we heard some good and bad things about him. But, through all of training camp and the preseason, this guy looks like he has that “it” factor. He has caught everything . He is effective on jet sweeps. He can be used on any route, he can stretch the field, he can return punts. He looks like the type of player who could be an instant Pro Bowler, and he was having success in camp regardless of what quarterback is throwing him the ball. Watching him is by far the No. 1 thing I’m eager to see at the beginning of the regular season, because we’ve seen this tremendous offseason, and now I want to see that it transforms to regular season action. Cleveland’s defense is also poised to remain a problem. Their defensive front has several top-tier players, and their secondary remains consistent. Having a new defensive coordinator, we still don’t know if the unit will suffer any dropoff from that, but I’m banking on them remaining a well-oiled machine. Question 5: Do you expect the Browns to cover as 8.5-point underdogs , and do you have a favorite player prop for the game? There are times when Cleveland can fall apart later in games from a snowball effect of negativity, but for as bad as they were last year, they still remained highly competitive in a lot of games. The Browns’ entire offensive line from last year is either retired, out of the league, or a backup on other teams in 2026, and the Browns went out and got five new starters. That could be a disaster in terms of chemistry, but also, it can’t get any worse than last year. With that improvement, plus a significant upgrade at wide receiver, the Browns have more pieces to be a better team than they were a year ago. The quarterback position might continue to hold them back from being a playoff team, but they should easily be right in these games, so I’d take the Browns to cover the 8.5-point spread. With how much I hyped up WR KC Concepcion above, I think it’s a solid bet to take the over on the 33.5 receiving yards for him. Thanks to Chris for taking the time to answer our questions. full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - JANUARY 04: Cole van Lanen #70 of the Jacksonville Jaguars is attended to by medical staff during the fourth quarter against the Tennessee Titans at EverBank Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars open their season at home Sunday against the Cleveland Browns, looking to build on a playoff berth a year ago and take the next step toward Super Bowl contention. But the road there got a little bumpier during training camp, where a rash of injuries resulted in most projected starters being held out of game action all preseason, leaving Jacksonville with potentially some game speed concerns heading into Week 1. Injuries have been a storyline all week for both sides. With Wednesday’s practice complete, here’s where things stand heading into Sunday: Jaguars Injury Report WR Jakobi Meyers – Thumb – Limited OT Cole Van Lanen – Knee – Limited RB LeQuint Allen Jr. – Hip – DNP Meyers jammed his thumb during a joint practice with the Panthers and sat out the following week’s joint sessions with the Buccaneers, but he’s listed as a limited participant and is expected to play. V an Lanen, recently activated off PUP , is still working back from the knee injury he suffered in Week 18 of last season — he too is limited in practice with hopes of suiting up. Allen Jr. has not practiced since suffering a soft-tissue hip injury a couple of weeks ago. Head coach Liam Coen said Wednesday that both Van Lanen and Allen Jr. will be game-time decisions. LeQuint Allen Jr. and Cole Van Lanen are both set to be game time decisions this Sunday pic.twitter.com/EDpZJ91vae — SleeperJaguars (@SleeperJaguars) September 9, 2026 Browns Injury Report C Parker Brailsford – Thumb – Limited DT Maliek Collins – Quad – Limited G Teven Jenkins – Back – Limited LB Carson Schwesinger – Shoulder – Full Participant On the opponent’s side, Browns starting right guard Teven Jenkins got tangled up during a practice drill on Wednesday and left practice with trainers. Schwesinger, who missed much of training camp with a shoulder injury, returned as a full participant on Friday. Collins has been managing a quad issue throughout the week. All three Browns are expected to play Sunday. The trio of Jaguars players on the mid-week injury report carry real weight for this game, so it’ll be interesting to see how things progress as we end the week. Which of the three Jaguars do you think is the most important for the results of Sunday’s contest?

summary: Regular season football is here, and I could not be more excited! The Jaguars kickoff the 2026 season at home against the Cleveland Browns. full_text: CLEVELAND - DECEMBER 19: Offensive lineman Ben Coleman #62 of the Jacksonville Jaguars blocks against the Cleveland Browns at Cleveland Browns Stadium on December 19, 1999 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by George Gojkovich/Getty Images) | Getty Images Regular season football is here, and I could not be more excited! The Jaguars kickoff the 2026 season at home against the Cleveland Browns . The former AFC Central Division rivals have played each other 20 times, and Jacksonville currently lead the series 12-8. Let’s take a trip down memory lane and look at the Jags beating Cleveland at home through the decades. The 1990s Week 6 on October 17, 1999 Final score: Browns 7 – Jaguars 24 Attendance: 62,047 The Jaguars recorded 21 first downs, 325 net yards, and a 32:24 time of possession, compared to the Browns’ 16 first downs, 243 net yards, and 27:36 time of possession. Kyle Brady and James Stewart both scored a touchdown. Mark Brunell completed 12 out of 19 attempted passes for 109 yards. James Stewart led the team with 58 rushing yards, and Keenan McCardell led with 76 receiving yards. Mike Hollis made the three attempted field goals. Kevin Hardy, James Roberson, Joel Smeenge, and Gary Walker sacked Tim Couch four times for a loss of 31 yards. The 2000s Week 14 on December 3, 2000 Final score: Browns 0 – Jaguars 48 Attendance: 51,262 Jacksonville dominated this game with 28 first downs, 449 total net yards, and 37:11 time of possession, and while Cleveland had a 22:49 time of possession, their two first downs and 53 total net yards could not compare. Fred Taylor scored three touchdowns, and Keenan McCardell, Mark Brunell, and Shyrone Stith each scored one. Mark Brunell completed 15 out of 31 attempted passes for 165 yards and was sacked twice for a loss of 13 yards. Fred Taylor led the team with 181 rushing yards, and Jimmy Smith led with 104 receiving yards. Mike Hollis made both attempted field goals. Kevin Hardy, Donovin Darius, Rob Meier, Joel Smeenge, Tony Brackens, Brant Boyer, and Gary Walker sacked Spergon Wynn and Doug Pederson collectively six times for a loss of 42 yards. Hardy led the team with seven tackles. The 2010s Week 7 on October 19, 2014 Final score: Browns 6 – Jaguars 24 Attendance: 61,341 Allen Robinson, Denard Robinson, and Storm Johnson scored touchdowns. Blake Bortles completed 17 out of 31 attempted passes for 159 yards. Denard Robinson led the team with 127 rushing yards, and Allen Robinson led with 60 receiving yards. Ace Sanders averaged 10.25 yards in punt returns. Bryan Anger punted eight times for 345 yards, and Josh Scobee made the attempted field goal. Telvin Smith had a 15-yard interception. Smith, Paul Posluszny, and Chris Clemons recorded sacks. Posluszny led the team with 12 combined tackles. The 2020s Hopefully this is the year. title: Chiefs-Broncos: 5 Questions with the Enemy before Week 1 battle
summary: On Monday Night, the Kansas City Chiefs face the Denver Broncos. We welcome Ian St. Clair of Mile High Report — our sister SB Nation site covering the Broncos— for Five Questions with the Enemy. Make sure you’re following Mile High Report in the SB Nation App in the lead-up to the Week 1 bout. […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 16: Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) meets Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) on the field after a game between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on November 16, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On Monday Night, the Kansas City Chiefs face the Denver Broncos. We welcome Ian St. Clair of Mile High Report — our sister SB Nation site covering the Broncos— for Five Questions with the Enemy . Make sure you’re following Mile High Report in the SB Nation App in the lead-up to the Week 1 bout. Download the app to your Apple device here , or to Android here . 1. Although Nix has said that he feels normal and has no limitations, how has he looked throughout training camp and the preseason? Do you expect him to be 100% against Kansas City, particularly when using his mobility outside the pocket? Based on reports from Broncos training camp and the limited action he played in the preseason against the Green Bay Packers , Nix looks fantastic. Nix will be 100% for the Monday night opener with zero limitations in anything he does, in the pocket or his mobility out of it. He’s going to be incredibly motivated for this game. 2. Was last season the beginning of a championship window the Broncos can sustain, or did it raise expectations to the point that anything short of a Super Bowl appearance would feel disappointing? It’s both. Denver returns 21 of 22 starters from that team, while adding Jaylen Waddle on offense. The Broncos have one of the best defenses in the NFL, and adding Waddle and Davis Webb as the new offensive play caller will help Nix and the offense be better and more consistent this season. The championship window is open in Denver, but anything less than a Super Bowl appearance will feel disappointing. The fact that the Broncos were so close will motivate this year’s team to take the next step. 3. Denver’s defense ranked second in total defense and third in scoring defense last season while leading the NFL in sacks for the second consecutive year. With most of the core returning under Vance Joseph, do you expect this unit to maintain that standard, take another step forward, or experience some regression in 2026? Look for the Broncos defense to take another step forward and be even more dominant. Creating turnovers is one area they struggled with last season. Joseph has made that an offseason emphasis. Denver will always be able to get after the quarterback; adding turnovers to the equation will make that unit even tougher and, in return, make the offense better. 4. Despite last season’s 14-3 record and deep playoff run, what is your biggest concern about the Broncos entering 2026—and why could that issue prevent them from returning to the AFC Championship Game? The biggest concern remains what it’s been the last few seasons: middle linebacker. I’m just not sold on either Alex Singleton or Justin Strnad. These guys are glorified special teamers. The reason they’re not exposed more is because of how deep and talented the rest of Denver’s defense is. Clearly, Sean Payton and George Paton feel differently. As long as these two don’t get in the way, it won’t prevent the defense from being one of the NFL’s best or the Broncos from returning to the AFC Championship Game. 5. Kansas City has made a clear commitment to improving its running game, headlined by the addition of reigning Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III. How well equipped is Denver’s defense to handle a more physical and balanced Chiefs offense, and what will be the key to containing Walker without giving Patrick Mahomes favorable opportunities through play action? The Chiefs bring serious questions at both tackle positions to a game where Denver can bring consistent pressure up the middle and on the edges. Add in that Denver has the best secondary in the NFL, led by the best cornerback in the league, and it comes down to the trenches. The Broncos know that if they stop the run, it limits what KC can do offensively.

title: Andy Reid reaffirms the Chiefs’ confidence in rookie Kahlil Benson
summary: When the Kansas City Chiefs host the Denver Broncos on the season opener of “Monday Night Football” to close Week 1, all indications are that rookie Kahlil Benson will start at left tackle. Starter Josh Simmons has been out of action since midway through training camp with a lower back ailment. Simmons missed this week’s […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: Offensive tackle Kahlil Benson #70 of the Kansas City Chiefs watches NFL preseason game action in the fourth quarter against the Los Angeles Rams at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the Kansas City Chiefs host the Denver Broncos on the season opener of “Monday Night Football” to close Week 1, all indications are that rookie Kahlil Benson will start at left tackle. Starter Josh Simmons has been out of action since midway through training camp with a lower back ailment. Simmons missed this week’s initial practice on Thursday. The decision is curious in that Benson went undrafted in April — and only signed with Kansas City after trying out at the team’s rookie camp. Also, the former Indiana and Colorado talent never took a snap at left tackle in college. Benson has played almost exclusively on the right side both at tackle and guard. Speaking before Thursday’s practice, head coach Andy Reid expressed confidence in Benson’s ability to hold down the fort for Simmons. Reid also defers to his own years of experience and that of the coaching staff. “He’s done a nice job for us,” Reid remarked of the rookie. “He’s obviously shown us that he has the ability to play, and we wouldn’t put him in there if we didn’t think that. “We’ve all been through that. I think when we first got hired, we thought we probably were pretty good at it. So, I want his confidence to be that and go out and play and just use his abilities and write a good story.” "Kahlil Benson has proven, at least in preseason up against what Spags has put out there in training camp, that he's held up pretty good." – @BaldyNFL on the undrafted rookie potentially starting at left tackle for the Chiefs (via @PatMcAfeeShow ) pic.twitter.com/UGnwbK95h6 — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) September 10, 2026 Benson will be tasked with protecting star quarterback Patrick Mahomes, who is expected to see his first game action on Monday since tearing multiple knee ligaments in December. A decade of NFL experience has taught Mahomes to be ready when backups are on the field. He trusts that Benson will get the job done — and the possible downgrade on the offensive line does not change his own responsibilities. “Either way,” said Mahomes on Thursday, “you’ve got to roll. That’s the beauty of football is that it’s next man up, and you have to go up there and compete. These guys have gotten a ton of reps in training camp. They’ve gotten a ton of reps throughout their entire life, and they’re going out and living their dream as well. “So, I’ve got trust in anyone that the coaches put out there, because I know that they’ve worked their tail off to be at that spot. There’ll be mistakes here and there, but at the end of the day, you’ve got to go out there and trust those guys and make the plays whenever the plays need to be made.”

NFL Week 1 latest intel, buzz questions, news, fantasy tips | ESPN Which player returning from a significant injury is best set up for a strong comeback? Graziano: Let’s start with the biggest name: Mahomes. He tore the ACL in his left knee late enough last season that many wondered if he’d play at all in the early part of the 2026 season. But it was clear early in camp that he attacked his rehab and would be ready to go in Week 1. We should see him Monday night against the Broncos, and though the injury to left tackle Josh Simmons does give me a little pause, I think there’s reason to believe the Chiefs’ offense will be better around Mahomes. Around the NFL Sean McVay calls loss to 49ers a ‘good humbling day’ | NFL.com “I always look inside-out,” McVay said. “I didn’t do a good enough job getting us ready to go. There were some opportunities where maybe the game could have flipped, but they deserved the win. They were ready to go. And we’ll look at it. We’ll see where we can improve and be better moving forward. “But this is a good humbling day. This is what can sometimes happen in sports. I love this locker room and, you know, the first thing that I’m going to look at is myself, and I have to do a better job for a group collectively, with our coaches, with our players, and we’ll look at this film, and we’ll get back to work because, clearly, that’s obviously what we’ve got to do, and sometimes sports can humble you, and today was one of those days.” Source: Patriots’ A.J. Brown likely out at least 4 weeks | ESPN The Patriots can expect to be without Brown for the Sept. 20 home opener against the Pittsburgh Steelers, then road games against the Jacksonville Jaguars (Sept. 27) and Buffalo Bills (Oct. 4). New England then has back-to-back home games against the Las Vegas Raiders (Oct. 11) and New York Jets (Oct. 18). X-rays did not reveal a fracture. “I know he’ll do everything that he can to get back as quickly as possible,” Vrabel said before the results of the MRI were known. Sam Darnold avoided serious injury, timetable still unclear, Mike Macdonald says | The Athletic “I don’t know yet,” Macdonald said. “In my mind, I’m kind of thinking Drew is going to play.” The coach did not have an update at a news conference Thursday afternoon, saying the team was still working through its plan. “The silver lining is we have some extra time here. We’ll kind of get things back up and running on Monday,” Macdonald said. “Hopefully by then, we’ll have a really accurate picture of the plan of attack and what we’ll do (in Arizona).” In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Clark Hunt reveals Chiefs likely won’t call new stadium ‘Arrowhead’ Speaking to FOX4 , Hunt responded to a question about the iconic name of Arrowhead Stadium as it relates to the team’s new stadium being built in Kansas City, Kansas, where the Chiefs are scheduled to start playing home games in 2031. “I don’t think we’ll call it Arrowhead, but we wanted to make sure there were enough elements in the design that reminds every fan who has attended a game at Arrowhead about what a great stadium that is. We really want to honor the legacy of Arrowhead and we know how important Arrowhead is to our fans.” In the new stadium, the Chiefs’ owner expressed the desire to have a facility that “can last 50 or 60 years” and “help us host big events, like a Super Bowl, in Kansas City or a World Cup when [it] comes back.” From The Feed Follow Arrowhead Pride on Social Media Facebook: Like our page Instagram: @ArrowheadPride X: Follow @ArrowheadPride AP Staff on X: See complete list

title: It will be hard for Patrick Mahomes not to be himself in Week 1
summary: It’s always good advice, no matter the circumstance in life, to just be yourself. Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, cleared to play in Week 1 after recovering from knee surgery this offseason, doesn’t feel there is any other option ahead of his first game back. Within 48 hours of tearing his ACL and LCL […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - OCTOBER 27: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs celebrates during an NFL football game against the Washington Commanders at Arrowhead Stadium on October 27, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s always good advice, no matter the circumstance in life, to just be yourself. Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, cleared to play in Week 1 after recovering from knee surgery this offseason, doesn’t feel there is any other option ahead of his first game back. Within 48 hours of tearing his ACL and LCL last December, Mahomes was through surgery and starting rehabilitation, locking in the mindset to heal as quickly as possible and as early as possible. So when the star quarterback drops back to pass against the Denver Broncos on “Monday Night Football,” it shouldn’t shock anyone if Mahomes plays like himself. He spoke with local media about the subject ahead of practice on Thursday. “I think it’s going to be hard for me to not just be myself once I step on the field,” Mahomes said at the podium. “If you saw me in training camp, the moment stuff started happening, I just became a competitor.” ⏰ @PatrickMahomes pic.twitter.com/kAJam8O9NN — Kansas City Chiefs (@Chiefs) September 10, 2026 Whether it was keeping the ball on an option play or attempting to execute a downfield block during practice, the two-time MVP never gave offseason spectators an indication that he would be unavailable for the season opener. “I’ll try not to lay any blocks, hopefully — unless it’s needed,” Mahomes said. “But other than that, I’m going to go out there and be myself and play football. We’ve built up all this strength over the offseason for that, so why not maximize it?” “I’m going to keep myself out of harm’s way like I always will, not try to take big hits and stuff like that, but I’m a competitor,” Mahomes clarified. “I signed up for this, and I’m going to go out there and play football. That’s how I’ve always rolled, no matter what it is, and that’s probably how I’ll be the rest of my career.” The 30-year-old gunslinger was driving the point home: he didn’t work around the clock all offseason to be a limited version of himself once he could take the field. Mahomes was kept out of all preseason action because, according to head coach Andy Reid, he was not fully cleared. Now he is. And with the Arrowhead lights beaming on the red of his helmet Monday evening, facing the reigning AFC West champions, the injury report will be far from No. 15’s mind when the pocket collapses and no receiver is immediately available. Mahomes’ adrenaline rush to move the chains in a big spot will mask any preconceived worries about his knee. “That’s what makes me who I am is that I just love competing,” Mahomes reiterated. “Playing quarterback is one thing, but you have to love competing to have success in this league.” Whether the goal is to get through the day of rehabilitation or get a win over the Broncos, the three-time Super Bowl champion has the same mindset: be himself. “It was a long process,” Mahomes said. “But we’re here now, and now I get to go out there and be myself.” Classic walk off from Patrick Mahomes at his press conference today. “Hopefully I’m done with questions about the leg.” pic.twitter.com/8QK07yDo0n — Matt Derrick (@mattderrick) September 10, 2026

title: 5 bold Chiefs predictions from the Arrowhead Pride staff
summary: They say fortune favors the bold. The Kansas City Chiefs have certainly been bold through the years, from trading away veteran quarterback Alex Smith to start Patrick Mahomes to trading away All-Pro wide receiver Tyreek Hill in his prime. The organization has three Super Bowl trophies to show for it. So now it’s time for […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 28: A general view of the football field prior to the NFL 2025 game between Baltimore Ravens and Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on September 28, 2025 in Kansas City, United States. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images They say fortune favors the bold. The Kansas City Chiefs have certainly been bold through the years, from trading away veteran quarterback Alex Smith to start Patrick Mahomes to trading away All-Pro wide receiver Tyreek Hill in his prime. The organization has three Super Bowl trophies to show for it. So now it’s time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to be bold. Here are five bold predictions about the Chiefs’ 2026 season: Rocky Magana The Chiefs hold opposing teams to under 280 yards from scrimmage per game. For reference, this would put the Chiefs in the echelons of the Denver Broncos and Houston Texans in 2025. But with the addition of a young pass rusher like R Mason Thomas, and a blue chip cornerback in Masoor Delane (who I think will be a multi-time All Pro recipient in his career), along with the return of L’Jarius Sneed and the addition of Alohi Gillman, I think this defense takes the big step from being good, to great this season. I think the Chiefs are going to win a lot of one-score games this year, and the defense slamming the door shut on opponents will be the reason why. Dakota Watson For the first time since 2017, the Chiefs will have a 1,000-yard rusher AND receiver. It is astounding that during the era of quarterback Patrick Mahomes, the Chiefs have never had a 1,000-yard rusher. That streak comes to an end with the signing of running back Kenneth Walker and with Mahomes coming off an injury, a (hopefully) more balanced attack. The last 1,000 yard rusher for the Chiefs was Kareem Hunt in 2017. The bold part of this prediction, is that the Chiefs will also have one wide receiver attain 1,000 yards. The last Chiefs’ receiver to reach 1,000 yards was Tyreek Hill in 2021. It’s time for both these ugly streaks to come to an end. Caleb James The Chiefs will lead the NFL in rushing yards. After multiple seasons of neglecting to develop running backs and putting a stunning lack of resources into acquiring them, the Chiefs signed the best free agent possible this offseason and also drafted a highly touted player. The endgame? Run the damn ball. Kenneth Walker showed the world a glimpse of who he can be in the playoffs this past season, and rookie running back Emmett Johnson has all the skills to develop into a star and to help the team hold a lethal one-two punch. This is what the interior of the offensive line was built for, and even with stability issues at tackle that could hurt the team in pass protection, Andy Reid is still savvy enough to scheme open runs as long as center Creed Humphrey and right guard Trey Smith blow open holes in the middle. Walker should come close to leading the NFL in rushing yards, and Johnson should have a very productive rookie season. Look for Walker to go over 1,300 yards, and Johnson to come close to 800 on the ground. Maurice Elston The Chiefs will finish the season top 5 among NFL teams in interceptions Kansas City recorded only 10 interceptions last season, ranking 22nd in the NFL, but its rebuilt secondary possesses greater ball-production potential. Cornerbacks Nohl Williams and rookie Mansoor Delane have demonstrated strong ball skills. Williams tied for the Chiefs’ lead with seven passes defended as a rookie while earning a 75.6 PFF coverage grade and allowing completions on only 37.1% of his targets. In his final college season, he led the FBS with seven interceptions and recorded 16 passes defended. Delane finished his final season at LSU with 13 passes defended, including 11 breakups and two interceptions, despite opponents rarely challenging him. The addition of safety Alohi Gilman also gives Kansas City a veteran safety with five career interceptions, compared with Bryan Cook’s three, while Chamarri Conner’s move into a more traditional safety role should create further opportunities. Ron Kopp Jr. Two Chiefs will finish in the top 5 of Defensive Rookie of the Year voting In 2025, the Atlanta Falcons had two rookies finish within the top 5 of votes for the NFL AP Defensive Rookie of the Year award: edge rusher James Pearce and defensive back Xavier Watts. I believe the Chiefs will have a similar duo finish within the top 5 this year: edge rusher R Mason Thoma and defensive back Mansoor Delane. This bold prediction could have been centered around Thomas and his sack total. With Kansas City’s ability to stuff the run and set up pass-rush situations, I see Thomas taking advantage of playing with defensive tackle Chris Jones and closing in on 10 sacks in his first year. However, his teammate on the boundary is going to take advantage of the revamped pass rush Thomas is leading. Delane looks the part of a physical cornerback that won’t be giving much room for completions on the outside. If he converts a handful of targets his way into highlight-reel interceptions, he and Thomas will both be vying for the award. What’s your bold Chiefs prediction for the 2026 season? Let us know in the comments!
