title: 3 Sean McVay philosophies that could be holding the Rams back
summary: The Los Angeles Rams opened the 2026 season with a rough 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers and though that can feel deflating in the moment, just keep in mind that last year’s Super Bowl champions lost to the 49ers at home in Week 1. That being said, the Rams have now incurred at […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Deebo Samuel Sr. #19 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates scoring a touchdown in the fourth quarter of the NFL football game against Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams opened the 2026 season with a rough 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers and though that can feel deflating in the moment, just keep in mind that last year’s Super Bowl champions lost to the 49ers at home in Week 1. That being said, the Rams have now incurred at least one loss in their first three games in five consecutive seasons. The last time that the Rams started 3-0, they won the Super Bowl and no that is not a coincidence . The most important goal for every team should be earning the number one seed. It’s just too powerful of a playoff advantage, but Sean McVay’s teams consistently fall a game or two shy of those aspirations and it’s because of slow starts: 2022: 2-3 2023: 3-6 2024: 1-4 2025: 3-2 The Rams have made the playoffs in each of the last three seasons, but they have been seeds 4, 5, and 6. That’s simply not good enough and it’s a large part of the reason why L.A. hasn’t reached the Super Bowl since 2021 and McVay has just a 3-3 postseason record since then despite Matthew Stafford, Puka Nacua, and plenty of other stars. He even has Sean McVay . Well, at times that — the McVay effect — feels like both a blessing and a curse. I’m not saying that these are “flaws” necessarily, but with a 20-point loss to start a season in which a strong start feels imperative, these are McVay philosophies that the team refuses to even address as potential setbacks in need of re-thinking. Will anything convince McVay or the Rams to look in the mirror if they fall short of expectations again in 2026? 1 – Not playing the preseason McVay has consistently sat starters and key players in the preseason since 2018. Could this be a factor in L.A.’s consistently poor openings to the season, looking “flat” and unprepared for Weeks 1-5 ? Compare this philosophy to the victorious 49ers: Kyle Shanahan doesn’t give his starters many preseason reps, but he doesn’t seem as fearful of preseason injuries as McVay does. Brock Purdy, Deebo Samuel, De’Zhaun Stribling, Kaelon Black, Marquis Sigle, and others were all active at points in the preseason this season. Yes, they are cautious, but not afraid. The 49ers do seem to have consistent injury problems, but none of these players got injured in preseason action. And Purdy looked far better in Week 1 than Matthew Stafford did. Tom Brady told the rookies in the nfl that he treated his preseason games like if they were superbowl games 🎥: @michaelrubin pic.twitter.com/jeV6DvNLuC — Shannonnn sharpes Burner (PARODY Account) (@shannonsharpeee) May 20, 2024 Is that less surprising than it should be given that Stafford also sits out at least half of the training camp and offseason practices? What if he wasn’t fully prepared for Week 1, regardless of how many seasons of football he’s played before. He’s never played with this exact team before. I often compare football players, especially quarterbacks, to Tom Brady and how he handled his business. Why not? He’s won seven Super Bowls. I’d pay attention. Here’s what Brady recently said about the preseason: “Preseason… Regular season… I never wanted to be taken off the field. Practice makes perfect,” the retired quarterback wrote. “Too many people looking for easy ways out these days. When you’re a football player, and it’s football season, your job is to play football.” Yikes. Sorry, that’s not how I’d want to be seen by players in the Hall of Fame. Like I was too afraid of getting hurt or too good for additional reps. Sean McVay has refused to consider if his preseason philosophy is a flawed one and I doubt that’s going to change in 2027. But if the Rams lose another game or two in the next few weeks, they absolutely should change it. 2 – “Rookies don’t matter” Let’s see: First round pick was used on a QB the team knew would be third string and inactive Second round pick was used on a TE the team knew would be fifth string and inactive Third round pick was used on a OL they team knew would be a backup this season You can definitely justify using a third round pick on Keagen Trost, especially given L.A.’s major free agency problem with the offensive line coming up in 2027. You can probably justify drafting Ty Simpson because Matthew Stafford is old for an NFL player and maybe this would be McVay’s only chance to get a decent prospect at the position to develop. Rams 2026 Draft Picks R1 – QB – Ty Simpson – Inactive R2 – TE – Max Klare – Inactive R3 – OT – Keagen Trost – Injured Reserve R6 – WR – CJ Daniels – Inactive R7 – DT – Tim Keenan III – Raiders Practice Squad — Nathan Jahnke (@FFNateJahnke) September 10, 2026 And yes, the Rams traded a first round pick for Trent McDuffie, which means Les Snead did get some immediate value out of the team’s 2026 draft capital. However, at what cost: L.A.’s extra first round pick didn’t come out of thin air. The team willingly traded out of the 2025 first round in order to acquire an additional first round pick in 2026. They don’t have a developing second-year first round talent on the roster because the Rams traded the pick to use a pick on Ty Simpson…a player who doesn’t play and won’t play any time soon. People always say “Ty Simpson or Makai Lemon” but that’s NOT the comparison you should be making! The comparison is Simpson or safety Malaki Starks? Simpson or tackle Josh Conerly? Simpson or linebacker Carson Schwesinger? Simpson or safety Nick Emmanwori? The Rams could be going into year two with the reigning Defensive Player of the Year (Schwesinger) instead of Omar Speights. But because the team does not value their rookie class , they have Terrance Ferguson (who had zero catches on one target) and Simpson (inactive). Flip this around on San Francisco and you’ll see that their first pick was Stribling, who is set to have a huge role but was injured in Week 1 before he got targeted; third round pick Romello Height, a defensive end who is at least in the rotation a bit; third round running back Kaelon Black, who had 70 total yards on Thursday; and fifth round pick Jaden Dugger, who had five tackles against the Rams. 49ers rookie RB Kaelon Black: · Played 44% of snaps with CMC healthy · Out-carried CMC 14-10 · Averaged 4.6 yards per carry · Most valuable handcuff in fantasy if CMC goes down And he's available in 74% of Yahoo leagues. pic.twitter.com/EHkoW4CcpO — Yahoo Fantasy Sports (@YahooFantasy) September 11, 2026 Injuries have taken a toll on San Francisco’s 2025 class and even then they had Sigle, CJ West, and Upton Stout contributing to their defense on Thursday. L.A.‘s 2025 class includes Ferguson, Josaiah Stewart (six tackles), Jarquez Hunter (traded), Ty Hamilton (one tackle), Chris Paul (released last preseason), and Konata Mumpfield (0 catches on 1 target). Any franchise that feels “F them picks” is banking heavily on their pro scouting department and their ability to find diamonds in the rough like Puka Nacua every year. However, in the past three drafts, the Rams’ best picks who are currently on the roster are: Braden Fiske (not a standout recently) Blake Corum (now half of the backfield) Kam Kinchens (maybe right now an above-average safety) Tyler Davis (a rising name at DT, but will Aaron Donald steal snaps?) And … that’s it. The team has traded Jared Verse and Hunter, and they’ve released five others (Paul, Josh Karty, Brennan Jackson, KT Leveston, and Tim Keenan). Jordan Whittington, Terrance Ferguson, Hamilton, and Stewart are still pretty irrelevant in the grand scheme of things. Beaux Limmer is a backup. And every 2026 rookie was unavailable on Thursday. Teams that make picks “for the future” can only justify that philosophy if they’re being carried by picks “from the past” and the Rams…
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: The Rams lost Week 1, 16 games to go
summary: If you follow the NFL, then by now you know the Los Angeles Rams were mauled on Thursday Night Football by the San Francisco 49ers. It was a humbling loss if you want to put it kindly, it was embarrassing if you want to use another adjective. A silver lining is the Rams have 16 […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Members of the Los Angeles Rams run onto the field prior to the NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Robert Cianflone/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you follow the NFL, then by now you know the Los Angeles Rams were mauled on Thursday Night Football by the San Francisco 49ers . It was a humbling loss if you want to put it kindly, it was embarrassing if you want to use another adjective. A silver lining is the Rams have 16 more games to go. Their season is far from over. Matthew Stafford was off, Myles Garrett didn’t make a tangible impact, Sean McVay was outcoached and the better team, the 49ers, won on Thursday. For the 49ers, this is a great start to the season (minus all the injuries). For the Rams, they clearly aren’t going to walk into the Super Bowl in February as so many preseason talking heads predicted. Now, the Rams roster looks good, but can they play like a team? A fair question after their latest loss. It’s alright to be disappointed in the loss, it’s alright to be frustrated, but the season isn’t over, and for the Rams, they need to get back home, and get back to work. It’s a marathon, not a sprint. Oh, and rumor has it some player who wears #99 may be coming back. The Rams season isn’t done, yet. Top moments, highlights as 49ers beat Rams in Australia (espn.com) “The 49ers handled their division rivals in a statement victory, putting up 379 yards of offense. After the Rams went up 7-3 early in the second quarter, they were outscored 24-0 the rest of the way. Los Angeles had a fumble, an interception and two turnovers on downs during that span. Brock Purdy threw for 205 yards with three touchdowns, becoming the first San Francisco quarterback with three passing scores in a season opener since Colin Kaepernick in 2013, according to ESPN Research. In his debut with the 49ers, wide receiver Mike Evans had six receptions for 49 yards and a score.“ Even 49ers poked fun at Rams’ Australian travel plan after 27-7 blowout — ‘Maybe a few days earlier would’ve been ideal’ (sports.yahoo) “The 49ers deserve credit for executing well and beating the Rams. The 49ers also deserve credit for a plan that had them spend a week in Melbourne acclimating themselves for Thursday’s game, which was actually on Friday morning in Australia. The Rams showed up the day before the game and looked very little like the Super Bowl favorite they had been touted to be all offseason. They looked tired. “Sometimes sports can humble you and today was one of those days,” Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters postgame. “I make no excuses. Whether you want to say it’s about travel, or whatever, we just weren’t good enough in that window. I didn’t coach good enough.” Rams’ lopsided loss to 49ers had nothing to do with Australia travel (ramswire) “We could spend all day dissecting the issues with the defense, as there are plenty. The bigger issue was the pedestrian nature of an offense that led the league in passing efficiency and scoring a year ago. Matthew Stafford looked out of his element, as if he’s forcing throws again because he can’t figure out the defensive puzzle.” NFL draft: Rams watch starts out great for Browns fans as Myles Garrett has his ‘worst’ game in years (dawgsbynature) “The Jaguars watch has ended; long live “Rams watch” for the 2026 season. Much like Jacksonville ended up being in 2025, the Los Angeles Rams are predicted to be very good this year after the Myles Garrett trade with the Browns. Unlike with the Jaguars, Cleveland fans will be on Rams watch for a few years moving forward.“ Rams’ disaster in Australia raises the question: Should the team have followed the 49ers there earlier? (foxnews) “Let’s be clear: This is no slight to the 49ers, a team many believe will earn a playoff berth in a loaded division. Rather, the noise and astronomical expectations for the Rams made this Week 1 performance a shocker to say the least. While the “overrated” talk has already begun for football fans on social media, the question must be asked: were the Rams right to fly to Melbourne less than two days before kickoff? The Rams arrived in Melbourne on Thursday morning local time, with 28 hours until kickoff to begin their season. On the other hand, the 49ers spent close to a week getting adjusted to Melbourne time, practicing multiple times and making sure the team was ready to play a Friday morning game.“ What we learned from Rams’ ugly opening loss vs. 49ers (usatoday.com) ““I know there’s gonna be a lot of narratives that appropriately put the blame on me, and then we’ll move forward the right way,” Rams coach Sean McVay told reporters after the game. “… I don’t believe (the travel plan) is why we didn’t play well enough. I really don’t.” The travel decisions will continue to be a topic of discussion in the coming days, but there are several other factors that could be attributed to the loss. Myles Garrett will benefit from Aaron Donald’s return Garrett has proven throughout his career that he can be the primary focus on a defense and still produce. He spent some time matched up against 49ers standout lineman Trent Williams and did not have a good showing by the defenders’ standards, finishing the game without a sack or tackle.“ NFL Week 1 statistical review: San Francisco 49ers vs. Los Angeles Rams (pff.com) “While the 49ers were clearly the better team, the game wasn’t quite as lopsided as the final score suggests. The Rams failed to capitalize on several opportunities, with Matthew Stafford throwing an interception in scoring range and failing to convert a fourth-down quarterback sneak at the goal line. Los Angeles also gave San Francisco a short field after fumbling in its own territory.“ In Australia, the NFL’s Super Bowl favorite looked a world away from its potential (nbcsports) “The Los Angeles Rams built a star-studded roster, only to sleepwalk through a “humbling experience” in a season-opening loss.“ Rams’ Garrett, without a tackle in loss to 49ers, cites knee (espn.com) “Garrett missed most of training camp while dealing with what Rams coach Sean McVay called swelling in his knee. Garrett declined to say which knee is injured but wore a sleeve on his left leg during several practices. “I’ve got to be better,” Garrett said. “I’ve got to find a way to recover and get back to the player I know I can be and I’ve shown that I’ve been before.” Asked what his focus was going into Week 2, Garrett said, “Getting healthy.” “When I was out there, I was a little bit more focused on myself and trying to stay healthy than what they were doing, and that showed,” Garrett said. “I wasn’t who I needed to be for my team.” Niners-Rams in Australia: What We Learned from San Francisco’s 27-7 win (nfl.com) “ Niners burst Rams’ bubble. Lying in wait for an upset in Australia, the 49ers stunned the NFL’s most-hyped squad — and their division rivals. New faces ( Mike Evans ), returning talents ( Fred Warner ) and familiar standouts ( Brock Purdy ) came to play and make a statement. Kyle Shanahan largely carved up the Rams’ revarnished defense with Purdy throwing three touchdowns passes and for 205 yards in front of 100,021 fans attending the NFL’s first-ever regular season game in Australia. Though they only collected three points, the 49ers’ opening drive set a stellar tone, with Purdy guiding them 65 yards on 15 plays, completing 9 of 12 passes with Christian McCaffrey , rookie Kaelon Black , George Kittle (returning from an Achilles injury), Deebo Samuel (returning after spending 2025 with the Commanders) and Evans all catching balls. An absolute beauty of a 39-yard TD pass to former Rams WR Demarcus Robinson led to a precarious 10-7 halftime lead for the 49ers, but in the second half, Purdy and Co. squeezed the life out of the Rams. Purdy’s 15-yard score to Deebo Samuel culminated an 11-play, 99-yard TD march to open the fourth…

title: Rams Reacts: Fans were very confident about team’s direction before loss
summary: Ahead of the Los Angeles Rams’ 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday, many fans expressed their confidence in the team’s direction. Following a 20-point loss to begin the season, it’s fair to wonder how those fans feel now, especially when the Rams were perceived as a heavy Super Bowl contender entering the […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams warms up prior to the NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ahead of the Los Angeles Rams’ 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday, many fans expressed their confidence in the team’s direction. Following a 20-point loss to begin the season, it’s fair to wonder how those fans feel now, especially when the Rams were perceived as a heavy Super Bowl contender entering the game. In the most recent SB Nation reacts poll, which was conducted just ahead of the season opener, a sizable chunk of the fanbase (93%) expressed confidence that the team was moving in the right direction. Heading into the season, that shouldn’t have surprised anyone, considering LA has the reigning MVP and Defensive Player of the Year on its roster. This offseason, the front office had seemingly put the team in position to make another potential Super Bowl run, or so many around the league expected. Now, a horrible loss in the first game of the season has undoubtedly dampened things. Remember, it’s a long season, and on the plus side, the Rams have yet to lose on American soil. Joking aside, there are reasons for optimism amid the darkness cast by the Week 1 loss. For starters, some fans believe the team is positioned for long-term success even after the front office’s blockbuster moves this offseason, signifying a desire to win immediately. With the post- Matthew Stafford world approaching in the near future, one fan shared that the team seems well-built to succeed whenever the veteran quarterback calls it a career. Ty Simpson will have enough solid, young pieces around him on offense and defense to find success in the post-Stafford era. Players like Puka Nacua, Kobie Turner, Terrance Ferguson, Byron Young and several others should grow alongside him as he develops. In theory, they should also keep the team in contention for quite some time, as long as the front office continues to hit on those late-stage draft picks and those key pieces are re-signed. In the survey’s comment section, fans believed the team should always be in good shape as long as Sean McVay roams the sidelines. And they should be, considering the Rams have won a Super Bowl under his watch and LA has finished with one losing record since he took over in 2017. Yes, losing in blowout fashion, to a division rival no less, is a rough way to begin the season, but that shouldn’t cause the fanbase to lose hope. The Rams still have McVay and an array of young talent to move past most challenges in their way. LA is still a Super Bowl contender and has 16 more games to live up to those lofty expectations and regain the fans’ confidence. title: Four down territory: Rams takeaways after flat performance
summary: The Los Angeles Rams time in Melbourne, Australia was short-lived and that might be for the best as LA suffered a 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday Night (Friday morning for others). Some might question the Rams decision to fly in the day before the game, although that did not seem to […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams is tackled after making a pass in the first quarter of the NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams time in Melbourne, Australia was short-lived and that might be for the best as LA suffered a 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday Night (Friday morning for others). Some might question the Rams decision to fly in the day before the game, although that did not seem to be a significant influence on the outcome in my opinion. Why did the Rams lose? Well here are 4 takeaways from Los Angeles’s week one loss to their division rivals. “1st Down”: Offense was self-inflicted After picking off a Brock Purdy pass, Stafford turned the ball back over to the San Francisco 49ers on 3rd & 10 from the SF 35. Instead of taking his underneath option (Terrance Ferguson), Stafford tried to force a pass on a deep corner to Puka Nacua. The ball was underthrown; giving SF momentum and taking 3 points off the board for LA. Had the Rams kicked the field goal on 4th down, they would have had a 10-3 lead. The other self-inflicted mistake was the turnover on downs with 3:46 left in the 3rd quarter. The Rams could not punch the ball in the endzone from 2nd, 3rd, and 4th & Goal (all within the 3 yard line). The latter being 4th & 1/2 yard. Those are simply must-have situations when down 10. “2nd Down”: Rams must solve run defense The Rams allowed 30 rushing attempts for 174 yards (5.8 yards per carry). The Rams won’t beat a Kyle Shanahan offense with that type of formula. No, it wasn’t because Aaron Donald was inactive. The Rams simply did not win the trenches getting pushed off the ball. Chris Shula will need to take a deep look at how to counter the 49ers usage of chips on his edge players as Myles Garrett was a non-factor in rushing the passer but also in defending the run. Something that will probably matter going forward: The Rams nickel/dime defense was no match vs SF's run game, which looks vastly improved from last year. Niners RBs averaged 6.5 yds/carry and a >50% success rate running into those looks tonight. — Mina Kimes (@minakimes) September 11, 2026 “3rd Down”: 3rd & Manageable The Rams offense was one of the best in 2025 because they were constantly in favorable down & distances. In this game against the 49ers, their 3rd down distances were: 5 yards, 2 yards, 6 yards, 10 yards, 13 yards, 1 yard, 2 yards, 15 yards, and 10 yards. The only true conversion was on 3rd & 2 via a Kyren Williams run. The other conversion was via defensive pass interference call late in the game. “4th Down”: Primetime performance must improve With 7 primetime games this season, the Rams must raise their level of performance. They will face the Giants, Broncos, Bills, Chiefs, Packers, and Seahawks on primetime television. Those games will be similar in difficulty to the 49ers. If LA wants the bright lights, they must show up.
author: Steven Ridings

title: Rams Winners & Losers: Is Matthew Stafford done for?
summary: It was clear the Los Angeles Rams and Matthew Stafford were out of sync from the game’s opening moments. They fell to the San Francisco 49ers 27-7 in an embarrassing opening week stunner. This game feels primed to be overanalyzed and ill-extrapolated. Week 1 brings surprises every year that never seem to age well. The […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams is tackled after making a pass in the first quarter of the NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was clear the Los Angeles Rams and Matthew Stafford were out of sync from the game’s opening moments. They fell to the San Francisco 49ers 27-7 in an embarrassing opening week stunner. This game feels primed to be overanalyzed and ill-extrapolated. Week 1 brings surprises every year that never seem to age well. The Rams will probably be fine, although this is a resetting moment and a good time to re-adjust expectations. Who is to blame for the loss? In a “winners & losers” first, we are going to start with the “losers” and then make our way to the “winners”. Losers Matthew Stafford, QB There was a lot to dislike about Stafford’s game on Thursday night. His first pass was aimed right into the hands of 49ers linebacker Fred Warner. He never really course corrected. Stafford airmailed long passes and had very little going outside of 10 yards. He easily could have finished with three or four interceptions. One of the most important plays of the game was a failed quarterback sneak on fourth down at the goal line. Stafford has never been great at this play despite it being one of the biggest advantages for offenses. The 49ers then drove 99 yards to effectively put the outcome away. Stafford looked very limited on the run, which is particularly limiting in the red zone. The most concerning aspect of this loss is Stafford’s inconsistency during his tenure in Los Angeles. He has yet to stack back-to-back positive seasons. It’s very possible we see regression from his MVP season and this is the first sign of that. The Rams need Stafford to play well in order to meet their lofty expectations this season—in part because they ask so much of their quarterback. In fairness, many were premature to call Tom Brady’s downfall after a brutal loss to the Chiefs. He went on to disprove the critics and win multiple Super Bowls thereafter. What matters most is whether Stafford rebounds. He’s 38 years old. He might not bounce back. Father time eventually comes for everyone, and we’ve seen very good quarterbacks fall straight off performance cliffs. Is this the beginning of the end for Matthew Stafford? Stafford INT 49ers get the ball right back (via: @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/aYDU8jygxm — B/R Gridiron (@brgridiron) September 11, 2026 Myles Garrett, EDGE Garrett missed significant time while managing a knee injury. He was very clearly on a snap count in Week 1. That limits the impact of a truly great defender. The bigger challenge is the fact that basically every other passing play was a screen play for San Francisco. Kyle Shanahan was never going to let the Rams’ aggressive pass rushers get comfortable. This may have caught the Rams off guard. It shouldn’t have. They will need to recalibrate and be more prepared for limited offensive play calling moving forward. Brock Purdy didn’t really need to do much in order to beat the Rams, although he did hit a long touchdown. The Rams were beat on overly routine plays. Garrett will have his chances this season. In some ways he is a symbol of LA’s downfall on Thursday night. This game plan was tailored to keeping him on his heels. Jaylen Watson, CB Mike Evans caught six of seven targets for 49 yards and a touchdown. He did most of his work against Quentin Lake and Jaylen Watson. Watson allowed the touchdown and was outmanned on an end zone fade. It wasn’t a strong Rams debut for their new corner. It’s a common theme that the players LA is counting on most—including their high-profile additions—did not perform well in this game. MIKE EVANS INEVITABLE pic.twitter.com/Zy1sZcZrvU — Sports (@Sports) September 11, 2026 Davante Adams, WR Davante Adams caught a few passes late in order to improve appearances in the box score. He was invisible in the first half mostly. He finished with three catches on six targets for 26 yards. One of the most concerning trends from LA’s offense last year is that Adams routinely only hauls in 50% of his targets. It’s not positive that he started off the season on this foot again. The Rams’ offense overall looked slow and Adams particularly showed his age on Thursday night. Winners Rams’ selection of Ty Simpson Ty Simpson delivers a TD strike to Brennan Presley 🔥 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/5Dc65aRqbk — NFL (@NFL) August 28, 2026 Few were willing to acknowledge the possibility that Matthew Stafford would decline late into his 30’s. Father time comes for all eventually. Was the Rams’ selection of Ty Simpson mostly about 2027 and beyond? For sure. The team may need their rookie first-round pick sooner than later if Stafford is truly declining at a rate faster than anticipated. Simpson would have fared better on the QB sneak than Stafford. It may be worth activating him on gamedays and preparing a red zone package in order to take advantage of his mobility. The Rams saw Justin Fields score his first career touchdown in 2021 in the same vein. It’s not unheard of. It’s very obvious that Stafford has evident physical limitations, even if he approaches his level of play from last season. There is value to gain from Simpson if the team is willing to tap into it. And whatever experience Simpson garners from this year will only pay dividends moving forward. The Rams maybe knew something we didn’t. They weren’t just preparing for Stafford’s retirement. They were also trying to be ready in case the quarterback cliff unexpectedly came for the veteran. It may be here.
author: JB Scott

title: Rams-49ers Final Score: SF kicks the crap out of L.A. in Australia
summary: The Los Angeles Rams lost to the San Francisco 49ers by a score of 27-7 in the first ever NFL game held in Australia. The 49ers put an embarrassing beatdown on the Rams as SF moves to 1-0 and Los Angeles falls to last in the NFC West at 0-1. Brock Purdy threw three touchdowns, […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers runs the ball in the third quarter of the NFL football game against Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Robert Cianflone/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams lost to the San Francisco 49ers by a score of 27-7 in the first ever NFL game held in Australia. The 49ers put an embarrassing beatdown on the Rams as SF moves to 1-0 and Los Angeles falls to last in the NFC West at 0-1. Brock Purdy threw three touchdowns, Kyle Shanahan called what he wanted, and Sean McVay and his Rams looked lesser on Thursday. For the all their offseason hype, the Rams looked terrible in this game. It’s one game, and there is plenty of time for L.A. to figure this all out, but as of Week 1, the Rams looked out matched and under prepared against the 49ers. People will criticize L.A. and their travel strategy of basically showing up a day before the game, and that’s fair. Another perhaps more important truth is one team looked better than the other on Thursday night, and the team that looked better won. The first half Stafford struggled in this one as last year’s MVP didn’t appear comfortable with some questionable passes to go along with errant throws. Whereas the 49ers and Purdy came out fairly sharp against what is assumed to be a stout defense for the Rams. The 49ers opened up the scoring with a field goal, after shutting down the Rams first two offensive drives. On L.A.’s third drive, Stafford showed some life when he found Puka Nacua for a long gain, an incredible play by Puka, and then Kyren Williams capped off the drive with a touchdown to take 7-3 lead after the successful Harrison Mevis extra point. Both Stafford and Purdy exchanged interceptions in the first half, but Purdy was the one to throw the long score when he found Demarcus Robinson to take a 10-7 lead. Shanahan has historically given McVay and the Rams a tough time and today was no different. McVay seemed to go away from the run when it was working through the first two quarters. Given how sporadic Stafford had been, it was curious to see McVay not lean on the run game more, then again, the 49ers defense under Raheem Morris was hitting and filling lanes. Whether it was due to travel, too much offseason hype or personnel, the 49ers looked a bit better overall in the first half, and the Rams didn’t look awful, but they didn’t appear consistent either. The 49ers took advantage and set themselves up to add on points coming out of the half. It was 10-7, so the Rams were still in it, but they had work to do. The second half Coming out of the half, the 49ers drove down the field effortlessly after a good opening return by Deebo Samuel, followed by some strong runs by Christian McCaffrey, capped off by a passing touchdown of Purdy to Mike Evans. With the score now 17-7, the Rams were likely farther behind in this contest than they had planned the entire offseason. But with plenty of time go in quarters three and four, there was still time for L.A. to respond. And to respond, the Rams showed life as Stafford started to click finding Nacua and Adams and his tight ends to take the Rams all the way down to the 1-yard line. Then, on fourth and one, the 49ers made the stop of the year when they stuffed Stafford on a sneak attempt. The 49ers had the ball with a chance to more or less put this game away, or take the game to the fourth quarter to make life even harder on L.A. who trailed by 10 points. The 49ers went on to dominate the third quarter. The 17-10 score properly reflected that, and when the score was 24-7 after Purdy found Samuel for another passing score, Purdy’s third of the day, it was not up for debate that the 49ers had outplayed the Rams. Tyler Higbee had a late fumble, Nate Landman was injured and Stetson Bennett came in late as the Rams basically gave up. Overall and for most of the game, the Rams looked lost and they went on to lose their opening game of the 2026 season. The Final It’s going to be a long break for the Rams before they play the New York Giants on Monday Night Football. All the talk of a potential 17-0 season, guaranteed Super Bowl contenders, that’s all gone for L.A. now. The 49ers gutted the Rams on Netflix. Can the Rams bounce back? They’ll have at least 16 more chances to do just that.

title: NFC West should remain the NFL’s best division in 2026
summary: The Seattle Seahawks proved Wednesday night that they remain the class of the NFC West, with the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers not far behind. With the Rams, Seahawks and 49ers set to be among the conference’s best teams, the division should remain the NFL’s best in 2026. The NFC West featured three […]
full_text: Football: NFC Championship: Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald and Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay greet each other at midfield following game at Lumen Field. Seattle, WA 1/25/2026CREDIT: Simon Bruty (Photo by Simon Bruty/Sports Illustrated via Getty Images) (Set Number: X164832 TK1) The Seattle Seahawks proved Wednesday night that they remain the class of the NFC West, with the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers not far behind. With the Rams, Seahawks and 49ers set to be among the conference’s best teams, the division should remain the NFL’s best in 2026. The NFC West featured three teams that finished with the best records in the NFL last season, with Seattle ultimately winning the bloodbath en route to its second Super Bowl title. Between the Seahawks, Rams and 49ers, they finished with a combined 38-13 record last season. The AFC East and AFC South were the only other divisions that featured multiple 12-win teams. But the NFC West had three. THREE! What a truly insane feat, yet one that’s incredibly on brand for the division over the last decade. The 2025 NFC West: The greatest division in NFL history. First division to feature three teams with 12+ wins — David Lombardi (@LombardiHimself) January 5, 2026 Since 2016, the NFC West has the third-best record by division at 343-315-3, just behind the NFC North (344-311-5) and AFC West (346-314). Of those three divisions, only the two West divisions feature multiple Super Bowl champions. The Chiefs won titles in 2019, 2022 and 2023, while the Rams won during the 2021 season and the Seahawks last season. Despite several great Packers teams quarterbacked by Aaron Rodgers and a few solid Vikings, Lions and Bears campaigns sprinkled in there, no NFC North team made a Super Bowl appearance in that span. In fact, the last appearance by the division came during the 2010 season when Green Bay brought the Lombardi Trophy back home — sorry cheeseheads! Every NFC West team (besides the Cardinals) has made at least one Super Bowl appearance in the last decade. The Rams and 49ers each appeared twice, while the Seahawks obviously made the most of their lone trip in 2025. That equates to all of Kansas City’s trips during their run of dominance, excluding last year: NFC West: 5 (Rams in 2018 and 2021; 49ers in 2019 and 2023; Seahawks in 2025) AFC West: 5 (Chiefs in 2019, 2020, 2022, 2023, 2024) AFC East: 3 (Patriots in 2016, 2018 and 2025) NFC East: 3 (Eagles in 2017, 2022, 2024) NFC South: 2 (Falcons in 2016; Buccaneers in 2020) AFC North: 1 (Bengals in 2021) NFC North and AFC South: 0 Eight times in the last decade, divisions have fielded three playoff teams. The NFC West (2021 and 2025) and AFC North (2020 and 2023) are the only two that have done it twice. When teams make the playoffs from the division, they have certainly earned it. So, it should come as no surprise that the three teams with the highest odds of winning the Super Bowl in February reside in the NFC West. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the three division playoff teams from last season are in the top 10 for odds to win the big game, beginning with the Rams at +550 (first), Seahawks at +1100 (third) and 49ers at +1800 (tied for eighth). That is truly a remarkable feat. As long as the Rams, Seahawks and 49ers remain competitive, there is truly no better division in the NFL than the NFC West. If things play out similarly to 2025, the Super Bowl could very well run through the division yet again this season.

title: Why the Rams should beat the Niners handily
summary: The L.A. Rams should have no trouble beating their division rival San Francisco 49ers in their Week 1 game in Melbourne on Thursday night and the reason is simple: The Rams were the better team last season and they’re even better this season. When analyzing the first game of the year against a division rival, […]
full_text: LA Rams' head coach Sean McVay speaks to the media at Marvel Stadium in Melbourne on September 10, 2026. The first-ever regular-season NFL game in Australia takes place at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026, featuring the San Francisco 49ers and the Los Angeles Rams. (Photo by Martin KEEP / AFP via Getty Images) / - IMAGE RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE - STRICTLY NO COMMERCIAL USE - | AFP via Getty Images The L.A. Rams should have no trouble beating their division rival San Francisco 49ers in their Week 1 game in Melbourne on Thursday night and the reason is simple: The Rams were the better team last season and they’re even better this season. When analyzing the first game of the year against a division rival, I look back at what happened in their games the previous season. In the first Rams-Niners games last season, a Week 5 matchup, the 49ers won 26-23 in overtime. If you only look at the score, it seems like a balanced match. It was anything but. The Rams missed five scoring opportunities due to self-inflicted errors: Two fumbles lost in the red zone (One at the two yard line ) a blocked PAT a missed FG 4th down stop at the Niners’ 11 yards line in OT Yes, the team from San Fran was missing a lot of starters and played admirably, but the game should have been won by the Rams. In the Week 10 rematch, the Rams were just getting their feet wet with their ‘13’ personnel offensive scheme, and the Niners had no answer for it. L.A. pulled out to a 21-0 lead early in the second quarter, and though the 49ers made it close by the start of the fourth (largely thanks to Mac Jones being almost flawless on short crossing routes) it was soon back to 42-20 and the Rams won 42-26. On Thursday, I would expect similar problems for the 49ers when it comes to stopping L.A.’s offense, but now Sean McVay has better answers for Kyle Shanahan on defense. It could be another blowout. WHAT’S NEW THIS SEASON? Les Snead addressed the Rams’ greatest weakness in the offseason by acquiring cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson from the Chiefs. He then pulled the trigger on the biggest trade of the offseason and brought the Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett into the fold. I think those two moves will allow Chris Shula to bring a safety or DB into shallow coverage on those crossing patterns I mentioned, something he was reluctant to do given the pedestrian quality of the Rams’ DBs last year. Also, Garrett’s presence on the line will force Brock Purdy to get rid of the ball much more quickly, especially given San Francisco’s lack of a quality guard on the left side. While the Rams made some huge changes in the offseason, the Niners only had a few notable moves, such as 33-year-old receiver Mike Evans, rookie receiver De’Zhaun Stribling, and defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa. When Evans is healthy, he’s good, but he’s been battling injuries for years now and even missed valuable time in training camp when he should have been gelling with Purdy. Odighizuwa was brought in to upgrade the defensive line, but then the 49ers lost defensive tackle Alfred Collins for the season a few days ago. The Niners are pinning their hopes this week on the return of many of their ‘ancient’ warriors after injury, but even then, these players may not play or may have a reduced workload. Players like Nick Bosa and George Kittle certainly move the needle when healthy, but how healthy are they this week? Does Shanahan still have McVay’s number? In any other game this year, the Shanahan factor would come into play, but not this week. The Rams will have a completely remade defense and some serious offensive twists to debut but there is zero 2026 L.A. tape for Shanahan to analyze. He’s completely in the dark as to what to expect. The Rams addressed their areas of weakness, but San Francisco, who the Rams already seemed better than, didn’t. They mostly just got older. In fact, they were the oldest roster in the NFL at final cuts, but 1.5 years. It’s football, so anything could happen in Australia. But this one feels like too big of an advantage for the Rams for them not to get the first-game win that they didn’t get against the 49ers last season.
author: John Newman

title: Rams-49ers Week 1 advantages
summary: The Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers open up their 2026 season with a matchup that features plenty of intriguing storylines on both sides of the football. With two talented rosters set to meet in Week 1, several areas could play a significant role in determining how the game unfolds. From offensive production and […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers open up their 2026 season with a matchup that features plenty of intriguing storylines on both sides of the football. With two talented rosters set to meet in Week 1, several areas could play a significant role in determining how the game unfolds. From offensive production and defensive execution to special teams and coaching, each category presents a different set of strengths and challenges for both teams. The Rams enter the matchup with expectations of making a deep postseason run, while the 49ers will look to establish themselves immediately against a familiar NFC West opponent. Before kickoff, here is a look at four key Week 1 advantages—offense, defense, special teams and coaching—that could help shape the outcome of Rams-49ers in Melbourne. OFFENSE: RAMS The Rams offense returns every single piece from its 2025 team that finished second in the NFL in scoring offense, including MVP Matthew Stafford. Running backs Kyren Williams and Blake Corum provide a strong tandem in the run game, while Puka Nacua and Davante Adams provide a 1A and 1B threat in the passing game. The Rams usage of 13 personnel will be on display as they boast five tight ends capable of seeing time. The 49ers offense isn’t bad as Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans, Trent Williams, and George Kittle carry loads of NFL experience. However, the 49ers have been nursing injuries throughout the summer; leaving some to wonder how they will transition back into the speed of the season. DEFENSE: RAMS The Rams caught the attention of the NFL world when they traded for Trent McDuffie and Myles Garrett this offseason. In addition, they added Jaylen Watson to the secondary. Oh.. and there is Aaron Donald. Even though, he will be inactive for this matchup, the Rams carry Kobie Turner, Braden Fiske, Tyler Davis, and Poona Ford along their defensive line; arguably the best in the NFL. The 49ers defense continues to age. Fred Warner and Nick Bosa return in 2026 after suffering season-ending injuries in 2025. The team also just announced that Alfred Collins will miss the entire 2026 season as of two days ago. San Francisco’s defense should be better than last year but can they slow down the Rams offense? SPECIAL TEAMS: 49ERS Until proven otherwise, the Rams need to dig themselves out of the hole they made with their special teams issues from 2022-2025. Harrison Mevis has gained confidence from the fanbase but questions still remain at punt returner and the team’s coverage units. Eddy Pinero is San Francisco’s place kicker and he was pretty clutch over for the team in 2025 after a stint with the Carolina Panthers. SF may have some coverage issues of their own but the Rams special teams was historically bad in 2025. COACHING: RAMS It’s a tight call in fairness but Sean McVay is the better coach. His seamless switch from 11 personnel as the team’s base offense to 13 personnel has been fascinating in the coach’s evolution. When the chips are in the middle, McVay usually rises to the moment unlike his opponent… Shanahan might be better with his schematics and play calling but their is certainly scrutiny to be had over how he disappoints in big moments. Shanahan’s brain has always led him to be a top 5 offensive mind but he needs the allocades to catch up to McVay’s status.

title: Raiders Week 1: Battle of rebuilding teams is must-win for Las Vegas
summary: What an opportune opponent for the season- and home-opener for the Las Vegas Raiders by hosting the Miami Dolphins this Sunday inside Allegiant Stadium. And to be candid, there aren’t many of these on the Silver & Black’s 2026 slate. The Week 1 battle pits two rookie NFL head coaches — the Raiders’ Klint Kubiak […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images What an opportune opponent for the season- and home-opener for the Las Vegas Raiders by hosting the Miami Dolphins this Sunday inside Allegiant Stadium. And to be candid, there aren’t many of these on the Silver & Black’s 2026 slate. The Week 1 battle pits two rookie NFL head coaches — the Raiders’ Klint Kubiak and the Dolphins’ Jeff Hafley — at the helm of two rebuilding franchises against one another. And in the clash of the AFC West against the AFC East, this game is a must-win for Las Vegas. Mainly because failing to capitalize on a favorable matchup in essence becomes a sharp uppercut to not only Kubiak and his coaching staff — on the opposite spectrum, a road win would be as supreme morale booster for Hafley’s crew — but also Raider Nation, a fan base that’s been through it’s fair share of disappointments and then some. Coming off back-to-back seasons with two different head coaches with the Raiders only able to win three and four games, respectively, the loyal fanbase needs proof the new coaching staff can deliver. And that’s where we’ll start in this explanation of why attaining victory in Week 1 against the incoming Dolphins is vital for the Raiders. Key players are gone, but Jeff Hafley doesn’t consider this a rebuild year… Watch the full episode now on YouTube! Miami Dolphin fans, what do you think?! pic.twitter.com/WaTyZrKuSo — Stephen A Smith (@stephenasmith) August 27, 2026 A Year Ahead As noted when I explored Miami’s must-account-for players in running back De’Von Achane and linebacker Jordyn Brooks, the Dolphins are in the midst of their tear down and rebuild by bringing in a pair of former Green Bay Packers at general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan and Hafley as head coach . The Dolphins roster this season compared to last are stark in comparison — the best way to relate this to Raiders’ fans was the initial season under then-GM Reggie McKenzie gutted the roster in 2012 order to chart a better course — with over half of it featuring new players. Hafley’s debut has brand-new starting quarterback Malik Willis leading the offense. And the signal caller marks the third major Packers’ import alongside the general manager and head coach. Las Vegas is in a similar boat with Kubiak making his head coaching debut with veteran Kirk Cousins at quarterback, however, the distinct difference with the Silver & Black is the rebuild began a year ago when John Spytek was hired as general manager. Yes, the team dumped Pete Carroll after a one-and-done 2025 season, but the Raiders roster overhaul is a year ahead. Which makes Sunday’s tilt against an unproven team an opportunity Las Vegas can’t afford to waste. Validating Captain Kirk Despite the announcement being delayed, the inevitable result of Cousins being Kubiak’s QB1 arrived and the veteran signal caller gets the nod over promising rookie — and No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft — Fernando Mendoza. Going with the experienced 38-year-old at quarterback, alongside the built-in familiarity Cousins has with Kubiak, offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko, and offensive line coach Rick Dennison, elevates expectations a bit in the desert. One can expect a smooth operation with a quarterback heading into his 15th season in the NFL where the offense is moving the chains, avoiding penalties, and either getting into the end zone or in range of field goal kicker Matt Gay. Starting the 2026 campaign with a win validates Kubiak’s decision to roll with Cousins and not throwing Mendoza into the fire too early as an NFL neophyte. All it takes is one poor performance from Cousins for Raider Nation to beckon for Mendoza become the starting quarterback — especially the home opener with the fan base’s hopes riding high. Raiders GM John Spytek talks about what progress looks like (besides winning games) within the organization that will give him confidence that the team is headed in the right direction #RaiderNation @YourboyQ254 pic.twitter.com/NNc78qdwYL — Raider Nation Radio (@RNR920AM) September 1, 2026 Brace Period It’s no secret that the Raiders’ slate of games in Kubiak’s first season as head honcho is notoriously brutal as the team holds the seventh toughest strength of schedule for the 2026 season. The opponent’s Las Vegas face this season sported a .529 win percentage in 2025 (219-195 combined record) hence why I turned the standard “grace period” term into “brace period”. After the home opener this Sunday, Kubiak and Co. go back-to-back road trips to face the Los Angeles Chargers and New Orleans Saints, before a staggering four games against: The Kansas City Chiefs (at home), New England Patriots (on the road), Buffalo Bills (home) and Los Angeles Rams (home). Las Vegas’ slate also includes matchups against the San Francisco 49ers, Seattle Seahawks, and then the slate of AFC West division tilts. Snagging a season-opening win creates the good vibes required for a grueling gauntlet of a 2026 schedule. Raider Renaissance The immediate buy-in was mentioned above, but it can’t be said enough. Victory isn’t only good for Kubiak and his players, but also Spytek, minority owner Tom Brady, and owner Mark Davis. A win substantiates not only the decision to axe Carroll but also the patient coaching search that landed the team Kubiak as the new head coach. Week 1 is very much a tone-setting matchup and while many will see “must win” as hyperbole as a win or loss doesn’t magically make the Raiders a playoff contender. That’s very well and true, however, for a Raiders team looking for a revival — a renaissance if you will — dropping the season-opening homestand despite having arguably the better roster than the incoming Dolphins is the opposite of the winning culture the Silver & Black seek. Let’s say it plain: A loss to Miami would be an embarrassing stumble for Las Vegas. A victory helps quiet the offseason questions — I’m not obtuse, they’ll still remain past Week 1 — but the AFC is believed to be a strong conference and the Raiders need to pick up any wins it can get. Especially one where they’re heavily favored.

author: Bill Williamson

title: Nakobe Dean, Quay Walker face tough test against De’Von Achane, Malik Willis in Las Vegas Raiders’ Week 1 key matchups against Miami Dolphins
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders have a good opportunity to start the 2026 season off on the right foot in Week 1 against the Miami Dolphins. While both teams are considered longshots to win the Super Bowl, the betting odds give Las Vegas a slight advantage over Miami. But if the Raiders are going to get […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders have a good opportunity to start the 2026 season off on the right foot in Week 1 against the Miami Dolphins . While both teams are considered longshots to win the Super Bowl, the betting odds give Las Vegas a slight advantage over Miami. But if the Raiders are going to get the ‘W’ in their season/home opener, winning these three key matchups will be paramount. Raiders LBs vs. Dolphins Backfield The Dolphins have one of the most electric running backs in the NFL. De’Von Achane has a career average of 5.6 yards per carry and is coming off his first 1,000-rushing-yard performance, finishing first among running backs in breakaway runs (24 rushes of 15 yards or more) and breakaway yards (622) last season, per Pro Football Focus . The Texas A&M product with 4.32 speed is a home-run hitter, and Miami’s backfield is expected to be even more dynamic after adding quarterback Malik Willis in the offseason. Willis comes over from the Green Bay Packers, where he spent the majority of the last two seasons backing up Jordan Love. However, the former Packer did appear in 11 games with three starts over the last couple of years, primarily being used in subpackages as a rushing threat with 42 carries for 261 yards (6.2 ypc) and three touchdowns during that timeframe. Now the Dolphins’ starter, one has to imagine Miami’s offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik will dial up at least a few read options or quarterback runs for Willis to maximize his skill set and force defenses to account for him in the running game. That puts a heavy emphasis on the Raiders’ new linebackers, Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker. Dean is known for his instincts, especially against the run. While a combination of injuries and a career-high 14.3 percent missed tackle rate led to a career-low 42.9 PFF run defense grade in 2025, two years ago he ranked third among NFL linebackers with 38 ‘ defensive stops ’ against the run and second with a 12.5 percent run stop rate . That coincided with a career-high 15 starts and resulted in a career-high 82.5 run defense mark. Additionally, the former Philadelphia Eagle has become one of the league’s best off-ball blitzers during the last two years, racking up seven sacks and 26 pressures on 101 pass rushes, per PFF . Considering Willis’ legs and scrambling ability, Dean’s ability to rush the passer and be an effective quarterback spy should play a big factor on Sunday. Meanwhile, Walker is still putting it all together as an NFL linebacker. He took big strides with his instincts against the run last year to finish tied for 21st at the position with 27 run stops and tied for 25th with a 7.8 percent run stop rate, per PFF . Also, the former Packer has been a pretty consistent tackler with a miss rate below eight percent over the last three years. Where Walker can get in trouble against the Dolphins is in coverage. His awareness in that phase of the game is still a work in progress, and Achane is also a dynamic receiver out of the backfield who has 172 career catches for 1,277 yards and 13 touchdowns over three seasons. The 2022 first-round pick posted a 9.63 Relative Athletic Score (RAS) coming out of Georgia, meaning he has the athleticism to get the job done when he’s in the right spot. Long story short, the former Bulldogs will have their hands full on Sunday with the Dolphins’ backfield. Glaze vs. Robinson The first true one-on-one matchup featured here will pit a pair of former Big Ten foes and 2024 draft classmates against each other. Raiders’ right tackle DJ Glaze hails from Maryland and Dolphins’ edge rusher Chop Robinson played his college ball at Penn State. In 2022, Glaze was in his second year as a starter and had his worst game in pass protection against the Nittany Lions, giving up a season-high four pressures (one sack) and recording a season-low 44.9 pass blocking grade, per PFF . Meanwhile, Robinson had an excellent outing with five pressures and two sacks on just 19 pass-rush snaps. Unfortunately, the latter missed the matchup the following year. In a way, that outing was a precursor to Glaze’s struggles in the NFL. He’s had issues in pass protection, yielding the second-most pressures (48) and sacks (10) among offensive tackles last season, according to PFF . More specifically, the third-round pick has had trouble with speed rushers, which has been and still is Robinson’s biggest calling card. The former first-round pass-rusher battled injuries a year ago, leading to a disappointing sophomore campaign with just 19 pressures and four sacks . However, when fully healthy as a rookie, he finished tied for 19th among all edges with 56 pressures (seven sacks) and trailed only 2024 Defensive Rookie of the Year Jared Verse (77) in the draft class. So, this will be an opportunity for Glaze to get some retribution and show how much he’s grown under new offensive line coach Rick Dennison. Also, the two players should be very familiar with each other because they were also teammates for a year in college. Robinson spent his true freshman season at Maryland in 2021, when Glaze was a redshirt freshman. Powers-Johnson vs. Sieler Zach Sieler may not have much name recognition with no Pro Bowl or All-Pro bids yet, but make no mistake about it: he’s a problem in the trenches. The nine-year pro did have a dip in pass-rush production with 32 pressures and 5.5 sacks last year. However, he had back-to-back seasons with double-digit sacks , recording 10 in both 2023 and 2024, and had 102 pressures during that timeframe. Additionally, Sieler has been a steady run defender throughout his tenure in Miami, posting PFF run defense grades in the mid-60s to high-70s six times in seven seasons. And the lone outlier is a solid 63.2 mark in 2023. Last year, a 69.1 grade was enough to finish 17th among defensive tackles , and 17 defensive stops against the run is nothing to scoff at. While the versatile defensive lineman recorded most of his snaps as a right defensive tackle ( 311 out of 780 ), he can play multiple alignments and will flip sides of the center. Especially since the Raiders had a position battle for the starting right guard spot, it wouldn’t be surprising to see the Dolphins test Jackson Powers-Johnson with Sieler early in the game. Powers-Johnson has provided strong moments and games over the last two seasons to give reason to believe that he has a bright future in the league, but he’s struggled with consistency. That’s especially true in pass protection, where the 2024 second-round pick surrendered 10 pressures (two sacks) on just 196 opportunities in 2025, per PFF. The good news for the Raiders is that he’s been solid in the running game, with run-blocking marks of 70.4 and 66.6 to help match up with Sieler on Sunday. Much like Glaze, this will be a good opportunity for JPJ to showcase the work he put in during the offseason.
author: Matt Holder

title: Las Vegas Raiders Week 1: Scouting the Miami Dolphins Defense
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders offense vs the Miami Dolphins defense is a chess match between two superior former coordinators turned first-year head coaches. Whereas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak is coming off a Super Bowl win, Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley is bringing his 4-3 scheme from the Packers. What’s interesting is that for all […]
full_text: (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders offense vs the Miami Dolphins defense is a chess match between two superior former coordinators turned first-year head coaches. Whereas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak is coming off a Super Bowl win, Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley is bringing his 4-3 scheme from the Packers . What’s interesting is that for all intents and purposes the Dolphins are running a scheme similar to Raiders defensive coordinator Rob Leonard’s. Linebackers “On paper,” a phrase ridiculously overused, the Dolphins’ strength is their linebacking corps. Jordyn Brooks led the league in tackles with 183 total tackles, adding 3.5 sacks, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery. Brooks recorded 20.5 run stuffs, according to ESPN.com. His play earned him a trip to the Pro Bowl in 2025 and he was rewarded with a three-year 51.3 million extension in the offseason. Brooks’ tackling ability, paired with the experience and playing wisdom of former Kansas City Chiefs linebacker Willie Gay Jr., will set the tone for the defense in 2026. Adding Jacob Rodriguez, the 2025 Dick Butkus Award winner, is the makings of a very impressive linebacking group. Providing run stuffing, good tackling, sideline-to-sideline speed, some blitzing capabilities and good pass coverage in the middle of the field. Blocking the second level of the defense will be paramount for any hope of success the Raiders may have in the run game. It will also test Kubiak’s mettle in devising ways for his short-to-intermediate passing attack to get guys open. Defensive backs Hafley’s specialty is developing young defensive backs and making them into quality players. A point of contention requiring emphasis because the secondary is composed of 2026 first-round pick Chris Johnson, former second-round pick JuJu Brents and multiple late-round picks. All that to say, the secondary is a work in progress, not very good and the first place the Raiders should look to attack. Jason Marshall Jr. was a 2025 fifth-round pick, producing an interception and 4 pass deflections in 12 games. Juju Brents is a big boundary corner on his second career stop and has played in 18 games over the course of three years. Amassing a career total of 1 interception and seven pass breakups. Dante Trader Jr., a 2025 fifth-round pick, is a smaller strong safety who Brock Bowers should pray lines up against him in man coverage. Michael Taaffe, the rookie from Texas, was also drafted in the fifth round and is expected to make moves and be a Swiss Army knife for the defense. The defensive backs are all uniform in size, roughly six feet tall, give or take an inch and within 3-5 pounds of 200 pounds overall. From their first preseason game against the Washington Commanders, Hafley and his defensive coordinator, Sean Duggan, have shown the scheme is all about the attempt to disguise coverages, blitz from multiple levels and confuse quarterbacks. Why? If Cousins is protected properly he should absolutely pick them apart. Defensive line There is a toss-up between which unit is worse, the secondary or the defensive front. Chop Robinson is a young, ascending edge player who is a former first-round draft pick in his third year, still looking at 2026 as his breakout year. Looking to build on the 15 games played in 2025 and the pedestrian 21 total tackles, four sacks, with a forced fumble. Josh Uche is a 226-pound rotational edge who tallied 23 tackles and a sack for the Philadelphia Eagles in 2025. Now as an undersized speed rusher, he is expected to start as the weak-side edge. Zach Sieler and Kenneth Grant are the two monsters in the middle and currently the best defensive linemen on the team. Sieler is the seasoned vet of the bunch with a good mixture of awareness, technique and ability. His counterpart, Grant, should be the nose tackle since he weighs 330 lbs and is tasked with clogging the middle and tying up blockers who would attempt to get to the second level to block the linebackers. As luck would have it, the Raiders will get to dodge him, as he was placed on the IR-designated return list. In his place is the Dolphins’ 2025 draftee Jordan Phillips. The second-year man out of Maryland is a big body who is still getting acclimated to the league. In his rookie campaign, he played in 17 games, starting 16 and tallying 34 total tackles and a single tackle for loss and QB hit. At 6-foot-3 and 324 pounds, he’s a big body to help eat up blocks and clog gaps. Bottom Line The Dolphins defense is like looking into a mirror for the Las Vegas Raiders. Up front, they are even more undersized than the Raiders are; the pass-rushing abilities of the guys on the line are limited, to say the least. In the run game, their job is to funnel the ball carriers into the linebackers while allowing them to flow freely to the ball. Once again, the linebackers are going to be the heartbeat of the team. The Raiders receiving corps drew an easy assignment in week 1, it’s up to them to go out Sunday afternoon and take care of business against this inexperience group of defensive backs.

title: De’Von Achane aiming for NFL rushing title, ready for Week 1
summary: The Miami Dolphins are set to begin their 2026 NFL regular season on Sunday, kicking off a 17-game-over-18-week schedule. The analysts expect the Dolphins to struggle this season, with many predicting Miami to own the first-overall pick in the 2027 Draft by the time the season ends. The Dolphins, themselves, are not buying into those […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - DECEMBER 28: De'Von Achane #28 of the Miami Dolphins runs with the ball against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the second quarter at Hard Rock Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Julio Aguilar/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins are set to begin their 2026 NFL regular season on Sunday, kicking off a 17-game-over-18-week schedule. The analysts expect the Dolphins to struggle this season, with many predicting Miami to own the first-overall pick in the 2027 Draft by the time the season ends. The Dolphins, themselves, are not buying into those prognostications and are still setting lofty goals – especially running back De’Von Achane. Miami’s 2023 third-round pick explained the importance of setting goals, saying, “I feel like you don’t got goals, I feel like what are you playing the game for? And you know, I kind of add more goals as we go through the season, but we always start with some.” When asked to share one of his personal goals, Achane set a lofty objective. “I always try to go for the rushing title so that’s just something I do,“ he stated. Achane, coming off his first career Pro Bowl selection, is expected to be the focal point of the offense this season. Head coach Jeff Hafley joked earlier in the summer that he would be looking to give Achane 45 touches per game this season. While 45 touches is not realistic, Achane was asked how many touches he thinks he will get in Sunday’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders. “I have no idea,” he replied. “I feel like, don’t nobody really know how many times you’re going to touch the ball. I feel like it’s just kind of a however the game is going type thing.” With all the focus on Achane, opposing defenses will likely keep defenders close to the line of scrimmage to slow him down. Asked about what they would do to the offense, the running back recognized how that would open up the passing game, saying, “It just gives opportunities for our young receivers, or whoever’s out there, to make plays. Like you said, this is a team game. I can’t just go out there and win by myself. So when teams do stack the box, we can still try to run the ball, but if we have to adjust, it just gives opportunities for receivers to make plays.” He continued, “It takes all of us. Just like they need me to run, I need them in the pass game. It goes both ways.” The Dolphins underwent a coaching staff change this offseason, with former head coach and offensive play caller Mike McDaniel fired after the year ended and former Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley hired as the 12th full-time head coach in team history. Bobby Slowik, working as the passing game coordinator under McDaniel, was hired as the offensive coordinator for Hafley, keeping some stability in the offense while bringing a new perspective to the attack. How will Slowick’s promotion impact Achane’s utilization? The fourth-year rusher said of the offense, “Of course it’s new…because it’s a new coach. So it’s kind of still the same, you add new stuff, but Slo was here last year with Mike, so some stuff is the same, some things are different. But at the same time, I feel like Slo uses me in the pass game, run game, so it’s good for me.” Achane has lofty goals for himself this season and is probably going to have a great opportunity to reach them. But, in the near term, he is excited just to get the season started this weekend, saying, “I mean, it feels good, man. Like you said, it’s been a long time since we actually played four quarters, and I’ll been excited to be out there and just to go out there, just watch our team, to see how we come and basically just see how we hold up against somebody else for a full game.”

title: What Will the 2026 Dolphins Passing Game Look Like? Let’s Ask the 2022–2023 Packers
summary: The Packers built a passing game without a WR1 — and the Dolphins might do the same. The Dolphins are heading into 2026 with one of the youngest receiver rooms in the league, with three rookies and a second‑year player expected to play real snaps – all catching passes from an unproven, first‑time starting quarterback. […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MD - AUGUST 14: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins looks over the Washington Commanders defense during the first half of a preseason game at Northwest Stadium on August 14, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Packers built a passing game without a WR1 — and the Dolphins might do the same. The Dolphins are heading into 2026 with one of the youngest receiver rooms in the league, with three rookies and a second‑year player expected to play real snaps – all catching passes from an unproven, first‑time starting quarterback. That might sound terrifying in the short term, but we actually have a modern template for how this can work: The Packers from 2022–2023, who rebuilt their pass‑catcher group while transitioning to Jordan Love. The parallels are striking: A young quarterback stepping into a bigger role, a receiver room built almost entirely from scratch and a front office willing to bet on development. Jon‑Eric Sullivan helped architect Green Bay’s youth movement, drafting Christian Watson, Romeo Doubs, Jayden Reed, and Dontayvion Wicks in a two-year span, and now he’s trying to build the same long‑term payoff in Green Bay South. So How Did It Pan Out in Green Bay? Even early in the youth movement, Green Bay’s passing game was solid – which is perhaps to be expected when you have a first‑ballot Hall of Famer behind center. In 2022, Aaron Rodgers’ final season with the Packers, the team finished with 3,890 passing yards and 26 passing touchdowns. Fifteen different players caught passes, and eight of them topped 200 receiving yards. Among the rookies, Christian Watson finished second on the team with 611 yards and 7 touchdowns, while Romeo Doubs added 425 yards and 3 scores. In 2023, with Jordan Love taking over, the passing numbers improved. Love threw for 4,159 yards and 32 touchdowns, and once again the ball was spread widely: sixteen players caught passes, and nine of them reached 200+ receiving yards. Reed, Doubs, Wicks, and Watson combined for roughly 2,500 yards and 25 touchdowns, but none eclipsed 800 yards – a sign that the Packers built the room around depth. (Incidentally, the trend continued beyond these transitional years. Reed and Doubs led the team in 2024 and 2025 with 857 yards and 724 yards, respectively, and six touchdowns apiece.) What Might This Mean for Miami? This isn’t apples to apples – Miami’s offense will look different. For one, the attack will likely run through De’Von Achane, who Jeff Hafley joked would get the ball 40–45 times per game . And Malik Willis brings a running element that Jordan Love didn’t, which will change how defenses play Miami. But when Willis does throw, the distribution may look a lot like Green Bay’s. The Dolphins have six receivers on their 53‑man roster, plus Achane, pass‑catching tight end Greg Dulcich, and several other skill players who can handle targets. The Packers’ young receivers made an impact right away – Reed led the team in yards as a rookie – but at no point did they produce a traditional WR1 with 1,000 yards and double‑digit touchdowns. Miami’s passing game may follow the same pattern, with broad distribution, steady growth and no single player dominating the stat sheet. Keep Expectations in Check As much as we all might love a breakout 1,200‑yard receiver in Miami this season to replace the Cheetah and the Penguin, that might be setting us up for disappointment. But if you can live with a deep and versatile group that gets better as the year goes on – the Packers showed that’s absolutely possible. And with Jon‑Eric Sullivan now running Miami’s roster, it’s no coincidence the Dolphins are trying to build something similar.

Tyler Forness and Dave Stefano of The Real Forno Show (Vikings 1st & SKOL / Bleav) preview Minnesota’s Week 1 home opener against Green Bay at 3:25 p.m. CT. The hook is the unknown: a Kyler Murray debut against former Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon, a light Vikings injury report, and a Packers front missing Micah Parsons and Josh Jacobs. “Kyler Murray could come out, throw for 400 yards and five touchdowns on Sunday, and it wouldn’t surprise anyone,” Forness said. “He also could throw for like 180, a touchdown, and two picks.” The offensive plan, as they sketched it, is incremental, not a full holster dump. Forness cited Murray’s 2024 split: 0.08 EPA per play in the pocket, 0.16 outside it. Expect bootlegs, floods, and half-rolls so Kevin O’Connell can “get him those confident reps.” Frank Smith’s motion is the other lever. Forness argued O’Connell’s run game has been too bland and that Smith’s Dolphins-style motions can change the math against a Packers edge group without Parsons. Dave wants to see Christian Darrisaw and Blake Brandel (and the whole O-Line) in wide zone. On Justin Jefferson, Stefano’s call was blunt: feature him early “to get Gannon to declare.” Forness’s caution: Gannon may simply refuse to let Jefferson beat him and live with Jordan Addison, Jauan Jennings, and T.J. Hockenson. Defense is one job. “You gotta stop Jordan Love.” Fantasy Points data they aired: Love’s intermediate-right window (10–20 yards, right of the hashes) was 96th percentile and 99th percentile in EPA per dropback at 1.105. Favorite concepts were outs and hitches. The counter: interior pressure, cross-dog linebacker games, contain from Andrew Van Ginkel and Dallas Turner so Love cannot escape and hit the scramble drill. “Get pressure up the middle, keep him in the pocket, and collapse on him.” Harrison Smith’s communication is the back-end glue. Forness’s bottom line: “This feels like a game that the Vikings should be able to win rather convincingly.” Will they? That’s the variable. Key Points Vikings injury report: Jacob Thomas (ankle), Jakobe Thomas (illness), Caleb Tiernan (ankle) Packers questions: Zach Bako-Bewele, Aaron Banks, Jordan Morgan, Javon Hargrave, Devonte Wyatt; Parsons and Jacobs out Line flipped from Packers −1.5 to Vikings −1.5 Murray mobility and a simplified early script Smith motion vs. a thin Green Bay edge Jefferson as the coverage tell Love’s right-hash / 12 personnel / Tucker Kraft Flores interior pressure + Hitman communication Forness lean: convincing Vikings win if the variables hold Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: Full episode: The Real Forno Show on Vikings 1st & SKOL. If you want the data, the quotes, and the argument before kickoff, that’s the listen. Fan with Us!!! Tyler Forness @TheRealForno of Vikings 1st & SKOL @Vikings1stSKOL and A to Z Sports @AtoZSportsNFL , with Dave Stefano @Luft_Krigare producing this Vikings 1st & SKOL production, the @RealFornoShow found at the @BleavNetwork . Open Question: If Gannon brackets Jefferson and Love still gets that intermediate-right window, does Minnesota’s Week 1 edge survive?
