title: Are you betting on the 2026 Eagles?
summary: Steve Maltepes, known as “The Philly Godfather,” will impart his gambling wisdom on the Eagles and where the smart money is going on various pro football games each weekend this season. Maltepes is one of the nation’s hottest sports betting experts who appears weekly on national radio and has his own website, www.thephillygodfather.com [thephillygodfather.com]. Much […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - DECEMBER 20: Dallas Goedert #88 of the Philadelphia Eagles catches a pass for a touchdown against Quan Martin #20 of the Washington Commanders in the third quarter at Northwest Stadium on December 20, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Greg Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images Steve Maltepes, known as “The Philly Godfather,” will impart his gambling wisdom on the Eagles and where the smart money is going on various pro football games each weekend this season. Maltepes is one of the nation’s hottest sports betting experts who appears weekly on national radio and has his own website, www.thephillygodfather.com [thephillygodfather.com] . Much is expected of the 2026 Philadelphia Eagles. Talk of a dynasty and winning consecutive Super Bowls ended last year in the Wild Card round of the playoffs, though it does not mean the Eagles will not contend as threepeat champions of the NFC East and make a deep run in the NFC playoffs. First and foremost on everyone’s mind is winning the NFC East. What comes first for professional gamblers is putting their money where their knowledge lies. So, in talking to Steve Maltepes, known as “The Philly Godfather,” one of the country’s elite sports betting authorities and a native of the Philadelphia area, his heart still lies with the Eagles, but his money will be placed on the Dallas Cowboys to win the NFC East and win more than the over/under wins-loss total of 10 games, while placing his money on the under for the Eagles’ total of 10.5 wins. “I have the under for 10.5 wins for the Eagles and Jalen Hurts under 3,250.5 yards passing, the Cowboys to the NFC East +200, and the Eagles to make the playoffs -175,” Maltepes said. “The great news for the Eagles is that the team nucleus is still one of the best in the NFL, and their offensive and defensive line projections are among the top five in the NFL. The first three weeks should go well, opening with Washington, Tennessee and ta Chicago Bears team a lot of people think will regress in 2026. They should be 3-0, and any team that starts 3-0 makes the playoffs 75-percent of the time. “Washington and Tennessee are projected to be sub-.500 teams with win projections expected to be 7.5 and 6.5 wins, respectively. All three teams rank near the bottom of the NFL in overall defense and not much has changed. It’s why I think the Eagles makes the playoffs.” The Eagles better count on going 3-0 to start the season, because after that, Maltepes warns, the schedule gets more difficult. They will then play the Los Angeles Rams, the odds-on favorite to win the Super Bowl, followed by the Jacksonville Jaguars, a team that won 13 games last year, and the Dallas Cowboys, who expected to win 10 games this season and have one of the best offenses in the NFL. The Eagles are fortunate to be going on the road twice in their first seven games, at Tennessee in Week 2, and at Chicago in Week 3. A 5-2 record is a real possibility. It is imperative that the Eagles do get off to a good start, because the five of the Eagles’ last 10 games are against playoff-caliber teams, and twice against a very improved New York Giants team. The Eagles are expected to win double-figure games, though the looming questions are how they will do it without their leading receiver of the last four years, A.J. Brown, and expected to do it with a first-time NFL play caller in new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. Brown is responsible for 36-percent of all the Eagles’ receiving yards the last four years. The Eagles scored only 379 points last year, two points more than the 4-13 Giants. “For the Eagles to exceed the 10,5 wins set by Vegas this year, they will have to be significantly better on offense and will be expected to be better without their leading receiver, Brown,” Maltepes said. “And they will have to be significantly better within their division, going 3-3. Even if they do go 3-3 within the division, can they win eight games among Jacksonville, Pittsburgh, Houston, Seattle, Niners and the Rams? Five of those teams were division winners last year. “It’s why I like the under is 10.5 wins. The other issue is the offensive line. Lane Johnson has spoken about retiring next year. The Eagles are very dependent on Johnson being and staying healthy. If he stays healthy, the Eagles will be okay. If he is not, the Eagles will struggle. Hurts continues to regress throwing the ball. From what we have seen, Mannion will be under a lot of pressure.” Maltepes likes the Falcons in the NFC South, the Packers in the NFC North, the Rams in the NFC West and the Cowboys in the NFC East. He foresees the Eagles winning a playoff game and getting knocked out of the divisional round. He likes the Kansas City Chiefs in the AFC West, Houston Texans in the AFC South, Buffalo Bills in the AFC East and Cincinnati Bengals to win the AFC North, and the Bengals to go on and win the AFC and beat the Rams in the Super Bowl. Cincinnati is projected to be the favorite in 15 to 16 games this season. “The Bengals are a good bet at 22-to-1 to win the Super Bowl, the Chiefs will rebound and win the AFC West, and the Texans are a scary team with their defense,” Maltepes said. “Injuries are big. The three healthiest teams last year were the New England Patriots, Seahawks and Eagles, and two of those three teams wound up in the Super Bowl. I can see the Eagles going 10-7, but too many things will have to go right to win more than 10 games this season.”

title: Big Dom is reportedly being investigated by the NFL because of Emmanuel Acho
summary: Eagles head of security (and a handful of other important titles) Dom “Big Dom” DiSandro was once an unknown figure who moved in the shadows, but in recent years has received his flowers from just about everyone inside the organization for his contributions to the team’s success. When Big Dom was suspended by the NFL […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 4: Dom DiSandro drives Cam Jurgens #51 of the Philadelphia Eagles during Training Camp at NovaCare Complex on August 4, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Eagles head of security (and a handful of other important titles) Dom “Big Dom” DiSandro was once an unknown figure who moved in the shadows, but in recent years has received his flowers from just about everyone inside the organization for his contributions to the team’s success. When Big Dom was suspended by the NFL after an altercation with Dre Greenlaw during an Eagles-49ers game, instead of being punished by his own organization, he was technically promoted . Now, DiSandro is reportedly being investigated regarding allegations of an incident involving former Eagles defender Emmanuel Acho years ago. The investigation was recently reported by Derrick Gunn, who posted : “The NFL is still investigating Eagles head of security Dom DiSandro based on comments made by Emmanuel Acho on his Speakeasy Podcast back in early August … Acho who played for 3 NFL teams never mentioned a name . But it has been widely speculated he was referring to Big Dom “ For the uninitiated, Acho told a story from his playing days of getting into a car accident and calling the team’s head of security for help. Acho alleged that that person set in motion a plan for the first cop at the scene to leave and a second cop to come in, place blame on the other driver, and keep things quiet for Acho. The former NFL player turned hot take artist didn’t specify whether this happened while he was with the Eagles, Giants, or Browns, but the assumption afterward was that it could’ve taken place in Philly. DiSandro recently gave his first-ever interview, after turning them down for years, and sat down with newly anointed Eagles fan Pete Davidson . The biggest takeaway from this 23-minute chat was how much he prioritizes player health and safety, which largely includes their mental health, and how he’s committed to players, both current and former. Philadelphia’s favorite cannoli expert even created a type of big brother program, pairing up guys in the locker room to learn from each other or help each other dealing with similar issues. We’ll have to see how the NFL’s investigation shakes out, and whether or not Big Dom faces any kind of punishment.

title: Eagles vs. Commanders Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 1 enemy
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are beginning their 2026 season with a home game against the Washington Commanders. Nick Sirianni and Jalen Hurts are aiming to reach 6-0 in Week 1 games together. In order to preview this NFC East matchup, I reached out to our enemies over at Hogs Haven. The affable Andrew Y kindly took […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 14: Jayden Daniels #5 of the Washington Commanders tackled by Jalen Carter #98 of the Philadelphia Eagles during the first quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on November 14, 2024 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are beginning their 2026 season with a home game against the Washington Commanders. Nick Sirianni and Jalen Hurts are aiming to reach 6-0 in Week 1 games together. In order to preview this NFC East matchup , I reached out to our enemies over at Hogs Haven . The affable Andrew Y kindly took the time took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let’s take a look at the answers. [For my answers to Andrew’s questions about the Eagles, check out HH .] 1) What are Commanders fans expecting from the team this year? Their win total over/under is 7.5 games, what side of that number are you leaning? I’m leaning to the over on 7.5 wins, but I think the Commanders have a very wide range of outcomes and I think most Commanders fans are bracing for the worst while hoping for the best and expecting anything as possible. There are a lot of reasons for this wide range of expected outcomes. On the one hand, the Commanders on paper had a worse roster in 2024 when they went to the NFC Championship game. At the same time, the reason they made it that far was due to their QB who elevated the entire offense, but couldn’t string together more than three consecutive healthy games in 2025. In addition, the team has two new coordinators in OC David Blough and DC Daronte Jones, both of whom are first-time playcallers. In addition to that, a large amount of the team’s success in 2024 and problems in 2025 was due to injury luck, which is difficult to predict. So I’d say the Commanders are one of the most boom-bust teams in the NFL heading into this season. 2) The Commanders have two new coordinators. How are fans feeling about David Blough and Daronte Jones ahead of Week 1? I think we’re feeling overall positive about both coordinators, but more confident in Daronte Jones than David Blough simply because he’s been coaching since 2002 and has coached under respected DCs like Brian Flores, Vance Joseph, and Mike Zimmer. In contrast, David Blough was a player in 2023 and has only ever coached the past two years in Washington. That said, Blough has risen quickly through the offensive coaching ranks here and drew interest from the Lions as a potential OC this past offseason, which forced the decision on promoting him here. In terms of what to expect? Daronte Jones is expected to run a very Brian Flores-like defense, which focuses on a 3-4 base with lots of disguise, frequent blitzing, and defensive pre-snap motion to confuse the opposing offense. It’s a defense that puts players in lots of different positions, often dropping DL back into coverage while blitzing DBs from unexpected locations, so it demands a lot of versatility from its players. Also, make no mistake, it will be Daronte Jones running the defense, not Dan Quinn. Quinn values empowering his coordinators and delegating responsibility to them so that he can focus on higher-level team/game management. David Blough is expected to run a very Ben Johnson-like offense, focusing on a wide-zone run game and heavy use of under-center play action and attacking the middle of the field in the passing game. Blough played for the Lions under Ben Johnson and seems to have been most influenced in philosophy by his time there. Blough is also an amateur magician and will probably lean heavily into the trick play aspect of Ben Johnson’s offenses, though we have seen none of that in the preseason as they save it for games that matter. My main concern with David Blough is his lack of coaching experience and a fear that he will lean too heavily into complexity and trick plays while failing to hammer down the fundamentals that are necessary to make those things work. The team took a big gamble in parting ways with established OC Kliff Kingsbury and promoting Blough to take his place, so I think this coordinator change best embodies the boom-bust nature of the Commanders’ season outlook. 3) The Laremy Tunsil injury is a big loss for the Commanders and it’s not the only concern with Washington’s offensive line. What are you expecting the starting five to look like in Week 1 and what’s your confidence level in that group? Laremy Tunsil was a top-5 LT in the NFL, so losing him before a game is played hurts. However, his backup Brandon Coleman is probably one of the team’s better backups, so I don’t expect that injury to completely alter the season. Vegas seems to agree, as the season-long win total for the team has remained stable at 7.5 wins both before and after the injury. I have confidence in the starting five to be an average NFL offensive line, but I think they are a thin group that cannot afford to lose any more players to injury. The starting five will almost certainly be the following – LT Brandon Coleman – As a rookie in 2024, Brandon Coleman was the starting LT for this team and helped us make it all the way to the NFC Championship game. The team still saw an opportunity to upgrade to one of the top LTs in the NFL in Laremy Tunsil, forcing Coleman to train at LG, but moving back to LT should not be a problem for him. – LG Chris Paul – Paul was the Commanders starting LG last year and played well enough, generally being seen as positive in pass protection and negative in run blocking. He was getting beaten out in training camp by Brandon Coleman, but the Tunsil injury forced Coleman back to LT and Paul back into the starting LG spot. – C Nick Allegretti – This is the position generating the most discussion amongst Washington fans. The team cut veteran Center Tyler Biadasz with what sounds like a handshake agreement to sign Tyler Linderbaum in free agency. Then Linderbaum got a godfather offer from the Raiders and went to Vegas. Meanwhile, the rest of free agency was a feeding frenzy at the Center position that didn’t leave many good options after day 2. The Commanders seem to have settled for last year’s backup IOL Nick Allegretti as the starting Center as a result. He played well at Center last year when called upon, but the only depth behind him is rookie 6th-round pick Matt Gulbin, which leaves Allegretti as paradoxically the least accomplished, but also most important player on the starting OL this year. It doesn’t help that he missed basically all of training camp and the preseason with a calf strain. He’s expected to play week 1 and Washington fans will cross every finger they have that he stays healthy. – RG Sam Cosmi – Cosmi has been a very good RG for the Commanders throughout his career. His 2025 season was mostly lost to injury, but I expect him to perform well this year. – RT Josh Conerly Jr – Conerly was a bit up-and-down for the Commanders after being selected in the 1st round last year. He got better as the year wore on though, so fans are hopeful he will pick up where he left off last year. 4) What’s the biggest matchup in the Commanders’ favor and the biggest matchup against their favor? The biggest matchup in the Commanders favor is probably their pass catchers in the middle of the field against the Eagles safeties. From what I understand, safety is likely to be the closest thing to an Achilles heel on the Eagles defense this year. At the same time, I mentioned the presumed David Blough offense is likely to attack the middle of the field aggressively and the Commanders signed Chig Okonkwo and Stefon Diggs particularly to help there. I’m most worried about the Eagles DTs against the interior offensive line of the Commanders. It’s obviously a problem that Nick Allegretti has spent very little time practicing with the first-team offense due to his injury in training camp and the Eagles have a very good DT group. If the Eagles can get consistent inside pressure with their DTs, it will be the…

title: 3 questions for the Sean Mannion offense
summary: The Eagles have handed the keys to the offense to Sean Mannion, who this time three years ago was an unemployed player. Supporting him is a coaching staff that is also pretty light on experience: passing game coordinator Josh Grizzard, offensive line coach Chris Kuper, tight ends coach Ryan Mahaffey, and offensive analyst Jerrod Johnson […]
full_text: The Eagles have handed the keys to the offense to Sean Mannion, who this time three years ago was an unemployed player. Supporting him is a coaching staff that is also pretty light on experience: passing game coordinator Josh Grizzard, offensive line coach Chris Kuper, tight ends coach Ryan Mahaffey, and offensive analyst Jerrod Johnson have 11 combined seasons as a position coach, pass/run game coordinator, or offensive coordinator. The Eagles are putting a lot of faith in a group of inexperienced coaches who run an offense that will feel foreign to the style of play they have had for years. Jeffrey Lurie has previously said he doesn’t want his team to be risk averse. This is definitely taking a risk. The players have talked up the new staff, and that’s great. But words don’t matter, results do. Nick Sirianni, Sean Mannion, and Mannion’s staff have three questions they need to answer this season. Can they get/do they want Jalen Hurts to run? It was talked about plenty last season, but just to quickly review, prior to 2025 Jalen Hurts averaged 9.9 rushing attempts a game. Additionally, in the seven games in two Super Bowl runs he ran for an average of, coincidentally, 9.9 attempts a game. In 2025, he had just 6.6 attempts a game. In his three first round exits he ran 8, 1, and 5 times. Was the lack of runs Kevin Patullo’s fault for not calling enough runs? Yes. Was the lack of runs Jalen Hurts’ fault for not wanting to run as much? Yes. For the Eagles offense to play at its highest level, Jalen Hurts is going to have to use his legs more. Can Sean Mannion get him to do that? Will Mannion even want him to? Mannion doesn’t come from offenses that ask the QB to run the ball. In Green Bay Jordan Love has averaged 2.6 attempts a game in three years as a starter. Mannion’s time on the Vikings under Kevin O’Connell was with Kirk Cousins at QB; his time with the Seahawks was with Geno Smith, who averaged 3.3 attempts per game when Mannion was there; and Russell Wilson, who averaged 3.1; his time on the Rams under Sean McVay was with Jared Goff. And as a player, Mannion was not at all a runner. Sean Mannion as a player and as a coach has never been in an offense with a QB who can threaten the defense on every down and distance with his legs. Nor has passing game coordinator Josh Grizzard, Baker Mayfield averaged 3.4 attempts while Grizzard was there, and his time with the Dolphins was with a collection of non-runners in Jay Cutler, Ryan Tannehill, Ryan Fitzpatrick, and Tua Tagovailoa. But absence of evidence is not evidence of absence. While Mannion and Grizzard have never been a part of an offense with a heavy dose of QB runs, they have also never been a part of an offense with a QB who can justify having a heavy dose of QB runs. If the Eagles aren’t going to use the legs of their mobile QB, what is the point of having that mobile QB? Can the offense show some complexity? When the Eagles offense is humming, like in 2022 and 2024, it has been pretty unstoppable. But when it is not, like in 2025 and 2023, it is frustratingly basic. Under Nick Sirianni and Jalen Hurts, the Eagles offense has not used all the tools in the toolbox. Motion Per PFF , since 2021 over half of all plays had some kind of pre-snap shift or motion, which has trended up every year since at least 2015. With Jalen Hurts at QB, the Eagles have infamously rarely used motion. In 2024 Kellen Moore used a lot of motion to start the season, but by the end the offense was in the middle of the pack . The Eagles don’t need to be one of the top teams in motion, doing so at a high rate guarantees nothing: four of the top ten teams in pre-snap motion last year were bottom nine in points scored. Just getting to the second quartile would be an improvement. Tempo Under Shane Steichen, the Eagles were 13th and 11th in seconds per play. Following him, 17th, 23rd, and 28th. Like motion, tempo isn’t everything, but waiting until the last possible second to snap the ball was yet another area where the offense became very predictable. Spreading the ball around In 2022 the Eagles offense was almost entirely AJ Brown, Devonta Smith, and Dallas Goedert. It got them to a Super Bowl. In 2024 they added Saquon Barkley and won it. There is little reason to stop giving the ball to superior players when they’re playing at a high level. But nothing about the Eagles offense in 2025 was superior or high level. And when support players would come in and give the offense a boost, they wouldn’t get more chances. Tank Bigsby ran 7 times for 86 yards in the 4th quarter against the Giants in a 38-20 win. Over the next five games, in which the Eagles went 2-3 and scored 16.2 points per game, he had 9 touches while Saquon Barkley averaged 3.8 yards per carry. In the playoffs, Bigsby had three straight runs for 4, 9, and 7 yards early in the 2nd quarter on what ended up being a TD drive. He had one touch the rest of the game. Jahan Dotson had a 51 yard catch in Week 1 against the Cowboys. The next game, 1 target. He had a 40 yard catch in the win over the Giants. The next game, where the Eagles threw for just 183 yards, he was never targeted. He had a 34 yard catch against the Lions. In the next game he was not targeted in a 3 point loss to the Cowboys. We saw this same type of usage in 2024 with Dotson, and in 2023 with Olamide Zaccheaus, who before and after his one year on the Eagles had 40+ catches for 500+ yards, respectable WR3 production. Over the course of a season there are times where you need to lean a little on complimentary players. The Eagles haven’t really done that under Nick Sirianni. The offense would see a backup do something positive and rather than give him a chance to keep it going, they’d forget about him. With AJ Brown gone, Dallas Goedert coming off his least efficient season, and Saquon Barkley coming off a major drop in efficiency, the Eagles need to lean on their complementary players more than they have with Hurts at QB. With yet another offensive scheme that is new to the team, if the offense remains as basic as it has been, then the team has a major problem. How much rope will Nick Sirianni give Mannion? Brian Johnson and Kevin Patullo had issues that showed up right away and never got resolved. Despite proclamations to the contrary, as those teams got deeper in the season and the play callers got deeper in the muck, Sirianni, as is his and the front office’s prerogative, got more involved. It made no difference. Kellen Moore also didn’t get off to a great start, scoring 21, 15, and 16 points in the Eagles second through fourth games of the season, then went on to finish 2nd in scoring. The 2022 offense scored 38 in the opener and then averaged 24.6 points over the next six games, then 30 over the rest of the season, including playoffs. So a sluggish September is to be expected. After that, though, what happens if the offense continues to struggle? If Sean Mannion turns out to be a Temu Sean McVay, will Sirianni put his hands back on the wheel? If so, as we have seen before, it’s probably too late.
author: Dave Mangels

title: Eagles News: “The Eagles do not consider 2026 to be a make-or-break season for either Jalen Hurts or Nick Sirianni”
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! I’m not disputing the Inquirer’s reporting but were the Eagles thinking that Doug Pederson and Carson Wentz were facing make-or-break seasons entering 2020? I don’t know. And I’m not suggesting that 2026 will be like that down year, I actually feel […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! I’m not disputing the Inquirer’s reporting but were the Eagles thinking that Doug Pederson and Carson Wentz were facing make-or-break seasons entering 2020? I don’t know. And I’m not suggesting that 2026 will be like that down year, I actually feel comfortable with the Eagles’ floor entering this season. My point is that things can always change faster than we might expect, for better or for worse. At this point in time, it does seem pretty likely that both Hurts and Sirianni will be back in 2027. NFL sources: Neither QB Jalen Hurts nor coach Nick Sirianni faces a make-or-break season in 2026. Good. – Inquirer An offseason of communications with various NFL sources indicated two things: The Eagles do not consider 2026 to be a make-or-break season for either Hurts or Sirianni. That’s because … Installing an offense that is so philosophically different than what’s come before it is not a 17-game undertaking. It’s a two-season project. This makes perfect sense. It is the proper way to view the matter. I’ll admit, it’s not the way I viewed the matter this spring. I thought Hurts’ limitations as a passer and decision-maker should imperil his status past 2026. I thought Sirianni’s inability to mature and his lack of offensive innovation should imperil his status as well. I came around. Several NFL insiders said that this season should not be crucial for either the coach or the QB. Why? Because, as long as the 2026 season doesn’t deteriorate into disaster, and as long as there is promise in December that the Birds can win big as soon as next season, the Eagles will have a better foundation than ever. They could be building something that lasts for the next decade. Mannion likely won’t be here for that long, since top offensive coordinators usually get hired as head coaches as soon as they show any aptitude. But Hurts is only 28. Sirianni can become a legend in Philly. That’s what the Eagles‘ brain trust wants. Eagles Injury Report: Jonathan Greenard and Eli Stowers limited – BGN The Eagles listed two players under LIMITED PARTICIPATION: Jonathan Greenard and Eli Stowers. We previously noted that Greenard returned to practice after missing all of training camp due to a pec strain. The Inquirer’s Jeff McLane reported that the Eagles want to see how Greenard fares in practice this week before determining his availability for Sunday. Even if the veteran edge rusher doesn’t suit up against the Commanders, he figures to be back in game action sooner than later. Good news for the Eagles’ defense. ‘Breaking down walls:’ Jalen Hurts goes deep on Sean Mannion and new offense – NBCSP “If he feels that’s what gives us the best chance to win, the best chance for him to see the game and find his flow and what he’s doing, that’s the direction we need to go in,” Hurts said. “So I’m going to support whatever makes him feel comfortable in that degree. And for me, you know coming to the year, you know, talking, thinking about breaking down walls of communication and talking and communicating the things that I’m seeing and whatnot, and there is a wall, you know, being in the box, but still having open dialogue using the red phone, calling if I see something, hearing them out, and I think in all it’s just a part of the process. I was thinking yesterday about how I would meet with Stout (Jeff Stoutland) every Tuesday and he would give me the game plan and do those things, and so a lot of it is new and there’s a transition, it’s a bit of an evolution. But we’ve got great guys here that I can lean on and that can fill those voids so we can do what we’re trying to do moving forward. So just take it a day at a time and continue to work and experience. Work, build, work, let the chemistry develop naturally.” NFL Week 1 latest intel, buzz questions, news, fantasy tips – ESPN GRAZIANO: I don’t think Jalen Hurts is in danger of losing his job this season, but I’m extremely interested to see how he looks early in Philadelphia’s new offense. Are there massive growing pains as the Eagles get used to Sean Mannion’s scheme? Does Mannion’s inexperience create issues? It’s a sneaky-big year for Hurts in Philly, and he has to show he can handle it and thrive amid all the change on offense if he wants to secure his long-term future there. I expect the offense to improve as the season progresses, but this first month will determine how far they have to go. […] FOWLER: That’s why I expect the Eagles to lean into the run game early. Saquon Barkley breaking off those 20-plus-yard runs in 2024 opened the field for Hurts, and the Eagles have the offensive line to make that happen again. The NFL’s Quarterback Rooms, Ranked – The Ringer 12) PHILADELPHIA EAGLES. If we’re looking at EPA, Jalen Hurts is coming off the worst season of his career—yes, even worse than his middling 2021 campaign and the 2023 Super Bowl hangover season. We can certainly blame at least some of Hurts’s issues in 2025 on a poorly designed offense that was too simple and predictable. Now he’s got a new offensive coordinator, Sean Mannion, who is installing pieces of the Shanahan-McVay style of offense in the hope of getting the most out of Hurts while his salary is a relative bargain. Financially, the Eagles’ quarterback room is healthy—for now. Hurts will make $51 million this year, which ranks 12th among quarterbacks. The best part about Hurts’s deal is that it won’t carry a cap hit of more than $47 million in any of the remaining years. This is all part of Philadelphia’s plan to utilize every salary cap trick it can for its most expensive contracts, keeping present-day costs down and trusting that the cap will keep rising year over year as cap hits balloon down the line. GM Howie Roseman has prioritized depth, including at quarterback, where McKee has been this team’s backup for the past three seasons. He has flashed fringe starter potential during limited preseason work, and he could potentially be a trade target for rebuilding teams this season. The Eagles’ quarterback room is well positioned, especially for a team without an elite individual talent. Reviewing Lincoln Financial Field’s new food items for the Eagles’ 2026 season – PhillyVoice The Philadelphia Eagles invited media to sample Lincoln Financial Field’s new menu items for the 2026 season on Wednesday. So, I went and had myself some lunch. Game Preview – WAS at PHI – Iggles Blitz That wasn’t a great group a month ago. Since then they lost Tunsil to a major injury and that means they will have mediocre to bad players at 4 of 5 OL spots. That’s not ideal when facing an Eagles front that is loaded with talent. The only real question for Philly is the status of Jonathan Greenard. He practiced on Wednesday and it feels like he’s trending to play in the opener. Washington does have a key X-factor in the person of Jayden Daniels. He is a mobile QB with dynamic ability when he’s at his best. The Eagles can win up front only to see him use his legs to make plays. They got that lesson when Daniels beat them 36-33 back in December of 2024. Vic Fangio has probably studied the heck out of that tape and will hopefully have more answers this time around. The Commanders aren’t afraid of this matchup. They think the line will have improved with practice time and that having a gameplan will make a substantial difference in the overall offense. They also really believe in Daniels and his ability to be a special player. This matchup will be a good test for both teams. Washington has better weapons than people realize. If the line can just be okay, the offense has a chance. The Eagles defense has talented playmakers at every level. They just need to get on the field in a game and show what they can do. title: Steelers-Falcons preview: What to expect from Atlanta’s offense, defense in Week 1
summary: The regular season is back, and so are Read & React’s game previews. This week, we’ll take a look at the Atlanta Falcons, who finished 2025 with an 8-9 record and third place in the NFC South. Atlanta, like Pittsburgh, will be debuting a new head coach in Week 1. The Falcons fired Raheem Morris […]
full_text: Jan 4, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson (7) runs the ball against the New Orleans Saints in the third quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The regular season is back, and so are Read & React’s game previews. This week, we’ll take a look at the Atlanta Falcons, who finished 2025 with an 8-9 record and third place in the NFC South. Atlanta, like Pittsburgh, will be debuting a new head coach in Week 1. The Falcons fired Raheem Morris after the team’s disappointing finish last year, hiring former Browns head coach Kevin Stefanski to lead the team in 2026. It’s a new era for the Falcons. What can the Steelers expect to face in their season opener? What to expect from the Falcons’ offense Rushing YPG 2025: 125.8 (8th) Passing YPG 2025: 207.2 (19th) PPG 2025: 20.8 (24th) The Atlanta Falcons are a strange offense to wrap your head around. On the one hand, they have three first-round talents that most of the football-watching community agrees are supremely talented. There’s Bijan Robinson, the do-it-all running back the Falcons selected eighth overall in 2023 and whom they just made one of the league’s richest ball carriers with an extension this offseason. Falcons also boast two highly drafted pass catchers: receiver Drake London (2022’s eighth overall selection) and Kyle Pitts (2021’s fourth overall selection). Both London and Pitts signed big-money extensions this summer as well. That collection of talent alone makes them a team you can’t afford to sleep on. However, outside of the Browns — whose coach last year is now the head coach in Atlanta —the Falcons might have the worst quarterback situation in the NFL. Another former eighth-overall selection, Michael Penix Jr., is still not healthy enough to take the field. That meant the Steelers were supposed to see former Dolphin Tua Tagovailoa, a player who just had a brutal preseason and whom Miami is paying just under $52.8 million to play anywhere else. Things were so bad for Tua this summer, NBC had this report ahead of the Patriots-Seahawks game yesterday: “If it doesn’t go well for Tua and he gets benched again, I’m told there is a strong possibility the Falcons will do what the Dolphins did and cut Tua Tagovailoa.” We haven’t even played yet. 😭😭😭 pic.twitter.com/h1I7xbbOhR — Carrie (@Carrie_ATL) September 10, 2026 Things took another turn Thursday when, less than 24 hours later, Tua seemed to suffer an oblique injury that has put his availability into question. Falcons QB Tua Tagovailoa appeared to suffer discomfort during individual throwing drills Thursday and briefly went to the ground. Tagovailoa missed the first week of training camp due to lower back spasms. — Josh Kendall (@JoshTheAthletic) September 10, 2026 As I mentioned before, ESPN’s Adam Schefter already reported that Penix would be inactive Sunday , so he isn’t an option should Tua have to miss this. That means the Falcons might be forced to turn to a player Mike McCarthy should be quite familiar with, having coached him in Dallas. Cooper Rush said he took all the reps with the 1s today. #Falcons — Marc Raimondi (@marcraimondi) September 10, 2026 All this is to say that the offensive situation for Atlanta is messy, and while that should set the Steelers up for success, it can make projecting the exact offense we’ll see a muddled picture. Still, Steelers fans should recognize elements of what the Falcons are likely to run Sunday. Stefanski was Cleveland’s head coach for six seasons. His offensive coordinator, Tommy Rees, was with the Browns the past two seasons as well, growing from passing game coordinator in 2024 to OC in 2025. As such, we should expect to see a run game featuring wide zone runs, a healthy dose of play-action and bootlegs from under center, and formations with multiple tight ends on the field. With that and the Falcons’ quarterback situation in mind, focus number one should be shutting down Robinson and the run game. Robinson is the most talented player on that offense, and he’s got the production to match. In three seasons, Robinson’s produced 3,910 rushing yards, 198 receptions for 1,738 yards, and 34 total touchdowns. He is the engine behind the Falcons’ attack, and he’s difficult to bring down. In 2025, Robinson was second in the league in average yards after contact (3.9) while the Steelers were 10th worst in that stat (3.10) as a defense. No. 3 on the NFL Top 100 Players of 2026… @AtlantaFalcons RB Bijan Robinson! @NFLFilms pic.twitter.com/seqOFrSuVx — NFL (@NFL) September 2, 2026 With a backup quarterback in, there’s a strong chance Robinson leads both the Falcons’ rushing and passing attack on Sunday. London and Pitts might arguably be more effective with Rush under center than they might have been with Tagovailoa. London is a traditional possession receiver who primarily lines up outside, but he also moonlights as a power slot, with 30.7% of his career snaps coming inside. London isn’t a player who creates a ton of separation with his routes, but he knows how to box out opposing defensive backs to secure the ball and has a 52% conversion rate on contested balls. 3 Minutes of @DrakeLondon_ jump balls #DirtyBirds https://t.co/eTBsfsQKRz pic.twitter.com/yBzjquRwWD — 𝙁𝙖𝙡𝙘𝙤𝙣𝙨 𝙈𝙪𝙨𝙚 (@ATLFalconsMuse) January 23, 2026 Meanwhile, Pitts had a return to form in 2025. After eclipsing 1,000 yards as a rookie, he battled injuries and inconsistent quarterback play in the three seasons that followed. Last year, he looked fully healthy again, totaling 928 yards and setting career highs in receptions (88), touchdowns (5), and yards after the catch (399). Know Stefanski’s proclivity for featuring tight ends in his offense, I would circle Pitts as the player the Steelers should be most focused on stopping after Robinson. Kyle Pitts Sr. 11 REC, 166 YDS, 3 TDs vs TB Tonight. HAVE A NIGHT KYLE PITTS. pic.twitter.com/l2ZAHeFwQx https://t.co/nesfyquOpL — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) December 12, 2025 Outside of Atlanta’s big three, the Falcons receiving corps is a bit of a hodgepodge of role players. Jahan Dotson might be familiar to the Penn State fans in Steeler Nation, but he’s on his third team in five seasons and has struggled to match the promise of his rookie season when he scored seven touchdowns for Washington. He was held under 20 receptions and under 275 yards in each of the past two seasons while playing for the Eagles. Likewise, Olamide Zaccheaus is an eighth-year NFL journeyman on his second stint with the Falcons. He has just 2,311 career yards and 15 touchdowns, and is more known for doing the dirty work offenses need from a complementary receiver. If there is one wild card I’d keep an eye on, it’s rookie third-rounder Zachariah Branch. Branch is a smaller receiver (5’10, 180 pounds) with a limited route tree, but a reputation for creating yards after the catch on designed touches near the line of scrimmage. Whether it’s Tagovailoa or Rush — who also has a spotty track record throwing deep with a career completion percentage of just 33.3% on throws 20+ yards downfield — I wouldn’t be surprised to see a few plays designed for Branch to try to create some easy-button looks that might still result in explosive gains, even with a limited quarterback. title: Steelers given blueprint on how to beat Patriots
summary: The first game of the 2026 NFL season brought real football back to our screens, and narratives-a-plenty to dive into over the next week until both the New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks each take the field again. Despite holding a 10-0 lead on a Seahawks team sans Sam Darnold, the Patriots found a way […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 09: Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots is sacked by Leonard Williams #99 of the Seattle Seahawks during the fourth quarter in the game at Lumen Field on September 09, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jane Gershovich/Getty Images) | Getty Images The first game of the 2026 NFL season brought real football back to our screens, and narratives-a-plenty to dive into over the next week until both the New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks each take the field again. Despite holding a 10-0 lead on a Seahawks team sans Sam Darnold, the Patriots found a way to give away what looked to be a win that was gift-wrapped. Drake Maye threw three fourth-quarter interceptions that allowed Seattle to score 13 unanswered points and steal a victory as the Seahawks defense dominated New England’s offense all night. With the Steelers facing New England in Week 2, they now have a blueprint laid out for them on how to handle Maye and the Patriots’ offense, as well as the best ways to beat their defense. For starters, Seattle’s timely blitzes were instrumental in their win. And it wasn’t that they were blitzing a ton, but when they blitzed and how they blitzed through the Patriots off kilter all night. Mike Macdonald is very good at showing you one thing and then doing another. He did it on a key third down early in the game, showing seven rushers at the line of scrimmage, but dropping a linebacker into coverage while sending Devon Witherspoon on a nickel blitz. The Patriots had no answer for it in the Super Bowl, and it was successful again to force a quick throw away from Maye. Overall, the Seahawks only blitzed on 23.8 percent of snaps, per Sumer Sports , which is over 10 percent lower than the league average from a season ago. However, their tackle for loss rate was over 3.5 percent higher than the league average. Seattle was able to get penetration in largely base and nickel looks. The constant ability to get pressure without blitzing makes the blitzes more successful. Maye was rattled by exactly that. It also didn’t help that the Patriots also had no success running the ball. Without Drake Maye’s scrambling, New England totaled 62 yards on 24 carries. So what does this mean for the Steelers? It looks highly unlikely that A.J. Brown will play, meaning New England’s receiving corps will be without its best weapon. Pittsburgh could stack the box and dare the Patriots to throw, but Seattle showed you can win with a base defense if you have a strong front, which the Steelers do. They don’t have to blitz constantly as long as they can get home with just four rushers. Well-timed blitzes and ensuring New England won’t be able to run the ball consistently should ensure a win come Week 2. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Cam Heyward voices displeasure with franchise tag
summary: Pittsburgh Steelers defensive tackle Cam Heyward dealt with his own contract dispute before agreeing to a contract sweetener before the 2025 season. Joey Porter Jr. finds himself in a similar predicament, looking for a new deal before the Steelers take the field against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. Porter is due to make just under […]
full_text: Pittsburgh Steelers defensive tackle Cam Heyward dealt with his own contract dispute before agreeing to a contract sweetener before the 2025 season. Joey Porter Jr. finds himself in a similar predicament, looking for a new deal before the Steelers take the field against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. Porter is due to make just under $4 million in the final year of his rookie contract. Top corners Devon Witherspoon (Seahawks) and Christian Gonzalez (Patriots) have reset the core back market with deals exceeding $100 million guaranteed. One angle the Steelers could take with Porter Jr., if they don’t agree on a deal, is to place the franchise tag on him and retain his rights for 2027. Porter Jr. would earn $24 million, a $20 million raise but less than the projected $27-30 million he could earn with a long-term contract. The longest-tenured Steeler thinks the franchise tag is pointless for players and shouldn’t be eligible to be used in the league. “It’s stupid,” Heyward said after practice . “It hampers players. Why should any team be able to take advantage of a player for one year?” The Steelers signed 2023 draft picks Nick Herbig, Darnell Washington, and Keeanu Benton to deals, leaving Porter Jr. as the lone remaining contributor. “It’s used in negotiations, and I think between the player options, the franchise tags, the way they control rookies, I think it’s kind of backwards,” Heyward said. The franchise tag is STUPID #Steelers Cam Heyward on how players get SCREWED by the tag pic.twitter.com/B89kLv3y71 — 93.7 The Fan (@937theFan) September 9, 2026 The Steelers put a team policy in place during the 1990s that they would not negotiate with players in season, meaning only days remain for Porter Jr. and the franchise to agree to terms. There is still time, and negotiations can change in a dime. NFL Network reporter Mike Garafolo said on Tuesday that the Steelers have made an offer to Porter Jr., but the two sides remain far apart. No consideration of IR at this point, but his timetable to return remains TBD. https://t.co/4YwSi91bV1 — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) September 10, 2026 If Darnold ended up on injured reserve at any point before the Cardinals game, he would not be available until at least Week 7 against the Kansas City Chiefs. full_text: Sep 11, 2026; Melbourne, AUS; San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans (5) makes a touchdown catch over Los Angeles Rams cornerback Jaylen Watson (35) in the second half at Melbourne Cricket Ground. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Los Angeles Rams entered the 2026 NFL season as overwhelming Super Bowl favorites following their headline-grabbing offseason. They almost made the actual reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks a total afterthought even though the Rams lost two out of three to Seattle. Well, they had their chance to make a great statement of intent down in Australia against the San Francisco 49ers, and while international games (in Week 1, nevertheless) can be noisy, the noise you heard in Melbourne was the loudest of farts. What an INT by Renardo Green 😮‍💨 SFvsLAR on Netflix pic.twitter.com/CEHqrX4RtN — NFL (@NFL) September 11, 2026 Other than some early rushing offense dominance against San Francisco’s vulnerable defensive interior, it was a disastrous opener on both sides of the ball for Sean McVay’s side. Brock Purdy shook off an early interception and threw touchdowns to Demarcus Robinson, Deebo Samuel, and Mike Evans. Matthew Stafford struggled with accuracy, threw a bad interception to offset the Purdy pick, and he was critically stopped on a 4th and goal sneak at the 1 when the score was 17-7 late in the third quarter. The 49ers unleashed a 99-yard touchdown drive to essentially kill the competitive portion of the game off. PURDY CONNECTS WITH DEEBO FOR THE TD!! SFvsLAR on Netflix pic.twitter.com/XKrxUtmLzI — NFL (@NFL) September 11, 2026 Myles Garrett, the prized acquisition of the entire NFL offseason, did absolutely nothing of consequence against the 49ers offensive line. Zero stats recorded. ZERO. No sacks, no tackles, no pressures, no QB hits, nothing. He was in-and-out of the lineup and looking visibly gassed. Tonight was Myles Garrett's first game without a pressure since 2018 Week 10 per PFF. — Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) September 11, 2026 Purdy wasn’t sacked once and the rushing attack, which was much more evenly split between Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black, racked up over 170 yards against LA’s defensive line, which of course doesn’t yet have Aaron Donald but he likely would’ve not made much of a difference in the game’s outcome. The final score was 49ers 27, Rams 7 and in the closing minutes we saw Stetson Bennett IV snaps instead of Matthew Stafford. To much debate and discussion, the Rams arrived late to Melbourne and may as well have never boarded at all. While it’s great to see the favorites falter, we can’t lose sight of the fact that the 49ers looked really good and will be playing the Miami Dolphins and Arizona Cardinals over the next two weeks, so they could easily be 3-0 before tougher games against the Denver Broncos and Seahawks to start October. The one down note for them is a potentially serious injury to rookie receiver De’Zhaun Stribling, who was carted off with a non-contact leg injury. Hopefully it’s not an Achilles rupture for the young man. The 49ers are atop the NFC West on division record tiebreaker over the Seahawks, who will get their first divisional game against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 2. Meanwhile, the Rams’ Week 2 game is on a Monday night at home versus the New York Giants. At least it’s much easier to root for the Giants in this scenario.

What is technically a Thursday night game in the United States is a Friday morning kickoff in Melbourne, and we’ll soon find out if staying in Australia for a week is a better strategy than flying in about as late as reasonably possible like the Rams did. title: Seahawks lose Bryce Cabeldue to Raiders following waiver claim
summary: Prior to Thursday’s victory over the New England Patriots, the Seattle Seahawks added some depth to their secondary with the elevation of AJ Finley to the 53 man roster to feel more secure in the home opener. With that came the corresponding move of cutting 2025’s sixth round pick Bryce Cabeldue. If the Seahawks hoped […]
full_text: Prior to Thursday’s victory over the New England Patriots, the Seattle Seahawks added some depth to their secondary with the elevation of AJ Finley to the 53 man roster to feel more secure in the home opener. With that came the corresponding move of cutting 2025’s sixth round pick Bryce Cabeldue. If the Seahawks hoped to get him back onto the practice squad, their hopes were squashed. The #Raiders have claimed G Bryce Cabeldue off waivers from the #Seahawks . — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) September 10, 2026 Per Mike Garafolo, Klint Kubiak added the guard to his squad over in Las Vegas. With familiarity with the scheme that he runs, it makes sense that Kubiak would want Cabeldue to join him with the Raiders. With the ability to play both right guard and left guard, as well as right tackle and left tackle, that helps Kubiak’s squad have depth along the offensive line that ranked dead last in the league in 2025 . Improving the offensive line was a focus for Kubiak, adding Tyler Linderbaum to anchor the interior at center, Evan Neal, and drafting Trey Zuhn III. As it stands right now, Cabeldue is the third left guard on the Raiders depth chart per ESPN behind Spencer Burford and Antonio Mafi. Update : Mafi was waived, so Cabeldue moves up the depth chart.

title: Seahawks-Patriots post-game analysis: Not exactly where we left off, but close
summary: Third quarter, down 10-0: “Well, it’s not like 2025 started that great, either.” Fourth quarter, as Drake Maye lofts the illest-advised pass of his career to your new favorite player, Joshua Jobe, Esq.: “Knew it. They had it all the way.” With a season-opening 13-10 rope-a-doping of Maye and his New England Patriots, the Seattle […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 09: Head coach Mike MacDonald of the Seattle Seahawks celebrates after defeating the New England Patriots in the game at Lumen Field on September 09, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jane Gershovich/Getty Images) | Getty Images Third quarter, down 10-0: “Well, it’s not like 2025 started that great, either.” Fourth quarter, as Drake Maye lofts the illest-advised pass of his career to your new favorite player, Joshua Jobe, Esq. : “Knew it. They had it all the way.” With a season-opening 13-10 rope-a-doping of Maye and his New England Patriots, the Seattle Seahawks began their Super Bowl defense the right way. The confounding questions surrounding the secondary were answered with three picks in the final frame, and the thorniest question about depth was answered when Drew Lock essentially saved the day in relief of Sam Darnold. Yes, it took Seattle three nigh-unwatchable quarters to get the bugs out. But once that fumigation was done, we were treated to an evening of fun-igation, punctuated with everything a championship team does when it’s not quite ready to relinquish its title. Including having a kicker who knocks ‘em through the uprights. Did I mention they answered just about all the preseason questions we had? But first, as is their modus operandi, the Hawks had to torture us like 53 grown versions of Sid Phillips, or maybe the pigeons from that old Bud Light commercial, you know, the ones who see poop targets on every car. Yes that’s it, felt like poop targets. Every time something cool happened, something stinky hit the fan and made you guano tear your hair out. The Seahawks committed eight penalties before the Patriots’ first flag. And you can’t really argue with any of them except maybe the fourth down offsides on the right side of the line. They gifted the visitors all ten of their points, through a roughing the punter brain fart and Jobe’s most impactful play of the young season, that foolish DPI on the underthrown ball at the goal line. Of course, Jobe was just setting up his own redemption arc. /puts hand to temple, flashes knowing grin They lost their starting quarterback on the fifth play of the season and played three scoreless quarters. Thing is, you play that fourth quarter usually, don’t you (copyright Pete Carroll, if he was more boring). And a lot can happen in the final fifteen minutes. A lot can happen in the final minute! "A TERRIBLE DECISION" — CJ Fogler (@cjzero.bsky.social) 2026-09-10T03:25:11.455Z Let’s zoom in for a second, on the feet, the perfect feet of the world’s greatest ballet dancer. Objectively, also Josh Jobe. What a fortuitous coincidence for the Seahawks and their fans! TIPTOBE JOBE — John Fraley (@johndavidfraley.bsky.social) 2026-09-10T03:25:59.358Z Jobe’s end zone pick is the biggest moment of the game, and it will never, ever get old to intercept a Patriots QB in the end zone. I hope it happens 49 more times before I die. Yet if we’re looking for the Plays Of The Game with an s, we’ll be looking all the way up and down the roster and the sideline. Drew Lock kicked ass. Yes, he got dinged for a delay of game late, opening the door for the Pats. He also got out of trouble repeatedly, scrambled smartly, took care of the ball, led three scoring drives in the fourth quarter and made more than one big boy throw under duress. No turnovers, 78.6 QBR and a 113 rating is why you keep a guy like that in your system for cheap. Julian Love was a handsome assassin everywhere on the field. Mike Macdonald and Brian Fleury adapted to the circumstances and pulled out a win when defeat looked certain. Nehemiah Pritchett won a starting spot at outside corner tonight in my opinion, and it’ll be incumbent on guys like Trevon Diggs and Terrion Arnold to wrest it from him, should they even get the chance. Jadarian Price carried the load like a vet, in his first-ever pro game. Jaxson Smith-Njigba might as well be called The Drummer because he missed exactly zero beats. The offensive line dominated. Uchenna Nwosu ensured he will continue to patrol the nightmares of every Patriot, as he has since February. Byron Murphy announced himself on the national stage. Michael Dickson pinned New England deep all night. Cooper Kupp single-handedly (get it!?) set up the first score, one that could’ve been a touchdown, if not for the meddling Cooper Kupp. Dang that’s a lot pf pixels. You want a tl;dr? Practically everyone came up huge on a night the Seahawks needed practically everyone up and down the 70-man roster. Let’s put their highlights in the recap, even though nobody should have to fully relive that first 45 minutes of football-adjacent behavior. Q1: SEA 0, NE 0 An opening drive that began about as auspiciously as possible, with matching explosives to Price and JSN, ended with a sack of Darnold. He limped to the sideline and originally didn’t go to the blue medical tent, but once he did, his night was over. It looked so innocuous, too. First quarter ending. The lowlight: — John Fraley (@johndavidfraley.bsky.social) 2026-09-10T00:53:47.567Z The Patriots’ first drive was strangely foreshadowy. A Maye scramble and two short gains set up third down and the NE quarterback being chased out of bounds on third down, where Derick Hall’s inexplicable late hit extended the drive. No matter, Nwosu’s very explicable domination of his counterparts did the job. A play you may have forgotten from Q1 — John Fraley (@johndavidfraley.bsky.social) 2026-09-10T05:19:22.075Z With Lock now in under center, it briefly appeared the offense would start humming, with eight yards to JSN to set up second and short… but the Seahawks failed to convert twice and settled for punting one fourth and one, a perfectly acceptable choice with Darnold out. The Patriots racked up 20 quick yards before reaching their own third and one. Which Julian Love saw coming. Did he ever. I will say it again, a devastatingly handsome tackle — John Fraley (@johndavidfraley.bsky.social) 2026-09-10T00:54:29.768Z Each quarter of game action gets its own Predator-Prey highlight this season, that’s how we’re gonna do it. It’s clearly Nwosu discarding Eli Raridon to meet Rhamondre Stevenson in the backfield and kill three birds with one stone: the TE, the RB and the second drive. The ease with which Chenna helped himself to Stevenson, as a snack, provided hope when it was in scarce supply. Q2: NE 7, SEA 0 Lock’s first pass of the second quarter, on a third and five, was more to Christian Gonzalez than Kupp. Almost intercepted and could’ve changed the game. Thing is, almosts and could’ves don’t pay the bills and the NFL’s richest corner will have to settle for taking the ball away some other day. We didn’t know it at the time, but that would simultaneously be Gonzalez’s best opportunity to flip the field and Lock’s worst toss. And yes, the Pats would score on their next drive anyway, aided by Jobe’s inability to look back for the ball, A.J. Brown’s veteran slowdown, and Josh McDaniels’ nifty goal-line playcalling. Raridon scored the first touchdown of the 2026 NFL season after a dummy block left him wide open, and somewhere, his mom’s fantasy team briefly took the lead in her Week 1 matchup. Smart play, Mom. Don’t know if it’ll work twice. The Seahawks looked poised to answer right back, driving to midfield when Lock fired an ICBM to Smith-Njigba for 21 yards on 3rd and 22. Replays suggested Macdonald could’ve successfully challenged the spot and won, but the Barnyard formation took the field, converted with an inspired second effort, to the crowd’s great delight, but what’s this ANOTHER FLAG, somewhat less to the crowd’s delight. It turns out Abe Lucas or Anthony Bradford set up in the neutral zone, maybe. Take a look yourself if you haven’t yet. the other calls have been correct. This one is bullshit. The ball is snapped before Lucas moves. — John Fraley (@johndavidfraley.bsky.social) 2026-09-10T01:19:40.168Z The language gives it away: I was big mad at the…

title: Seahawks injury update: Sam Darnold expected to miss Week 2 vs. Cardinals
summary: The Seattle Seahawks may have won their opening game against the New England Patriots, but the Super Bowl champions did lose starting quarterback Sam Darnold on the opening drive of the season with a hip injury. When it’s anything to do with the hip, the fear is a fracture or something that could indicate a […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 09: Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks prepares to take the field prior to the game against the New England Patriots at Lumen Field on September 09, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks may have won their opening game against the New England Patriots, but the Super Bowl champions did lose starting quarterback Sam Darnold on the opening drive of the season with a hip injury. When it’s anything to do with the hip, the fear is a fracture or something that could indicate a long-term absence, but it does not seem like that will be the case for Sam. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Thursday morning that Darnold underwent an MRI on his hip, and while the Seahawks anticipate he’ll miss at least one game, a major length of absence appears to have been avoided. Seahawks QB Sam Darnold underwent an MRI on his hip this morning that team doctors still are reviewing to determine how much time he will miss. It is expected to be some, but for now the team believes it, as one source described, “dodged a bullet.” pic.twitter.com/w3SIU8pi7x — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) September 10, 2026 Ian Rapoport followed up by saying Darnold will likely miss Week 2 at the Arizona Cardinals, a place where the Seahawks have definitely never had catastrophic injuries before, but he might be back fairly soon even after that. Sam Darnold is expected to miss next week's game, but he should be back sooner, rather than later, sources say. Could be just a few weeks. With 17 days from Wed. until their Week 3 game against the #Commanders , Darnold gets a schedule break, as well. https://t.co/UjGk85IYPA — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) September 10, 2026 Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said on his radio show that Darnold’s injury appears to be more of a muscle issue instead of the hip structure itself, which is a massive relief. Mike Macdonald, on @SeattleSports with @BrockHuard and @TheMikeSalk , said Sam Darnold’s hip is intact and that it appears the injury is more muscular. “That’s good news,” he said. “Now, how long that is, we don’t know.” — Brady Henderson (@BradyHenderson) September 10, 2026 Without reading too deeply into this, it sounds like Darnold will avoid short-term IR and thus miss at least the next four games. Also a relief for the Seahawks? Drew Lock stepped up in an emergency and made several timely throws (often in the face of pressure) in Seattle’s comeback win. While Lock started twice in Geno Smith’s absence in 2023, this was the first time in his Seahawks career he’d been tasked with extended reps due to starter injury. He’ll presumably get all of the starting reps in practice next week, and ideally the communication issues between himself and offensive coordinator Brian Fleury will be smoothed over now that there’s an actual gameplan that can be developed. It will be interesting to see if Jalen Milroe is incorporated in any way for the game(s) Lock starts, as he’ll be QB2 next week and therefore active on game day. But the big story is that Darnold has an injury, he’ll miss time, but it’s not as disastrous as it could’ve been.

title: Seahawks show that the ‘Ready Squad’ is more than just a saying in win over Patriots
summary: Mike Macdonald and John Schneider routinely mention that the Seahawks are not just 53 guys. Rather, they are a full 70-man roster, and that numbers 54-70 are not just a practice squad, but rather a “ready squad.” This sentiment was a large theme throughout “Hard Knocks” these past few weeks. Well it did not take […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 9: Rodney Thomas #24 of the Seattle Seahawks celebrates after an interception during the fourth quarter of an NFL football game against the New England Patriots at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Mike Macdonald and John Schneider routinely mention that the Seahawks are not just 53 guys. Rather, they are a full 70-man roster, and that numbers 54-70 are not just a practice squad, but rather a “ready squad.” This sentiment was a large theme throughout “Hard Knocks” these past few weeks. Well it did not take long to really exemplify that the “ready squad” is a lot more than just a saying; it is a true belief in the full 70-men that make up this Seattle Seahawks team. The team’s week one victory over the New England Patriots exemplifies this perfectly. On only the fifth play of the game, Sam Darnold went down with a hip injury that cost him the rest of the game . Enter in backup quarterback, Drew Lock. Despite a slow start, Lock ended up with a respectable stat line (16/22 for 187 yards, one touchdown, and zero interceptions) , clearly outplaying 2025 MVP runner-up Drake Maye (23/33 for 178 yards, one touchdown and three interceptions). Although Lock is on the 53-man roster and is not technically on the “ready squad,” his role as the backup quarterback exemplifies the same mindset; practicing each and every day with the belief that they must be ready to help this team succeed at a moment’s notice. Just listen to Lock talk postgame about how he has to draw plays on a whiteboard next to his bed in order to stay ready for a game with the lack of reps that he gets as the backup quarterback. However, let’s take a look at the actual “ready squad” players who were activated for the game (Rodney Thomas II and Velus Jones Jr.) Playing as a starting safety in place of injured Ty Okada, Rodney Thomas II put up four tackles and one significant pass deflection. That pass deflection helped led Drake Maye to throw his first interception of the game to Nehemiah Pritchett . That interception led to the Seahawks scoring a 45-yard touchdown to wide receiver, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, tying the game at 10-10. Mike Macdonald doesn’t sweat when he has to play backups. He’s excited to see what they can do because he knows they’ve earned the right to be in the lineup. Rodney Thomas (24) and Nehemiah Pritchett exemplifying that here. pic.twitter.com/apLYl29qjT — Dugar, Michael-Shawn (@MikeDugar) September 10, 2026 The other “ready squad” elevation, running back, Velus Jones Jr. also made an impact play in the game, even if it didn’t show up in the box score. Middle of the third quarter, Michael Dickson punted the ball, and Jones Jr., playing as a gunner on the play, quickly made his way down the field to down the ball inside the five-yard line. This under the radar play helped lead the Patriots to go three and out and punt the ball back to Seattle with great field position. That next drive by the Seahawks (aided by Jones Jr.’s key special teams play) led them to scoring their first points of the game, a field goal by Jason Myers. All of these plays, from Drew Lock, Rodney Thomas II, Velus Jones Jr., and others, helps exemplify that the Seahawks “ready squad” and full 70-man roster are more than just a saying. It is a true faith in the team. A faith that already, just one week into the season, has proven to be a big difference between the team being 0-1 and 1-0.
author: John Tapia

title: Seahawks opens Khosla era with patented ‘Seahawks Primetime BS’ game
summary: The entire season for the Seattle Seahawks flashed before all of our eyes just five plays into the 2026 season opener against the New England Patriots. As most fans were still looking up and admiring the new Super Bowl 60 championship banner, Sam Darnold was sacked to stall the opening drive. It seemed like a […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 9: Julian Love #20 of the Seattle Seahawks celebrates after an NFL football game against the New England Patriots at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The entire season for the Seattle Seahawks flashed before all of our eyes just five plays into the 2026 season opener against the New England Patriots. As most fans were still looking up and admiring the new Super Bowl 60 championship banner, Sam Darnold was sacked to stall the opening drive . It seemed like a normal play at the time, but Darnold was shown to limp a bit coming off the field. He was even reported to not be entering the blue medical tent for treatment. Fast forward a few minutes, and Darnold was indeed heading into the tent. Worse than that, he went right into the locker room and was quickly ruled out. By God, that’s Drew Lock’s music! Lock entered the game in an extremely adverse situation and the offense sputtered early on. After the Seahawks went down 10-0, the defense started to come alive. That momentum transferred to the offense as new offensive coordinator Brian Fleury made some damn fine adjustments to score 13 unanswered points. The defense bent to the very edge, but slammed the door once again at the end, picking off Drake Maye for the third time to end the game to cap off a frankly ridiculous comeback that I am SO here for. Seahawks Droppings Mike Macdonald said in his postgame presser that the early news on Darnold is encouraging in that there isn’t a fracture . If Darnold avoided serious injury, we should all feel very fortunate. There’s extra rest until the second game, so we’ll have to see when (hopefully) Darnold can make it back on the field. Drew Lock has some “Seattle Primetime Magic”. Flash back to the game against the Philadelphia Eagles in the rain with the game-winning TD pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Tonight, Lock was thrown into the fire and struggled at the beginning, then put together some fantastic play down the stretch. His stat line won’t wow you, going 16/22 for 187 yards and 1 TD, but he outpassed last year’s No. 2 in the MVP race, Drake Maye. Most importantly, Lock took care of the ball. There were some procedural errors on the final scoring drive which was likely the difference between coming away with a FG instead of a TD, making the defense’s last stand even more ulcer-inducing. Overall, Lock stepped up in a big way and might be counted on for the next few weeks. Kudos to Brian Fleury . I’m sure having his starting QB knocked out of the game on the first drive wasn’t on his bingo card, Yet, Fleury was able to make the necessary adjustments to move the ball with Lock under center. His ability to adjust on the fly and overcome adversity is a great sign. Guys, I think Jadarian Price might be pretty good . He only had 10 carries, but turned that into 52 yards. Price showcased his vision running both inside and outside. He also caught both of his targets. As Price’s role expands, he could be an extremely dangerous weapon. Jaxon Smith-Njigba had one of the sneakiest 122-yard games I can remember . His long TD catch-and-run brought the Seahawks back from the dead, and he was always open when they needed him. It’s such a luxury to have him on our team. The whole secondary was awesome tonight with three huge interceptions. Julian Love was all over the field laying the wood along with picking off the ball. Nehemiah Pritchett played a hell of a game with his own INT and another huge pass breakup. He even made a great tackle, something he’s not known for. Josh Jobe is known for his tackling which showed up tonight. Oh, and he iced the game with his own INT. I’d be remiss if I didn’t mention Rodney Thomas II, starting in place of Ty Okada. Thomas tipped the ball that Pritchett caught and was in the general vicinity of Romeo Doubs when he dropped that wide open pass so I’ll give him credit for the intimidation. Devon Witherspoon was his usual self flying around the field and being a disruptor. They stepped up with Okada and Nick Emmanwori down with injury. The defensive line turned it up at the end of the game when it was needed most . I could call out most of the guys here, but the main one I want to single out is Uchenna Nwosu. He was a got-danged demon out there against New England. Chenna lived in the backfield all game and shut down plays all by himself. With the rest of the firepower along the line, he doesn’t get the credit that he deserves. That dude is a stud. Jason Myers made all of his kicks. That’s all I have to say about that. The Khosla family was baptized into the Seahawks fire in the most perfect way possible . It never ceases to amaze me how many times per year this team attempts to shorten my lifespan. Seriously, the Seahawks are mayhem incarnate. I’m fully convinced that I will die by the time I’m 40 just by watching Seattle play football games, particularly those in Primetime. I hope the Khosla’s have good medical insurance! I’m going to get a cardiac test before the next @Seahawks game. The team and 12s won it tonight. Hard to imagine a better roller coaster — Vinod Khosla (@vkhosla) September 10, 2026 This game was essentially “New year, same Seahawks Primetime Bullshit.” Mike Macdonald’s team showed grit, never wavered, and found a way to make it happen in the end. It definitely wasn’t always pretty, but I’ll take a win every time. They give me a tension headache nearly every game, and I’m sure our new owners will find that out very soon. I can’t wait until next season when we get some ridiculous game with those sublime white throwbacks! Time to end it here because I think I need a cigarette…and I don’t even smoke.

title: Seahawks News: Seahawks grind out big win at home over the Patriots
summary: For several concrete reasons, your favorite team’s first game of an NFL season is always a bit messy, unpredictable, and usually is not an exact indicator of how the remainder of the schedule will play out. Bad teams look good early; good teams look bad early. Last night, our Seattle Seahawks endured an injury at […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 9: Drew Lock #2 of the Seattle Seahawks celebrates after an NFL football game against the New England Patriots at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images For several concrete reasons, your favorite team’s first game of an NFL season is always a bit messy, unpredictable, and usually is not an exact indicator of how the remainder of the schedule will play out. Bad teams look good early; good teams look bad early. Last night, our Seattle Seahawks endured an injury at a critical position, a slow start, penalties (lots of them), and a feisty New England Patriots squad to eek out a notable victory in their home/season opener. The defending champions found a way to win by pass rush, interceptions, and some nifty and timely play-calling from first time play-caller Brian Fleury. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, still disrespected despite winning OPOY last season, shouldered the weight of the offense to score a huge touchdown to tie the game late. Then, after Julian Love picked off Drake Maye (his second interception of the game), the Seahawks calmly marched down the the field, and despite themselves (a few odd procedural penalties, geez), kicked a FG to take the lead. From there, Coach Macdonald ratcheted up the Darkside and put enough pressure on the Pats to force Maye and Mike Vrabel into some bad decisions. One Drew Lock postgame interview later, and we are still the toast of the town. How did you enjoy the game? How happy are you that our squad is back at it again? Was the game ever in doubt for you? Are you encouraged by OC Brian Fleury’s play-calling? What are you worried about? Where are you content? Lots to talk about. Let us know what you’re thinking in the comments below.
